Selbstorganisierter Aktionstag gegen Rassismus und Ausgrenzung – Geschäftsschließungen von 10 bis 16 Uhr – Kundgebung von 14 bis 16 Uhr auf dem Marktplatz in Halle. Siehe Initiative „MigraStark“ (leider nur)

Weiter aus der

Für viele Menschen mit Flucht- und Migrationsgeschichte ist diese Entwicklung keine abstrakte parteipolitische Frage. Sie erleben eine zunehmende Unsicherheit darüber, welche Zukunft sie und ihre Familien in Sachsen-Anhalt haben, ob ihre Zugehörigkeit weiterhin selbstverständlich sein wird und welche politische Macht in einer neuen Landesregierung entstehen könnte.


Der Flüchtlingsrat erklärt dazu: „Menschenwürde hat keine Legislaturperiode. Grund- und Menschenrechte gelten jederzeit – und für alle. Ihr Schutz muss von jeder Regierung sichergestellt werden. Hierfür setzt der Aktionstag in Halle ein deutliches Zeichen.“

Die Aktion erreichte weit über Sachsen-Anhalt hinaus öffentliche Aufmerksamkeit. Entscheidend war dabei nicht allein die Zahl geschlossener Geschäfte. Entscheidend war, dass Menschen selbst ihre Stimme erhoben, einander unterstützten und deutlich machten: Wir lassen uns nicht gegeneinander ausspielen.


Halle knüpft nun mit einer eigenen, selbstorganisierten Initiative daran an.


Dabei gilt auch diesmal: Niemand muss durch Arbeit, Steuern oder wirtschaftlichen Nutzen beweisen, dass er oder sie dazugehört. Menschenwürde muss man sich nicht verdienen

…“

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Home Office Unlawfully Blocks Gaza Children From Joining Families in UK
content:
The Home Office is refusing to allow mothers and their children trapped in Gaza to join family members in the UK, even after a judge said the government’s position is unlawful.


The two women, who have five children between them aged seven and under, were told to submit biometric information as part of a security check to obtain family reunification visas.


But the application centre where they would need to submit fingerprints and other information has been closed since the start of Israel’s genocide in October 2023.


On 30 September, a judge in the immigration and asylum chamber of the upper tribunal ruled that the Home Office, by refusing to waive the biometric requirement for these families, had unlawfully applied its unsafe journeys policy.


In her ruling, judge Fiona Lindsley said the mothers and children – who have been granted anonymity – “have too little food and are suffering from malnutrition. They dare not go to US aid collection points as they are aware that people have been killed by Israeli forces at these places.”


She said the children’s fathers, who are based in the UK, were also suffering severe psychological hardship. One has been diagnosed with PTSD due to his experiences in Gaza “coupled with the continuous threat” to the survival of his wife and children, she added.


The Home Office has appealed the judge’s decision and a hearing is set for 16 December. But the Greater Manchester Immigration Aid Unit (GMIAU), whic

h


represents the families,

 said th

at process will further delay reunification and put the families “in grave danger” in Gaza.


“The children are all traumatised,” said Decla Palmer, a lawyer from GMIAU. “They have gone to bed every night to the sound of bombs, suffering from nightmares, with rats and mice crawling around their tent. The mothers are completely exhausted and without hope.”


“Every day the families remain in Gaza, they are at risk of death,” said GMIAU.


Surgeons who have worked in Gaza have said Israeli forces

 deliberately and systematically

 kill children. Dutch newspaper Volkskrant last year

published testimony from doctors

 who had encountered at least 114 children with multiple bullet wounds in the head and chest.


A Home Office spokesperson told Novara Media that “enrolment of biometrics enables comprehensive checks… to identify individuals who may pose a threat to national security, public safety or immigration controls.”


Ghassan Ghaben of the British Palestinian Committee, an advocacy group, said the government was applying a double standard against Gazan families.


“The UK has shown in other situations that, when there is the political will, rules can be adapted to the realities of war – and in this case, genocide,” he said. “The Ukraine Family Scheme recognised that ordinary immigration procedures were not appropriate in the circumstances and enabled people to reunite with their families.”


Since the Russian invasion in 2022, Ukrainians and their children have been able to live and work in Britain under special temporary humanitarian visas.


“Palestinians have been asking for a similarly practical response since 2023, yet the response has instead been to maintain or introduce even stricter barriers,” said Ghaben.


He added there was “a real contradiction” between the shift in rhetoric about Gaza from Andy Burnham’s Labour government and its treatment of the families. 


“The home secretary has recently announced the reopening of the UK Resettlement Scheme, and spoken about creating safe and legal routes for people fleeing persecution,” he said.


“Yet at the same time, the Home Office is continuing to fight against the reunification of Palestinian mothers and young children with their fathers who are already in the UK.”


During the genocide in Gaza, the UK has

allowed weapons

 sales to Israel, flown spy flights over Gaza, allowed

military planes to depart

 from its bases bound for Israel and

refused to investigate British nationals

 who joined the Israeli military.


Home secretary Shabana Mahmood was accused last month of


giving people in Gaza “false hope”

 after announcing a new safe route to the UK for Palestinian refugees. The route only applies to those who have

already escaped to Lebanon or Jordan

 and will benefit only a few hundred people a year.


Last year, the government suspended a programme that allowed people granted asylum in the UK to bring their family members over.

title: SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!
content:
Oh, wait… sorry. The Judge already did that in court.


John ‘Pinocchio’ Henty’s case ends in acquittal

.


Thank you to


South Suffolk Hunt Sabs


for this guest article.


A court case brought by former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty against a hunt saboteur has ended in a resounding victory for the defence, with the saboteur found NOT GUILTY.


John Henty outside court.


Following allegations made to police, former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty pursued a prosecution alleging abusive and threatening behaviour under Section 5 of the Public Order Act. The case followed an incident on a quiet country lane in which Henty pursued the hunt saboteurs’ vehicle, blocked it in, approached it and attempted to provoke a reaction.


What followed was a lengthy legal process based on Henty’s account of events. However, when his evidence was examined in court, serious questions arose about the credibility of that account and whether the alleged behaviour actually amounted to a criminal offence.


A case that should never have reached court?


The Judge was highly critical of the way the case had been handled by the CPS and the police officers involved, making clear that the alleged actions did not meet the legal threshold required for a criminal offence.


Both the prosecution and the defence barrister sought to discontinue the case on more than one occasion. The case was nevertheless directed to proceed. The circumstances surrounding that decision raise serious questions about why so much time and public money were spent pursuing a prosecution that ultimately failed.


Former Essex & Suffolk Hunt huntsman John Henty is now at The Ludlow Hunt.


The evidence tells a different story


Henty submitted two video clips, recorded by himself, which were played in court. The footage showed Henty pulling his vehicle alongside the hunt saboteurs’ Land Rover, getting out of his own accord and filming the encounter.


Our saboteur told Henty to ‘f*ck off’ before closing the vehicle door. Rather than disengaging, Henty continued filming and engaging with the occupants. Despite claiming under oath that he had been alarmed and distressed, the circumstances captured on his own footage told a different story.


The prosecution was unable to produce further evidence demonstrating that Henty had experienced the alarm or distress alleged.


Henty spun a yarn of lies that should never have made it to court.


The judge’s conclusion


Having heard Henty’s evidence under cross-examination and considered the footage and relevant law, the Judge concluded that:


Henty had parked his vehicle alongside the saboteurs’ vehicle of his own accord.


He had got out of his vehicle voluntarily.


He had chosen to film the encounter.


He had continued the interaction of his own accord.


He had not contacted the police immediately, instead reporting the incident to 101 approximately two hours later.


These circumstances were central to the Judge’s assessment of Henty’s claim that he had experienced fear, alarm and distress. Following Henty’s evidence and cross-examination by the prosecution and defence, the case concluded without our hunt saboteur needing to take the stand.


The verdict

:

Not guilty. Acquitted.


After all the allegations, the police involvement, the CPS proceedings and the considerable expenditure of public resources, the case ended in an acquittal. A considerable amount of time, money and public resources had been spent pursuing this matter, only for the court to reach a conclusion that raises serious questions about why the prosecution was pursued in the first place.


Hunt saboteurs will not be intimidated out of exposing illegal hunting. And they will not be silenced by allegations that cannot withstand scrutiny in court.


The South Suffolk One stands vindicated.


SAVE THE SOUTH SUFFOLK ONE!


South Suffolk Hunt Sabs remain steadfast and will not be intimidated or silenced.

title: Lois Waisbrooker - A Sex Revolution
content:
Author

: Lois Waisbrooker

Title

: A Sex Revolution

Date

: 1894

Notes

: Second Edition

Source

http://www.pierssen.com/misc/treasures/asr.htm

>


Preface.


 Dear Reader:—The history of the past shows us that nations rise, go through a longer or shorter period of prosperity and then decay. The ruling motive in the life of nations, so far, has always been the same, the aggressive or masculine. Self-aggrandizement,

our

 nation right or wrong, all to be laid upon the national altar in the name of patriotism, a centralizing of wealth and power in the hands of the few at the expense of the many, and the result has always been what? Go, gather together the human wrecks of any one nation and you have your answer.


 Now will not this latest and brightest of nations perish also unless methods are changed, unless the social lever is reversed? Already the seeds of decay are taking root; is there not some law through which we may take a new lease of life, and what is that law, if there be such, if it be not that


 “woman, take the lead?”


 True, woman is already quite prominent, is becoming more so, but she does not seem as yet to realize that with man’s methods she will succeed no better than man has done. She must formulate her own methods before her true work can appear. Woman must be free, must refuse to be led, must believe in herself, before the evils attendant upon imperfect motherhood can be eliminated, and as I see things, the only hope of our nation lies in this direction.


 Let us once rise above the necessity of armies, navies, prisons, almshouses, asylums, etc., then the future will stretch out before us with ever increasing brightness. The first step toward this desirable consummation is to believe that it

can

 be done; the next is that it

will

 be done, and lastly to determine to do it

ourselves

.


 L. W.


Chapter I.


 First, a little something about myself. I, Margaret Mulgrove, am a childless widow. My husband, Richard Mulgrove, went into the Union army at the beginning of our last war and never came out alive. My only child, little Bessie, took the scarlet fever in the second year of my widowhood, and though employing the most skillful physician in the whole country around, I could not save her. To say that I was desolate does not begin to express the feeling I had.


 An aunt, my father’s only sister who lived in another State, hearing of my bereavement, decided to come and stay with me awhile and wrote me to that effect. Now my father and mother had in their lifetime (I forgot to say that I was an orphan also) had been good orthodox Christians and had brought me up to walk in the same path, so when Aunt Belinda wrote me she was coming I was a little troubled, for I had been told that she was an Infidel.


 I believed infidelity to be something awful, and as our community was a very respectable one, to have a woman of that character come among us, and as my relative was an affliction I had not counted on, but it could not be helped; aunt would be there the next day and I must make the best of it. So the next morning I went to work to put things in the best order possible to receive my expected relative.


 She came about ten o’clock, a pleasant faced, white haired lady toward whom my heart instinctively went out, and in spite of my prejudices I felt that I should love her. She stayed with me several months during which time nothing was said or done which brought up the subject of beliefs. True, I had purposely avoided everything that could lead in that direction, but she did not seem at all inclined to be aggressive.


 The Sunday, and in fact the day before she left, our minister’s sermon called out some remarks from her that surprised me very much.


 “Why aunt,” I exclaimed, “I thought you were an Infidel!”


 “And so I am to church theology.”


 “And yet you have just affirmed your belief in the underlying principle of all church theology.”


 “How is that?” she asked.


 “You said you believe in God manifest in the flesh.”


 “I said I believed God manifest in the flesh was necessary to the salvation of the race, but I did not say I believed it had already taken place.”


 “Not taken place! do you then look for a coming Christ?”


 The old lady smiled. “Before you can understand me,” she said, “you must learn that a narrow personal application of a general principle is, must be false. The universal spirit of life can never be manifest in its fullness through, or be embodied in …

author: Lisa Xu
title: Reform Candidate Says UFCW Rep Tailed Him for 300 Miles to Thwart Petition Effort
content:
In a union that has been headed by one family with no competitive elections since 1984, a group of grocery workers is organizing for change. But this week, they say, union staff who back the incumbent administration went to outrageous lengths in an attempt to make sure there’s no election this year either.


On Monday afternoon, Eric Marcuz, a veteran Northern California Safeway worker, stopped at the union office to pick up blank petitions to get on the ballot in the union’s upcoming election. Marcuz is running for president on the

At What Cost

 slate in the 23,000-member United Food and Commercial Workers (UFCW) Local 8-Golden State, one of the largest locals in the union.


To get on the ballot, Marcuz and his slate-mates have to collect 443 petition signatures—2 percent of the local’s active members—in the next two weeks. If they don’t get enough signatures, no election will be held.


After Marcuz picked up the petitions from the local’s Roseville office, he got in his car to drive three hours south to Fresno, to start collecting signatures with another candidate on his slate at a Save Mart store there. (The local spans a 10-hour stretch from Bakersfield up to the Oregon border).


When Marcuz stopped for gas, he said he noticed that a black Dodge Ram pickup stopped as well. When he got back on the freeway, so did the truck.


At the next gas stop, Marcuz spoke to the man driving the truck. It was Jeff Berns, a staff representative for Local 8-GS. His brother, Mark, is also a rep for the union—and the local’s election chair, responsible for overseeing the election.


Marcuz asked Jeff Berns why he was following him. According to Marcuz, Berns said he wanted to make sure that all the members got the “accurate information” that Marcuz’s slate was going to “divide” the union. He said he was going to follow him the entire time Marcuz was out, all the way back to Marcuz’s house in Redding, several hours north. Marcuz jokingly asked him if he needed a place to stay. Berns said he didn’t—because he’d been staying a lot in the Redding area lately himself, which Marcuz said he thought was “creepy” because that’s where Marcuz lives with his family (and is not where Berns lives).


Berns would live up to his promise—following Marcuz for the next 300 miles, through every stop, exit, and U-turn. He even followed him inside the Fresno Save Mart, and camped out for an hour with another union rep while Marcuz ate dinner at a supporter's house 100 miles north in Modesto.


NO COMPETITIVE ELECTIONS


At the gas station, Berns repeated the mantra, “Solidarity works!” That’s the motto of the incumbent president, Jacques Loveall, who is heading the

Solidarity Works Team

 slate in this election.


Loveall was appointed to lead the union in 2004, when his father, Jack Loveall, stepped down. The elder Loveall had held the top office since 1984; when he retired he was one of the highest-paid union officers in the country, earning the equivalent of $1 million today. (The

Contra Costa Times

 reported that he had a $28,000-a-year country club membership and “two pilots on staff to chauffeur him in a private jet.”) Neither father nor son has ever faced a competitive election in the local.


Back on the freeway, Marcuz called a Department of Labor agent whom he had already been in touch with. They had previously spoken about the local’s apparent attempt to

cancel the election

 by merging with a mysterious organization called the Staffing Agencies Federated Employees, an entity which listed one of Loveall’s relatives as its president on its initial filing. The agent told him to report the intimidation to the election chair and tell him to get the rep to back off.


Marcuz then called Mark Berns, the election chair, who he said told him he would talk to staff about acting in a professional manner.


MORE REPS


However, when Marcuz arrived at the Save Mart store in Fresno to begin collecting petition signatures, he and another slatemate, Mike Romero, said that three union reps were waiting for them, including Jeff Berns. One of the others was John Micheletti, a longtime Local 8 vice president. Far from being called off, they said, the intimidation had actually intensified.


Marcuz and Romero said the reps interfered with every conversation they attempted to have with workers about signing their nomination petition. The very first worker they engaged about signing, a longtime acquaintance of Romero’s, fled once a rep entered the …

author: Andrew Crocker
title: We’re Asking the Ninth Circuit to Hold Reverse Location Warrants Categorically Unconstitutional
content:
Yesterday, along with the ACLU, EFF filed an

amicus brief

 in the Ninth Circuit court of appeals in

United States v. Spurlock

, a case involving a “tower dump” warrant. These overbroad warrants require cellular providers to turn over location data about every phone in a given area at a given time. This is the first such case to be heard by a federal appeals court since the

US Supreme Court ruled this summer

 that highly similar “geofence” warrants are searches under the meaning of the Fourth Amendment.


Spurlock

involves an investigation into two murder victims discovered on the side of a rural California highway. Police also found a car belonging to one of the victims several miles away on the same highway. They quickly sought a tower dump warrant for an area covering this stretch of road, which eventually revealed location data on nearly 1,700 unique phones. Faced with a motion to suppress, the district court relied on a

Fifth Circuit court of appeals decision

 about geofence warrants to hold that tower dumps are similarly categorically unconstitutional “general warrants” that violate the Fourth Amendment. However, the court refused to suppress evidence on the basis of the “good faith doctrine.”


Our amicus brief on appeal makes several key arguments.


First, we point out that the Supreme Court’s decision in the geofence case

Chatrie v. United States

this summer only strengthens the arguments that tower dumps are unconstitutional general warrants. Tower dumps are a somewhat older technique than geofence warrants, but they are both “reverse location searches,” in which police “tap into an all-encompassing database, allowing them to undertake nearly perfect, retrospective surveillance of countless persons and places.” This is the sort of untargeted “general warrant” the framers of the Fourth Amendment wanted to prevent. As we write in the brief, “Searching all people in an area without probable cause to believe they were all involved in the criminal activity under investigation reproduces the evils of general warrants and is not constitutionally permitted.” It’s this rule of law that prevents police from searching the houses of a hundred, or even a thousand people in the vicinity of a crime.


Second, we note that even if high courts continue to allow tower dump and geofence warrants in any cases, core Fourth Amendment law requires strict limits to protect the privacy of innocent bystanders, including limits on the scope and duration of the warrants, as well notice to affected individuals and after-the-fact deletion and minimization of irrelevant data.


Finally, we argue that the Fourth Amendment requires the court to set aside the good faith doctrine in cases like these and actually decide the constitutional issue. Too often courts pass the buck in cases involving novel surveillance techniques, leading to situations where police can continue using the technique for years or even decades without a definitive ruling.

title: U.S. Citizens to Submit Evidence to International Criminal Court Seeking Arrest Warrants Against Trump, Rubio, Other Senior U.S. Officials
content:
By

Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide (TAAG)

, November 4, 2026


Following federal court victory, a delegation will present eyewitness testimony, sworn affidavits, and documentary evidence of alleged U.S. aiding and abetting the genocide in Gaza.


On Wednesday, 11 November 2026, a delegation of U.S. taxpayers and international human rights attorneys will arrive at the International Criminal Court in The Hague. They will hand-deliver evidence to the Office of the Prosecutor and call for arrest warrants against President Donald Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and other senior U.S. officials for aiding and abetting Israel in the commission of genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity in Gaza.


The submission draws on evidence gathered for nearly a year by individuals and organizations now working with the

Taxpayer Alliance Against Genocide (TAAG)

, and follows a

recent federal court victory

 protecting TAAG’s First Amendment right to share evidence with the ICC.


The evidence includes sworn affidavits from doctors who worked in Gaza, firsthand eyewitness accounts, whistleblower testimony, videos, and extensive documentation concerning U.S. political, military, diplomatic, and financial support for Israel.

Press conference with taxpayers and international human rights attorneys concerning the submission of evidence to the ICC and calls for criminal accountability for senior U.S. officials.

TAAG brings together U.S. taxpayers who are seeking the accountability of U.S. officials for allegedly aiding and abetting the genocide in Gaza. TAAG maintains that U.S. political, financial, diplomatic and military support has helped enable the ongoing genocide.

title: Carcere e domiciliari per la manifestazione del 31 gennaio a Torino
content:
Questa mattina la Questura di Torino ha eseguito diverse misure cautelari inerenti il filone di indagini sulla manifestazione nazionale contro lo sgombero del centro sociale Askatasuna di Torino, del 31 gennaio 2026.


All’alba diversi compagni e compagne sono stati prelevati dalle loro abitazioni dalla Digos per eseguire le misure cautelari decise dal Giudice per le indagini preliminari.

Due compagni sono stati portati in carcere, sette agli arresti domiciliari, sei si vedono applicato il divieto di dimora a Torino con obbligo di firma quotidiana e un ulteriore obbligo di firma quotidiana.


Tutto questo avviene dopo che, una decina di giorni fa, la prima fase dell’operazione giudiziaria aveva convocato una ventina di persone davanti al Giudice per gli interrogatori di “garanzia”.


Compagni e compagne da diverse città del paese sono stati colpiti da questa inchiesta con accuse talvolta anche molto gravi come il

“tentato omicidio”

, nell’intento di criminalizzare poche persone per un corteo di più di 50 mila persone che erano scese in piazza per protestare contro la stretta repressiva del governo Meloni e la “punizione” che questo aveva voluto infliggere alla città di Torino, colpendo uno dei simboli delle lotte cittadine.

Il Gip avvalla quasi in toto le richieste della Procura torinese disponendo misure che colpiscono in maniera pesante le persone inquisite.

 Le accuse spaziano dalla resistenza a pubblico ufficiale e danneggiamento fino al tentato omicidio e la rapina. I reati smisurati che vengono contestati sono l’immagine plastica di come la le istituzioni vogliano trasformare il dissenso e il conflitto sociale in un problema di ordine pubblico. Viene sposata una lettura della manifestazione che non tiene conto della spontaneità della rabbia di quella giornata e cerca di rinchiuderla tutta all’interno del solito teorema di “un’oscura premeditazione” , arrivando a disporre i domiciliari anche per chi è accusato solo di essere stato presente vicino o sopra il furgone del corteo.


Le lotte che hanno seguito lo sgombero di Askatasuna si sono inserite in un contesto più ampio di opposizione al governo e di rifiuto del genocidio contro il popolo palestinese, di cui è tutt’ora complice. In questi mesi assistiamo ad una grande sollevazione sociale contro il carovita di guerra e i suoi responsabili, gli arresti di oggi rientrano nella strategia del manganello adottata dal Governo per punire chi protesta.

 Oggi però non sarà solo il primo passo concreto di una ingiusta e criminale operazione repressiva, ma l’inizio di un’iniziativa di solidarietà che dovrà saper sostenere chi è stato colpito nelle spese legali che dovrà affrontare e per non lasciarli soli.

Il 31 gennaio c’eravamo tutti e tutte! Que viva Askatasuna!


Network Antagonista Torinese

author: Trojka
title: Ten pociąg już odjechał. Lewica w konflikcie o TK. (komentarz)
content:
Kolejne starcie w walce o polityczną kontrolę nad Trybunałem Konstytucyjnym wprawia w wyraźne zakłopotanie lewicowy komentariat.


Od piątkowego wieczora, gdy pod ochroną policji delegaci obecnej władzy opanowali budynek TK lewicowe blogi zdominował przekaż “nie moje małpy, nie mój cyrk”, tezy o zastępczym konflikcie wywołanym przez cichy sojusz władzy i prawicowej opozycji, ubolewanie, że społeczne emocje nie skupiają się na “prawdziwych problemach.”


Jest zrozumiałe, że problem bezprawnych działań rządu czy wykorzystania zinstytucjonalizowanej przemocy by zmienić skład instytucji, powołanej do kontroli poczynań władzy metodą faktów dokonanych może być niekomfortowy dla zwolenników państwowego socjalizmu, widzących w zdobyciu władzy politycznej przez lewicę drogę do realizacji ideałów wolności i sprawiedliwości. W końcu to zagrożenie oligarchizacją i samoistnym przekształceniem każdej władzy w dyktaturę są jednymi z najważniejszych argumentów w krytyce etatyzmu, nie tylko tej anarchistycznej. Milczenie lewicy w chwili, gdy zagrożenie to staje się realne nie jest dowodem jej intelektualnej wyższości, lecz własnej niemocy i braku przekonujących odpowiedzi na pytania, stawiane przez rozwój politycznej sytuacji.


Anarchizm i socjalizm to nie “prawie to samo”

. Od czasów sporu Bakunina z Marksem o konieczność powołania “państwa socjalistycznego” jako etapu budowy bez państwowego społeczeństwa anarchiści rozwijają własną krytykę hierarchicznej władzy, a kolejne, historyczne doświadczenia potwierdzają słuszność jej założeń. Z anarchistycznego punktu widzenia to, czego jesteśmy świadkami to po prostu kolejny przykład tego, jak władza ustanowiona dzięki społecznym protestom i społecznej mobilizacji w krótkim czasie zmienia się w oligarchię, zmierzającą do przejęcia wszelkich instytucji mogących ograniczać jej kompetencje i gwarantować choćby niewielki zakres kontroli jej poczynań aż do momentu, gdy jedynym ograniczeniem uprawnień rządu staje się jego własna wyobraźnia. Historycznie proces ten był udziałem wszystkich “socjalistycznych demokracji” jakie próbowano ustanowić w różnych okresach i różnych punktach świata. Dziś, na naszych oczach, dotyka zaś demokracji liberalnych – udowadniając że zasada rządów prawa, demokratyczny konsensus czy konstytucyjne bezpieczniki nie są w stanie powstrzymać rządu, zdeterminowanego by poszerzyć własne kompetencje poza te zapisane w prawie. Liberalne państwo i jego demokratyczne instytucje nie jest w stanie powstrzymać samego siebie przed demontażem liberalnego porządku, gdy staje on na drodze realizacji “sprawczości” władzy. Może to zrobić tylko społeczeństwo, o ile jest zorganizowane, świadome swoich interesów i zdeterminowane do działania.


To fakt, że realistyczny zakres politycznych wyborów sprowadza się dziś do wyboru między dżumą a cholerą. Bez względu na to, czy w obecnym konflikcie zwycięży “uśmiechnięta dyktatura” czy “nowy faszyzm” – nie przybliży to w żaden sposób realizacji anarchistycznych ideałów. Wciąż jednak w naszym interesie jest, by ktokolwiek wygra, nie był dość silny by rządzić bez stałego zabiegania o społeczne poparcie. By w sporze z władzą, ktokolwiek będzie ją sprawować, sprawczość była po stronie społeczeństwa. Nawet pozorowane, sprokurowane na potrzeby politycznego spektaklu konfrontacje są realne o tyle, o ile generują realne społeczne napięcia i definiują nowe linie społecznych podziałów. Stać z boku i krytykować je z wyżyn własnej, intelektualnej refleksji to przegrać walkę o społeczeństwo na starcie – to jak stać na peronie i czekać aż nadjedzie wagon z napisem “uprawniony, socjalny konflikt społeczny” w czasie, gdy pociąg społecznych emocji znika już za horyzontem.

content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Προβληματισμοί για τη χάραξη της γραμμής 4 στα Εξάρχεια & γιατί πρέπει να ανοίξει η πλατεία Εξαρχείων


Η εκδήλωση θα μεταδοθεί από το OmniaTV

:


YouTube


PeerTube


Facebook


Η γραμμή 4 του μετρό, το μεγαλύτερο δημόσιο έργο της χώρας, έχει εκτροχιαστεί. Οι σοβαρές ζημιές στα κτίρια της Κυψέλης,  η απόρριψη της μελέτης για τον σταθμό Ριζάρη από το ΣτΕ, οι δικαστικές διαμάχες σε Γουδί, Αλεξάνδρας και Εξάρχεια αποκαλύπτουν ότι ο τρόπος σχεδιασμού του δεν έγινε προς το συμφέρον των ανθρώπων της πόλης, αλλά με γνώμονα τα υπερκέρδη των μεγαλοεργολάβων, θυσιάζοντας την ασφάλεια και την ποιότητα ζωής όλων μας.


Η επιλογή χάραξης της γραμμής – των σημείων που κατασκευάζεται η σήραγγα και που βγαίνουν οι σταθμοί –  οι ελλιπείς και σε κάποιες περιπτώσεις ανύπαρκτες μελέτες για το υπέδαφος, τα κτίρια, το περιβάλλον, η αδιαφορία για τα «θέλω» και τις ανάγκες των ανθρώπων των γειτονιών διαμόρφωσαν εξαρχής ένα ασφυκτικό πλαίσιο. Οι γειτονιές μας έχουν μετατραπεί σε απέραντα εργοτάξια, οι ελεύθεροι χώροι μας καταστρέφονται, τα σπίτια μας, τα σχολεία και τα δημόσια κτίρια κινδυνεύουν. Σε όλα αυτά έρχεται να προστεθεί και η εκτίναξη του κόστους του έργου, που ήδη υπολογίζεται στο μισό δισεκατομμύριο ευρώ, σε συνδυασμό με τις καθυστερήσεις παράδοσής του, αφού πια γίνεται λόγος για το 2036 και αν.


Οι γειτονιές αντιστέκονται και τα Εξάρχεια ήταν από την αρχή μπροστά. Η ανοιχτή συνέλευση «Όχι μετρό στην πλατεία Εξαρχείων» εδώ και 5 χρόνια, με έρευνα και πολλή δουλειά, έχει ξεσκεπάσει με κάθε μέσο που διαθέτει την σκανδαλώδη επιλογή κυβερνήσεων, ΕΛΛΗΝΙΚΟ ΜΕΤΡΟ και αναδόχων του έργου να χρησιμοποιήσουν τη γραμμή 4 ως μέσο αλλαγής φυσιογνωμίας της γειτονιάς μας. Η επιλογή κατασκευής του σταθμού στην πλατεία,  όπου ο σταθμός δε χωράει ακόμα και με τεχνικούς όρους, η υποβάθμιση της ζωής των κατοίκων της με την κοπή των δέντρων, τις λαμαρίνες, το κλείσιμο δρόμων κ.ο.κ., η απομόνωση και πραγματική υποβάθμιση των συνθηκών κατοικίας και δραστηριοποίησης στην περιοχή είναι πλέον εμφανείς ακόμα και στους πιο δύσπιστους. Και βέβαια η απάντηση σε όλα αυτά από την πλευρά της κυβέρνησης είναι η καταστολή.


Η πλατεία Εξαρχείων πρέπει να απελευθερωθεί! Όποιος ακόμα επιμένει ότι το έργο αυτό πρέπει ουσιαστικά συναινεί στην καταστροφή όλων αυτών που ορίζουν τι είναι η γειτονιά.


Την Πέμπτη, 5/11, παρουσιάζουμε και συζητάμε μελέτες που αποδεικνύουν την επικινδυνότητα συνέχισης του έργου με τους υπάρχοντες όρους στα Εξάρχεια, ενημερωνόμαστε και προχωράμε ένα βήμα πιο κοντά στην τελική νίκη! Κανείς πλέον δεν μπορεί να ισχυριστεί ότι δεν ήξερε. Όλοι και όλες μαζί θα σώσουμε την πλατεία Εξαρχείων, την ύπαρξή μας στη γειτονιά όπως εμείς την ορίζουμε.


Ανοιχτή Συνέλευση “Όχι μετρό στην πλατεία Εξαρχείων”


*Στην εκδήλωση θα παρουσιαστούν μεταξύ άλλων στοιχεία που αφορούν το σύνολο των κτιρίων που βρίσκονται επί της χάραξης και της ζώνης επιρροής εργασιών στην περιοχή Νεάπολης – Εξαρχείων, καθώς και η κατάσταση του υπεδάφους στην ίδια περιοχή.Επιπλέον, εκτός των ομιλητών/τριών παρεμβάσεις θα γίνουν από τη δικαστική επιμελήτρια, Ξένη Κεσίνη και τον Νίκο Κρασάκη, δομοστατικό πολιτικό μηχανικό.

author: Unknown
title: Mekke Anlaşması Meclis’te: İlk madde Genel Kurul'dan geçti
content:
Türkiye, Pakistan ve Suudi Arabistan arasında imzalanan Mekke Ortak Savunma Anlaşması'nın onaylanmasına ilişkin kanun teklifi Türkiye Büyük Millet Meclisi (TBMM) Genel Kurulu'nda görüşülüyor.


Genel Kurulda, teklifin tümü üzerinde görüşmelerin tamamlanmasının ardından maddelerinin görüşmelerine geçildi.


Teklifin ilk maddesi de gece saatlerinde kabul edildi. Bunun üzerine TBMM Başkanvekili Celal Adan, birleşime ara verdi. Diğer maddeler üzerindeki görüşmeler bugün 14.00’te devam edecek.


Ancak dün akşamki görüşmeler tartışmalı geçti. İktidar ve muhalefet partileri anlaşmanın Türkiye açısından nasıl askeri yükümlülükler doğuracağı ve ülkeyi bölgesel çatışmalara dahil edip etmeyeceği üzerinden tartıştı. 


AKP ve MHP anlaşmanın bölgesel güvenliği ve caydırıcılığı güçlendireceğini savunurken, CHP de barış ve iş birliğine katkı sağlayacağı gerekçesiyle destek vereceğini açıkladı.


YENİ Parti, DEM Parti, İYİ Parti ve Yeni Yol ise Türkiye'nin üstleneceği askeri yükümlülüklerin belirsizliğine ve bölgesel çatışmalara dahil olma riskine dikkat çekti. Askerin yurt dışında görevlendirilmesi ve olası savaş riskleri üzerinden tartışmalar yaşandı.


Genel Kurul görüşmelerinden öne çıkanlar


AKP Kayseri Milletvekili Hulusi Akar, anlaşmanın Pakistan ve Suudi Arabistan'la mevcut askeri iş birliklerini kurumsallaştırmayı amaçladığını belirterek, "Bu anlaşma hiçbir şekilde NATO'ya alternatif vesaire değil; bu tamamlayıcı bir birliktelik ve hiçbir ülkeye de karşı değil" dedi. Akar,  askerin yurt dışında görevlendirilmesinin söz konusu olması halinde bunun "mutlaka Meclisin iznine tabi" olacağını söyledi.


MHP Erzurum Milletvekili Kamil Aydın da anlaşmanın "kolektif caydırıcılığı artıracağını" savunarak MHP grubunun teklife destek vereceğini açıkladı.


CHP Grup Başkanı Faik Öztrak ise anlaşmanın yeni çatışmaların değil, bölgesel barış ve iş birliğinin aracı olması gerektiğini söyledi. Öztrak, "Bu iş birliğinden doğan güç yeni savaşlar açmak için değil savaştan caydırmak, barışı sağlamak, sınırlarımızı korumak ve ticareti geliştirmek için kullanılmalıdır" diyerek CHP'nin anlaşmaya olumlu oy vereceğini açıkladı.


İYİ Parti ise anlaşmanın sınırlarının belirsiz olduğunu savundu. Grup adına konuşan Lütfü Türkkan, "Bizim itirazımız işbirliğine değil, belirsizliğedir, ortak savunmaya değil sınırları çizilmemiş yükümlülükleredir" dedi. Türkkan, Türkiye'nin askeri ve mali yükümlülükleri ile bölgesel çatışmalara taraf olma riskine karşı güvencelerin açıklığa kavuşturulmasını istedi.


DEM Parti Antalya Milletvekili Saruhan Oluç da Türkiye'nin yeni vekalet savaşlarına dahil edilmemesi gerektiğini belirterek, "Türkiye herhangi bir vekalet savaşının parçası olmamalıdır, bunu reddediyoruz" dedi. DEM Parti Diyarbakır Milletvekili Ceylan Akça Cupolo ise partisinin "hayır" oyu vereceğini açıklayarak, "Gözümüz kapalı bir şekilde savaşa gitmeyi reddediyoruz" ifadelerini kullandı.


Yeni Yol Grubu'ndan Hasan Karal, savunma iş birliklerinin güçlendirilmesini desteklediklerini ancak askeri yükümlülüklerin ve Meclis'in denetim yetkisinin açık biçimde belirlenmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Karal, "Bu konulardaki belirsizlikler giderilmediği için kanun teklifine mevcut haliyle olumlu yaklaşamadığımızı ifade ediyorum" dedi. Aynı gruptan Selçuk Özdağ da anlaşmaya ret oyu verdiklerini açıkladı.


YENİ Parti İstanbul Milletvekili Namık Tan ise anlaşmanın Türkiye'yi sınırları belirsiz askeri operasyonlara sürükleyebileceğini savundu. "Mehmetçik'in asli görevi Suudi vatanını değil, kendi vatanımızı korumaktır" diyen Tan, anlaşmaya karşı olduklarını söyledi.


TBMM Dışişleri Komisyonu Başkanı Fuat Oktay ise eleştirilere yanıt verirken anlaşmanın otomatik olarak asker gönderilmesi anlamına gelmediğini savundu. "Anlaşma onaylandığı takdirde, Suud çöllerine Türk askerini, Mehmetçik'i gönderiyoruz... Böyle bir uygulama da söz konusu değil, böyle bir şey de yok" diyen Oktay, olası adımların tarafların değerlendirmesi ve oydaşmasıyla belirleneceğini söyledi. Oktay'a göre destek; istihbarat ve tecrübe paylaşımından ekipman desteğine veya askeri karşılığa kadar farklı biçimler alabilecek.


Oktay ayrıca, anlaşmanın ilk 10 yılında çekilmeye getirilen sınırlamayı savunarak bunun uzun vadeli stratejik anlaşmaların doğasından kaynaklandığını söyledi. "10 yıl süre içerisinde de herhangi bir konuda oydaşma sağlanamazsa [...] Türkiye'nin arzu etmediği bir konunun uygulamaya alınması asla ve asla mümkün değildir" dedi.


Suudi güvenliği için üçlü askerî ittifak: Mekke Anlaşması …

title: PENa Kurd dê li Amedê konferanseke li dar bixe
content:
PENa Kurd dê li Amedê bi navê, “Di pêvajoyên lihevrûniştin, lihevkirin, aştî û wekheviyê de rola wêje, ziman û rewşenbîriyê” Konferansa Wêje û Aştiyê li dar dixe.


PENa Kurd di 6ê Mijdarê de bi tevlibûna gelek rewşenbîr, nivîskar, helbestvan û siyasetmedaran li Amedê Konferansa Wêje û Aştiyê li dar dixe. Di konferasê de dê li ser gelek mijaran gotûbêj were kirin û konferans wê 2 rojan berdewam bike.


Bername


Roja yekemîn a konferansê bi mijara, “Ziman, Wêje û Mafên Gerdûnî di Pêvajoyên Aştiyê de” dest pê dike û axêver jî wiha ne:


Moderator Dîba Keskîn (Nivîskar), Burhan Sonmez (Serokê Giştî yê PENa Navneteweyî-London), Dr. Bêrîvan Doskî (Seroka Rûmetê ya Navenda PENa Kurd-Silêmanî), Weysî Aktaş (Siyasetmedar-Amed), German Rojas (Serokê Komîteya Nivîskarên ji bo Aştiyê ya PENa Navneteweyî –Santiago/Çîlî)


Beşa 2emîn a konferansê bi mijara, ‘Rola Qada Navneteweyî, Siberoja Wekheviyê û Mafên Mirovan’ û beşdariya; Moderator: Zana Farqînî (Zimannas), Carles Torner (Cîgirê Serokê PENa Navneteweyî – Katalanya), Tanja Tuma (Alîkara Serokê PENa Navneteweyî -Slovenya), Mueyed Teyîb ( Helbestvan- Hewlêr), Şadiye Manap (Nivîskar – Amed) berdewam bike.


Beşa 3emîn a konferansê bi mijara, “Rabûna Bandora Şer û Ragêşiyê ya Li Ser Ziman û Azadiya Xwederbirînê” û bi tevlibûna; Moderator: Mîna Acer (Nivîskar), Urtzî Urrutîkoetxea (Serokê Komîteya Mafê Ziman û Wergerê ya PENa Navneteweyî yê Berê – Bask), Dr. Dilawer Zeraq (Akademîsyen-Nivîskar – Amed), Fîlîz Yildirim (Akademîsyen li Cambridgeê) bi dawî bibe.


Daxuyanî


Di roja duyemîn a Konferansa Wêje û Dîrokê de beşdarvanên konferansê dê li cihên dîrokî yên Amedê bigerin û serdana Komeleya Wêjekarên Kurd, Yekîtiya Weşangerên Kurd (YEW-KURD) Enstîtuya Kurdî ya Amedê, MED-DERê, Komeleya Rojnamegeran a Dîcle Firatê (DFG) û Komeleya Rojnamegeran Jin a Mezopotamyayê (MKG) bikin.


Konferans dê bi daxuyaniya hevpar a li ser navê beşdaran, bi banga ji bo aştiyeke birûmet, wekheviya zimanê Kurdî, azadkirina zindaniyên siyasî, rojnamegeran û pêşxistina çanda demokrasiyê bi dawî bibe.

author: Paul Tiyambe Zeleza
title: The End of the Trump Era: The Democratic Sweep of the Midterm Elections
content:
Early this morning, I was woken up by a text from my daughter in Atlanta, nine hours behind Sharjah, UAE, where I’m currently located. Dems are leading, she exclaimed. Can you chat for a quick second? Before I called her, she sent another text, saying, it’s breaking news: Keisha Lance Bottoms is the projected winner as Governor of Georgia. My daughter, who has lived in Atlanta since she went to university there in the early 2000s, was ecstatic beyond measure.


Our celebratory chatter woke up my wife, a political scientist and keen observer of American politics. The ancestors must be smiling, she proclaimed with giddy excitement. We switched on the television and followed the elections on American stations we had access to, including CNN International and Bloomberg, while simultaneously perusing newspapers including The New York Times and The Guardian.


The more we talked and thought about the unfolding election results, I couldn’t help and filtering the elections through Africanist and global lenses, the clearer it became that this stunning blue wave, which polls had been predicting, represented political triumph in five dimensions, what I would the 5Ds: democrats, democracy, diversity, demography, and development.


The Democratic Victory


The Democrats won a resounding victory. Their victories swept the electoral map in Congress and across red states, as they held on to their constituencies. It was a political tsunami that routed President Donald Trump and the Republicans in a stunning rebuke of their failed policies and divisive politics, in which diversionary and inflammatory cultural wars trumped the deteriorating material conditions and interests of the electorate.


Democrats seized both chambers of Congress. Their candidates flipped seven Republican seats in Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina, and Texas, red states some of which had not elected a Democrat in decades. They retained seats in five states, namely, Georgia, Michigan, Minnesota, New Hampshire, and Virginia.


At the time of writing, the Democrats had flipped 35 seats previously held by Republicans in the House, including multiple seats in states won by Trump by more than 10 points such as Texas, Iowa, Florida, and Pennsylvania, along with key wins in Kentucky, Missouri, Nebraska, Ohio, and Utah. They successfully defended all or nearly all of their incumbent districts , including 22 that were considered vulnerable because Trump carried them by more than 10 points in the 2024 election, and are projected to win 242 to 258 seats when all the votes are counted, 40 more than they need to form a majority.


In a tectonic shift, at the time of writing, with 32 of the 36 seats contested, Democrats had also flipped five state governorships from Republicans in Texas, Georgia, Ohio, Iowa, and Nevada, and successfully defended 15 states. They won a total of 29, earning a majority of governorships for the first time since 2010.


So far, with final calls still processing, Democrats have flipped 12 of the 88 state legislative chambers on the ballot from Republican control in Pennsylvania (Senate; they already controlled the House), Wisconsin (both chambers), Arizona (putting Republicans in a legislative minority for the first time in 26 years), North Carolina (House), and drastically broke Republican supermajorities in states like Florida, South Carolina, and Indiana. They successfully defended 25 legislative chambers, including competitive ones in states like Maine, New Mexico, Oregon, and Washington, where they were able to preserve existing Democratic trifectas.


Similarly, Democrats dramatically outperformed Republicans in races for attorney general and secretary of state offices. For the former, the biggest upsets were in Texas and Georgia, while key defensive holds included Nevada and Michigan. Democrats also won the majority of contested secretary of state offices, seizing several from Republicans and holding those they held before.


The Resurgence of Democracy


America’s beleaguered democracy won. Electoral democracy in the United States has always been compromised by gerrymandering, voter suppression, politicization of the judiciary, and the financialization of politics. funding. This is why a conservative outfit like The Economist considers the United States a flawed, rather than a full, democracy compared to its increasingly alienated Western allies such as Canada.


Gerrymandering spectacularly backfired for Republicans …

author: Anele Mbi
title: Polls close and the counting of votes has begun
content:
The Western Cape electoral officer, Michael Hendrickse told reporters that there were more people who voted in this year’s local government elections compared the previous poll in 2021. By 18h00, over 1.5 million people had voted. “Its clear that the number of voters is going upwards and will surpass the number of voters in the local government elections in 2021. But, there were fewer registered people in 2021 compared to this year. So, I’m not comparing the turnout as a proportion but looking at the numbers of people who voted,” he said.


Hendrickse said that there were still people waiting to vote at around 21h45 as they were in the queue by 21h00.


In Cape Town


Elitsha


reported earlier

 that voters in Khayelitsha and Mitchells Plain said that youth unemployment and lack of basic services are some of the issues that the next council should prioritise. Zine Malusi from ward 89 in Khayelitsha pleaded with political parties to work together to improve the lives of the poor even if they end up in coalition governments.


Her views were echoed by Fiona Jacobs from Portlands who said there was a need for the media to play an educational role in the elections to make sure that voters are clear who to vote for.


In Johannesburg


In Alexandra, unemployment and poor municipal services featured prominently in the concerns of young voters.


Bonang Makola, a first-time voter, said unemployment and the deteriorating state of Johannesburg influenced her decision at the ballot box. She had followed interviews in which political parties outlined their plans to reduce unemployment over the next five years, and their proposals helped shape her choice.


“As a young person, unemployment is one of the biggest issues. Some parties said they would reduce it by 0%, while others said they would reduce it by 2% every year. That influenced my decision on which party to vote for,” she said.


Makola said residents in her community continue to experience electricity problems, water interruptions and poor refuse collection. The accumulation of rubbish in Alexandra, she added, had become a serious health concern.


Thato Couch, a resident of Tsutsumani in Alexandra and a first-time voter, believes that the growing dissatisfaction with political parties has contributed to voter apathy. She said some residents no longer saw the point of voting because they felt that elections had brought little improvement to their circumstances. “People choose not to vote because they think it’s useless. There’s no change, no progress and nothing is actually moving. We just keep voting for the same thing,” she said.


Municipal workers fixing a blocked drain outside ward 89 voting station in Khayelitsha

.


Meanwhile, Rene, a Sandton resident, said Johannesburg’s deteriorating infrastructure requires urgent intervention, regardless of whether the next administration was formed by a single party or a coalition. She supports coalition governments provided political parties cooperate and share a commitment to fighting corruption and improving service delivery. “Johannesburg is falling apart. There has to be a party, whether it’s a coalition or a single party, that fixes this wonderful city because it’s broken through neglect,” she said.


Rene argued that political disagreements and leadership disputes should never take precedence over residents’ basic needs. “We’re the people. We pay our taxes and rates, yet our streets are full of potholes, we have no water, no electricity and the garbage isn’t being collected,” she said.


She also highlighted the dangers posed by poorly maintained roads, particularly for elderly motorists navigating streets without adequate lighting and road markings.


Across the interviews, voters expressed different perspectives on political parties and coalition government but shared a common expectation: those elected must demonstrate accountability and deliver tangible improvements. For Johannesburg residents, the real test of the elections will not simply be who wins political power, but whether that power translates into jobs, functioning infrastructure and reliable basic services.


In KuGompo City


Mdantsane residents, in Buffalo City Metropolitan Municipality, said that youth unemployment and service delivery should be one of the key things that the next council should focus on.

author: Fikayo Akeredolu
title: Nigeria's petrol subsidy was also an electricity policy
content:
As long as households and businesses in Nigeria depend on generators and cannot rely on the grid for electricity, some form of fossil fuel subsidy will always be necessary. Despite the costs, and despite what the World Bank, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), and the climate research community say. This is because fossil fuel subsidies, in my opinion, are the country’s largest and most decentralized electricity access program, and any attempt at reform without explicitly accounting for this will fail. This essay explains why.

As a starting point, I need everyone to read Dr. Neil McCulloch’s book

Ending Fossil Fuel Subsidies

. The book explains how subsidies are effectively a political prosthetic. Imagine you run a developing country with weak administrative capacity. You cannot reliably deliver schools or clinics, but you need to give citizens something that shows you are on their side and ensures you stay in power. Cheap energy through fossil fuel subsidies is the one thing you can deliver somewhat easily. Weak states, like Nigeria, lean on subsidies because a subsidy is a substitute for the public goods the state cannot otherwise provide.

Citing a Nigerian study, he shows that the subsidy mostly benefits the rich — the bottom 40 percent of households consumed only 3 percent of petrol, while the richest fifth captured around 27 times more benefit than the poorest fifth. By 2018, Nigeria was spending roughly $300 million a month on the petrol subsidy, more than its entire budget for basic education. Considering all of this, anyone can see that the subsidy is a bad political and economic deal.

Beyond the numbers, there is the climate change literature. McCulloch notes that fossil fuel subsidies are sometimes a key blockage to the wider development of renewable energy. Cheap petrol and diesel weaken the incentive to switch to cleaner alternatives. The reformist logic follows rationally — remove the subsidy, allow prices to reflect the true cost of fuel, and households and businesses should begin moving toward cleaner energy. And this logic from the literature is intuitive. But it makes assumptions that anyone who truly understands Nigeria will tell you just do not apply.

It assumes grid electricity already exists and the question is simply how it should be generated. But for many Nigerians, electricity means a petrol generator. Remove the subsidy and the choice is not necessarily dirty electricity versus clean electricity; it is instead between some electricity versus none.

The reformist logic also assumes a certain level of demand elasticity. The assumption here is that people can meaningfully reduce their demand when prices rise. But if petrol is running the generator that powers your home or business, there is only so much consumption you can cut before you have a bigger problem. It also assumes a substitute is readily available. A higher petrol price only pushes someone toward solar and electric vehicles if solar and electric vehicles are actually affordable, available, and accessible. It assumes subsidy removal mainly hurts a powerful fossil fuel industry. In Nigeria, it also hurts households and small businesses that rely on petrol generators because the grid does not work. And probably most importantly, it assumes a state government capable of capturing the savings from subsidy removal and redirecting them transparently, efficiently, and effectively into the transition.

If the assumptions do not hold, how exactly is the price signal of subsidy removal supposed to work? Post subsidy removal, what was the immediate short-term plan for providing electricity? If you make petrol for running generators more expensive, yes, the price signal should move people to cleaner sources, but are the cleaner sources within a price range that allows everyone to make the switch?

As someone who has lived in Nigeria, sat through more blackouts than I care to number and then gone on to do a PhD on this topic, I think that there was a key part of this debate that analysts, international financial institutions, and policymakers did not seem to fully reckon with. And it is this — on a not insignificant note, Nigeria’s subsidy was about generating electricity just about as much as it was a fiscal matter. Effectively, Nigeria’s petrol subsidy was a key part of its electricity policy.

And recommending and enacting its removal without explicitly accounting for this made the average Nigerian’s life worse. I say the average …

title: A Russian state firm will map more than half of Mali. Who will own the data?
content:
Two contracts signed in Moscow give a Russian state firm the job of mapping Mali’s subsoil and building the system that will hold the data. The accounts published so far do not say who will own it.


On 28 October, at the Russia–Africa summit in Moscow, Mali’s Mines Minister, Amadou Keïta, signed 

two contracts

 with Zarubezhgeologia, the foreign-projects arm of the state-owned geological holding Rosgeologia, also known as Rosgeo. The first commissioned geological maps at a scale of 

1:200,000

 of two areas that together cover more than half of Mali, over 24 months. The second, scheduled for eight months, purchased a national geological information system called “Subsoil Management”.


The mapping includes training for staff of Mali’s National Directorate of Geology and Mines. Reuters, relaying the company’s statement, says the information system is meant to let Mali manage geological data, mineral licensing and regulatory oversight. Other reports describe only spatial storage with tools to visualise and analyse the data.


Bamako’s partnership with Moscow has mostly been read through security, from the arrival of Wagner in 

late 2021

 to the Africa Corps, which has operated under Russia’s Defence Ministry since last year. These contracts reach somewhere else: the records of the Ministry of Mines.


A database beside the cadastre


On 17 April, President Assimi Goïta presented a 

new cadastre

, fully digital and designed by Malian experts, already listing 631 titles and linked to the financial platforms of the Ministry of Mines, the Treasury and the tax directorate. Keïta 

said

 the system answered the head of state’s wish that the sector be reclaimed by the Malian state.


ITIE Mali’s 

description

 of the cadastre platform, SICAM, says users can apply for titles, follow the processing of their files, pay fees and consult data that includes geological maps. A system designed by a Russian firm will therefore enter an administration that already handles titles and maps digitally.


Titles are moving again, slowly. After a freeze on permit procedures that began in late 2022, the Council of Ministers authorised 

24 renewals

 for gold and lithium between 21 August and 30 September, the Mines Minister said on 22 October. Applications for new titles were 

still suspended

 in mid-October. The licensing and oversight functions that Reuters reports for the new system raise a further question: how will a system designed by a Russian firm interact with the existing cadastre, and who will administer the information it holds?


So far, the published accounts leave out the price, the exact boundaries of the two survey areas and any provision on who owns the data once the work is done.


Three questions are easily run together: who owns the maps and the data, who may use the data and on what terms, and who controls the software, its updates and its day-to-day operation. The announced training covers satellite-image interpretation, which builds skill in reading the data, not control of the system. A state can own data it cannot maintain without its contractor, or hold broad rights over a database it does not own.


Mali is building institutions of its own for this. On 30 September, four weeks before the Moscow signing, the Council of Ministers approved draft texts creating a 

new agency

 to research, produce, secure and disseminate geological knowledge. It would replace a programme set up in 1990. The 

mining code

 already limits what the administration may release: information gathered from title holders stays confidential for the life of the title plus a year, and may not go to third parties for three years without the author’s consent (Articles 121 and 122). That covers company data, not a survey the state commissions, so the new contracts’ terms remain open.


A 1:200,000 map will not tell anyone what a deposit is worth. It shows where to look. New applications are still on hold. When they reopen, 

Article 29

 of the mining code gives an exploration authorisation to the first applicant who qualifies, though state-owned companies have priority. Whoever knows where to look can get there first. A ministry holding the same data can also weigh applications against more than the applicant’s own word.


Mapping first, exploration later

author: ROAPE
title: Africa on the map, but still off the table
content:
On 4 September 2026, the United Nations General Assembly adopted a non-binding resolution that might initially appear to belong to the relatively technical world of cartography. The resolution, “Correct the Map: Rebalancing Global Cartographic Representation and Promoting Equitable Representation of the World’s Regions, Particularly Africa,” was introduced by Togo on behalf of the African Group and adopted by 164 countries, with one country voting against and six abstaining.


In presenting the resolution, Togo’s Foreign Minister Robert Dussey argued that maps are not merely technical tools: their repeated use in schools, the media and digital platforms shapes how people understand and visualise the world. The African Group argued that the Mercator projection, designed for specific purposes—especially maritime navigation—had become a general-purpose image of the world that visually minimises Africa and other regions near the Equator.


The delegation framed the initiative around scientific and educational accuracy, cognitive justice, historical memory and the equal dignity of peoples. It also stressed what the resolution would not do: condemn the Mercator projection, impose a single map for every use, alter borders or take a position on territorial claims. Instead, it encouraged the use of projections such as Equal Earth when comparing the relative areas of continents, alongside better teaching about the strengths and limitations of different projections.


The resolution encourages the use of equal-area map projections, including Equal Earth, particularly when the relative size of regions matters. It also highlights the implications of existing representations for geographical and cartographic literacy. Importantly, however, it does not replace the Mercator projection, redraw international borders or alter the legal status of any territory. So why does a map matter? And why now?


These questions are more significant than the technical debate over which projection should be used. The UN resolution opens a much larger question about who has historically possessed the authority to represent the world, whose knowledge becomes universal knowledge, and what happens when previously marginalised actors begin to challenge that authority.


Mercator Map versus Equal Earth (wikicommons)


The map is not the territory—but it shapes how the territory is imagined


Gerardus Mercator’s famous projection was first published in 1569. It was developed primarily as a tool for maritime navigation, as its preservation of angles and constant compass bearings made it particularly useful for sailors plotting routes across oceans. The projection was never intended to provide an accurate comparison of the relative size of continents. Its distortion, however, has had a long afterlife.


Because the Mercator projection increasingly enlarges landmasses as they move away from the Equator, Greenland can appear comparable in size to Africa, despite Africa being approximately fourteen times larger.There is therefore an important distinction to make. Mercator was not invented as a deliberate attempt to make Africa smaller. Its original purpose was navigational. The political question emerges from what happened afterwards: how a projection designed for a particular technical purpose became normalised as a general image of the world.


A cartographic choice made for navigation became, through repetition, an educational and cultural convention. Maps entered classrooms, atlases, newspapers, television graphics, websites and digital platforms. In doing so, they did more than provide geographical information. They participated in producing a particular visual imagination of the world. This is where cartography becomes political. Can a two-dimensional map ever be neutral?


From geographical distortion to cognitive hierarchy


The significance of the new

UN resolution

 therefore lies less in replacing one map with another than in recognising that representation itself has consequences. The resolution’s language is striking. It connects cartographic representation to education, perception and collective understanding, framing the correction of historical distortions as a matter of equitable representation. The UN Office of the Special Adviser on Africa has presented the initiative as an African-led effort to challenge the symbolic minimisation of the continent. But the tension remains.


If representation contributes to how societies imagine the world …

author: Abahlali_3
title: We mourn the loss of Des D’sa
content:
30 October 2026 Abahlali baseMjondolo press statement

We mourn the loss of Des D’Sa, father, uncle, grandfather, and a comrade to many

The death of Desmond D’Sa has plunged many people on the left in Durban and beyond, across numerous organisations, into shock and despair. Siyakhala ngo Des.

Comrade Des was a stalwart in the struggle against apartheid and was a well-known organiser who formed the South Durban Community Environmental Alliance (SDCEA), an environmental organisation that raised the concerns of families living in the oil- and gas-affected areas of Wentworth and the Bluff.

His activism and the fight against injustices did not end with environmental issues and it definitely did not end in Wentworth and the Bluff. Comrade Des fought against all forms of oppression and injustice, including gangsterism and the mining companies in rural areas, and supported everyone from fisherfolk to migrants and poor people, whether living in flats, hostels or shacks. He did not back down when struggle became dangerous. Comrade Des spoke fluent isiZulu and engaged everyone with the same respect.

He joined the first march against ANC councillor Yacoob Baig organised from Kennedy Road in 2005, which became part of the process towards the formation of our movement. He stood with our movement from the beginning, and was one of the few who never wavered in his support even when we were under severe attack and isolated.

Comrade Des was one of the founders of the Right to Know Campaign that fought fought against secrecy while promoting the right to information. He was also one of the founders of The Durban Coalition, which was first formed in response to the devastating floods of 2022. The Coalition, which unites community organisations across the city in a united front, is thriving today and is an important formation in the city.

We will miss Comrade Des so much. He was always on the side of the people. He was always so warm and kind. We always laughed when he was around.

We wish to thank his family for him. And wish to express our heartfelt condolences to his family, friends and comrades.

It is so sad and devastating that you have left us. Till we meet again.

Hamba kahle Comrade Des D’Sa. Ubuyiqhawe.

author: WoMin
title: From Mombasa to Yaoundé, the vision and the demand is for reparative justice
content:
Through WoMin’s work alongside African women organising against extractivism, against the drivers of the climate crisis and its impacts, the destruction of the commons through false solutions, unjust energy transitions (and generally a world order that serves a minority over the global majority), we have been asking: what is the full range of impacts and costs in the face of environmental and climate impacts? Who and whose work absorbs these impacts and costs? And what would repair mean from the perspective of women, their communities and the ecosystems they care for and are cared for at the frontline of the climate crisis, where centuries of continued systems of accumulation by dispossession and destruction meet?


Our experience shows us that reparations cannot simply be another form of compensation. They must confront the very systems producing the harm – extractivism, odious and illegitimate debt, colonial legacies, patriarchy, racism, and corporate power promoting more false solutions whose aim is not climate justice but profit. Reparations must indeed offer us all a real chance to build Pan African feminist futures that centre care, including the restoration of the commons, and the conditions that make life possible.


Connecting the “c-words” – colonialism to climate reparations


The recent

African Symposium on Climate Reparations

 in Mombasa, Kenya, started on that same note: “there is no “c-word” that we cannot bring into conversations on climate reparations”, argued a comrade in his opening remarks. And indeed, the current

climate disorder

1

 is a historical process, and Colonialism (the c-word that in other climate justice spaces some shy away from) is part and parcel of it. As is, we argue at WoMin, capitalism. What is more, not only do climate reparations need to address colonialism and neocolonialism, but also the solution to the climate crisis will not be found within capitalism. Or as Audre Lorde put it, “… the master’s tools will never dismantle the master’s house. They may allow us temporarily to beat him at his own game, but they will never enable us to bring about genuine change.”


Not only we need our own tools, but also a broad alliance, as broad, yet united in principles and analysis, as broad and urgent is the task ahead. And the symposium offered an important space to bring together many working for reparations across the continent and in the diaspora, in conversations navigated along four main tracks: rights of nature and ecosystems stewardship; finance, debt and tax justice; law and human rights; and lived realities from frontline communities.


And the timing matters. We are entering the Decade of Justice and Reparations for Africans and People of African Descent, while the debt crisis in Africa continues to exponentially grow and deepen climate vulnerability, false climate solutions continue to expand, further threatening the commons millions of Africans depend upon for their everyday subsistence, and the African Court considers an Advisory Opinion on States’ obligations in the climate crisis.


As powerful expressed in an

open letter

 which emerged from the symposium, a Pan African position and action plan for climate reparations is urgent, but it cannot be constructed only through states, legal and financial tools. Those at the frontlines absorbing the costs of extractivism, ecological destruction and climate disruption have to shape what counts as harm, what constitutes repair, and what must stop. And importantly, we need to organise at all levels the collective power to make repair possible.


African women united for climate justice and reparations


This was the task of the 4th

Women’s Climate Assembly

 (WCA) in Yaoundé, Cameroon, held in early October under the theme, “Our lands, our voices: African women united for climate justice and reparations!”. The Assembly convened over 75 women community leaders, activists, feminist organisations, civil society groups and allies from twelve countries including Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Guinea-Conakry, Liberia, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal, and Zambia.


Oh ancestors, watch over Africa and let everything return to Africa! If we are coveted today, if there are wars, it is because our ancestors bequeathed this land to us. They did not abuse its riches. author: Mada Masr
title: Lina Attalah in custody after court issues LE3 mn fine, orders Mada Masr’s closure
content:
Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah was fined LE3 million by the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, which convicted her on charges of managing an unlicensed website, issuing an order for the website’s closure. Attalah was taken into custody after the issue of the ruling.


Tuesday’s session at the ninth circuit of the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court, presided over by judge Mohamed Mubarak, was temporarily suspended for deliberations after Attalah’s defense counsel requested time to review the case file.


After the court returned from deliberations, the judge ordered the courtroom cleared of everyone except Attalah and her defense counsel, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights’ executive director Hossam Bahgat, who was also present, told Mada Masr. The room then filled with plainclothes officers and guards, with a National Security Agency officer in attendance, he added.


The presiding judge and a Supreme State Security Prosecution representative returned to the session and the judge announced that the court has decided to stand by its rejection of all the procedural arguments presented by the defense, including requests to bring in any documentation or hear any witnesses.


The judge then asked the defense team to present its plea. The counsel insisted that it would not submit a plea as long as its requests were unanswered by the court.


The judge then abruptly asked for a lawyer unknown to any member of the defense counsel to be brought in, “in a move that astonished all those present,” said Bahgat, and announced that the court decided to appoint a lawyer for Attalah.


At that point, all members of the defense counsel cried out to reject the court’s appointment of a lawyer when the eight chosen lawyers were present. Attalah herself spoke to say she did not accept the court-appointed lawyer acting on her behalf, an objection the judge refused to have recorded in the session’s minutes.


“In an even more shocking move,” said Bahgat, the judge himself began to log down the requests of the court-appointed lawyer, without the lawyer having said a word. The judge then read out the conviction amid shouts and protests from the defense counsel.


The judge sentenced Attalah to the maximum possible penalty: a LE3 million fine, the closure of Mada Masr’s website and the confiscation of its property.


Security personnel then surrounded Attalah, lifted her off the ground and took her out of the courtroom, where she remains in custody in the courthouse.

author: AfricanFeminism
title: Morocco’s First Woman Prime Minister and the Terms of Freedom
content:
Something changes when a woman occupies an office men have treated as their natural inheritance. Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri’s

appointment

 on 29 September 2026 makes that change visible in Morocco. For women whose competence is routinely scrutinised, the pleasure is neither naïve nor trivial.


But the woman forming a government and the woman labouring in the fields, raising children without pay and denied an equal share of her inheritance encounter power differently. Representation changes who governs; emancipation changes what all women have the power to do. That distinction shifts our attention from PM Mansouri’s gender to the politics of the centre-right

 Party of Authenticity and Modernity (PAM

)

, which she leads. Will its programme redistribute the resources and rights on which women’s freedom depends?


The history beneath the headline


Calling women’s leadership foreign to Morocco requires forgetting its history. Historian Osire Glacier

documents

 women’s authority long before the contemporary premiership. Kenza al Awrabiya, the Amazigh mother of Idris II, helped secure the Idrisid dynasty, founded in the late eighth century in what is now Morocco. Zaynab al Nafzawiyya influenced eleventh-century Almoravid politics around Aghmat, near Marrakech. Sayyida al Hurra governed Tétouan, a city in northern Morocco, during the sixteenth century. Khnata bint Bakkar intervened in eighteenth-century dynastic politics.


Across the region,

Dihya

 is remembered as an Amazigh queen who led resistance to the Arab conquest in the Aurès, in present-day Algeria, during the late seventh century. Tuareg oral tradition remembers

Tin Hinan

 as a queen and founding ancestress of noble lineages in the Ahaggar, in present-day southern Algeria.


These histories expose how male authority is made to appear natural. Fatima Mernissi’s

The Forgotten Queens of Islam


challenges that selective memory. Colonialism also reorganised authority: French Protectorate administrators

reshaped

 customary courts around imperial priorities. What survives as tradition can carry the history of political intervention. 


Religious interpretation can give exclusion another claim to permanence. Islamist and other conservative opponents invoke this

hadith

 against women’s political authority:


«لَنْ يُفْلِحَ قَوْمٌ وَلَّوْا أَمْرَهُمُ امْرَأَةً»


Usually translated as saying that a people governed by a woman will not prosper, it becomes a prohibition irrespective of her competence. Asma Lamrabet, a

Moroccan Islamic feminist thinker

, questions turning a

narration linked

 to Persia’s dynastic succession into a universal ban. She reads it against the Qur’anic Queen of Sheba, whose judgement demonstrates capable leadership. Her argument contests male authority’s claim to divine necessity.


PAM’s promises and its record


Women have long contested how authority is distributed within the family. Fatima Sadiqi

documents

the Union de l’Action Féminine’s 1992 million-signature campaign to reform the Moudawana, Morocco’s family code. The 2004 reform abolished wives’ duty of obedience but retained unequal inheritance and exceptions to the marriage age of eighteen. Proposals announced in December 2024 left fundamental equality demands unresolved. In October 2025, more than sixty civil society organisations and public figures

joined to call for comprehensive reform

. Rights in Morocco have advanced through organised demands, not the gender of an officeholder.


PAM, a centre-right party founded in 2008,

advocates

 social modernisation and positions itself against the Islamist Justice and Development Party (PJD). It entered government in 2021 alongside the National Rally of Independents and conservative nationalist Istiqlal. Opposition to Islamist conservatism, however, does not itself entail reforming the laws and economic conditions that subordinate women.


PAM’s

2026 programme

 promises improved widow pensions, childcare, safe transport, a women’s enterprise fund and labour inspection. The commitments leave inheritance equality, abortion reform and decriminalisation of consensual same sex relations unaddressed. Mansouri called for

banning child marriage

 without exceptions in 2024, yet PAM’s electoral programme

omits that commitment

. Employment can support independence, but a wage does not cancel criminalisation or unequal property rights. The programme leaves those constraints intact.
