title: Συγκέντρωση ενάντια στη φασιστική επίθεση σε μαθήτρια και φοιτητές, Τετάρτη 4/11, στις 18.00, στη πλατεία Ταραμπούρας, Πάτρα
content:
Δολοφονική επίθεση εναντίον  μαθήτριας, μέλους της ΚΝΕ,

την οποία είχαν στοχοποιήσει εδώ και μέρες, και

εναντίον φοιτητών

, που βρέθηκαν στο πλευρό της για να την υπερασπιστούν, εξαπέλυσαν

 φασιστοειδή

 το βράδυ της Τρίτης στην

Πάτρα,

στην περιοχή της Νεάπολης Ζαρουχλέικων.


Συγκεκριμένα, σύμφωνα με την ανακοίνωση των οργανώσεων Αχαΐας του ΚΚΕ και της ΚΝΕ, εδώ και μερικές ημέρες, φασίστες απειλούσαν και έβριζαν

μαθήτρια του 8ου Λυκείου Πατρών

, μέλος της ΚΝΕ και της Συντονιστικής Επιτροπής Μαθητών της Πάτρας, σε μικρή πλατεία έξω από το σπίτι της, τις βραδινές ώρες.


Το βράδυ της Τρίτης και ενώ για ακόμη μία φορά επαναλαμβανόταν το ίδιο σκηνικό, μαθητές και φοιτητές στην παρέμβασή τους προς άτομα που βρισκόντουσαν κάτω από την οικία να σταματήσουν την απαράδεκτη συμπεριφορά τους, δέχθηκαν

τραμπούκικη βίαιη επίθεση από περίπου 40 φασίστες.


Το

 Εργατικό Κέντρο Πάτρας όπως και οργανώσεις και συλλογικότητες καλούν σε αντιφασιστική συγκέντρωση ενάντια στην φασιστική αυτή επίθεση, την Τετάρτη 4/11, στις 18.00, στη Πλατεία Ταραμπούρας, Πάτρα


Κάλεσμα/Αφίσες:


Εργατικό Κέντρο Πάτρας


Σε

συλλαλητήριο σήμερα Τετάρτη 4 Νοέμβρη

 στις

6 μ.μ.,

στην

 πλατεία Ταραμπούρα,

στην

 Πάτρα

, καλεί το

 Εργατικό Κέντρο Πάτρας

, καταγγέλλοντας την

απρόκλητη φασιστική επίθεση εναντίον πρωτοπόρας μαθήτριας και εναντίον φοιτητών

 στην περιοχή των Ζαρουχλέικων.


Το Εργατικό Κέντρο καλεί όλους τους φορείς της πόλης να καταδικάσουν την επίθεση των φασιστών και να συμμετάσχουν σήμερα το απόγευμα στο συλλαλητήριο.


Αναλυτικότερα, το ΕΚΠ με την ανακοίνωσή του «καταγγέλλει την απρόκλητη επίθεση που είχε στόχο νεολαία πρωτοπόρα μαθήτρια στην περιοχή των Ζαρουχλέικων από θρασύδειλους φασίστες-ναζί μαζί με άλλους εγκληματίες. Έστησαν καρτέρι κάτω από το σπίτι της και επιτέθηκαν με μαχαίρια και σιδερογροθιές σε φίλους και πρωτοπόρους νεολαίους που βρέθηκαν εκεί για να την υπερασπιστούν».


Με τον τρόπο αυτό, τονίζει το ΕΚΠ, «προσπαθούν να τρομοκρατήσουν τη νεολαία και τον λαό, αλλά και όποιον αντιστέκεται στην αντεργατική, αντιλαϊκή πολιτική της κυβέρνησης και των άλλων συστημικών κομμάτων».


Συνεχίζοντας αναφέρει:


«Δεν θα τους περάσει! Δεν τρομοκρατούμαστε!

 Οι φασίστες που βγήκαν από τις τρύπες τους για να χύσουν το φασιστικό τους δηλητήριο θα απομονωθούν και θα πάρουν την απάντησή τους από το οργανωμένο εργατικό και λαϊκό κίνημα. Η λαϊκή δυσαρέσκεια που γεννάται από τα ίδια τα προβλήματα που αντιμετωπίζει η εργατική – λαϊκή οικογένεια είναι φόβος και τρόμος για το σύστημα του κέρδους και των φασιστών που το υπηρετούν, ακριβώς γιατί είναι αυτή που μπορεί να μετατραπεί σε οργανωμένη απόφαση για ανατροπή αυτού του βάρβαρου συστήματος.


Οι δήθεν πατριώτες ναζί που πατρίδα τους είναι το κεφάλαιο

 και ορκίζονται μόνο σε αυτό και τα συμφέροντά του, θέλουν την εργατική τάξη και τη νέα γενιά να μένει αδιαμαρτύρητα στοιχισμένη πίσω από τους ματωμένους “εθνικούς στόχους” των επιχειρηματικών ομίλων, της πολεμικής εμπλοκής και των αμύθητων κερδών. 

Έχουν ορκιστεί να τσακίζουν κάθε προσπάθεια διεκδίκησης των σύγχρονων αναγκών μας! Γι’ αυτό επιτίθενται στους πρωτοπόρους!


Θα ξαναμπούν στις τρύπες τους, όσο και αν προσπαθεί η αστική τάξη και τα επιτελεία τους στα ΜΜΕ να τους διαφημίζουν

. Στις εργατογειτονιές δεν χωρούν οι υμνητές του Χίτλερ, οι δολοφόνοι του Παύλου Φύσσα και του Σαχζάτ Λουκμάν. Δεν χωράνε αυτοί που χτυπάνε πρωτοπόρους εργάτες που παλεύουν κόντρα στο σάπιο σύστημα της εκμετάλλευσης, για να μπορέσουμε να ζήσουμε με βάση τις ανάγκες μας. Δεν χωράνε αυτοί που χτυπάν πρωτοπόρους μαθητές που διεκδικούν δημόσια και δωρεάν Παιδεία. Δεν χωράνε πουθενά οι “ψευτόμαγκες της φακής” που θέλουν να σπείρουν φόβο στις γειτονιές μας. Σπάμε τον τσαμπουκά των φασιστών παντού!


Καλούμε όλους τους φορείς της Πάτρας να καταδικάζουν την επίθεση των φασιστών στην πρωτοπόρα μαθήτρια.


Όλοι στο συλλαλητήριο των φορέων

ενάντια στην εγκληματική φασιστική επίθεση, σήμερα Τετάρτη 4 Νοέμβρη στις 6 μ.μ., στην πλατεία Ταραμπούρα».

Δημοτική Αρχή Πάτρας

το

, ο

 Σύλλογος Δημοκρατικών Γυναικών Πάτρας (μέλος της ΟΓΕ)

, ο Ο 

Σύλλογος Γονέων και Κηδεμόνων του 25ου Δημοτικού Σχολείου Πάτρας

και ο

Σύλλογος Πολιτικών Συνταξιούχων Δημοσίου Αχαϊας

title: Erklärung zum Tod von Henry
content:
CN: Suizid


Henry, Beschuldigter im Antifa-Ost-Komplex, ist am 24. Oktober 2026 an den Folgen eines Suizidversuchs gestorben.


Wir sprechen von Herzen der Familie, seinen Freund*innen, seinem Umfeld und (ehemaligen) Wegbegleiter*innen unser tiefes Beileid aus.


Unsere Gefühle wechseln zwischen Trauer, Erinnerungen an ihn und auch Wut.


Wut auf Journalist*innen, die der Familie und seinem Umfeld keine 24 Stunden der Trauer gelassen haben. Wut auf Neonazis, die auch nach seinem Tod ihn nicht in Frieden lassen können. Wut auf das Gericht, weil es ihm seine therapeutische und medizinische Unterstützung immer wieder erschwerte und zum großen Teil nicht gewährte.


Wir verstehen, dass (seine) Anwält*innen auf die Ungerechtigkeiten bis hin zu rechtswidrigen Taten von Behörden gegen Henry und andere Antifaschist*innen in Leipzig und Sachsen verweisen. Antifaschist*innen stehen seit jeher im Fokus der Repressionsbehörden (*). Die SoKo LinX hat die Kriminalisierung und Verfolgung antifaschistischen Engagements in Sachsen im Besonderen betrieben.


Dies haben Henry und seine Familie immer wieder zu spüren bekommen. Die letzten Jahre von Henry waren von Repression und öffentlichen Diffamierungen seitens Behörden und Neonazis gegen seine Person geprägt, was für ihn, seine Familie und sein soziales Umfeld sehr belastend war.


Aber neben diesen Tatsachen gibt es noch weitere. Wir sind auch wütend auf Henry. Doch können wir dies nicht mehr mit ihm ausmachen. Wir möchten nicht, dass seine Person und sein Leben in der Öffentlichkeit bewertet werden, deswegen werden wir das hier auch nicht tun. Wir wünschen uns, dass dies respektiert wird. Zumal die Strafverfahren gegen das Konstrukt einer angeblichen antifaschistischen kriminellen Vereinigung weiter geführt werden.


Die Verkürzung, die wir in den letzten Tagen öfter gelesen haben, dass der Staat ihn umgebracht habe, finden wir nicht richtig. Es geht uns dabei nicht darum staatliche Stellen von ihrer Mitverantwortung frei zu sprechen, doch so einfach, wie einige meinen, ist es eben nicht.


Bei aller Trauer und emotionaler Erschütterung ist es Teilen der Familie, jenen die ihn die letzten Jahre begleiteten, und uns wichtig, dass der Tod von Henry nicht instrumentalisiert wird. Wir bitten euch daher von öffentlichkeitswirksamen Aktionen abzusehen. Es fühlt sich als Antifaschist*innen, die seit Jahrzehnten in Sachsen von dieser Repression auf unterschiedliche Weise betroffen sind und waren, falsch an.


Für uns ist es gerade besonders wichtig jene zu unterstützen, die im Moment am meisten leiden: Henrys Familie, die diesen Verlust verarbeiten muss.


Wir möchten daher Spenden für die Familie sammeln, damit diese mit den Auswirkungen des Todes nicht alleine bleibt.

https://www.antifaostkomplex.org/erklarung-zum-tod-von-henry/


Wir wünschen uns, dass Henry nun in Frieden ruhen kann.

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: Hennepin County Charges Far-Right Influencers Following Election Fraud Stunt
content:
Minneapolis, MN – Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty

announced

 felony charges of identity theft and unlawful voting against far-right influencers James O’Keefe and Cam Higby

on Wednesday

, Oct. 28.


“Before the August 11 primary election this office was very clear that reports of unlawful activity related to the election would be investigated and charged if appropriate,” Moriarty said during a press conference held on Oct. 27.


The charges stem from a series of videos produced by the duo during the Minnesota primary election on Aug. 11, where the two attempted to document what they alleged was a flaw in the state’s voter registration system that allows voters to prove their residence by having neighbors vouch for them. 


In the videos, Higby and O’Keefe, representing O’Keefe’s Florida-based Citizens Justice League, provide the names of actual voters in the area to poll workers but stop short of signing the oath to receive the ballot.


“Minnesota law states clearly that no individual shall intentionally misrepresent their identity in applying for a ballot,” Moriarty said, addressing the fact that neither man actually received a ballot. “The charges filed today are appropriate to address the conduct of Mr. O’Keefe and Mr. Higby.”


Read the charging complaints at the end of the article or click the name:

Cam Higby

 /

James O’Keefe


The vouching system in Minnesota is rarely used, accounting for less than 0.6% of all votes cast during the 2024 election, according to Moriarty. The system is most often used among those who live in senior living facilities, where residents often do not obtain drivers licenses updated with the facility’s address.


Despite this, both men disguised themselves as Muslim women and visited polling locations across Minneapolis. 


In one video published Aug. 14 Higby made a clear case for election fraud against himself. In it, he appears dressed in a niqab, with the area around his eyes painted a shade of brown, while attempting to vote under his assumed aliases, all of which were the real names of registered voters.


Throughout the video, Higby repeatedly asks the poll workers if the potential voter being vouched for needs a form of identification. At the first polling location, the poll worker tells him the other person needs one.


“No,” Higby said in a forced accent. “We don’t have ID. We no have pocket.”


If a voter is being vouched for at a polling place, they still need to provide either their Minnesota driver’s license, an ID card number or the last four digits of their social security number,

according to the Secretary of State website

.


Poll workers immediately reported Higby and O’Keefe’s group after their visits,

Minnesota Secretary of State Steve Simon told KSTP News later that day

.


“Their apparent goal was to cast doubt on one or more Minnesota election laws that have been in force for over fifty years,” Simon said in a statement. “Instead, they revealed their ignorance of how those laws actually work – while putting themselves in legal jeopardy.”


O’Keefe defended his and Higby’s actions that day by citing his earlier work with Project Veritas “investigating” the 2012 and 2016 elections in New Hampshire.


Project Veritas, founded by O’Keefe in June 2010, was

described by the Southern Poverty Law Center

 in 2022 as a “hard-right propaganda group that engages in sting operations.”


Related – 2025:

Newly Revealed FBI Document Confirms Collaboration Between DC Police and Discredited Far-Right Group Project Veritas


In New Hampshire in 2012, O’Keefe’s group visited a polling location and requested the ballots for numerous dead people whose names had yet to be culled from voter rolls. The state opened a criminal investigation into O’Keefe and his group,

quietly dropping the charges the next year

.


The strategy used in Minneapolis in August of sending somebody into a polling location under false pretenses dressed in a burqa is not entirely new to O’Keefe. During the 2016 presidential election, a female Project Veritas journalist dressed in a burqa entered a New York City polling location and requested the ballot of Huma Abedin.


On Oct. 26, two days before Hennepin County announced the charges, the two attempted the same investigation in Florida, both still dressed as Muslims.


In 2010,

O’Keefe pleaded guilty

 to entering federal property under false pretenses, for which he was ordered to pay a $1,500 fine and placed on three years’ probation …

author: dev
title: La menace de l'auto-justice
content:
Au lendemain du 17 octobre, le garde des sceaux Gérald Darmanin, brandie le menace de milices d'auto-défense : « si la réponse pénale aux violences liées au 17 octobre n'est pas extrêmement ferme », alors « les commerçants et les habitants feront justice eux-mêmes ». Une semaine plus tard, le 24, des milices fascistes sous-couvert de défense des petits commerçants attaquent des manifestations dans plusieurs villes de France. De nombreuses vidéos diffusées sur les réseaux sociaux attestent d'une collusion voir d'une collaboration avec les forces de l'ordre. Pour tenter d'y voir plus clair dans cette intrication étonnante entre pouvoir politique, police, milices d'extrême droite et auto-défense populiste, nous avons invité Gilles Favarel-Garrigues et Laurent Gayer, chercheurs au CNRS qui ont travaillé sur l'histoire de l'auto-justice ainsi que Vanessa Codaccioni, politiologue dont les recherches portent sur la répression, la délation et la société de vigilance.


À voir lundi 2 novembre :

author: Tom Sullivan
title: Mass protests defeat the far right in Brazil, but Lula is no way forward
content:
With the winds in Latin America blowing decisively towards the far right over recent years, voters went to the polls in the continent’s most important country, Brazil, in October. The Workers’ Party (PT), led by long-time leader and incumbent president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, lost in the first round, but achieved a remarkable turnaround in the second round.

Lula, as he is popularly known, was running against Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro, Lula’s predecessor. Jair is currently serving a 27-year sentence for an attempted coup after he lost the 2022 election. During his term he oversaw the deaths of over 700,000 people during the pandemic and is a close ally of President Trump. 

In the first round, Flavio Bolsonaro won 47 percent against Lula’s 45 percent. The right also took control of Congress.

The PT’s first-round loss shows how much support the PT has lost among its traditional base. The outgoing Lula administration was committed to a fiscal framework of zero budget deficits, resulting in caps on public spending and wages. It also allowed further oil exploration of the Amazon. During the campaign, Lula gave ground to the right's tough-on-crime platform, indicating his support for lowering the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16.

The PT’s poor performance in the first round makes its turnaround in the second round even more impressive. Over the three weeks, the PT’s vote increased by over ten million, giving the party 52 percent of the vote. Facing criminal allegations of money laundering, Bolsonaro fled to Miami.

The key factor in the sharp jump in the PT vote was the huge rallies that spread across the country between the two rounds of voting. The day after the first round, students at the Federal University in Rio de Janeiro held an assembly that turned into a rally, spilling out onto the streets. Social media and WhatsApp groups exploded with calls for demonstrations. On 7 October, the National Union of Students called demonstrations in several major cities that saw tens of thousands come out. 

These initial demonstrations were about mobilising to defeat the far right, defending public education, and fighting to reduce the work week to five days from six, a demand that Lula’s government has resisted. Although backing for the PT’s re-election was present, it received much less emphasis. One slogan was: “No to the father, no to the son.”

By 9 October, even small cities were holding assemblies and demonstrations. In Ponta Grossa, a city of around 350,000, university and high school students held an assembly of over a thousand people, promoted as “students against fascism”. It decided on an action plan that included leafleting and door knocking. Similar scenes played out at universities across the country.

“The first few days after the election were like a frenzy”, said Veronica O’Kelly, a national leader of the socialist group Revolucão Socialista. She continued,

“WhatsApp groups promoted rallies across the country. Students led demonstrations out of the universities into the streets. Their demands were immediately far beyond anything the PT was offering. This is what kicked off the mass demonstrations that came over the following weeks.” 

On the first weekend after the first round over one million joined marches in Sao Paolo and Rio de Janeiro under the slogan “The class is in the streets”. Lula was a prominent feature of the rallies, standing on top of a bus in Sao Paolo, surrounded by throngs of people. In other cities, hundreds of thousands joined marches. 

But students remained the driving force. On 14 October, the student union at the University of Brasilia held a demonstration of over 50,000 in the capital under the slogan “Bolsonaro never again and end the 6x1 now,” referring to the six-day work week.

The fact that the rallies raised major economic demands alongside support for the PT put pressure on Lula not just to offer promises after the second round but to take immediate action. On 14 October, Congress passed a constitutional amendment reducing the work week from six days to five with no loss of salary. This was a monumental victory for the Brazilian working class that the movement imposed on not just the PT but the entire ruling class. The measure passed the Senate 75 to 1, with even Bolsonaro’s party voting for it.

author: Unknown
title: Tuncay Yılmaz: We want to build a united front of resistance in Europe - Part Two
content:
ANF spoke to Tuncay Yılmaz, founding co-chair of the Socialist Refoundation Party (SYKP), about the outcomes of the Cologne meeting, the need for a common struggle, the situation of left-wing and democratic forces in the face of the rising far right in Europe, and the roadmap for the proposed alliance.


The first part of this interview can be read

here

. 


On 17 October, 25 organisations from different political traditions came together in Cologne. Similar attempts to build alliances have been made in Europe before. Why has the need to establish a common platform for struggle emerged again today? What distinguishes this meeting from previous initiatives?


Organisations from different political traditions and social groups in Europe have come together at various times. Previously, there was the European Assembly for Peace and Democracy (ABDEM). We then extended the organisation of the Peoples' Democratic Congress (HDK) in Turkey to Europe, establishing a broad organisation under the name HDK Europe. This organisation later became the European Democratic Forces Union (ADGB) and continued its activities under that name. Most recently, ahead of the NATO summit, a joint initiative called PANEV was established against imperialist aggression, wars and NATO.


All these initiatives emerged from efforts to find ways for the forces of democracy, peace, equality and freedom to become better organised in Europe and pursue more effective political action against the enormous aggressive power confronting us.


The alliances we established at different times sometimes lost their effectiveness, both because of changes in the objective conditions in which they were formed and, to speak frankly, because of our own shortcomings. This is a reality, and we are aware of it. Indeed, this was one of the issues on the agenda of our meeting. We want to learn from our previous experiences.


However, the mistakes we made in the past or the changes we have experienced should not prevent us from bringing democratic forces together again and carrying out a common struggle. And indeed, they are not preventing us. One of the main motivations that brought us together at this meeting was the growing hostility towards migrants in the European countries where we live, the rise of the right, fascist movements coming to power and increasing state violence. The fact that laws targeting asylum seekers have reached almost inhumane proportions is also deeply concerning to all of us. We want to build a united front of resistance against all of this.


At the same time, however, all our attention, thoughts and concerns are focused on developments in Turkey. Looking at Turkey, we see a totalitarian regime being built step by step. Everyone who opposes it becomes a target. Presidential candidates are arrested. Selahattin Demirtaş has been imprisoned for years, as has Figen Yüksekdağ. Ekrem İmamoğlu was subsequently arrested. The Republican People's Party (CHP), which prides itself on being the founding party of the state, is also under serious pressure. Attempts are being made to divide the party, and many of its representatives have been arrested.


Alongside all this, a negotiation process has begun. It has not yet reached the stage of a peace process. However, this negotiation process has the potential to generate a collective strength capable of pushing back attacks on democracy through the positive developments it could bring to the country's political life. Despite this, we see that the political authorities are acting with appalling arbitrariness in this process as well.


To speak frankly, this process has been made possible by the determination and goodwill of Abdullah Öcalan and the Kurdish Freedom Movement. After all, decisions were taken to lay down arms and dissolve the organisation. These decisions represent a profound transformation in the movement's historical existence.


Despite this, the state continues to display an extremely indifferent and unserious attitude towards taking steps on these issues, potentially jeopardising the process. Its actions could allow the anti-democratic practices it maintains throughout the country to continue in different forms in this area as well. We can all see that, for months, instead of implementing the legal arrangements brought onto Parliament's agenda with broad support, the authorities have merely continued saying, "We want this as well, and we want that too."


Frankly, they are acting entirely with …

author: paradox-a
title: Die falsche Welt des Gute-Laune-Faschismus
content:
Zum Posterboy des Gute-Laune-Faschismus wurde Ulrich Siegmund gekürt, der AfD-Ministerpräsident in spe aus Sachsen-Anhalt. Die AfD fuhr hier mit 43,8% ihr bislang bestes Ergebnis ein. Je strukturschwächer, gottverlassener und migrationsärmer die Gegenden sind, desto stärker ist der Zuspruch zum nationalistischen Autoritarismus. So bereisen die ewig grinsenden Rattenfänger das Land und punkten unter Deutschen, die die Überwindung ihrer eigenen bürgerlichen Existenz herbeisehnen und hoffen dies auf dem Weg der Zerstörung der liberalen Demokratie zu erreichen.


Der Wohlfühl-Faschismus ist ein Phänomen, das vor zwanzigdreißig Jahren noch völlig unvorstellbar gewesen wäre. Und in zweidrei Jahrzehnten werden wir uns ebenfalls fragen, was in dieser Phase eigentlich passiert ist. Wer sie verstehen will, muss sich dazu nicht nur die Wahlkampf-Strategien der AfD anschauen, sondern auch kultur- und medienwissenschaftlich vorgehen. So ist es kein Zufall, das seit Anfang des Jahres 2026 massenhaft KI-generierte Songs bei Youtube erscheinen. Aufgrund ihrer hohen Klickzahlen landen diese wiederum durch die Algorithmen sehr schnell in der Vorschlagleiste.


Die extrem rechte Propaganda-Maschinerie bedient sich somit nahezu perfekt abgestimmt der Mittel, die der Plattform-Kapitalismus entwickelt hat. Und sie greift auf eine künstlich-sentimentale Popkultur zurück, die unterm Strich meistens schon sehr schlicht und beschränkt war. Ob volkstümelnd wie Heino, oder neu-deutsch-hart wie Rammstein, sülzig wie Julia Juls, Runa&Rebellin oder pop-rockig wie Weimar, Sleipnir und andere – Vorbilder für die extrem rechte Computermusik gibt es genug…


Sicher könnte man auch dagegen halten und sagen, dass die Generierung von Musik und Video-Material durch technische Sprechapparate von allen möglichen Leute mit kommerziellen Absichten, um Aufmerksamkeit zu erhalten oder einfach nur aus Langeweile generiert wird. Und das stimmt auch. Bedenkt man, wie durchproduziert und geglättet kommerziell erfolgreiche Musik heute ist, scheint der Schritt zur sogenannten KI klein zu sein. Dennoch gibt es eine spezielle Affinität von faschistischem Denken zur offensichtlich künstlichen Kultur, die den Anschein von menschlicher Kreativität verlässt und damit post-human ist. Laut Jason Stanley wird damit auf die Herstellung von „Unwirklichkeit“ abgezielt.


Um ein paar Beispiele von viralen KI-generierten Songs und „Künstler“ zu nennen, sind da beispielsweise:


– „Spätestens HIER wacht jeder auf! Der Sound des Wandels“ („Aufbruch Deutschland“, 501.537 Aufrufe)


– „Steh auf, wenn du Deutscher bist | Stolz auf Heimat und Kultur“ („Ottilie“, 339.081 Aufrufe)


– „Was ist aus unserem Land geworden? | Ein Lied über den Verlust der Heimat“ („Fenja“, 338.697 Aufrufe)


– „Dorfmarie – So war es, so soll es wieder sein“ („Dorfmarie“, 160.534 Aufrufe)


– „DIE WACHT AM RHEIN (LIVE) | Rock-Version eines historischen Gedichts“ („Julia im Exil“; 113.198 Aufrufe)


– „Kein schöner Land… WO DIE EICHEN STEH’N“ („Freya“; 18.974 Aufrufe)


– „Thüringen Ein Land Eine Geschichte Ein Herz“ („Der Heimatklang“, 4334 Aufrufe)


– „Heimweh nach Deutschland“ („Liv Eisen“, 2067 Aufrufe)


Die Titel verraten schon das Wesentliche. Wenn man die Textzeilen hört oder liest, wird deutlich, dass die immer gleichen Narrative, endlos wiederholt werden. Stets geht es um den Verlust einer imaginären „Heimat“ oder glorreichen „Nation“, um eine angebliche „Überfremdung“, anknüpfend an den Verschwörungsmythos eines „großen Austauschs“. Der Gute-Laune-Faschismus lebt in der ewigen Wiederholung von Mustern immer gleicher Opfer-Inszenierungen, dem Streicheln narzisstischer Kränkungen, sowie der Vorstellung einer zukünftigen Größe, die nur durch die Erniedrigung der ausgemachten Feinde erreicht werden kann. All dies sind Produkte einer staatlich-kapitalistischen Gesellschaftsform, die mit Patriarchat, Rassismus und Naturbeherrschung verknüpft ist. Zusammengefasst ist die Computer-produzierte Lyrik in ihrem billigen Abklatsch armselig – und faschistisch.


Dabei darf man nicht vergessen, dass auch der historische Nationalismus keine naturwüchsige Volksbewegung war, sondern ein Elitenprojekt, das eine Nation und eine darin angeblich ursprünglich vorhandene Kultur verordnete, anerzog und drillte.


Hört man die künstlich erzeugten Lieder und ihre Texte an, greifen Form und Inhalt ineinander. Bekanntlich ist den Fans derartiger wohlfühlfaschistischer Erzeugnisse vollkommen egal, ob sie ein KI-generiertes Lied …

author: Maríangeles Guerrero
title: Rosa Amorim: "Hablar de reforma agraria en Brasil es hablar de un proyecto de dignidad de vida"
content:
“Com a barriga vazia não consigo dormir,

E com o bucho mais cheio, comecei a pensar.

Que eu me organizando posso desorganizar

Que eu desorganizando posso me organizar

Que eu me organizando posso desorganizar”.

Da lama ao caos, Nação Zumbi - Chico Science


“Con la panza vacía no puedo dormir,

Con el buche más lleno, empecé a pensar.

Que desorganizándome puedo organizar

Que organizando me puedo desorganizar

Que desorganizándome puedo organizar”


Por Mariángeles Guerrero y Carla Perelló

Desde Brasil


Rosa Amorim es la primera mujer del Movimiento de los Trabajadores Rurales sin Tierra (MST) en ser electa diputada nacional en Brasil. Es negra, lesbiana, oriunda de Pernambuco, nordeste del país, y tiene 29 años. Integra el Partido de los Trabajadores (PT). Durante la pandemia, mientras gobernaba Jair Bolsonaro, fue una de las impulsoras de la red de cocinas solidarias que enfrentaron el hambre en los barrios populares de las ciudades. La reelección de Lula da Silva significa una victoria popular y una esperanza, pero la conformación de un Congreso con mayoría de la extrema derecha plantea sus propios desafíos. En ese escenario, sostiene que la “lucha parlamentaria” será vital. “Queremos que Brasil deje de ser uno de los países que más venenos y agrotóxicos consume”, afirma.


Hija de la lucha por la reforma agraria, Amorim creció en las filas del MST y también fue dirigente estudiantil. Desde sus orígenes, el movimiento campesino mantuvo su autonomía aunque apoyó candidaturas del PT. Pero, en 2022, tras el retroceso en materia de derechos que significó el gobierno de Jair Bolsonario, presentó sus propios candidatos. Ese año, ella fue electa diputada del estado de Pernambuco.

El pasado 5 de octubre fue electa diputada nacional; una de lxs 38 legisladorxs LGBT+ que obtuvieron un escaño y una de los cuatro integrantes del MST que estarán en el Congreso brasileño

.


En el histórico proceso electoral que consolidó a Luíz Inácio Lula da Silva como presidente por los próximos cuatro años, Amorim fue una de las jóvenes que acompañó la campaña para revertir la derrota que el PT obtuvo en la primera vuelta.

Llevará las banderas de la reforma agraria y la soberanía alimentaria al Poder Legislativo. Allí el agronegocio presiona, de la mano de la bancada ruralista, para obtener beneficios y seguir extendiendo la frontera agropecuaria

, causando deforestación y contaminación.


En contraste, el MST lleva cuatro décadas de lucha por la tierra para la producción de alimentos sanos.

“Alimentamos al pueblo porque con comida en la panza podemos tener mentes pensantes y con mentes pensantes podemos organizarnos”

, sostuvo en entrevista con Tierra Viva, haciendo honor a la histórica banda nordestina Nação Zumbi liderada por Chico Science.


Foto: Prensa PT


Las cocinas solidarias, que define como “una tecnología social para organizar al pueblo”, se convirtieron en política pública en 2023, durante el gobierno de Da Silva. Su objetivo es vincular el campo con la ciudad, llevando alimentos sanos a espacios comunitarios de los barrios populares. En esos ámbitos se brinda un plato de comida pero también escucha, alfabetización, contención y cuidados. Para la diputada, comer es el primer paso para cuestionar por qué existe el hambre y la pobreza.


—¿En qué situación está hoy la soberanía alimentaria en Brasil?

—Hablar del hambre no es solamente hablar de si el pueblo come por la mañana, por la tarde y por la noche. Es más profundo. Combatir el hambre también significa hablar de la calidad de lo que se come. Y para eso vamos a tener que librar una lucha muy grande. Ya la estamos librando, pero va a ser todavía mayor: la lucha contra el agronegocio, contra el modelo de producción vigente que hace que las personas se enfermen por lo que consumen todos los días. Queremos que Brasil deje de ser uno de los países que más venenos y agrotóxicos consume. Y esto tiene una relación directa con la lucha parlamentaria. Vamos a tener que librar una enorme disputa contra el agronegocio en el Congreso para reducir la cantidad de agrotóxicos que se autorizan en Brasil. También vamos a tener que poner en la agenda la ampliación de las tierras cultivables destinadas a la agricultura familiar y campesina.

Llego al Congreso Nacional para conformar y construir la bancada de la tierra, de la agricultura familiar y de la agricultura campesina. Queremos debatir cómo combatir el hambre y qué estamos consumiendo en Brasil.

Tenemos que debatir la …

title: Mehtap Sakinci: Femicide is political
content:
Lawyer Mehtap Sakinci, one of the founders of the 10 October Peace Association, spoke to ANF about peace, justice and the women's struggle on the 11th anniversary of the 10 October Ankara Train Station Massacre.


Sakinci said that femicide was political and criticized Turkey's withdrawal from the Istanbul Convention and the shortcomings in the implementation of Law No. 6284. She stressed that women played an important role in building peace and called on women to stand together and strengthen their struggle ahead of 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.


 


'

Women are an important part of the struggle for peace'


Mehtap Sakinci lost her husband, lawyer Uygar Coşgun, in the Ankara Train Station Massacre carried out by the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS) on 10 October 2015. She continues to honor the memory of those who lost their lives at the peace rally 11 years ago and to express their longing for peace on every platform.


Sakinci expressed her enthusiasm about attending the conference, where women's role in building peace was being discussed and said: "I was genuinely excited to take part in this event, where women stand together and the importance of women's role in building peace is truly emphasized."


Sakinci said that women coming together reminded them of their collective strength in social struggles. She continued: "By reminding ourselves that being a woman and the strength women demonstrate in this country, in this world and under the circumstances we live in should never be underestimated, we are showing one another just how important a role women play in the struggles for peace, democracy and labor rights in this country."


'Courtrooms stand strong through the power of women'


Mehtap Sakinci said that she had served as president of the 10 October Peace Association for nearly 10 years before handing over the position to her colleagues a year ago. She spoke about the association's establishment and the struggle for justice carried out by women who lost loved ones in the massacre.


Sakinci said that women's voices and solidarity had played a decisive role in the legal struggle following the massacre and added: "I handed over responsibility for the process to my colleagues a year ago. But as a woman, as someone who lost her husband and as a woman who has paid a price in this country, I remain a living witness to just how difficult it is for a woman to carry this struggle forward.


When we established the association as families of those who lost their lives, I embarked on this journey as a woman who had lost her husband, alongside fathers who had lost their children. Throughout this process, I have seen how deeply women's voices, strength, cries and tears have resonated, particularly those of mothers who lost their children.


Today, as the proceedings concerning the 10 October massacre continue, it is once again the strength of women that sustains the courtrooms. They echo with the voices of my fellow women lawyers."


'I have no doubt that peace will come through women'


Mehtap Sakinci emphasized the responsibilities women assumed in building peace and the power of solidarity, stressing that women coming together would strengthen the struggle for peace.


Sakinci said: "I believe it is important to emphasize this: If peace is to come to this country, and if people are to take responsibility for building that peace, I have absolutely no doubt that women will be the ones to make it happen.


Perhaps we also need to remind ourselves of something on platforms like this: People heal one another's pain, and women are a homeland for one another. Women who have suffered, who have paid a price and who have truly stood at the forefront of the struggle for rights in this country need other women beside them. I believe that only when women come together can we bring peace with a louder and stronger voice."


'Turkey withdrew from the Istanbul Convention, and Law No. 6284 remains insufficient'


As 25 November approaches, Mehtap Sakinci recalled Turkey's withdrawal from the Istanbul Convention and criticized the inadequacy of legal provisions and practices intended to protect women from violence.

author: Mag
title: Frauen in Argentinien gegen die Kettensäge, Femizide und den Machismo: „Ni una Menos“ (Nicht eine weniger)
content:
Dossier


„

Wieder einmal haben sich die Frauen und verschiedenen Bildungsarbeiterinnen von CTERA der feministischen und transfeministischen Bewegung angeschlossen und unter dem Slogan „Ni una Menos“ gegen Femizide, Transfemizide und Transvestizide im ganzen Land, im Rahmen unserer CTA-T und durch alle Basisorganisationen von CTERA, diese Forderung, die vor 9 Jahren auf die Straße ging, begleitet. (…) „Hass und Hunger töten“, gewalttätige, fremdenfeindliche, frauenfeindliche, diskriminierende, verleugnende, antifeministische und LGBT+-hassende Diskurse sind das, was tagtäglich in unserer Gesellschaft zirkuliert, ausgehend von denen, die uns regieren, einer Regierung, die es sich zur Aufgabe gemacht hat, öffentliche Politiken mit einer Gender- und Diversity-Perspektive im Hinblick auf die Menschenrechte zu entleeren

…“ Aus dem span.

Aufruf bei der Bildungsgewerkschaft CTERA

 (maschinenübersetzt) zu landesweiten Frauenprotesten am 3. Juni 2024 – siehe mehr zum Thema und Hintergründe:


„Nos falta Nancy“: Bildungsgewerkschaft CTERA hatte am 29. Oktober zu landesweitem Lehrkräftestreik und Protesten in ganz Argentinien nach Femizid an Lehrerin Nancy aufgerufen


Femizid an Lehrerin führt zu Protesten in Argentinien


„

Buenos Aires/Esquina. Im ganzen Land hat der Gewerkschaftsverband der Lehrkräfte (CTERA) in Argentinien am vergangenen Donnerstag infolge des Femizids an der Lehrerin Nancy Godoy zu einem nationalen Trauertag und zu Streiks aufgerufen. Die Protestierenden zogen in verschiedenen Provinzen, darunter Buenos Aires, Corrientes und Córdoba, durch die Straßen und machten mit Bannern und Schildern, auf denen „Nos falta Nancy“ (Nancy fehlt uns) zu lesen war, auf den Mord an der Lehrerin aufmerksam. Mit dem Fall rücken auch die Bedingungen in den Fokus, unter denen Lehrkräfte in ländlichen Regionen arbeiten. Godoy selbst hatte sich gegen die Missstände ausgesprochen.


Die 52-Jährige war stellvertretende Leiterin der ländlichen Schule Nr. 626 im Paraje El Malezal in der subtropischen Provinz Corrientes im Nordosten Argentiniens. Unter der Woche blieb sie dort, da der Weg nach Hause bis zu drei Stunden dauerte. Mobil- und Satellitenempfang gibt es in dieser Gegend oft nicht. Ihre letzte Meldung an einen ihrer Söhne erfolgte daher rund eine Woche, bevor diese sie am 7. Oktober als vermisst meldeten. Am vergangenen Mittwoch fand die Polizei ihre Leiche. Laut vorläufigem Obduktionsbericht hatte sie Stichverletzungen und Abwehrverletzungen. author: anred
title: De Loan a Nancy: Corrientes se tiñe de sangre, pero nadie habla de Valdés
content:
El femicidio de Nanci Godoy, la maestra rural asesinada en Esquina (Corrientes) tras denunciar las pésimas condiciones de la escuela donde se desempeñaba, generó un impacto a nivel nacional que trascendió las fronteras provinciales. Sin embargo, muy pocos focos están puestos en el gobernador de la provincia, Juan Pablo Valdés, responsable político de la seguridad y la educación a nivel provincial.

Por El Grito del Sur.


Loan Peña es un niño correntino que desapareció el 13 de junio de 2024, cuando estaba en un almuerzo familiar en la casa de su abuela, en la localidad de 9 de Julio, en Corrientes. El juicio comenzó el 16 de junio de este año y tiene 17 imputados, pero visibiliza la complicidad policial y política de los funcionarios provinciales con la desaparición del niño, cuyo paradero aún se desconoce. La Alerta Sofía por el menor sigue vigente. Pero no es el único escándalo provincial del que (extrañamente) el gobernador Juan Pablo Valdés sale indemne.


Valdés viene vaciando la educación al ritmo que pide Milei: en marzo de 2026 descontó los días de paro de docentes que se movilizaban por mejoras salariales y edilicias. Además, los pobladores rurales denuncian la ausencia total de medidas paliativas para las inundaciones derivadas del fenómeno del Niño que han afectado campos, unidades productivas y escuelas.


La familia Valdés gobierna hace diez años: dos períodos de Gustavo y luego la sucesión en su hermano, Juan Pablo. Expresa una continuidad de 25 años de feudalismo radical en la provincia que ha sumido a Corrientes en la pobreza, laconcentración de la riqueza en pocas manos y el ataque frontal al interior provincial y la ruralidad.


El 41% de la población del Gran Corrientes se encuentra debajo de la línea de pobreza, según datos del primer semestre de 2026. También se encuentra dentro de las tres provincias con mayor mortalidad infantil del país, alcanzando el dato de 14 por cada 1.000 nacidos vivos en 2024, la más alta de Argentina para ese año. La provincia tiene datos de analfabetismo superiores al promedio nacional.


Ni hablar de la concentración de la tierra: un 81,64% de la superficie está en explotaciones mayores a 1.000 hectáreas, según consigna la Estrategia Provincial para el Sector Agroalimentario (EPSA 2022). La concentración de la tierra coincide con el despoblamiento rural: en 1970 un 42% de la gente vivía en el campo, pero para 2022 era de apenas el 12%.

author: groundxero
title: Where Women Make History: Reclaiming Agency in History and in Movements
content:
Gargi’s book is a historiographical recovery of the junctures when women fought and moved another inch towards occupying half the sky. 


 


By

 Vertika Mani 


 


The first intriguing thing to notice about V. Gargi’s

No Women, No History

 is the cover page of the book itself. Published by Virasam Books, the cover depicts women holding guns, marching with axes and also hugging trees. The image with its wide range of contrast yet a commonality of women as marchers and fighters interacts with its readers to convey the larger argument that this book seeks to make. The book was initially written as a collection of notes by V. Gargi, a revolutionary activist who dedicated this book

“To all the women who fought against overwhelming odds, made great sacrifices to the extent of even laying down their lives to make this place better for all of us…”


 


The first edition of

No Women No History: Women in Indian Movements (19th century – 2004)

 was published last year in August, at a pit stop, when the mainstream feminist discourse in India and abroad mostly associate women with power of intellect and pen, which are all quite a matter of privilege and can therefore be politically disabling at times. In that context, reading

No women No History

 is refreshing as it takes us down the road of history of women’s struggle, almost on a rampage to discover the truth of the fighting spirit that Indian women have always stood for.


 


An extraordinary range of political histories 


 


The book covers an extraordinary range of political histories and geographical contexts from 19th Century to the year 2004 covering histories of peasant and Adivasi uprisings, anti-caste struggles, labour movements, revolutionary politics, autonomous women’s organisations, ecological movements, struggles in the North-East, cultural organisations and contemporary campaigns. Its approach is broad and, for the most part, non-sectarian. Rather than treating “women’s issues” as a separate political category, Gargi locates women within the wider structures of social and political struggle, as peasants, workers, artisans, Dalits, Adivasis and members of minority communities.


 


This method of writing makes gendered oppression therefore appear not as an isolated structure but is seen in relationship with caste, class, feudal relations, economic exploitation and political power. This is among this book’s most important methodological contributions which allow the history of women’s liberation to be read as history of movements rather than that of organisations. A history of movements in which women fought over land, wages, labour, caste hierarchy, food, displacement, forests, political representation and state power. The breadth of the historical canvas is therefore significant to explore beyond conventional boundaries of women’s history.


 


Beginning with women’s participation in tribal and peasant rebellions, Gargi moves between the histories of Ranis and Begums and those of ordinary women who participated in the political ferment of the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. The juxtaposition prevents women’s history from becoming a gallery of exceptional female figures. It takes a dive into the political labour of ordinary women, particularly peasant, working-class, Dalit, Adivasi and other marginalised women, who have so frequently remained outside the central narrative of political history.


 


One of the salient feature of discussions around movements is the notable references made to the women pioneers, for instance, of Self-Respect Movement which is mostly associated with Periyar but more often than not misses to speak of Maniyammai, the woman who went on to lead the Kazhagam after Periyar’s death. Similarly, Gargi talks about Ambedkarite and Dalit movements including women’s role at length. Other such references include the distinctive forms of women’s participation in movements like Jail Bharo Satyagraha of 1960–65. The histories of women in the freedom struggle, women revolutionaries and communists are similarly placed alongside organisational histories that are less familiar in mainstream accounts.


 


Similarly, the book discusses collectives which are again, less talked about. For instance, The Mahila Atmaraksha Samitis (MARS), which emerged as an important form of women’s mobilisation before Partition. The further chapters trace the experiences of women during and after Partition, discovering a phase in history where …

author: Sara Fayyazi
title: Making Women’s History Part of the Curriculum
content:
Two teachers from Sacred Heart Preparatory School in California, Kristen Kelly and Serene Williams, have proposed an Advanced Placement U.S. Women’s History course in response to the issue of students not learning about women’s history. The courses would allow studying women’s experiences and contributions in greater depth. Establishing this course would create a better understanding of American history as it includes the diverse experiences of women and would help students connect the historical struggles for equality to gender issues today.

Women have contributed to shaping the nation’s politics, economy, and social movements, yet their participation is often overlooked by traditional history classes. From fighting for the right to vote, challenging discrimination, and advocating for female autonomy, women have had a significant role in building the foundation of the United States today.

One of the main arguments for WAPUSH is that women’s experiences are not explored in the classroom. In the article Educational Activism: Creating an AP U.S. Women’s History Course, Serene Williams, Kristen Kelly, and Clara Robinson explain that topics such as women’s suffrage and reproductive rights receive limited attention in the current AP U.S. History curriculum. The women’s suffrage movement involved decades of organizing, political campaigning, and resistance. However, teachers may not introduce this topic to students or have enough time to examine its strategies and leaders in detail. A dedicated course would allow students to study these movements more thoroughly and understand how women helped shape American democracy.

Women’s history is much broader than the fight for voting rights. The proposed WAPUSH curriculum includes women’s labor, politics, religion, culture, war, and violence against women. It also examines how race, class, sexuality, religion, and other identities shaped women’s experiences. This approach is important because women throughout the years have never shared one universal experience. Indigenous women, Black women, Immigrant women, etc., have faced different opportunities and forms of discrimination. Studying these differences would help students develop a greater understanding of American history and that America was not built on just our founding fathers, but by women who paved the path for opportunity and development through blood, sweat, and tears.

An AP course would also help students recognize the connection between historical events and current issues. The debate over reproductive rights and other feminist struggles today cannot be fully understood without examining the laws and political movements that shaped access to contraceptives, abortion, and female economic support. Studying topics from the suffrage movement to the Equal Rights Amendment can help students understand the political equality that has developed through activism and engage in feminist discussion. Learning this history would give students the context needed to evaluate debates instead of viewing them as different events.

Establishing this course would show that women’s history is worthy of advanced academic study. The WAPUSH campaign began in 2022, and according to its website, the campaign gathered more than 4,000 petition signatures and received encouragement from College Board leadership as it worked toward launching this course. Its proposal has also received university support, while the campaign continues seeking letters from high schools willing to offer the course. This continued support brings women closer to bringing light to women’s history and giving women a space in school systems and curricula. This petition is one step closer every day to its goal to educate and inform people all across America of women’s contributions.

An AP U.S. Women’s History course would make education more comprehensive, inform students even more about the history of the U.S., and connect past struggles to present issues. Women have influenced American politics, economics, culture, and social movements, yet their experiences are not always given sufficient attention in existing courses. By offering students an opportunity to examine these experiences, the College Board could help create a more inclusive and accurate understanding of the nation’s past. Women’s history is not separate from American history but instead an essential part of it.

author: CMI Argentina
title: El martirio de Nancy
content:
A Nancy Godoy el estado la dejó sola. Horas a caballo para llegar a su escuela, en medio de la nada, en el territorio de una estancia, que tenía dentro una escuela para sus peones. Llegó por primera vez y era una ruina. Lo denunció con detalles. La ignoraron. No llegó a cobrar un sueldo desde agosto. Apareció asesinada. Toda su lucha debió conocerse antes.


Por Silvana Melo


Nancy Godoy tenía ocho alumnos en una escuela pública dentro de una estancia. Es decir, en un territorio privado. Para llegar tenía que recorrer decenas de kilómetros de caminos rurales correntinos hasta ese punto de poder donde la alcanzaban hasta el paraje en el que un caballo la trasladaría durante tres horas para llegar a la escuela. Cruzando bañados, riachos y soledades escampadas que se volvían de una hostilidad imprevisible en caso de lluvias.


Tenía 52 años cuando ese 15 de agosto llegó a la escuela N° 626 del paraje El Malezal, en Esquina, Corrientes, para hacerse cargo de una suplencia. Era una casita desgastada, destruida, como si por ella hubiera pasado no sólo el tiempo, sino la desidia estatal y el desprecio privado.


Después de hacerse un panorama general de aquello a lo que se enfrentaba –suciedad extrema, ausencia de años de cualquier autoridad, falta de registros de todo tipo, situación sanitaria peligrosa, imposibilidad de habitar para ella, que debía quedarse la semana entera- el 15 de agosto escribió una carta manuscrita para enviar al ministerio de Educación de Corrientes. Y denunció cada detalle. Envió un expediente y sostuvo que la escuela estaba totalmente abandonada, sin agua, con inodoros llenos de tierra y ratas, que tuvo que acudir a una madre y a la baqueana que la acompañaba en el último tramo de su trayecto, María Rosa Leguizamón. En su casa tuvo que dormir las tres primeras noches porque la escuela era inhabitable. Esa misma mujer quedó involucrada después en la investigación por el crimen.


Decía que el techo se le caería encima, que las ventanas estaban rotas, que la humedad se comía el edificio, que las ratas y los murciélagos se habían apropiado de la casa, que el olor de sus heces era insoportable, que no había muebles suficientes, que los libros se habían mojado. Ella era docente, cocinera, portera y directora. Y era la responsable del edificio.


La carta que escribió Nancy a las autoridades educativas


Y la dejaron sola.


El estado la dejó sola. En medio de la nada, dentro de una estancia, en las manos de un propietario que hacía y deshacía, que tenía dentro de su propiedad una escuela para sus peones. Y ella debería comportarse como su maestra, directora, portera y cocinera. Con un sueldo pagado por el estado que la dejaba a la buena de dios. Sola de toda soledad.


Su denuncia fue ignorada por las autoridades educativas, sólo sostenida después de su desaparición por la comunidad de Esquina, sus docentes y su familia.


Pero esta lucha de ella debió conocerse antes de la tragedia.


No después. Cuando alguien la asesinó por el motivo que sea. Por ser mujer. Por ser maestra rural. Por tener coraje. Por denunciar.


Nancy se pasaba los días en esa escuela que tuvo que rehacer con sus manos y el fin de semana volvía con su familia. Sin señal de celular, sin comunicación de ningún tipo, su familia sabía que seguía viva cuando regresaba su sonrisa destruida por el cansancio. Pero aquel fin de semana no volvió. Y todo comenzó a volverse sombrío.


La dejaron sola. Tres horas a caballo y sin señal.


Apareció asesinada.


A metros del aula que había sabido reparar con sus manos, en la tapera del capataz, había ropa quemada.


Hay un estado que manda una trabajadora sola. A educar. Precarizada. A caballo. Sin señal de ningún tipo. Sin procurarle un transporte oficial. A que llegue como pueda. A una escuela en ruinas. Dentro de una propiedad de un estanciero. Ese estado cajonea su denuncia. Investiga su desaparición. Y la encuentra cuando fue asesinada.


En el territorio de la estancia El Curupí. En una escuela pública dentro de una zona privada.


El espacio Docentes Autoconvocados Corrientes – Sector 2019 aseguró que Nancy Godoy fue asesinada sin llegar a cobrar un solo sueldo a pesar de trabajar desde agosto.


A pesar del sacrificio para llegar. A pesar del desastre que encontró y del que nadie se hizo cargo. A pesar de que el docente que hacía años que no iba a la escuela seguía cobrando su salario.


Y ella fue asesinada por ser maestra en una escuela pública y tener que afrontar una realidad …

author: Amy Goodman
title: Remembering Legendary Farmworker Organizer and Activist Dolores Huerta
content:
Huerta wasn’t just an organizer — she also loved life, says journalist Maria Hinojosa.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Immigrant rights and labor icon Dolores Huerta died Wednesday at the age of 96. Huerta co-founded the National Farm Workers Association in 1962 and then the United Farm Workers of America, working with Cesar Chavez. From 1965 to 1970, the union organized the historic Delano grape strike, which ended in major gains for farmworkers’ labor rights.

In the years that followed, Huerta became heavily involved in the women’s liberation and immigrant rights movements and became a major supporter of the Democratic Party. In March, The New York Times published an investigation into Cesar Chavez’s history of sexual abuse of women and girls in the farmworkers’ movement, prompting Huerta to reveal that she, too, had been raped by Chavez. Huerta said the assaults led to the births of two of her children.

Dolores Huerta appeared on Democracy Now! many times over the years. We remember her legacy with Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist Maria Hinojosa, who says, “Dolores was not only a labor organizer, a civil rights organizer, a feminist, committed, always optimistic about the possibilities of this country, but she loved life, and I want people to remember that.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman.

The legendary labor organizer, feminist and civil rights activist Dolores Huerta has died at the age of 96. She was co-founder of the National Farm Workers Association in 1962 and then the United Farm Workers of America. She worked with Cesar Chavez at both groups. The United Farm Workers grew out of a merger between the National Farm Workers Association and the Filipino-led Agricultural Workers Organizing Committee.

Dolores Huerta coined the phrase ”¡Sí se puede!,” “Yes, we can!” It became a rallying cry for farmworkers, a lasting slogan for social justice movements.

Dolores Huerta appeared on Democracy Now! many times. We’ll hear her in her own words later in the broadcast, but first let’s turn to the trailer of the 2017 documentary Dolores, which featured interviews with Angela Davis, Gloria Steinem, Hillary Clinton and Nancy Pelosi.

author: Marx-lover
title: The Cornell Case and the Left's Betrayal of Itself
content:
Here's an article about the feminist reaction to the "Cornell 7" case that has been in the news recently (October 2026). A version of it was published in "Compact." (The hyperlinks have been deleted, unfortunately.) The general point is that contemporary feminism has become an albatross for the left, and is also contributing to destructive social and cultural trends.

In the 1960s, feminists demanded that women and men have legal equality, that women be treated as mature adults who are free to make their own choices be it with regard to sex or their careers, that patriarchal paternalism be dismantled. In the 2020s, feminists demand that women be constantly protected against men, that patriarchal paternalism be resurrected, that women be legally treated as not responsible for decisions they’ve made because, in certain contexts, only men have agency. And men, they argue, are inveterate misogynists, abusers, and rapists, so the agency they manifest is almost invariably malign.

The reaction to the “Cornell 7” case is the latest example. A remarkable wave of hysteria has swept liberal and left culture, from mass media and social media to university campuses. Misandry is drenching the discourse; mobs are going after anyone who questions the dominant narrative; the guilt of the accused is automatically assumed, because the accused are men and men are by definition guilty. Is it any wonder that millions of men in recent years have turned away from the left—which seems to hate them—and fallen into the clutches of the far-right and the “manosphere”?

Consider what has transpired. Far from condemning the wildly irresponsible comments of public figures like Governor Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James, which treat as established fact accusations made in a civil lawsuit, leftists themselves, including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Zohran Mamdani, have talked as though the case has already been decided. This is despite the highly ambiguous evidence that has been presented, much of which tends to exonerate the alleged perpetrators of the “gang-rape.” Not only is presumption of innocence thrown out the window; it is obvious that even if the accused end up being found innocent, most liberals and leftists will remain sure of their guilt.

Lynch mobs have been out for blood. A few weeks ago, it was easy to find thousands of people “liking” public demands to kill the accused. Even innocent bystanders were victimized. The campaign of overwhelming harassment to which the journalist Michael Tracey has been subjected for questioning the “guilty until proven innocent” narrative led to his father receiving “thousands of nonstop crazed texts/calls/voicemails” threatening him with brutal violence. The current owners of Tracey’s childhood home were “inundated” with “crazed threats,” and received suspicious packages at their house. Friends and family of the accused men were harassed by thousands. So was the family of an innocent man who happens to have the same name as one of the accused.

Since liberals and leftists are refusing to stand up for decency and the rule of law, it is left to conservatives to do so—which enables them to claim the moral high ground against “lunatic” leftists and thereby score political points. It turns out that many conservatives take women more seriously as (potentially) responsible adults and moral agents than most leftists do.

Feminist moral panics may seem well-intentioned in that they’re allegedly motivated by concern for the safety of women, but these episodes illustrate the extent to which the (so-called) “left” has been corrupted and co-opted by neoliberal dynamics, particularly in the era of social media. The atomized, polarized, siloed, anti-intellectual, narcissistic soundbite culture of social media—itself a reflection of capitalist tendencies—has helped produce a liberal-left that dehumanizes others, reflexively assumes the worst of men, exploits controversies for social media clout, and contributes to the very social breakdown that leftists rightly attack neoliberalism for engendering. After all, a feminism that teaches women to hate and fear men, and to view themselves as being on a higher moral plane, doesn’t exactly promote healthy relationships. It exacerbates gender wars and culture wars, thus, again, gifting the right wing with talking points and grievances to rally around.

title: [“In a world that constantly shames us for our bodies, genders, or sexualities, we can trick…
content:
gatheringbones

:

[“In a world that constantly shames us for our bodies, genders, or sexualities, we can trick ourselves into thinking that we are “taking control” and that achieving a certain body ideal is liberation. It is far from that.

For those of us who face multiple forms of oppression, developing eating disorders is not simply wanting our bodies to meet the impossible aesthetic ideal associated with people in dominant culture. Queer and trans people don’t develop disordered eating simply because we want to assimilate to cisgender, heteronormative culture. Of course, appearances can be and often are part of the picture. But when we attribute eating disorders solely to the desire for our bodies to look a certain way, the conversation stops. And we miss out on opportunities for crucial conversations about the connections between eating disorders, trauma, and survival.

Eating disorders help us to survive trauma and oppression.

 For queer and trans folks, the way we both conceptualize and heal from eating disorders must account for the ways we are harmed by systems of power. Eating disorders help us to cope with everyday microaggressions and macroaggressions. They help us to get by in the face of food insecurity. They can keep us safe in a world in which being read as queer or trans can mean life or death.

For many people, disordered eating or behaviours are attempts at shape control, which are attempts to blend in and not become a target. For many of us, eating disorder “treatment” that aims to strip us of the very armour that has allowed us to stay alive, can actually cause more harm if there isn’t an adequate substitute or systemic change to help us to safely exist in the world. Treatment cannot simply be aimed at challenging our “distorted thoughts” or symptom reduction or cheerleading body positivity. Treatment approaches that aim at skills training (e.g., dialectical behaviour therapy) and challenging unhelpful thought patterns that fuel an eating disorder (e.g., cognitive behavioural therapy) are often crucial, but they are not enough for a true sense of feeling safe and at home in one’s body.

Most mainstream treatment approaches perpetuate white supremacist, capitalist systems of harm. Fat people are told that they are holding on to their fat as protection and that if they worked through their trauma, the weight would fall away. Thin people are told they need to restore their weight but they are not to go beyond an established “upper limit.” When we demonize “emotional eating,” there is an inherent assumption that the individual can get to a calm, neutral state at all times when their body needs or wants to be fed. Sometimes “emotional eating” is harm reduction.

Our disorders and symptoms, the things that we feel shame about, were once what helped us to get through the night. We might still be in survival mode. Or, we might have a hard time recognizing that we no longer need to be in survival mode. But before we move on, we might have to pay respect and allow ourselves to grieve how we have been called to protect ourselves in ways that are simultaneously brilliant and destructive.”]

sand c. chang, from dreaming bigger: body liberation and weight inclusivity in health care, from The Care We Dream Of: Liberatory & Transformative Justice Approaches to LGBTQ+ Health, edited by Zena Sharman, 2021

and once I had control over my life quiting was easy but relapse was also easy as soon as I lost that control
but I needed control over my life FIRST and healing second

author: Shefali Luthra
title: Missouri Voters Reject Effort to Overturn Their State’s Abortion Protections
content:
The measure would also have banned gender-affirming care for transgender minors, which is already illegal in the state.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Missouri voters rejected an effort to overturn their state’s abortion protections, according to a projection by Decision Desk HQ, ensuring that the procedure will remain legal and enshrined in the state constitution despite dedicated efforts by Republican leadership.

Amendment 3 would have reversed the results of a 2024 vote that enshrined abortion protections into the state constitution and made Missouri the first state with a constitutional ban on the procedure. It would also have banned gender-affirming care for transgender minors, which is already illegal in the state.

The measure’s failure offers a rebuke to efforts by Missouri’s Republican leaders, who largely oppose abortion. Amendment 3 was put forth by Republican lawmakers who, troubled by the 2024 vote’s results, hoped a second vote might result in the undoing of abortion rights. The state’s first lady, Claudia Kehoe, served as treasurer for the campaign to pass Amendment 3.

Polling conducted this summer suggested that while Missouri voters largely supported abortion rights, they opposed keeping gender-affirming care legal for trans minors, a point emphasized by Amendment 3’s backers.

“We’re trying to do everything. We’ve had canvassers knocking on thousands of doors,” Tom Estes, a Republican state Senate staffer working on the pro-Amendment 3 campaign, told The 19th earlier this year. “There are several pieces of this that resonate really well, that we may not have gotten last time. The number one piece of that is the trans issue.”

The campaign also argued that the abortion protections enacted two years ago had made the procedure unregulated and dangerous, suggesting that the new ban would protect women and children.

The reality, according to abortion providers in the state, has been different: Abortion has been highly regulated and only sporadically available. Even prior to the fall of Roe v. Wade in 2022, abortions in Missouri had become almost impossible to obtain, the result of a maze of restrictions enacted by the state’s conservative legislature. By 2022, only one clinic in the state offered abortion, in St. Louis.

“I would love to provide abortion services four to six days a week in Springfield,” Dr. Margaret Baum, the chief medical officer at Planned Parenthood Great Rivers, told The 19th at the end of August. “I think the demand is there.”

author: La Zarzamora
title: Lulén y Max, dos jóvenes trans llevan año y medio encarcelados por defenderse de su agresor
content:
Lulen y Max son una pareja de dos personas trans condenados por intento de homicidio agravado con tentativa hacia el padre adoptivo de uno de ellos.

Los hechos habrían ocurrido en febrero del 2025 cuando ambos jóvenes se reúnen en la casa del padre de Lulen “Willian Watts” en Córdoba, con el motivo de buscar algunas reliquias de su abuela quién había fallecido recientemente.

El contexto de la familia adoptiva de Lulen es clave para entender los hechos, ya que desde su adolescencia se vio enfrentado a la violencia psicológica y física que perpetuaba el padre hacia la madre; a la homofobia del padre por su orientación sexual y posteriormente por su transición de género.

El día de los hechos como era recurrente hubo una discusión. Lulen y Max se defienden golpeando a Willian Watts hasta que un vecino escucha gritos, interrumpe la pelea y llama a la policía. Watts se encontraba inconsciente por una supuesta asfixia, pero queda vivo y sin lesiones. Desde ese día en febrero del 2025 Lulen y Max se encuentran secuestrados, presos en la cárcel de Córdoba.

La fiscalía les condenó a 12 años y seis meses de cárcel por intento de homicidio agravado con tentativa, primero por el vinculo familiar, segundo por alevosía y tercero por una supuesta teoría de premeditación (tentativa).

Sin duda ha habido diferentes vulneraciones desde el sistema judicial en su totalidad, ya que no dan ninguna relevancia a los hechos de violencia consecutiva y daños previos ejercidos por Willian Watts, tampoco otorgan valor al transodio y sostienen una hipótesis de película sin entender la legítima defensa y el malestar que puede llevar a una persona a defenderse.

En palabras de su red de apoyo:

“A pesar de que cayeron casi todos los agravantes que pidió el fiscal, la condena es insólita en su dureza y no se tuvieron en cuenta las circunstancias atenuantes que pidió la defensa; la de años de abuso y violencia psicológica hacia Lulén por parte de su padre.”

“Aún transitando el dolor y la bronca, estamos dispuestos a seguir a la próxima instancia judicial para lograr un mejor resultado. Seguiremos con actividades para terminar de juntar el dinero para terminar de pagar la defensa y vamos a sostener y abrir la campaña de libertad para Lulén y Max. Porque no aceptamos este fallo y no dejaremos que todo lo que se presenció quede impune.”

“Las vidas Trans importan, y ningún fiscal transodiante ni menos un tribunal discriminatorio nos van a parar o amedrentar.”

author: CMI Argentina
title: Cómo fue el ataque a las trabajadoras sexuales trans en los Bosques de Palermo
content:
En la madrugada del domingo, un grupo de ciclistas atacó a mujeres trans que estaban realizando trabajo sexual en los Bosques de Palermo. La violencia que crece.


En la misma semana en que la Ciudad de Buenos Aires se prepara para la

35 Marcha del Orgullo

, un grupo de varones que participaba de una bicicleteada nocturna atacó a trabajadoras sexuales travestis y trans en los Bosques de Palermo el domingo en la madrugada. El hecho se difundió y viralizó a partir de los videos que los agresores subieron a las redes sociales. Y desataron el repudio de gran parte de la sociedad.


 


Ver esta publicación en Instagram


 


Una publicación compartida por Presentes (@presenteslatam)


Una mujer trans que estuvo presente cuando ocurrió la agresión contó a

Presentes

lo que vivió esa madrugada. A las chicas “las cercaron. Fue así como un torbellino, un huracán. Las rodearon a todas ellas en la esquina de Ombúes y Bello. No podías entrar a defenderlas porque eran más de 150 ciclistas”, dijo Leticia . “Fue como a las tres de la mañana. Pude zafar porque cuando vi que ellos venían con esa intención, que empezaban a insultar, a gritar y tenían cosas en la mano, me metí en el bosque”.


Desde la

Defensoría del Pueblo de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires

 informaron a esta agencia que, tras la agresión, hay varias mujeres trans heridas. “Lo que pudimos saber es que por lo menos hay seis compañeras lesionadas. Una bastante grave. No corre peligro de vida, pero tiene muy afectada una de sus orejas”, sostuvo María Rachid, titular del Instituto contra la Discriminación de la Defensoría del Pueblo de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires.


“Estamos trabajándolo y hablando con la fiscal Andrea Verónica Scanga, la fiscal especializada en discriminación, quien ya abrió de oficio una investigación. Vamos a aportar el testimonio de las compañeras que presenciaron la agresión, los videos y print de pantalla que tenemos”, agregó Rachid.


Qué se sabe de los hechos


Algunos de los agresores, luego de subir los videos, cambiaron la privacidad de sus cuentas mientras que otros difundieron versiones que tendrán que probar en la Justicia. Por ejemplo, “sugerir” que reaccionaron a un ataque, cuando, hasta ahora, no existe un solo video que registre el supuesto ataque. Por el contrario, varios muestran desde distintos ángulos las agresiones a las personas trans.


También dijeron que un grupo se separó del recorrido central de la bicicleteada organizada para la noche de Halloween que recorrió la Ciudad.


Desde la Federación Argentina LGBT+ (FALGBT+) presentaron una denuncia penal. “No vamos a tolerar la violencia ni la impunidad. Por eso, presentamos una denuncia penal exigiendo justicia y el esclarecimiento inmediato de los hechos. Frente al odio y los ataques, nuestra respuesta es la organización y la presencia en las calles”, expresaron a través de sus redes y convocaron a marchar el 7/11: “Que el orgullo en las calles sea nuestra resistencia”.


 


Ver esta publicación en Instagram


 


Una publicación compartida por Federación Argentina LGBT+ (@falgbt)


Violencia permanente


No es la primera vez que las trabajadoras sexuales de esa zona de la Ciudad sufren ataques. Hace más de un año que vienen denunciando en distintas oportunidades situaciones de hostigamiento y persecución por parte de la Policía de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires.


Los videos se conocieron horas antes del

Paro de Trabajadoras Sexuales

en el que, entre otros reclamos, plantearon los ataques y agresiones que se agudizaron en los últimos meses. “Estamos frente a una situación de violencia de manera permanente. Todo el tiempo nos llegan videos, mensajes, audios, denunciando violencia por parte de la policía y de los vecinos. En Palermo, en los bosques, los jóvenes van a la zona de trabajo sexual a violentar a las compañeras, filman con los celulares y suben ese contenido a TikTok o a sus redes sociales”, describió Georgina Orellano, secretaria general de la

Asociación de Mujeres Meretrices de Argentina

 (Ammar).  Ella misma fue detenida en varias oportunidades


Por el hecho interviene el

Ministerio Público de la Ciudad

, a través de la Unidad de Flagrancia Norte, a cargo de Ángel Palopoli, que dispuso iniciar actuaciones por “averiguación de lesiones”. Fuentes vinculadas con la investigación informaron a

Presentes

 que el caso se está investigando para determinar qué pasó. En el proceso se hizo un pedido para acceder al registro de las cámaras de la zona y a testigos.


Artistas …

title: Фестиваль «Дед Мороз против Путина» возвращается в Хельсинки!
content:
9 января 2027 года в столице Финляндии пройдет уже двенадцатый фестиваль «Дед Мороз против Путина».

История нашего фестиваля началась 12 лет назад, в 2014 году, с простой идеи: создать безопасное пространство в Хельсинки, где гражданские активисты могли бы открыто обсуждать политические и социальные проблемы России, делиться опытом и находить единомышленников.

С началом войны в Украине контекст радикально изменился. Сегодня наш фестиваль — это важнейшая точка сборки для всей русскоязычной эмиграции и солидарных жителей Финляндии.

Фестиваль создается для и силами новой волны российской эмиграции. Мы рады видеть антиавторитарных активистов, феминисток, антимилитаристов, антифашистов, правозащитников, художников и исследователей.

Наша площадка открыта для всех, кто был вынужден покинуть РФ, а также для жителей Финляндии, мигрантов и беженцев, которые поддерживают борьбу гражданского общества против путинского авторитарного олигархического режима.

Если вы хотите приблизить падение диктатуры, остановить войну и верите в потенциал массового оппозиционного движения — присоединяйтесь к нам!

Пока мы можем объявить одну из выступающих: Саша Казанцева, ЛГБТК-активистка, секспросветительница и блогерка, выступит с лекцией «Секс, ЛГБТ, Путин. Почему диктатуры борются с квирами и секспросветом?»

Между лекциями будет организован вкусный веганский обед по очень доступной цене.

В завершении вечера по обыкновению состоится музыкальный концерт. Исполнители будут объявлены позднее.
