title: Elisée Reclus - The Vivisection of China
content:
Author

: Elisée Reclus

Title

: The Vivisection of China

Date

: 1898

Notes

: From the September 1898 issue of The Atlantic

Source

: Retrieved on October 22, 2026 from an archived copy of https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/1898/09/the-vivisection-of-china/636369/


 THE great events which are creating such an excitement in the West Indies over the last shreds of the ancient colonial empire of Spain will undoubtedly have consequences of extreme importance, and become, in the fullest sense of the term, a part of history. But, however intense their interest, and however marked the change which they are certain to occasion in the equilibrium of the world, they remain altogether inferior in real significance to the revolutions which are taking place in the Far East.


 War of some sort between America and Spain on the subject of Cuba had long been unavoidable. No less than a century ago, — at the time when France lost her plantations in San Domingo, and the republic of Hayti was born, — it was easy to foresee the rupture of the ties which had bound to the Spain of Cortez and Pizarro the insular fragments of the great hemisphere appropriated by Pope Alexander VI. The various colonies were sure to break away, one by one, from their metropolitan stepmother, set up for themselves, and live their own life. Cuba and Porto Rico, sucked into the whirlpool of war, are but accomplishing their “manifest destiny,” and fulfilling the prophecies repeatedly uttered by the historians of the last generation but one.


 The progress of events in the eastern portion of the Asian continent had by no means been so fully anticipated. One might certainly have ventured to predict that there, also, populations long crushed by civil and military oppression would one day lay claim to the rights of free men; but it could never have been foreseen under what amazingly dramatic conditions the claim would be asserted. Our ancestors, at the beginning of the nineteenth century, would never have harbored, in their wildest dreams, the fantastic notion that Japan, the empire of the Rising Sun, would spontaneously transform itself into a “European power;” European, at least, if not in language, history, and traditions, in the complete recasting of its administration, institutions, customs, and theories, in its devotion to science, and in its entire and unreserved acceptance of a policy based on observation and experience.


 This is the great event of the century, — one which casts into the shade all the other occurrences of an epoch which has nevertheless been rich in memorable events. And it will be no solitary

avatar;

 there are unmistakable signs that other transformations of the same character are about to take place in the vast empire of China, and in all those countries where inhabitants of different race, yellow, red, or black, are brought into close contact with the men of our own Aryano - Greco - Latin civilization. So vanishes that oft-repeated assertion of the ethnologists, that

race

 is a final and irreducible fact, and that no possible progress in the perception of scientific or moral truths can ever prevail against it. It is from this point of view that the recent history of the Far East presents phenomena to which it behooves us to devote our most serious attention.


 There are those, of course, who tell us that all these events are illusory; that the prodigious changes which have taken place in the Japanese world are a lying phantasmagoria and a vain show; that the national mind and character have undergone no real modification; and that the Japanese are sure to escape, sooner or later, from the sphere of European attraction. We hear them compared to savages, who, having learned in the schools of London or Paris the customs of civilization, make haste, as soon as they get back to their forests and savannas, to cast aside their conventional garments, and array themselves in the toggery consecrated by ancestral instinct and hereditary custom.


 Such assertions appear to us to rest on a complete misconception of indisputable facts. The Japanese have most certainly entered into that realm of civilization on which Bacon and Darwin have set their seal; for if imperial caprice and the spread of bourgeois fashions have power to alter the external aspect of a nation, such influences can have but little effect on its underlying moral sense, its religious beliefs, its educational theories, and the essential principle of its …

author: Benji
title: Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies
content:
Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies

Tiere leiden vor dem Schlachten Höllenqualen bei CO₂-Betäubung

ARIWA veröffentlicht jetzt erstmals umfangreiche Aufnahmen aus einem Schlachthof von Tönnies. Schlachthöfe gehören zu den schwierigsten Herausforderungen für Undercover-Aufnahmen, da sie extrem gut gesichert sind. Die Betreiber setzen alles daran, dass das, was dort geschieht, nicht an die Öffentlichkeit gelangt.


19.10.2026, Deutschland


 NDR berichtet mit Videomaterial von ARIWA.


Er ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie: Tönnies. Als Marktführer produziert er 30 Prozent des gesamten deutschen Schweinefleischs. Allein 2023 meldete der Konzern einen Jahresumsatz von über 7 Milliarden Euro. Dafür tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen


Schweine. 


Das uns vorliegende Material zeigt, wie Mitarbeiter*innen die Tiere beim Zutrieb schlagen und sie unter automatischen Toren eingeklemmt werden. Es zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf in der CO₂-Anlage mit Tieren, die in Gondeln vor Angst schreien und versuchen zu fliehen. Und es zeigt zahlreiche Verstöße gegen die gesetzlichen Vorschriften vor und während der Schlachtung.


Von der Ankunft bis zum Tod:

Erste Undercover-Aufnahmen aus Tönnies Schlachthof


Das vorliegende Material dokumentiert erstmals unabhängig den gesamten Ablauf der Schlachtung von der Ankunft der Tiere im Schlachthof bis zur Tötung. Die Aufnahmen zeigen, wie leidvoll die letzten Stunden im Leben der Tiere sind. Das liegt auch an einer Maschine im Schlachthof, die grausamer nicht sein könnte: Die sogenannte CO₂-Betäubungsanlage.


Die Betäubung vor dem Schlachten ist gesetzlich vorgeschrieben. Die Tiere sollen so vor Schmerzen und Stress geschützt werden. Auch zur Betäubung selbst gibt es eindeutige Vorgaben: Paragraf 12 der Tierschutz-Schlachtverordnung legt fest, dass Tiere “schnell und unter Vermeidung von Schmerzen oder Leiden in einen (…) Zustand der Wahrnehmungs- und Empfindungslosigkeit” versetzt werden müssen. Der Betäubungsvorgang darf also keine Schmerzen oder Leid auslösen und muss bis zum Tod des Tieres anhalten. Doch die Aufnahmen zeigen eindeutig, dass die Betäubung mit CO₂ gegen diese Vorschrift verstößt!


Ankunft im Schlachthof


Am frühen Morgen kommen die ersten LKWs auf dem Schlachthof an. An den aufgenommenen Tagen werden mindestens fünftausend Schweine pro Tag hier angeliefert und getötet. Tönnies verfügt über ein riesiges Netz von Zulieferbetrieben in ganz Deutschland.


Nach ihrer Ankunft werden die Tiere in enge Wartebuchten gebracht. Hier läuft sanfte Musik, sie soll die Tiere entspannen. Es wirkt makaber. Neunzig Minuten lang sollen sich die vom Transport und Ausladen gestressten Schweine hier beruhigen, dabei ist zu erkennen, wie ängstlich sie sind.


Doch das wahre Grauen kommt erst noch. Nach anderthalb Stunden öffnet sich ein Tor. Ein Mitarbeiter beginnt, die Tiere in einen Treibgang zu scheuchen. Dabei kommt Gewalt zum Einsatz: Wenn die Schweine panisch versuchen zu fliehen, schlägt der Mitarbeiter mit der Treibstange zu, auch ins Gesicht. Die Schweine werden nach und nach in Sechsergruppen aufgeteilt. Als nächstes geht es für sie in die Betäubungsanlage.


Per Gondel in den Erstickungskampf


Die Schweine sind jetzt in einem engen Abteil, aus dem es kein Zurück gibt. Ein Mitarbeiter treibt die Gruppen nacheinander in die Gondelkäfige, mit denen es in wenigen Augenblicken gut 9 Meter nach unten in eine mit CO₂ gefüllte Grube geht. Manche Tiere werden von den schweren hydraulischen Trenngittern eingeklemmt und können sich nicht alleine befreien. Sie schreien vor Schmerz.


Sobald die erste Gruppe von Schweinen in ihre Gondel getrieben wurde, schließt sich der Käfig aus dicken Metallstangen. Kurze Zeit später setzt sich die Gondel in Bewegung. Die versteckte Kamera fährt mit. Innerhalb weniger Sekunden reagieren viele Schweine mit Panik. Viele schreien, schnappen nach Luft, werfen sich gegen die Gitterstäbe und steigen aufeinander. Die Fluchtversuche können so heftig sein, dass manche Tiere sich verletzen und Blutspuren an der Anlage zurücklassen.


Je tiefer die Tiere in den Schacht fahren, desto heftiger werden ihre Fluchtversuche. Die CO₂-Konzentration beträgt nach wenigen Metern schon 80 Prozent. Zeitgleich wird oben die nächste Gruppe in die Gondeln getrieben. Sie können die Angstschreie ihrer Artgenossen aus den Gondeln unter ihnen hören.

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als weibliches Rind in der Milchindustrie zu leben
content:
Die Milchindustrie ist ein grausamer Kreislauf des Leids und endet mit einem gewaltvollen Tod.


Wie fühlt es sich an, in dieses System hineingeboren zu werden, ohne die Möglichkeit, dem zu entkommen?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Auch du sollst Kinder gebären, immer wieder, damit du Milch produzierst. Milch, die dann von Menschen, statt von deinem Kalb konsumiert werden kann.


Du wirst fixiert, während jemand das Besamungsgerät in deine Vagina sowie seinen Arm in deinen Anus einführt. Wenn die Zwangsbefruchtung nicht beim ersten Mal zur Trächtigkeit führt – was oft der Fall ist –, wird dieser Vorgang mehrfach wiederholt.


Neun Monate – wie bei uns Menschen – wächst dein Kalb in dir heran. Du spürst eine Verbindung, merkst, wie es sich bewegt und immer größer wird. Je schwerer du selbst wirst, umso stärker werden deine Gelenkprobleme. Die rutschigen und harten Spaltenböden, auf denen du fast dein ganzes Leben verbringst, führen oft zu Verletzungen.


Dann bringst du dein Kalb zur Welt. Um dich herum riecht es extrem nach Kot und Ammoniak, von den Ausscheidungen der Tiere.


Endlich ist es da, noch ganz nass und schwach. Du leckst ihm über das Fell, um es zu wärmen. Es sucht deine Nähe und will an deinem Euter die für ihn so wichtige Erstmilch trinken. Sie stärkt sein noch schwaches Immunsystem und gibt ihm Kraft. Doch dann kommen die Arbeiter*innen.


Sie zerren dein noch ganz wackelig stehendes Kalb weg von dir. Es ruft nach dir. Du versuchst, bei ihm zu bleiben, aber du hast keine Chance. Die Menschen haben es weggebracht – du wirst es wahrscheinlich nie wiedersehen und nach nur zwei Monaten direkt wieder gewaltvoll befruchtet.


Du wirst nach der Geburt monatelang mehrmals täglich in den Melkstand getrieben – und die meiste Zeit davon bist du bereits wieder schwanger. Dein Körper muss gleichzeitig ein neues Kalb versorgen, das in dir heranwächst, und täglich über 22 Liter Milch produzieren. Dein Euter und deine Zitzen schmerzen. Aufgrund der extremen Überzüchtung produzierst du viermal so viel Milch, wie du es natürlicherweise für dein Kind tun würdest.


Die Prozeduren und Haltungsbedingungen zehren stark an deinem Körper. Dein Euter ist entzündet und schmerzt bei jeder Berührung. Andere Tiere humpeln, weil ihnen jeder Schritt wehtut. Viele sind schwach und ausgelaugt.


Wenn du nicht schon vorher stirbst oder getötet wirst, weil dein Körper nicht mehr kann, dann wirst du voraussichtlich nach nur fünf Jahren getötet – obwohl du unter natürlichen Bedingungen 25 Jahre alt werden könntest.


Dann kommt der Tag, an dem du als nicht mehr profitabel giltst. Du wirst aus dem Stall getrieben – das erste Mal nach Jahren verlässt du ihn, aber das ist kein Grund zur Freude.


Zusammen mit anderen erschöpften „ausgedienten Milchkühen“ wirst du auf einen Transporter verladen. Du hast Mühe, über die Rampe zu gehen. Deine Gelenke schmerzen vom jahrelangen Stehen auf Spaltenböden. Im engen Transporter stehst du dicht an dicht mit den anderen Tieren, der Lkw wackelt. Manche fallen hin und werden versehentlich getreten. Eure Fahrt in den Schlachthof dauert mehrere Stunden, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung, ohne Pause.


Angekommen erwartet dich ein brutaler Tod. Überall riecht es nach Blut, du bekommst Panik, aber es gibt keinen Ausweg. Dann ein Bolzenschuss in deinen Kopf. Wenn die Betäubung korrekt durchgeführt wurde und wirkt, brichst du zusammen. Wenn nicht, kann es sein, dass du bei Bewusstsein und unter extremen Schmerzen erlebst, wie dir deine Kehle aufgeschnitten wird und du verblutest.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Mutterrinder in der Milchindustrie erleiden müssen.


Der wahre Preis von Milch


Ein Ermittler von Animal Equality hat mehrere Monate undercover in einem deutschen Milchgewinnungsbetrieb gearbeitet und den Alltag der Tiere dokumentiert. Was unsere Undercover-Recherche zeigt, ist der wahre Preis von Milch: Ausbeutung, Gewalt, Schmerz, Leid und Tod.


Auf unserer Webseite erfährst du mehr und kannst die Stellungnahme des Betriebs nachlesen:


Zur Undercover-Recherche


Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht!


Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel. Im Supermarkt findest du zahlreiche Alternativen zu Milch, wie:


Hafermilch – mild, cremig, perfekt für Kaffee und Müsli (oft die günstigste Option!)


Sojamilch – proteinreich, ideal zum Kochen und Backen


Mandelmilch – leicht nussig, besonders lecker in Smoothies


Reismilch – süßlich und gut verträglich …

author: hsa_oryx
title: OCTOBER ROUND UP
content:
First conviction under Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023


October kicked off with

Glasgow Hunt Sabs

 reporting that Claire Bellamy, ex-huntswoman and former Master of the Lauderdale Hunt, was found guilty under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023. Footage which was obtained by sabs shows hounds chasing a fox outside the area covered by a licence that had been granted by NatureScot, and was described by the judge as “

gut wrenching

.” This is the first ever conviction under the new Scottish legislation and you can learn more about the legislation in Scotland and what led to Claire’s conviction

here.


Claire Bellamy found guilty of deliberately hunting a fox with dogs in January 2025.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs


Drone theft


On the 3

rd

 of October Dorset Borders Sabs reported that their drone had been stolen by The Cattistock Hunt as they hunted in Corscombe, Dorchester. The last image visible on the drone was a known member of the hunt running towards it in a field. The incident has been reported to the police and thanks to the generosity of supporters

Dorset Borders Sabs

 raised enough funds to replace the drone.


What do you do when you receive a CPW? If you’re a fox hunt then you break it as soon as possible of course


It didn’t take the Four Burrow Hunt long to break their Community Protection Warning (CPW) which had just been freshly issued by Devon and Cornwall Police. On the 10

th

 of October the hunt was caught breaking condition 7 of the CPW, by failing to give police 24 hours’ notice of their meet. As they had failed to give the details of the meet this means they won’t have provided a map of their “trail” meaning they will have broken more conditions that just number 7. It remains to be seen what action the police will take.

Read our recent article about CPW’s.


Four Burrow Hunt were issued with a CPW after years of trespass and livestock worrying.

Image:


Kernow Sabs, Monitors and Animal Rights Team-Cornwall


Stag hunting horror continues


The horror of stag hunting has continued to escalate in the south west. On the 12

th

 of October the Quantock Staghounds hunted a stag towards the A39 between Nether Stowey and Holford. This is a stretch of road where the hunt are continually causing chaos and putting people’s lives in danger.


This particular incident resulted in a

hunted stag running across the road and colliding with a car.

 A witness described how the terrified stag “

was flipped over the top of the car. Its leg kicked out smashing the rear nearside window. The Stag landed heavily on the verge.”

 Luckily the woman driving and her small child were not hurt but were badly shaken up.


The cruelty doesn’t end there. Two weeks later

North Dorset Hunt Sabs

 reported that the Quantock Staghounds had once again inflicted sickening suffering and pain on a stag. This particular large stag had a visibly infected wound on his side and it is also suspected he had a broken leg. These injuries unfortunately indicate that it is likely the stag that was hit by the car. Despite these injuries the hunt continued to torture him, subjecting him to a chase through thick gorse which no doubt would have caused him unbearable pain.


A stag hunted and terrorised by the Quantock Staghounds.

Credit: North Dorset Hunt Sabs


On the 22

nd

 of October hunt master of the Quantock Staghounds, Christopher Gibbons and huntsman Martin Watts, appeared at Taunton Magistrates Court. Gibbons is facing two counts of hunting a wild mammal under the Hunting Act, and Watts is facing one relating to the barbaric five-hour chase and ultimate

killing of a stag on the 23

rd

 of April 2026

. Both have pleaded not guilty and the case has been adjourned until the 18

th

 of January 2027 for a case management hearing; no trial date has been set. In the meantime, the Quantock Staghounds are continuing to commit abhorrent levels of animal cruelty whilst putting the safety of the general public at great risk.


This stag was tortured for five hours and ultimately killed on the 23

rd

 of April by the Quantock Staghounds.

 Huntsman and hunt master have both pleaded not guilty to charges under the Hunting Act.

Credit:


Mendip Hunt Sabs


They’re blatantly hunting foxes


Amidst the CPW’s, convictions, court hearings, road chaos and trespassing, foxes are still being chased, like the one pictured below.


Beds and Bucks Hunt Sabs

 along with

Peterborough Hunt Sabs

 have been keeping the pressure on …

author: PETA-Team
title: PETA Vegan Award 2027 – jetzt bewerben für den Bereich Food
content:
Immer mehr Menschen entscheiden sich für eine

vegane Lebens-

 und

Ernährungsweise

. Zudem greifen auch vermehrt Menschen auf vegane Alternativen zurück, die sich

vegetarisch

,

pescetarisch

 oder omnivor ernähren. Um der wachsenden Nachfrage in dieser Branche gerecht zu werden, bieten mittlerweile zahlreiche Marken und Unternehmen vegane Produkte an.


Um diese bemerkenswerte Entwicklung hin zu mehr Tierschutz durch ein zunehmendes veganes Produktangebot in der Ernährungsindustrie zu würdigen, verleihen wir von PETA Deutschland jährlich den

PETA Vegan Award im Bereich Food

.


Der PETA Vegan Award im Bereich Food


Mit unserer jährlichen Auszeichnung werden tierfreundliche vegane Lebensmittel wie Alternativen zu verschiedensten Milch-, Eier- und Fleischprodukten sowie Snacks und Fertiggerichte prämiert.Wir zeichnen zudem Produktreihen, Sortimente und Supermärkte für ihren Beitrag aus, eine vegane Ernährung in der Gesellschaft zu etablieren.


Der PETA Vegan Award ermöglicht den Gewinnern eine deutschlandweite, reichweitenstarke Plattform, um ihre herausragenden Produkte zu präsentieren, die vegan und tierfreundlich sind.


„Mit dem PETA Vegan Award im Bereich Food 2027 wollen wir zeigen,, dass tierfreie Innovationen nicht nur die Zukunft der Ernährung prägen, sondern auch Spaß machen, inspirieren und positive Veränderungen für Tiere, Menschen und unseren Planeten bewirken können. Jetzt ist die Zeit, eure Ideen sichtbar zu machen!“

Tobias Schalyo, Senior Corporate Engagement Manager bei PETA Deutschland


In den vergangenen Jahren wurden bereits Unternehmen und Marken wie LIDL mit der Eigenmarke VEMONDO, die Fleischalternativen von GREEN MOUNTAIN, Fischalternativen von UNFISHED, der Haferblock von THE VEGAN COW als Butteralternative und MAGNUM für sein veganes Angebot an Eis mit der heißbegehrten Auszeichnung gewürdigt.


		Jetzt bewerben


In diesen Kategorien werden Awards vergeben


Für den PETA Vegan Award 2027 im Bereich Food gibt es zwölf klar definierte Hauptkategorien. Pro Kategorie wird grundsätzlich maximal ein Award vergeben. So schaffen wir mehr Exklusivität der eingereichten Produkte.


Die Kategorien umfassen:


Beste vegane Innovation


Beste vegane Fleisch- oder Wurstalternative


Beste vegane Fisch- oder Meeresfrüchtealternative


Beste vegane Käsealternative


Beste vegane Milch- oder Joghurtalternative


Bestes veganes Frühstücksprodukt oder bester Aufstrich


Bestes veganes Convenience-Produkt


Bester veganer herzhafter Snack


Beste vegane Süßigkeit oder bestes Dessert


Beste vegane Sauce, bester Dip oder beste Würze


Bestes veganes Getränk


Bestes veganes Protein- oder Functional-Food-Produkt


Zusätzlich können bis zu zwei jährlich wechselnde Kategorien hinzukommen, sofern ausreichend qualifizierte Einreichungen vorliegen.


Unser Auswahl- und Bewertungsverfahren


Sie möchten ein Produkt für den PETA Vegan Award einreichen? Dann füllen Sie zunächst unser

Bewerbungsformular

 aus. Voraussetzung für die Teilnahme ist, dass das Produkt vollständig vegan ist und die Teilnahmebedingungen erfüllt.


Die eingereichten Produkte werden anschließend anhand dieser einheitlichen Bewertungsmatrix von unserer Jury beurteilt:


Geschmack, Textur und sensorische Qualität:

 30 %


Innovationsgrad:

 20 %


Potenzial, tierische Produkte zu ersetzen:

 20 %


Alltagstauglichkeit und Marktzugang:

 15 %


Nachhaltigkeit:

 10 %


Transparente und glaubwürdige Kommunikation:

 5 %


Für die Bewertung sind standardisierte Produkttests vorgesehen. Ein Produkt sollte dabei mindestens 75 von 100 Punkten erreichen, um für einen Award infrage zu kommen. Wenn kein Produkt die Qualitätsansprüche erfüllt, bleibt die Kategorie unbesetzt.


Während der Auswahl werden pro Kategorie drei Produkte für eine Shortlist nominiert. So erhalten diese bereits vor der Bekanntgabe der Gewinner zusätzliche Sichtbarkeit. Abschließend werden die ausgezeichneten Produkte in einer Award-Übersicht mit hochwertigen Grafiken und individuellen Jurybegründungen vorgestellt. Pro Marke wird grundsätzlich maximal ein Award vergeben.


So geht es nach der Verleihung des Awards weiter


Als ausgezeichnetes Unternehmen können Sie Ihren Award nutzen, um Ihr Produkt zu bewerben. Dazu können Sie das Award-Logo auf Ihrem Produkt einsetzen und die Auszeichnung gemeinsam mit uns kommunizieren.


Zudem bleiben wir mit allen teilnehmenden Unternehmen im Austausch. Dadurch möchten wir neue Kooperationen schaffen und langfristige Partnerschaften …

author: Unknown
title: Karasu: The Republic must be democratised according to today's understanding of democracy
content:
Mustafa Karasu, a member of the KCK Executive Council, spoke about current affairs during a special programme broadcast on Medya Haber.


The first part of this interview can be read

here

.


The AKP government is entering into various alliances, particularly in the region. The benefits and drawbacks of these alliances continue to be debated publicly. Can the AKP secure its own position through such alliances?


After Devlet Bahçeli made his call, what did both Bahçeli and Erdoğan repeatedly say? They said that we needed to strengthen the domestic front. They also described this process as one of strengthening the domestic front. Yes, resolving the Kurdish question means strengthening the domestic front. This is because, from the Ottoman period onward, whenever Turkey has come into conflict with the Kurds, it has lost. Whenever it has maintained positive relations with the Kurds, it has achieved stability and strengthened its position.


Indeed, one of the most important factors in the decline of the Ottoman Empire was its failure to resolve its problems with the Kurds. From the nineteenth century onward, it entered into conflict with them. Once it became hostile to the Kurds, it began to decline rapidly. Had it resolved the Kurdish question and adopted the right approach, the Ottoman Empire might not have disintegrated to the same extent. Now, if the government claims to be pursuing a policy of strengthening the domestic front and repeatedly emphasises this objective, yet then assumes that it can secure its position through alliances formed abroad, I have to say that this is a misconception. No matter what alliances you form abroad, they will not achieve much if you do not first consolidate the domestic front. They may even produce the opposite results. In fact, the anxiety that has led to the formation of so many alliances stems precisely from the failure to strengthen the domestic front. This is preparation for war. The formation of so many alliances in the Middle East, which lies at the centre of ongoing wars, amounts to preparation for such wars—or to taking sides on the various war fronts.


If the domestic front were strong, if Turkey genuinely resolved the Kurdish question and took steps towards democratisation, it would not feel the need—or fall into the misconception—that it could save itself by forming one alliance with this party and another with that one. In this respect, let me be clear: the formation of so many alliances is also taking place under the direction of certain external powers. In his statement, Tom Barrack indirectly indicated that the alliances Turkey is forming are known to us, serve our interests and form part of our policy; they are not separate from it.


Thus, this alliance policy may be an attempt to secure Turkey's position, but it also creates antagonisms. Every alliance is, at the same time, directed against someone else. Of course, a state can form alliances and may need to do so. But because Turkey has failed to consolidate its domestic front, it feels weak. Consequently, it considers entering into various alliances necessary—or, more precisely, it feels compelled to create new enmities.


We do not believe that Turkey can resolve its own problems through alliance policies. The policy of strengthening the domestic front is correct, and this is what the government says it is pursuing. Yet instead of fulfilling the requirements of that policy and strengthening the domestic front, the government prefers to create its own fronts abroad and take sides in existing conflicts. This will not benefit Turkey very much. Turkey will suffer the consequences.


Abdullah Öcalan, the leader of the peoples, has described the process he initiated as one of change and transformation. In this context, efforts to organise a movement for a democratic republic are also on the agenda in the field of political struggle. What would you like to say about these discussions?


A republic was established in Turkey. Yes, a republic is a system of government in which those in power come to office through elections. Of course, a republic does not automatically mean direct democracy. There are many republics in the world that are undemocratic, even dictatorial. Conversely, there are countries without republics, where monarchies still exist, and certain offices are not filled through elections. Sweden, Norway and the Netherlands are examples, yet these countries do have certain democratic institutions, albeit …

author: Marianne Lavelle
title: Activists Hope Midterm Wins Set the Stage for Renewed Energy and Climate Policy
content:
Environmental advocates point out voters are angry at Big Oil, which is making record profits while families struggle.

Environmental advocates point out voters are angry at Big Oil, which is making record profits while families struggle.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Democrats on Tuesday won control of both houses of Congress and a decisive mandate to put a check on Donald Trump’s tumultuous presidency, a victory propelled by voter anger over high prices, corruption and the unchecked spread of data centers.

Some of the same concerns helped to lift Democrats to victories in statehouses, where they gained a majority of the country’s governorships for the first time in more than a decade.

Voters in Ohio, South Carolina and Texas — states Trump won by double digits two years ago — put Democrats over the top in the U.S. Senate. And the Democratic wave surmounted a seawall of money: the unprecedented spending the GOP’s tech industry allies poured into the races in recent weeks to protect the status quo and their freedom from regulation.

Activists believe the result sets the stage for renewed environmental and climate policy, even though candidates seldom mentioned those issues by name in their campaigns. They argue that any action Congress takes on voters’ top issues — soaring energy prices, undue industry influence and the surge of artificial intelligence infrastructure — will curb the upward trajectory of U.S. fossil fuel consumption that Trump has encouraged.

“Voters rejected the Trump administration’s failing energy policies, which have pushed electricity bills higher,” said David Kieve, president of EDF Action, the political arm of the nonprofit Environmental Defense Fund, which invested $18 million in the midterms. “Families know that blocking clean energy raises rates. Paying companies to abandon wind projects, canceling grants meant to lower rural utility bills, and using emergency orders to keep coal plants running when cleaner, cheaper options are available all moved us in the wrong direction.”

A president’s party typically loses seats in Congress in midterm elections, and in the face of that history, Trump urged voters to “pretend I’m on the ballot.” The results indicated that voters listened. Trump’s sagging approval became a millstone Republicans were forced to carry, as opponents attacked them for their complicity in an unpopular war that had caused U.S. energy prices to soar. (The decision to unilaterally join Israel in airstrikes against Iran on Feb. 28 resulted in “incalculable political damage for Trump’s party,” political pundit Charlie Cook wrote on the eve of the election.)

In unfortunate timing for Republicans, the U.S. oil industry last week reported its profits — $130 billion over the past six months, or triple the earnings of one year ago, all due to the war-related run-up in prices. On the campaign trail, Trump tried to frame the oil industry’s boon as a blessing for Americans.

“They’re making hundreds of billions of dollars — our country is — on oil,” Trump said at an Oct. 26 rally in Georgia. Trump said his advisers warned him not to mention that “because people are paying a little bit higher,” but he said he didn’t care how his words would be portrayed. “I don’t give a damn,” he said. “We’re making a freaking fortune!”

But Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) seemed to better capture the mood of his state’s voters in his last days of campaigning for reelection: “Under failed president Donald J. Trump, it costs more than ever in American history to fill up your truck, stock your fridge, visit the doctor or power your home.” Ossoff coasted to re-election as expected, and former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated Republican Rick Jackson to win the Georgia governor’s race.

Opposition to data centers helped Democrats in many races, such as in Ohio, where Democrat Sherrod Brown staged a political comeback and defeated Republican Sen. Jon Husted. Brown dubbed his opponent “the face of data centers,” and sought to tie Husted to tax breaks and other policies that have attracted the giant computing centers to Ohio.

Trump’s foes — including environmental groups — blanketed the airwaves in swing states and districts with ads tying the pain of high gasoline and electricity prices to cozy Republican relationships with oil and utility companies, tech giants and the insurance industry …

author: David Swanson
title: Young Voters’ Congress in Chicago Declared What Issues Mattered Most in Then-Upcoming U.S. Elections
content:
By

World BEYOND War – Illinois

, November 4, 2026


Baby Boomers, Gen Xers, Gen Z, and Millennials exchanged ideas about issues mattering the most to them in the November elections.


Featured speakers included:


Kayla Pilgrim, Communications Lead for Sunrise Movement Chicago


Tree Palmeras, Director of Black Lives Matter Chicago


Henna Ayesh, Media Liaison during DePaul University’s spring 2024 student encampment for Palestine


CODEPINK National Co-Director Danaka Katovich


Kathy Kelly, Board President of World BEYOND War


3-time Emmy-nominated poet Trey Baker


The Young Voters’ Congress aimed to amplify the voices of young people whose concerns about genocide, ecological collapse, racism, nuclear weapons, and affordability are overlooked while powerful institutions instead pay heed to billionaires and the executives of corporations that provision war-makers with weapons, exacerbate the potential for ecological collapse, endanger the lives of migrants, and expand the prison-industrial complex.


“Many young people whose voices have been stifled and censured look forward to the upcoming elections,” said Annie James, a lead organizer for the event who decided to intern with the Illinois World BEYOND War chapter after nearing completion of her studies as a peace and justice major at DePaul U. “The Young Voters’ Congress welcomed people to declare which issues will most influence them at the polls and in formation of future alliances.”


Kayla Pilgrim, Communications Lead for Sunrise Movement Chicago, was the keynote speaker. Profound concern for two younger sisters affected by asthma had motivated Kayla to tackle issues related to poisoned environments. At age 20, she has learned to connect the dots and called on the assembled group to join her in overcoming fears by forming community and becoming active.


“We are here to first crush fascism,” Kayla noted. She decried abuses of the military-industrial-media-congressional complex and urged the DNC to stop funding genocide and instead fund efforts to avoid ecological collapse. Kayla noted that the Sunrise Movement in Chicago had recently occupied AIPAC offices in Chicago to protest support for candidates tolerating Israel’s genocide against Palestinians. She also issued a call for Illinois residents to oust ICE for good.


A panel entitled “Militarism, Racism, Inequality and Climate Collapse: The Tentacles of the War Machine,” moderated by CODEPINK’s Danaka Katovich, featured Tree Palmeras, Director of Black Lives Matter, Chicago, and Henna Ayesh from the DePaul University 2024 encampment for Palestine. They covered issues ranging from motivation for activism to the repugnance of paying taxes to kill children at home and abroad.


Henna Ayesh noted the irony of the United States, on land stolen from Indigenous peoples, provisioning weapons and surveillance capacities to Israel for use in perpetrating Israeli genocide against Palestinians.


Panelist Tree Palmeras said Haitian family members encouraged her, as a child, to resist militarism. She decried the violence that decimates communities whether perpetrated by U.S. wars abroad, or though heavily militarized policing and incarceration in U.S. cities.


Danaka Katovich (CODEPINK), the panel moderator, called on participants to resist the NDAA (National Defense Authorization Act) 1033 program, which donates surplus U.S. Department of War weapons to U.S. police departments. She also noted that the U.S. Department of War funds Quantum Computing in Chicago.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: NTI has a plan to adapt to climate change but needs money to implement it
content:
Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. has set a new vision for responding to climate change in the territory.


The plan – Anijaarniq Strategy: An Inuit Approach to Addressing Climate Change in Nunavut – identifies 15 goals based on engagement sessions with Nunavummiut. 


Nunavut’s three Inuit associations, the Kitikmeot Inuit Association, Kivalliq Inuit Association, and Qikiqtani Inuit Association hosted the workshops over 2024 and 2025. 


“This is one of the most intensive processes I believe that we’ve gone through in terms of the development of a strategy,”

 said NTI research director Cheryl Wray, who oversaw the development of the

Anijaarniq Strategy

.


The plan calls on the territorial and federal governments to commit money to achieve the goals identified in it, which include building more climate-resilient housing; transitioning to renewable energy systems; and creating Inuit-led climate research and adaptation programs. 


“We require funding for this plan to be actionable,” Wray said.

“This is a plan which requires all partners to come to the table.”


She said NTI has yet to decide how much to ask for from each government.


Those consulted as part of the plan said their top concerns are rapid changes in sea ice, harms to wildlife, unsafe travel, permafrost thaw and extreme weather events.


“One of the key issues that we’re facing up here is the delay in the sea ice freezing, especially for the migrating animals like caribou,” said Derek Elias, a business development officer with the Kitikmeot Inuit Association who organized the engagement session in Cambridge Bay. “We’ve had animals drown when trying to cross.”


He said the sea ice between Victoria Island and the mainland forms later each fall and isn’t as thick as it used to be. 


“We’re just hoping that the territorial government is going to take climate change seriously and [provide] the appropriate funding, tools and resources for us to be able to tackle climate change and its effects,” Elias said. “It’s for our future generations.”


GN Environment Department spokesperson Estęla Aguilar declined to answer questions about how the department intends to work with NTI.


In a statement to Nunatsiaq News, Carolane Gratton, spokesperson for Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada,

said the department recognizes the importance of “predictable, long-term climate funding.”

She noted that it helped fund the development of the action plan.


She also said that since 2016, the department has provided NTI with over $8 million to support climate adaptation initiatives and policy development.


Over the same time frame, she said, the department also committed $90 million into infrastructure vulnerability assessments, clean energy and emergency preparedness in Nunavut.

author: Kavita Naidu
title: Kavita Naidu: You cannot destroy the Global South for the Global North’s renewable transition
content:
Kavita Naidu is an international human rights lawyer and feminist climate activist from Fiji. She delivered this speech at the No Cop-Outs at COP31: Climate Action Now rally at Sydney Town Hall on Gadigal Country, on October 24.

For the Pacific, going above 1.5 degrees is a death sentence we will not be quiet about.

The 1.5 degree threshold is not only anchored in the International Court of Justice (ICJ), it was also what the Pacific pushed for in the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea and the Inter-American Court of Human Rights.

For the first time we have a very powerful legal floor, and you can see in Australia there are legal cases which will establish what these advisory opinions mean in practice.

Pacific rejects false climate solutions

Pacific community service organisations met in Tuvalu ahead of Pre-COP in Fiji to issue the Funafuti Call for Climate Justice, which speaks for Pacific peoples. The rallying cry was “Lose Tuvalu, Lose our World”.

The Pacific is calling for an immediate phase out of coal, oil and gas and an end to new exploration, licensing, expansion and subsidies, with developed states phasing out first and fastest.

We are rejecting all false solutions, including carbon capture and storage, nuclear energy, offsetting, geoengineering and “managed transition pathways” as substitutes for cutting production.

We reject deep-sea mining, we reject a “just transition” based on green and blue colonialism, opening frontiers of dispossession of land and oceans to sate the need for developed states to transition.

A transition for who? And a transition for what? We are not questioning the consumption of energy as a problem, we are simply looking at the source of energy and we need to beyond this.

You cannot destroy and extract from the Global South to suit the transition needs of the Global North, that is not just and equitable.

We do not understand, because so much of it is greenwashed, but the rush for critical rare earth minerals is not just for solar panels, it is tied to the militarisation of this region. It is tied to missiles and drones.

You just need to see the billions the Australian government is putting into militarisation, because they want to go for our land and oceans and they need a military to protect those resources.

The Funafati Call rejects a securitised, militarised and nuclearised Pacific. It names AUKUS, the Papua New Guinea–Australia Mutual Defence Treaty (Pukpuk Treaty) and the Vuvale Union as attempts to seize control of our economic resources and make us beholden to what the Australian government demands of us.

We condemn all missile testing in our waters and we condemn any future weapons testing in our waters.

We assert our right to remain on our islands with dignity. We reject mobility deals traded against the sovereignty and security of our people.

The Pacific is a region that is still occupied. Struggles for self-determination continue in West Papua, Guam, Kanaky and Tahiti.

We cannot talk about climate justice without recognising self-determination of the indigenous people who continue to be on the frontlines of the worst climate impacts in this region.

This is why we must call out our Pacific leaders for endorsing Zionism by supporting Israel at the United Nations, opening Israeli embassies in the region and signing “development cooperation” deals.

We reject endorsing a genocidal state and commit to tackling the scourge of Zionist fundamentalism on our islands.

The other thing about the Pacific that people don’t understand is that we have among the highest rates of violence against women in the world. We recognise that we must incorporate gender justice into our climate justice campaigns.

That includes recognising and redistributing unpaid care, social protection guarantees and attention to gender-based violence and sexual and reproductive health rights.

The Pacific has also been very progressive in recognising how artificial intelligence and data centres are coming for us. We already have data centres being built, subsea cables and other digital infrastructure in the region, but their energy, water and emissions footprints are not being disclosed.

The Pacific asserts data sovereignty and the protection of indigenous knowledge from AI. We also question the duality of purpose of AI and its use for military surveillance and intelligence.

We will not be complicit in killing people in other parts of the world by providing the infrastructure in …

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: St’át’imc Chiefs Council challenges Ottawa’s pipeline plans in court
content:
A group of First Nations in British Columbia announced they have filed a federal court application for a judicial review of the federal government’s decision to fast-track the proposed Pacific Link oil pipeline between Alberta and BC as a “project of national interest.” In a press conference held in Richmond B.C. this morning, members of the St’át’imc Chiefs Council — representing eleven Nations of the St’át’imc people (also known as Lilloee) —decried what they called a lack of consultation and stressed the need for the courts to slow the developmental process.

Chief Bonnie Adolph of the Sekw’el’was (Cayoose Creek) First Nation began by outlining threats to the salmon upon which her people rely. She said that when her community wrote to the Major Projects Office asking to be consulted about listing the project under the Build Canada Act, they were told since their land was not on the proposed pipeline route, the Crown would not consult with them.

“When we told the Major Projects Office their narrow geographic approach failed to account for downstream, interconnected and cumulative environmental risks to our inherent St’át’imc title and rights,” Adolph said, “We were told that we could send comments like any member of the public, but not as a First Nation whom the Crown had a legal [duty] to consult. This is not lawful, this is not constitutional, this is not consistent with the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous People.”

The salmon central to the lives of St’át’imc people are all over the waters threatened by an oil spill from the pipeline, said Chief Travis Peters from N’Quatqua (Anderson Lake) First Nation.

“The salmon we rely upon travel the Fraser Estuary and the Fraser River twice,” he explained. “Once, as juveniles heading out to the ocean, and [again] as adults returning home to spawn. There are salmon in the river system almost all year. The idea of the construction of new crude oil infrastructure in the heart of the Fraser River Estuary on unstable soil is terrifying.

“What happens if there’s an earthquake? What happens if the pipeline leaks? What happens if the tankers run aground?”

Peters noted that 100 First Nations signed the 2010 Save the Fraser Declaration, but “if anything, the health of the Fraser River salmon has only worsened since 2010. The cumulative impacts of climate change and development have become more severe.”

Chief Justin Kane from Ts’kw’aylaxw First Nation (formerly Pavilion Indian Band), who is also Chair for the St’át’imc Chiefs Council, said the Chiefs Council filed for a judicial review because the federal court failed to meet its constitutional duties to St’át’imc.

“We know this project could have serious, potentially catastrophic risks for our fishing rights and way of life,” he told media. “Salmon is part of who we are. It’s part of our identity. And we have the right to understand what those risks are and to be immediately consulted about whether they are actually working.”

The federal government forced the Chiefs’ hands, Kane said, by insisting that the only question is how — and not if — the project will go ahead.

“If this decision is not challenged in court,” Kane argued, “it sets a dangerous precedent all Canadians should be concerned about. It is foolhardy for the government to try to push through a project at breakneck speed without proper assessment and consultation. Canada is attempting to circumvent its own laws, and ours.”

He said Ottawa has said it would consult with First Nations later, despite the fact that the project is moving ahead.

“Because the Pacific Link is listed under the Building Canada Act,” he said, “the Act says it must be granted a conditional document that is deemed to be all environmental approvals for the project. How can the future of consultation be meaningful if the decision is already made?”

Hugh Braker is a member of Tseshaht First Nation on Vancouver Island as well as of the First Nations Summit Political Executive.

In his statement to media, Braker noted that Mark Carney has said repeatedly that taking action to protect against climate change is “a moral duty.”

“Those were his words,” Braker said. “And what’s he doing about it? He’s building a pipeline. Probably the worst thing he could do. Our prime minister wears a coat of hypocrisy. And he has to realize that. He has to realize that things like life expectancy are going down because of climate change.”

author: Unknown
title: Ejército Zapatista de Liberación Nacional - Don’t Forsake Us!
content:
Author

: Ejército Zapatista de Liberación Nacional

Title

: Don’t Forsake Us!

Subtitle

: Zapatista Women in ’94

Date

: 1994

Notes

: Originally published by Ediciones OnA, València-Chiapas: 1

st

 edition May 2018, 2

nd

 edition January 2019, 3

rd

 edition July 2019, 4

th

 edition January 2020.

 English translation by Ediciones Bloodfruit/Malvivientes, 2026.

Source

: Retrieved 10/30/26 from https://www.patreon.com/bloodfruit/posts/dont-forsake-us-173797846


 The money raised from the this first volume are going to the benefit of Compañera M. Mother,

 Social Warrior, Multiply Employed, Indigenous.


 The best way to understand the path of the women who struggle is through their own words. These brief texts, interviews and declarations of the women of the Zapatista Army for National Liberation in the first months of the armed uprising of 1994 showcase the situation of indigenous women in Mexican territory, and are a mirror of the dignity that has kept the Zapatista struggle alive despite male chauvinism, racism and capitalism.


 This edition was part of a mutual aid initiative to redistribute the

funds of the circulating texts and “Independent” editions among

the struggles’ female protagonists


Words From Comandanta Ramona and Major Ana María


Another concern that indigenous

women have is the free choice of partners.


“The dowry custom still exists,

the girl is never taken into account,

she is sold off (in this region,

the average price of nuptial dowry is

two thousand pesos). The idea of

having a boyfriend doesn’t exist; it is sin.”


 Ana María, Infantry Major: “Don’t Forsake Us!” is the desperate plea of the women of the Zapatista Army for National Liberation so that their hopes of being heard within and without their communities may not die. “We ask all women to fight alongside us” is what Comandanta Ramona and Major Ana María say in Tzotzil and Spanish. Their call to Mexican women is not one to take up arms, but rather so that, within their spaces, they may support the changes proposed by the Revolutionary Law of Women, as well as their extensive list over equality, justice, health, education and housing. That night, the penultimate they would spend at the Cathedral, they arrived through the back of the altar, accompanied by Subcomandante Marcos.


 He, dressed in his unmistakable military uniform. Some steps behind, the only two women of a group of the 19 delegates of the Indigenous Clandestine Revolutionary Committee. “I’ll leave them with you so that you can speak to them about anything you wish,” he said in a joking tone as he bid his farewell to the group of five female reporters and two photographers intent on interviewing the women of the Zapatista Army. Ramona’s wide and sharp eyes revealed weariness. The black wool skirt, the beautifully embroidered loom-woven blouse, and her short stature contrasted with Ana María’s gray

ruana

 and sturdy frame. Alongside them, Comandante Javier remained behind (to translate Ramona’s Tzotzil’s words into Spanish). The words of the Comandanta, even if in Tzotzil, flow smoothly from her indigenous heart.


 I left my community in search of work because of necessity itself, there was no longer anything to live off of. When I arrived someplace else I began to learn that it wasn’t the same situation as that of women in the countryside. I learned there to understand and gain conscience of the differences, that’s how I learned of the organization (EZLN), and that it was also necessary to organize women.


 Within EZLN women’s participation in key. Ramona belongs to the political group that works in the communities; Ana María is part of the approximately 30% of female combatants/insurgents who voluntarily refuse to form a family in order to engage in armed struggle.


 “I am an insurgent. I’ve dedicated my entire life and time to the cause,” affirms Ana María, a 26 year old Infantry Major who, when speaking of displacement and suffering endured, furrows her brows in sadness, the only sign of expression able to be seen beneath her balaclava. “It’s a long story,” she says,


 Ever since I was eight years old I took part in peaceful struggles, in marches, in meetings. My family was one that fought, that always organized in order to have a dignified life, but that never achieved it through that route. We were in an organization —won’t say which— with other persons, with other peoples. We would go there, the children too, and that’s how we went began …

author: Kay Pacha / Equipo Pueblos Originarios del SERPAJ
title: La UNSa y su trabajo con los Pueblos Originarios
content:
Recordando que el reciente 12 de octubre, el Día del respeto a la Diversidad Cultural, en todo el país hubo actividades llevadas a cabo por organizaciones y comunidades originarias.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Pastrana-david.-Pueblos.mp3


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Pastrana-david.-Pueblos.mp3


Descargar archivo


Y uno de esos lugares fue la Provincia de Salta, en donde la Universidad Nacional de Salta reunió a referentes de pueblos originarios, autoridades, realizadores audiovisuales y miembros de la comunidad en una jornada de diálogo, memoria y reconocimiento de las realidades territoriales.


Esa actividad se llamó “Voces del Territorio: Memoria, Identidad y Continuidad” en donde se proyectó la Película “Senda India”, con la presencia de la directora Daniela Seggiaro.


Esto dio lugar a espacios de intercambio y debate sobre la situación territorial de los pueblos originarios y la agenda legislativa vinculada a sus derechos.


Cabe destacar que la película se hizo tomando como base las filmaciones realizadas por el joven wichí Miguel Ángel Lorenzo, quien filmó con una cámara de video Hi8, con humor, sensibilidad y junto a sus paisanos, recorridos por el monte, por casas vecinas, en actos escolares, pericias arqueológicas y visitas de un juez, como parte de las pruebas para un juicio que llevaba adelante su comunidad desde 1986.


Esta jornada fue organizada de manera conjunta por la Universidad Nacional de Salta, a través de la Coordinación de Pueblos Originarios de la UNSa, el Instituto Provincial de Pueblos Indígenas de Salta (IPPIS), el C.I.P.I., el MinPPi y EIB Salta.


Por eso, contamos ahora con el testimonio de David Pastrana, Coordinador de Pueblos Originarios de la UNSa, quien comenta con más detalles acerca de las reflexiones que tuvieron lugar en esa oportunidad. Agradecemos al programa Protagonistas de la Mañana de la Radio Universidad de Salta por este material.


El Micro Kay Pacha se realiza con el apoyo de la organización Otto per Mille-Chiessa Valdense

author: Stelinsky
title: Μπέικον και δουλεία
content:
Το σημερινό άρθρο είναι επετειακό. Πριν από 350 χρόνια διαδραματίστηκαν στην αγγλοκρατούμενη ακόμα Αμερική τα γεγονότα που επιτάχυναν την εδραίωση της δουλείας στην αμερικανική ήπειρο, και η αφορμή ήταν στην περιοχή της Βιρτζίνια, και συγκεκριμένα στην πόλη του Τζέιμς Τάουν, και αυτή θα παρουσιάσουμε σήμερα.

Ας τα πιάσουμε όμως από την αρχή. Υπάρχει μία εύλογη ερώτηση στην ατμόσφαιρα· πριν από το 1676 δεν υπήρχε δηλαδή δουλεία στην Αμερική; Υπήρχε, απλά αποτελούσε εκείνη την περίοδο τη μειοψηφία στις εργασιακές σχέσεις. Η πιο διαδεδομένη όμως εργασιακή σχέση ήταν κάπως διαφορετική. Για να μπορέσει η Βρετανική Αυτοκρατορία να αποικίσει την ανατολική ακτή των σημερινών Ηνωμένων Πολιτειών, πρόσφερε στους μεγαλοκαλλιεργητές κάποια κίνητρα για να προσελκύσουν Άγγλους υπηκόους. Μέσω μίας σύμβασης με έναν τσιφλικά μπορούσες να προσληφθείς για 3 με 7 χρόνια, και να εργαστείς στις αμέτρητες εκτάσεις καπνού που είχε στην προκειμένη περίπτωση η Βιρτζίνια, και μετά το πέρας του συμφωνημένου χρόνου δικαιούσουν μία μικρή έκταση για να γίνεις και εσύ από μεριάς σου ένας αγρότης με το δικό του χωράφι. Ο «εργοδότης» σου από την άλλη, για κάθε έναν νέο άποικο που ερχόταν για λογαριασμό του, έπαιρνε 50 εκτάρια γης, και μόνη του έγνοια ήταν να σου πληρώσει ένα εισιτήριο για να έρθεις μέχρι την Αμερική, και αρκετό φαΐ ώστε να επιβιώνεις. Αυτή η σύμβαση ήταν καλύτερη από την απόκτηση ενός δούλου για τον εξής λόγο: Εάν εσύ που είχες υπογράψει τη σύμβαση πέθαινες, είτε κατά τη διάρκεια του ταξιδιού, είτε εξαιτίας των ασθενειών ή των συνθηκών που επικρατούσαν στην άλλη μεριά του Ατλαντικού, τότε ο τσιφλικάς είχε αποκτήσει τα 50 εκτάρια, και για την αντικατάστασή σου απλά θα έβρισκε κάποιον άλλον φουκαρά που θα ήθελε να ξεφύγει από την ανέχεια. Αντιθέτως για τους τσιφλικάδες η αγορά από τα σκλαβοκάραβα, που έφερναν σωρηδόν κόσμο από την Αφρική, ήταν μια μπίζνα ριψοκίνδυνη καθώς αγόραζαν ανθρώπους σε μία εποχή που η θνησιμότητα βάραγε κόκκινο.

Η δεκαετία του 1670 όμως δεν είναι και τόσο καλή για τον κόσμο που έρχεται στην Αμερική από το Ηνωμένο Βασίλειο. Κυβερνήτης της Βιρτζίνια είναι ένας από τους αγαπημένους του στέμματος, ο ηλικιωμένος Μπέρκλεϊ, ο οποίος έχει δημιουργήσει μια σταθερή κατάσταση στην περιοχή. Οι εχθροπραξίες με τους ιθαγενείς είχαν περιοριστεί, αλλά ο Μπέρκλεϊ είχε και σοβαρές εμπορικές δραστηριότητες μαζί τους. Έτσι και έσοδα έρχονται και δεν είναι υποχρεωμένοι να πληρώνουν για σοβαρά έξοδα για τη φύλαξη της περιοχής. Το πρόβλημα πού βρίσκεται λοιπόν; Κόσμος έρχεται στην Βιρτζίνια, δουλεύει στα καπνά, αλλά δεν υπάρχει η απαραίτητη γη για να τους δοθεί ως αντάλλαγμα. Έτσι έχουμε στα περίχωρα του Τζέιμς Τάουν ένα μείγμα λευκών δυσαρεστημένων που θέλουν περισσότερα από αυτά που τους δίνει η εξουσία. Και για αυτή την κατάσταση φταίνε φυσικά από τη μία ο Μπέρκλεϊ και από την άλλη οι ιθαγενείς. Και εδώ εμφανίζεται ο ήρωας της σημερινής ιστορίας· το όνομα αυτού Ναθάνιαλ Μπέικον. Ο Μπέικον δεν είναι κάποιος τυχαίος. Τον έστειλε ο πατέρας του από την Αγγλία στη Βιρτζίνια, αγόρασε εκεί εκτάσεις και έγινε τσιφλικάς στα περίχωρα κοντά στα νοητά σύνορα με τους ιθαγενείς. Φαινομενικά στην όλη κατάσταση ο Μπέικον δεν είχε κανέναν λόγο να εμπλακεί. Ήταν ένας γενικά κλειστός άνθρωπος, χωρίς κάποιο ιδιαίτερο ενδιαφέρον για τα κοινά. Όμως μία σειρά αντεγκλήσεων με ιθαγενείς στην περιοχή, οι οποίες δεν αφορούσαν καν τον ίδιο, τον έκαναν να αναλάβει δράση. Χαρακτηριστικό παράδειγμα είναι η σύλληψη από μέρους του κάποιων ιθαγενών οι οποίοι, σύμφωνα πάντα με τον Θάνο μας, έκλεψαν καλαμπόκι το οποίο δεν ήταν καν δικό του. Ταυτόχρονα η συμβιβαστική στάση του Μπέρκλεϊ τού δημιουργεί την εικόνα μίας διεφθαρμένης κλίκας στο Τζέιμς Τάουν που δεν νοιάζεται να αντιμετωπίσει τα προβλήματα των κατοίκων της.

Έτσι, λοιπόν, ο Μπέικον αποφασίζει να πάρει την κατάσταση στα χέρια του. Δημιουργεί μία πολιτοφυλακή με άλλους κατοίκους (λευκούς και Αφρικανούς) και μπαίνει σε εδάφη των ιθαγενών και ξεκληρίζει χωριά. Ο κυβερνήτης Μπέρκλεϊ κρατάει μία αρκετά συμβιβαστική στάση και προσπαθεί να ηρεμήσει τα πράγματα, αλλά ο Μπέικον είναι ανένδοτος, αναγκάζοντας τον πρώτο να τον κηρύξει στασιαστή. Έτσι τον Ιούλιο του 1676 ο Θάνος γράφει τη Διακήρυξη του Λαού· ένα δριμύ κατηγορώ απέναντι στον κυβερνήτη που του επιρρίπτει ευθύνες για τον κίνδυνο που διατρέχουν οι κάτοικοι της περιοχής, για τη βαριά φορολογία και τον αποκλεισμό του κόσμου από τα κέντρα λήψης αποφάσεων. Ένα μανιφέστο αρκετά ωραίο στα αυτιά, αλλά που επ’ ουδενί δεν επιδιώκει να δώσει κάποια πιο δημοκρατική …

author: Darío Aranda
title: Del cautiverio doméstico al tráfico de especies: “La fauna silvestre no es mascota”
content:
Por Ivonne Guevara


Una tortuga en un patio, un loro en una jaula o un animal exótico dentro de una casa pueden parecer escenas inocentes, hasta pintorescas. Pero detrás del mascotismo de fauna silvestre hay pérdida de biodiversidad, riesgos sanitarios y un tráfico ilegal que se cuenta entre los mercados ilícitos más lucrativos del mundo. Claudia Nigro, activista y veterinaria, aclara: “Bastaría con decir que sin vida silvestre la especie humana no podría sobrevivir en el planeta”.


A veces la relación entre las personas y la fauna silvestre comienza con una intención que parece buena, como cuidar, proteger, tener cerca, darle “hogar”. El problema aparece cuando ese vínculo se transforma en apropiación.

El ser humano domesticó algunas especies y las convirtió en animales de compañía hace miles de años. Sin embargo, aquella relación construida a lo largo de generaciones suele confundirse todavía con otra muy distinta, la de querer tener cerca, poseer o encerrar a un animal porque resulta bello, exótico o entrañable.


El problema excede largamente al ejemplar encerrado en una jaula.

El comercio ilegal de vida silvestre mueve,

según Interpol

, hasta 20.000


millones de dólares

 por año a escala mundial y se encuentra asociado con otras formas de criminalidad organizada. Detrás de muchos animales que terminan en una casa existe una cadena previa de captura, traslado, comercialización y muerte.

Nigro es médica veterinaria de la Universidad Nacional de Rosario, especialista en salud animal con orientación en epidemiología, cofundadora y coordinadora académica de la Cátedra Libre de Fauna Silvestre. “Debemos conservar nuestro patrimonio natural y cultural no solamente porque las generaciones futuras también tienen derecho y necesidad vital de ello, sino además porque es una cuestión ética. Consiste en

considerar a

la naturaleza como sujeto de derecho

”, enfatiza.


Foto: Cátedra Libre de Fauna Silvestre


Animales de compañía, no mascotas


Férrea defensora de la fauna y de la naturaleza en todas sus formas y especies, pone en relevancia que

cada ser que está vivo merece su vida

 y existe una razón para esa existencia. Reflexiona, entonces, sobre esta convivencia entre seres humanos y no humanos en un planeta “preparado a lo largo de millones de años para proporcionarnos, sin pedir nada a cambio, lo que necesitamos para seguir presentes como especie y ser felices”. Propone como tarea “amorosa, estratégica y futurista”

repensar nuestra manera de cohabitar la Tierra

.


Al hablar del mascotismo, principalmente cuando involucra especies silvestres, Nigro se detiene incluso en la

palabra mascota, ligada en su origen a la idea de amuleto o talismán. “Nada más lejano a un ser vivo”

, exclama. Por eso sugiere hablar de animales de compañía cuando se trata de especies que pueden efectivamente convivir con los seres humanos.


Pero para que exista esa convivencia hay una historia anterior. Un animal doméstico es el resultado de un proceso de domesticación desarrollado a lo largo de miles de años. Ese proceso se dio a través de la selección de características generación tras generación, con transformaciones genéticas, fisiológicas y comportamentales que permitieron que determinados animales se adapten a la vida junto a las personas.


Pero un animal silvestre no deja de serlo porque haya nacido en cautiverio, porque coma de una mano o porque haya aprendido a tolerar la presencia humana. “A lo sumo se podrá amansarlos de alguna manera y esto está muy ligado a métodos crueles en muchos casos, pero no domesticarlos porque eso llevaría demasiado tiempo”, indica Nigro.


Foto: Claudia Nigro


Una historia de miles de años


La pregunta sobre si alguna especie nació para ser domesticada resulta inevitable. Hoy convivimos con perros, gatos, caballos, vacas, ovejas o cabras con tal naturalidad que resulta difícil imaginar que detrás de esos vínculos existieron alguna vez poblaciones silvestres.


La respuesta de Nigro es clara: “Fue una decisión tomada por el ser humano que aprovechó un agriotipo, que es una especie silvestre ancestral, la hizo atravesar un proceso de domesticación y originó así nuevas especies como perros, gatos, vacas, ovejas, cabras, cerdos, caballos, conejos”.


Con respecto al perro, quizás el compañero más estrechamente asociado a nuestra especie, la veterinaria analiza que la intervención fue tan exitosa que los seres humanos podemos expresar afecto sabiendo que el animal es capaz de interpretar …

author: Robert Whitaker
title: Dangerous Gifts: Rethinking Madness, Healing, and Human Connection – A Conversation With Sascha DuBrul
content:
H

ello, my name is Robert Whitaker, and today I have the great pleasure of having as my guest on Mad in America Radio Sascha DuBrul. Sascha will be well-known to most Mad in America listeners. He’s been a leading activist in psychiatric circles for more than two decades now.


He co-founded The Icarus Project and worked closely with the Institute for the Development of Human Arts. His interests lie at the intersection of the public mental health system and the Mad Underground.


The transcript below has been edited for length and clarity. Listen to the audio of the interview here.


Robert Whitaker: Sascha, welcome to Mad in America Radio.


Sascha DuBrul

: I’m so happy to be here, Bob.


Whitaker: I’d like to tell a little story about how I first discovered you and the Icarus Project. I had come out with a book,

Mad in America

, in 2002, and at that time, I wrote about MindFreedom, David Oaks, and the psychiatric survivor movement. Then all of a sudden, the Icarus Project popped up on my screen, and I could see that it was different in its orientation from the psychiatric survivor movement, and yet it was user-led. Sascha, can you tell us what led you to co-found the Icarus Project?


DuBrul:

 First of all, it’s great to have this conversation with you after all these years, because one thing that just occurs to me is when you started the Mad in America website, I was one of the first people

blogging

 on it.


When we started the Icarus Project, there was the psychiatric survivor movement that you were talking about, and then there was biological psychiatry. There were the NAMI meetings that my mom had gone to when I had been hospitalized and diagnosed with bipolar disorder, but there was nothing really in between. There was no space to say, Hey, you know what? These things that we’re talking about, mental illness if we want to call it that, or the extreme states that we’re experiencing, or these hard times that we’re going through, we don’t have language to talk about it.


The psychiatric survivor language never really resonated with me or with the other people that were originally part of Icarus, and part of that was a generational thing. The psychiatric survivor movement came of age in a time when people were getting locked up in institutions for long periods of time. We were the biomedical generation, where we were getting diagnosed and put on drugs, but not having these long, extended stays in the hospital.


Icarus started because I wrote an article in the

San Francisco Bay Guardian

. I was 27 years old, and I was asking questions like, I don’t trust the pharmaceutical industry, but the drugs that they’re giving me seem to actually be helping me. I’m looking for other people out there that are just trying to figure this stuff out. That’s the context in which Icarus started.


Whitaker: The Icarus Project is often referred to as a radical group. Yet on the one hand, you’re finding the drugs helpful; many members did. I presume you were in a position of choice, right? People like the drugs, that’s great. If they don’t like the drugs, that’s good too.


DuBrul:

 When we started, we said very clearly, if you take the psychiatric drugs or you think they’re poison, you’re welcome to be a part of the Icarus Project. If you use diagnostic categories, like bipolar disorder or schizophrenia, or you think all those categories are ridiculous, you’re welcome to be a part of the Icarus Project. We opened up a lot of space for people who wouldn’t necessarily agree with each other to be in the same room.


Whitaker: But you shared the experience of having been diagnosed, of having some exposure to the psychiatric system, and in some ways finding it unhelpful. Isn’t that correct?


DuBrul:

 For sure, but I think what that actually means is for people to say, yeah, that was really horrible the way those doctors treated me. They treated me like I couldn’t even make decisions for myself. But what is that language they use? The language of harm to self or harm to others. Maybe I actually was going to hurt myself if they didn’t put me in the hospital. Maybe I was actually going to hurt somebody else if I wasn’t put in the hospital.


We opened up space for all kinds of questions like that, that I think the traditional psychiatric survivor movement really didn’t have language or space for in the way they were thinking.


Whitaker: Tell me, Sascha, what did you do when you started? Did you have meetings in person? What …

author: daniel
title: Ableistisches journalistisches Versagen
content: Dieser wurde aber weitgehend totgeschwiegen. Es gab kaum Presseberichte. Selbst über die Besetzung eines Bundesministeriums berichtete einzig die Frankfurter Rundschau. Journalist*innen schreiben lieber über Einzelschicksale. Mitleid-erweckende Berichte generieren online Klicks und gefallen Leser*innen. Die Berichte bleiben oberflächlich und die systemischen und politischen Hintergründe werden nicht beleuchtet. Betroffene als Objekte einer bequemen Berichtserstattung. Sobald Betroffene als Akteur*innen auftreten und das System, das sie behindert, anprangern, werden sie unsichtbar gemacht. Die Redaktionen stehen offenbar zu dieser ableistischen Linie. Der Lüneburger Behindertenbeirat kritisierte die Nicht-Berichtserstattung der Landeszeitung (LZ) über eine Kundgebung am europäischen Protesttag für die Gleichstellung von Menschen mit Behinderung. Die Redaktion antwortete am 22. Mai 2026 wie folgt: „Anm. d. Red.: Am Protesttag selbst hat die LZ tatsächlich nicht berichtet. Wir stellen hingegen regelmäßig Schicksale von Menschen mit Einschränkungen in den Mittelpunkt von Geschichten – unabhängig von Protest- oder Gedenktagen. So haben wir beispielsweise am 9. Mai von der 16-jährigen Lotti berichtet, die trotz Unterstützungsbedarf ihren Traumberuf lernen will.“ Selbst die verwendete Sprache ist hier ableistisch. Das Wort „Behinderung“ wird gemieden, obwohl dies kein Schimpfwort ist, sondern eine neutrale Eigenschaft. Das ist ein journalistisches Versagen. Die Graswurzelrevolution wird dagegen über die Proteste und ihre Hintergründe ausführlich in der GWR 514 berichten. Seid auf den Schwerpunkt der Dezemberausgabe gespannt!

author: Sarah Hughes
title: Members Alarmed by End-Run around Democracy at Buffalo Health Care Local
content:
Things had been tense for some time inside the leadership of Communications Workers (CWA) Local 1168, a 4,800-member health care union based near Buffalo, New York. Still, it was a high-functioning local with a busy calendar of events, stewards handling grievances, organizers pursuing leads, and leaders organizing at work.


So it was a surprise to members in June when their parent union, CWA, put the local into trusteeship, at the request of the local’s president and seven of the nineteen executive board members.


Trusteeship meant the union’s bylaws and elected leaders were suspended, and most of its work temporarily ground to a halt. The appointed Director of Organizing and Mobilizing Mary Nowocien and elected Vice President Patrick Weisansal II found themselves locked out of their group chats, email, and union hall, and facing an internal union prosecution.


A staffer of CWA District 1, Erin Spaulding, was assigned as trustee—tasked with maintaining the functioning of the local, setting up and overseeing judicial processes for the charges against officers, and making a plan to return the union to local control.


Nowocien and Weisansal saw the sudden trusteeship as an escalation of a long-running conflict and a deliberate undermining of the upcoming union elections. Weisansal had just announced his intention to run against incumbent President Cori Gambini.


Now the elections are on hold until the trials are over, whenever that is. And lately, the employer has been taking advantage of the turmoil in the union.


While the allegations are serious, members are concerned that the trusteeship was a nuclear option for an internal financial matter and that it has torn apart relationships at the local, weakened opposition to management’s schemes and denied democratic processes to an active, engaged union membership.


ALLEGED TIMECARD ISSUES


The trusteeship filing lists the cause as “serious allegations of financial misconduct” from officers and “dueling charges” between leaders.


Gambini and Executive Vice President Robert Andruszko had accused Nowocien and Weisansal of defrauding the local of thousands of dollars, by getting paid by both the union and their employer for the same hours worked, and by falsifying records. These issues came to light during a timecard audit in the fall of 2025 by their employer, Kaleida Health.


Nowocien and Weisansal acknowledged there were significant errors on old timecards and paychecks, but said it was the product of the employer’s faulty timekeeping and payroll system, and human error. The majority of other officers also had issues, they pointed out, but only some were being singled out for discipline by the local and the employer.


Spaulding, the trustee, interviewed all the suspended officers and allowed the majority to return to their paid positions—with the exception of Nowocien, Weisansal, and three others not facing any charges: the Communications and Political Directors and one of the Area Vice Presidents. Also fired were two longtime staff organizers, on the grounds that there was no work for them to do, according to one, Ann Converso, who had recently helped organize a new unit of substance use disorder counselors and was gearing up for their first contract fight.


Many current leaders on both sides of this schism were part of a reform caucus in Local 1168, the Caucus of Rank-and-File Healthcare Employees (CORHE), which dissolved when they won their positions in 2020.


Since winning, Gambini and a few others have butted heads with Weisansal, Nowocien, and others over how to tackle problems. The latter camp frequently organized their facility—Buffalo General Hospital, the union’s largest unit—to push back against management’s changes and violations. Gambini and leaders aligned with her argued that that wasn’t the right approach—that they had to pick their fights and not overextend the membership, according to Weisansal.


One Buffalo General steward, who asked to not be named, said members were appalled that the trustee had removed elected officers. “If our employer treated one of our members in a similar fashion,” the steward said, “union leadership would rally around them and fight to return them to their position!”


Spaulding wrote in a public FAQ posted on the local’s social media that the temporary administration “is not intended to be punitive or find guilt against any individual in the Local. It is intended to stabilize the Local while issues are …

author: Solarpunk Magazine
title: Solarpunk Horror, Lunarpunk Submissions, and 2027 Magazine Submissions
content:
We’ve got some exciting announcements to share! There’s a brand-new lunarpunk anthology seeking submissions, our special horror-themed issue of Solarpunk Magazine is available for preorder, we’re going to start publishing solarpunk novellas and novels, and our complete 2027 submissions schedule is now up on our website’s submissions page.

So whether you’re a reader looking for your next great story or a writer dreaming up better futures, here’s what’s coming.

Submission Window: November 1 – December 31, 2026

Android Press is preparing to venture into the shadows with What Blooms in Darkness: A Lunarpunk Anthology, edited by our co-editor-in-chief, Justine Norton-Kertson, and scheduled for publication in autumn 2027.

Lunarpunk shares solarpunk’s commitment to ecological regeneration, social justice, community, and liberatory futures, while exploring the possibilities that emerge in darkness, mystery, privacy, dreams, and the hidden corners of our world.

What Blooms in Darkness asks some fascinating questions: What kinds of communities thrive beyond the reach of surveillance? What knowledge survives underground? What forms of liberation become possible when people are free to remain unseen?

Android Press is seeking stories about everything from nocturnal ecosystems and underground communities to secret mutual-aid networks, hidden cultures, rituals, and resistance movements. The anthology welcomes imaginative interpretations of lunarpunk, especially stories that challenge the assumption that darkness is inherently dangerous or frightening.

Genre: Lunarpunk, climate fiction, and related speculative fiction

Eligibility: Original, unpublished fiction by human authors worldwide

Expected publication: Autumn 2027

Whether you’re a writer or a reader, you can easily sign up to get a notification when the anthology’s crowdfunder launches in March 2027!

We’ve spent years exploring what better futures might look like. Now we’re inviting some monsters into the garden. We’re thrilled to reveal the cover and complete table of contents for Solarpunk Magazine Issue #30, our special Solarpunk Horror issue, arriving November 10, 2026!

Horror and solarpunk might seem like an unusual combination, but we think they have a lot to say to each other. What happens when the ghosts of ecological destruction refuse to stay buried? What kinds of monsters might haunt societies struggling to heal centuries of exploitation? And how do things like fear, grief, survival, and resistance fit into our visions of better futures?

This extra large special issue brings together fiction, poetry, essays, and artwork that explore the darker edges of solarpunk imagination. We’re especially excited about the lineup of writers and artists contributing to this issue.

“The Unrooted Sea” by Seiba Rosario

“Bottles, Bones, Skein” by Marisca Pichette

“A Sweetness On The Breeze” by John Leahy

“Blood of the Town, Veins of the Earth” by Katharine Tyndall

We’re incredibly grateful to all the contributors who helped bring this experiment in solarpunk horror to life.

Issue #30 releases November 10, 2026, and is available for preorder now for $6.
