author: Tam Saavedra
title: WEI and UN Women Co-Launches Guide for Disability-Inclusive
content:
Across Asia and the Pacific, 350 million women and girls with disabilities navigate conflict, crisis, and climate instability. While they are frontline peacebuilders, community leaders, and human rights defenders, they remain systematically excluded from formal peace and security decision-making.

To break down these barriers, Women Enabled International (WEI) and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific have officially launched a landmark publication today: the Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive National Action Plans on Women, Peace and Security in Asia and the Pacific. Released ahead of the annual UN Security Council high-level debate in New York, this first-of-its-kind guide provides a practical, policy-oriented blueprint for governments, policymakers, and civil society.

Read the full Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive NAPs on WPS in Asia and the Pacific

Historically, women with disabilities in peace policies have been viewed narrowly as victims or passive recipients of protection. Co-drafted through consultations with 26 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities, in collaboration with Women Enabled International and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, this guide directly challenges that narrative. It grounds its framework in a human rights model of disability and the core movement principle: “Nothing about us without us”.

As WEI Executive Director Maryangel García-Ramos Guadiana stated during the launch:

“The true value of this Guidance Note is that it exists, not as a siloed document, but as a means to ensure we, as feminist disabled change-makers, are not left out of the agenda, but we are the ones who get to set the agenda.”

UN Women Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific, Christine Arab, added:

“National Action Plans on WPS that include everyone lead to peace that lasts.”

The publication was shaped by participatory research, drawing on focus groups and surveys with 26 grassroots leaders with diverse disabilities across the region. It addresses critical ground-level hurdles—including digital exclusion, inaccessible evacuation infrastructure, and ableism in mainstream spaces—ensuring that the voices of women, girls and gender-diverse people with disabilities form the foundation of the guidance.

The publication urges stakeholders to align National Action Plans (NAPs) with international standards—including the CRPD, CEDAW, and UN Security Council Resolution 2475—across all four WPS pillars:

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

The guide also features a practical Disability-Inclusive WPS NAP Checklist to help stakeholders evaluate progress at every stage of policy implementation.

This Guidance Note was made possible with the generous support of the Government of the Republic of Korea (through the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family) as part of the project “Promoting Leadership of Future Generation Peacebuilders and Change-makers in Asia and the Pacific”, and of the Australian Government under the Regional Framework Towards Peaceful, Inclusive Societies (2023–2027).

author: Sara Luterman
title: Nursing Home Residents Have a Right to Vote — Despite What Trump CMS Agency Says
content:
The Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 requires facilities to support their residents in exercising their rights.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Cindy Napolitan and her daughter Melissa have multiple sclerosis, a degenerative condition in which the immune system attacks the brain, spinal cord and nerves. They have lived together at a nursing home in Mesquite, Texas, for nine years. In previous elections, Cindy and Melissa Napolitan voted by mail, but this year they took an unusual step: They voted in person. They worried their mail-in ballots — and even their in-person votes — may not be counted.

“I’ve never worried like this before. I’ve never worried that I don’t have the proper ID. I’ve never worried that somebody is going to intimidate me. Will I encounter somebody that’s going to threaten me or make me feel less than? So yeah, I’m very worried, and I shouldn’t be,” Cindy Napolitan said. “I shouldn’t have to be worried about stuff like that. This is the 19th Amendment. I’m allowed to vote.”

Nursing home residents are guaranteed the right to vote. Around two-thirds of all nursing home residents in the United States are women, making aging and long-term care gendered issues.

There is no data on how many nursing home residents exercise that right. Cindy, 70, and Melissa Napolitan, 48, at least, feel like they’ve had good experiences with voting at their facility. Cindy Napolitan, in particular, has worked with the activities coordinator to organize rides to the polls for her, her daughter and other interested residents.

“We are scheduled to go on the first day of early voting. So in case there are any issues that we come across, we still have time to rectify the situation and be allowed to vote,” Cindy Napolitan said.

Cindy and Melissa Napolitan are more concerned this year than in previous years about government interference and voter suppression. Their fears are not unfounded: Experts and advocates for the rights of nursing home residents, older adults and people with disabilities are worried too.

In July, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services rescinded previous guidance affirming that nursing home residents have the right to vote.

“The memo does not alter the underlying law. Nursing homes are governed by the Nursing Home Reform Act of 1987 and its implementing regulations,” said Nina Kohn, a professor at Syracuse University and expert on elder law. “That law still requires facilities to support their residents in exercising their rights as Americans.”

The memo also emphasized voter fraud in nursing homes, specifically around mail-in ballots. For years, President Trump has disparaged mail-in ballots, insisting without evidence that fraudulent votes by mail had a role in his loss during the 2020 presidential election. His comments have led to some states restricting who can use a mail-in ballot and in what contexts.

According to experts, including Kohn, there is no evidence that voter fraud is a serious or widespread problem in nursing homes. Instead, Kohn is concerned about the chilling effect that it may have on residents’ rights.

“The language in the memo itself is intimidating, and it may understandably make staff think that they could face criminal prosecution or be in some other form of legal trouble if they help residents vote,” Kohn said.

Cindy and Melissa Napolitan do everything together — and on Monday, they voted together. They are also roommates at the facility; most people living in nursing homes are assigned roommates who are strangers.

“Unlike other people that have roommates that don’t get along, I’m very lucky and fortunate that I have somebody that loves me and I love her,” Cindy Napolitan said.

This is the second time Cindy and Melissa Napolitan have voted in person since entering a nursing home. The first time was during the 2024 presidential election.

“I’ve been checking my status weekly to make sure that I haven’t been dropped off the voter rolls, making sure my daughter and I don’t have some sort of issue that says that we can’t vote,” Cindy Napolitan said.

People living in nursing homes and other long-term care facilities face specific barriers. Some residents may need assistance filling out their ballots because they lack the movement or dexterity to hold a pen or press buttons on a computer screen. People with dexterity or coordination issues may also be unable to produce the same signature twice …

author: Mostafa Hosny
title: ‘Citizens’ health’ session at Egypt Forum 2026 boasts spending success with no mention of declining hospital bed numbers
content:
On Tuesday, the second day of Egypt Forum 2026, Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar described the political leadership’s support for the healthcare sector as unprecedented.


Speaking at the “citizen’s health”

session

 of Egypt Forum 2026, he said the approach dated back to the beginning of President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi’s presidency in 2014, when, he

said,

 Egypt faced a massive “disease burden,” with a lack of data and years of inadequate budget allocations that had failed to meet developmental ambitions for the system, particularly as population growth accelerated.


The minister said the state’s development plan had delivered gains in the sector, citing 16 presidential initiatives that had benefited 95 million citizens at a cost of LE44 billion. 


Abdel Ghaffar stressed that success in healthcare should not be measured by spending levels, but by the results citizens ultimately experience.


Mada Masr looked into some of those results, drawing from government

data

 published by the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics (CAPMAS).


One clear result over the time period is the notable decline in the number of beds in public hospitals between 2013 and 2024, with a drop from around 98,291 to 84,225. 


Over the same period, the number of beds in private hospitals rose from 26,009 to 36,014. 


Still, the combined total of beds in public and private hospitals fell from 124,300 in 2013 to 120,239 in 2024.


While Abdel Ghaffar portrayed inadequate budget allocations as a problem of the past, the state

has consistently fallen short

 of the constitutionally mandated minimum for healthcare spending.

 Article 18 of the Constitution requires the state to allocate at least three percent of gross national product to public healthcare starting in FY 2016/17 and gradually increase spending over time. The state has not met this threshold since the Constitution was adopted in 2014. Since then, healthcare spending has not exceeded 1.7 percent of GNP in most years.


The government allocated 1.51 percent of GNP to healthcare in the current fiscal year’s budget, half the constitutional minimum. 


Meanwhile, the government has

introduced

 a different method for calculating budget allocations that allows it to claim it is meeting the minimum spending threshold.

 


Rather than using its previous classification, which was based on the Health Ministry’s expenditure, the government now uses a “broader and more comprehensive” definition. Under this new definition, healthcare expenditure also encompasses spending by a number of off-budget economic authorities and companies as well as “any other entities providing healthcare services, such as police and military hospitals, Al-Azhar hospitals, the comprehensive health insurance system and its associated programs,” a Finance Ministry source previously told Mada Masr. Without publicly available data on these entities’ healthcare spending, it is impossible to verify whether they bring total annual healthcare spending to the constitutionally mandated minimum.


The same expansion of what constitutes annual “health spending” also allows the government to include the budgetary allocation for these entities’ debt repayments as investment in the sector, according to the same source.


The president

confessed

 three years ago that the state is not meeting the constitutional requirements, saying in a public address that “the required numbers aren’t available, folks.”

 His comment came days after the government’s assertion that it was meeting the required spending levels.


Aside from its commentary on expenditure, the government’s Egypt Forum 2026 also highlighted the Universal Health Insurance System, one of the leading presidential health initiatives.


Egypt’s Healthcare Authority head, Ahmed al-Sobky,

described

 the system as a comprehensive reform of Egypt’s healthcare sector, capping an “enormous leap forward” under Sisi, following earlier historic transformations under King Fouad I and former President Gamal Abdel Nasser.


Shortly before the forum, the government began promoting the second phase of the Universal Health Insurance System, launching a pilot phase in Minya Governorate. 


The first phase launch in the governorates of Port Said, Ismailia, Suez, South Sinai, Luxor and Aswan began in 2018 and was

completed

 in 2025.

 


Sobky said the system had achieved its objectives by strengthening social justice and reducing poverty by lowering …

title: Ulus: Healthcare must be free and accessible to all
content:
Structural problems in public hospitals and shortcomings in healthcare services are making it increasingly difficult for citizens to access medical care. People struggling to secure appointments through the Central Physician Appointment System (MHRS) sometimes have to wait at least 15 days just to submit an appointment request. Patients who eventually manage to obtain appointments after considerable effort must then try to explain their health problems within limited consultation times due to overcrowding in hospitals.


Difficulties in securing appointments and restrictions on consultation times are further deepening problems concerning the quality and accessibility of healthcare services.


Mehmet Nuri Ulus, Co-Chair of the Diyarbakır (Amed) Branch of the Health and Social Service Workers’ Union (SES), spoke to ANF about the problems facing public hospitals.


‘Healthcare is not being transformed, it is going backwards’


Ulus recalled that the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government has introduced healthcare reform and transformation programmes since 2002. He said that the policies implemented in recent years have caused serious problems in healthcare services and continued: “The AKP government has announced numerous programmes under the names of healthcare reform and healthcare transformation. However, particularly over the past 10 to 15 years, what has been called healthcare transformation has, from our perspective, meant collapse and regression. We have experienced both the COVID-19 pandemic and the earthquake during this period. These major crises showed us just how inadequate the healthcare system was in responding to the problems that arose.


The healthcare system should have been prepared for these crises and should have had the capacity to meet society's healthcare needs. Healthcare is a service that must be provided within the framework of the social welfare state. Everyone must be able to receive healthcare services equally, accessibly and in their mother tongue.


However, in recent years, we have seen healthcare services increasingly turn into a system in which those who have money can access care more easily. The proliferation of private hospitals is one aspect of this. Another is the emergence of an approach in which even public hospitals link faster access to certain tests, radiological examinations, medical reports and surgical procedures to payment. This undermines the principle that healthcare services should be equal for everyone.”


‘Physical queues have been replaced by virtual queues’


Ulus addressed the appointment crisis in the healthcare system, pointing out that the queues once seen outside hospitals now continue through the Central Physician Appointment System. He said appointment systems should make healthcare more accessible, but many citizens are currently unable to secure appointments.


Ulus said: “The AKP government used to say that people had to go to hospitals early in the morning and wait in queues to see a doctor. Today, physical queues have been replaced by virtual queues. Instead of waiting for hours outside hospitals, people now try to book appointments on their phones or online. However, when you access the system, you cannot find an available appointment. The queues have therefore not disappeared; they have simply changed form. Citizens now find themselves waiting in front of digital systems to access healthcare.


People face serious difficulties securing appointments, particularly in departments such as ear, nose and throat, ophthalmology and dermatology. Citizens who cannot obtain appointments are then forced to turn to private hospitals. However, considering the economic crisis, the struggle to make ends meet and the housing problems in Turkey, not everyone has the financial means to seek treatment at private hospitals.


As a result, the inability to access healthcare has become another dimension of economic hardship. Healthcare should be free and accessible, yet citizens are forced to stretch their financial resources to obtain the medical care they need.”


‘The budget is not allocated to preventive healthcare services’


Ulus said that the problems facing the healthcare system are not limited to difficulties in securing appointments. He drew attention to the following issues: “When we look at the Ministry of Health's budget and healthcare policies, we see that preventive healthcare services are consistently pushed into the background. author: Donald Zrebiec
title: She Was Here: Finding My Grandmother After Willard
content:
I

 often mention that I was the only one of Catherine Smoral’s grandchildren to see her alive. I was six years old, and the visit to Willard State Hospital was a bad experience for all four of us who were there: my mother Anna, my Uncle Tony, me, and my grandmother Catherine. The three of us who came from Syracuse were all shocked at the physical and mental condition of our mother and grandmother. Our visit upset her, and we spent a very short time there before being asked to leave.


My grandmother was born in Poland in 1884. She emigrated to the U.S. in 1900, and in 1902 she married my grandfather, Karol Smoral. They were married at Sacred Heart, a beautiful Polish church that still stands on the west side of Syracuse. They were a happy couple who went on to have nine children, a happy and healthy brood. Karol bought his own home on Morgan Avenue, and a family burial plot at Sacred Heart Cemetery not far from it. In the early 1920s, disaster struck the household.


I received, I believe from Ancestry.com, a copy of an article from the Syracuse Herald from the early 1920s. This is how it read:


SMORAL FAMILY WOES CULMINATE IN COMMITTAL OF EIGHT TO INSTITUTIONS. Mother and Son Are Sent to Willard. Six Younger Children to Various Orphanages. Father Died in December.


Mrs. Catherine Smoral and son Stephen, 15, were committed to Willard. Until death delivered its first blow at 107 Morgan Avenue, the family of Karol had something resembling happiness. The mother, who had been in a State Hospital before, had been returned to her family apparently cured. Stephen, then the oldest child, was of working age at 16. The children were sufficiently nourished and progressing. When Karol died, his wife became melancholic, and their son Stephen succeeded her as both mother and father of the household. The burden of being both mother and father broke him down. An investigator from the International Institute found the family nearly destitute. The son Stephen had been employed in a laboratory, but conditions for work were made impossible.


Awaiting his transfer to his new home, Chester drugged himself [he was a year and a half old at the time] with some chocolate he was given by someone in the courtroom. He smeared himself with the chocolate . . . Welfare workers are working to find him a home in a Polish family. The four girls had been all dressed up for the trip and were quiet. They had been weeping.


No matter how many times I see or read this article, I get emotional. It encapsulates the reason I wrote the book. I have a lot of trouble with it. First, it is inaccurate, and it tries to make those kids into clowns instead of marveling at their courage. Perhaps what bothers me most is the comment early on that the family had “something resembling happiness.” Who in the hell was that reporter to make a judgment like that? That’s my family he is talking about. How did they make this family tragedy a front-page story, and why did they try to turn it into some semi-comic farce? Every time I reread it, I would like to hit that reporter right in the face. But at the time, maybe mental illness and sudden death were subjects for fun and light-heartedness.


His name was never Chester. His given name was Vincent, and his nickname was Chet. I get upset about his “drugging himself” on chocolate when he was a year and a half old. He may never have had chocolate until that day. I always admired him. He became a scholarship athlete who went to college and was the first member of the Smoral family to graduate, and he was an excellent role model for his children.


Then there is the way they described the girls, all dressed up but weeping. Those girls were about six, eight, and ten years old. They had just lost both parents, their home, and probably each other, and the newspaper noticed that they had been crying. This was my family they were talking about. They should have had the sense to commend those children for holding up so well. A lot of children could not have, and I wouldn’t have blamed them. This article encapsulates all of the sadness in this whole story.


Zrebiec family photo. Courtesy of Don Zrebiec


I got over the visit to Willard pretty quickly. My picture of my grandmother faded after a short time, and I became immersed in the process of growing up. I talked to my mother about her mother at times, but she always seemed reluctant to go very deep in these conversations and often changed the subject. She had been hurt by …

content:
Le 31 octobre, c'est Halloween – la fête des morts. Généralement ils reviennent exiger des bonbons ou des sorts. Le 17 octobre, le gouvernement a choisi les sorts. Résultat : on vient de quitter l'époque contemporaine et, depuis, Bismillah, c'est les ténèbres. Mais ces ténèbres, elles sont super drôles.


Jamais autant de créatures multiformes n'avaient déferlé dans nos insurrections. Il nous a fallu analyser cet étrange phénomène. Alors on a invité deux experts des ténèbres joyeuses : le philosophe Norman Ajari et l'essayiste Pacôme Thiellement. La brèche entre les mondes vient de s'ouvrir, elle n'est pas près de se refermer. C'est la première fois que la révolution s'apparente à la chorégraphie du Thriller de Michaël Jackson. Si le Gilet Jaune de 2018 s'est ajouté au k-way noir de 2016, désormais : c'est l'intégralité du multiverse qui se fait costume. Il n'est pas certain que, dans cette immense Battle d'aura avec le gouvernement, ce soient la police qui ait le meilleur déguisement. Joyeux Halloween.

title: ¡Las Directrices de la CDPD de la ONU sobre Interseccionalidad están aquí!
content:
Read in English


Las Directrices de la CDPD de la ONU sobre Interseccionalidad acaban de cambiar las reglas del juego para los derechos de las personas con discapacidad: Esto es lo que necesitas saber

 


¡Grandes noticias para las mujeres con discapacidad y para todas las personas defensoras, aliadas y organizaciones feministas y con discapacidad en todo el mundo!

 


Durante su 35º Período de Sesiones en agosto de 2026, el

Comité de las Naciones Unidas sobre los Derechos de las Personas con Discapacidad

 (CDPD de la ONU)

 adoptó oficialmente las

Directrices sobre la Identificación y Abordaje de la Discriminación Interseccional Contra las Niñas, Adolescentes, Mujeres y Mujeres Mayores con Discapacidad

.

 


Este hito representa un paso gigante para los derechos de las personas con discapacidad. Por primera vez, los Estados Partes cuentan con orientación explícita y accionable para respaldar sus obligaciones en la intersección entre género y discapacidad.

 


Lee las Directrices oficiales de la CDPD de la ONU aquí

 


¿Qué son las Directrices de la CDPD sobre Discriminación Interseccional?

 


Las Directrices constituyen un marco internacional autorizado, desarrollado por la CDPD de la ONU, para ayudar a los Estados a prevenir, supervisar y abordar de mejor manera la discriminación interseccional.

 


A lo largo de años de procesos de revisión de países por parte de la CDPD de la ONU, el Comité identificó una brecha persistente y crítica:

los derechos humanos específicos de las mujeres con discapacidad y la discriminación interseccional y compleja que experimentan, rara vez son comprendidas o abordadas por los gobiernos.

 


Al celebrar el 20º aniversario de la CDPD de la ONU

, e

stas Directrices fueron emitidas para cerrar esa brecha, garantizando que la convención se aplique a favor de

todas

las mujeres y niñas con discapacidad, y las personas de género diverso con discapacidad a lo largo de sus vidas.

 


¿Por qué estas Directrices cambian las reglas del juego?

 


Los documentos internacionales rara vez se centran de forma explícita en las experiencias de vida y los derechos de las mujeres con discapacidad. Estas Directrices nombran y explican las barreras sistémicas que las mujeres y personas de género diverso con discapacidad enfrentan a diario en todo el mundo, incluyendo:

 


Salud y Derechos Sexuales y Reproductivos (SDSR):

 Abordar y prevenir la esterilización forzada, la anticoncepción forzada, la falta de atención médica accesible, las restricciones al aborto y la falta de atención perinatal, menstrual y menopáusica.

 


Violencia de Género y Basada en la Discapacidad:

 Exponer la violencia institucional, el abuso digital/en línea y la falta generalizada de servicios de apoyo para las víctimas.

 


Reconocimiento de las labores de cuidado:

 Validar a las mujeres con discapacidad como cuidadoras activas y madres, en lugar de tratarlas únicamente como receptoras de cuidados.

 


Exclusión económica y educativa:

 Destacar las barreras en el mercado laboral y la exclusión de la educación durante la pubertad.

 


Respuesta a crisis y cambio climático:

 Combatir la exclusión agravada durante desastres ambientales, emergencias climáticas y esfuerzos de ayuda humanitaria.

 


Por nombrar sólo algunas.

 


7 avances clave en el enfoque de las Directrices

 


Lo que hace que este documento sea un instrumento transformador único es su enfoque estructural y progresista:

 


Inclusión explícita de la diversidad de género:

 Las Directrices abarcan explícitamente los derechos de las personas transgénero, intersexuales, no binarias y de otras diversidades de género con discapacidad, y solicitan una interpretación inclusiva de la diversidad de género de todas las obligaciones descritas.

 


Reconocimiento de las raíces históricas:

 El Comité aborda explícitamente el legado y los impactos continuos del colonialismo y la esclavización, estableciendo que los Estados que se benefician de estos sistemas históricos tienen la responsabilidad particular de reparar sus efectos actuales.

 


Un catálogo abierto de diversidad:

 El texto reconoce que las mujeres con discapacidad pertenecen a comunidades multimarginalizadas —incluidos grupos indígenas, afrodescendientes/negros, dalit, adivasi, refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, minorías religiosas, pastoriles o personas que viven en asentamientos informales, entre otros— dejando espacio para todas las identidades interseccionales.

content:

Es drängt uns, eine Frage von eminenter Wichtigkeit und folgenschwerer Bedeutung unter das Secirmesser der Kritik zu bringen, die Organisationsfrage nämlich. Es ist dieser Gegenstand von weit grösserer Wichtigkeit und Tragweite, als es bei einer flüchtigen Betrachtung den Schein haben mag: denn die Organisation ist das wichtigste Werkzeug des obschwebenden geistigen Riesenkampfes, und ist von grosser Wichtigkeit, ob eben dieses Instrument scharf und spitzig oder schartig und stumpf ist: die Organisation kann aber auch, wenn sie tauglich geformt wird, zur wirksamen Triebkraft, zum zweckdienlichen Sauerteige für die künftige Kulturform werden, sowie andererseits zum Geiste, der beschworen wurde und sich nicht zähmen lässt, wie der von Goethe’s Zauberlehrling.

Dem Wesen nach unterscheiden wir zwei Systeme der Organisation, und zwar den Centralismus und den Föderalismus. Beide sollen nun untersucht werden.

Was zunächst den Centralismus anbelangt, so ist derselbe nichts Anderes wie ein misslungener Abklatsch des despotischen oder absoluten Regierungssystems und zeigt uns, dass nicht allein der Affe, sondern auch der Mensch den Nachahmungstrieb besitzt.

Die Despotie zeigt uns den Centralismus in seiner vollendetsten und ausgebildetsten Form.

Caligula und Nero, Philipp der Zweite von Spanien und Richard III. von England, sowie Ludwig XI. von Frankreich: sie Alle waren Centralisten, die unser Augenmerk fesseln, denn sie waren gross, wenn auch als Tyrannen, wenn auch im Schlechten, sie ragen über die Mittelmässigkeit hoch empor: sie waren Verbrecher an der Menschenwürde, aber sie waren es voll Kraft und Mut, voll Kühnheit und Energie. Was sind aber die Tyrännchen, die sich die Arbeiter durch den Centralismus erzeugen, indem sie sich von Mauldreschern bethören lassen? Erbärmliche Jammergestalten im Vergleiche mit jenen Titanen, deren Andenken glühenden Hass in unserer Seele weckt? Sie sind armselige Zwerge, Liliputaner, und thun wohl daran, sich spreizen und viel und laut von der Redner-Tribüne herunter zu deklamiren und zu kreischen, denn sonst würde man sie gar nicht wahrnehmen. Sie zu verachten, wäre zu viel Ehre für sie, nein, ein mitleidiges Bedauern ist Alles, was ihnen zugewendet werden kann. Sie sind der Vergessenheit geweiht und haben dereinst zwecklos gelebt: das alleinige Ziel ihres Strebens ist das Wohlleben, und dafür treten sie das Heiligste, Erhabenste, die himmlische, ewige Idee in den Kot: sie unterscheiden sich in nichts von einem Mastschwein, das auf nichts denkt wie auf vielen und guten Mais und einen trefflichen Stall, nur erstreben sie beides in einer anderen Form. Ärmliche, kleinliche Menschlein! – Und sie wären vielleicht fähig, ihr ephemeres Sein an die ewige unvergängliche Kette von Ursachen und Wirkungen, Grund und Folge zu knüpfen und ewig zu sein im Erlösungswerk der Menschheit durch ihr fruchtbringendes Wirken, sie wären vielleicht befähigt zu schaffen, so dass sie darin das reinste Glück, ein Gefühl von Seligkeit empfänden im Glücke und Paradieses-Sein Aller, dass sie für künftige Generationen anzubahnen helfen würden.

Der Centralismus vernichtet die individuelle Selbstständigkeit und Freiheit vollständig, wie wir es im despotischen Staat antreffen. Hier ist der Wille des Autokraten Gesetz, dort der Wille des Parteigötzen, den man auf das Piedestal emporhob: der Druck ist ärger noch als im despotischen Staat, denn in einem solchen soll nur eine gesetzwidrige Handlung gerichtet werden; die Spitze der centralistischen Pyramide aber richtet nicht allein die Handlungen, sondern sogar die Meinungen, sie erforscht Herz und Nieren der Menschen wie Jehova, und es sollte auch der Wille solcher Parteigötzen unter Donner und Blitz zeitweilig verkündet werden, wenigstens hätte das Colophonium stärkeren Absatz und die Spängler fänden bei der Anfertigung von Donnerblechen vielleicht lohnende Arbeit.

Treffend bezeichnet ein Engländer den Centralismus, indem er sagt: “Stelle ein Schaf vor die andern und Du hast die Herde fertig.” Ja wohl, eine Herde ist es und weiter nichts, und diese Herde geht hin, wohin der Hammel sie führt, und wenn er in einen Sumpf hineinplumpst, so wandern Alle in den Morast, und thatsächlich stecken gegenwärtig die Bekenner der alleinseligmachenden Sozialdemokratie mit ihrer achtundvierziger Theorie im Schlamme der Reformpolitik und leiden an …

En svensk förf. Fredrik Lindholm, har någon gång år 1909 "gjort" en skrift om anarkismen, vari han åtagit sig att framställa anarkismens uppgifter. Skriftens huvudsakliga innehåll har blivit ett upprepande av de kungamord och tsarmord, som anarkisterna anklagats för, och i vissa fall väl även utfört.

Den omfattar en period då despotismen, liksom nu i många länder, intog högsätet, då folket var helt rättslöst, då anarkisterna och andra motståndare till stats- och utsugningsmonopolen, behandlades som förbrytare och fördrevs ur landet. Ofta fanns det blott en utväg att väcka uppmärksamhet för dessa ohyggliga förhållanden: Bombens detonation.

Bomben var avsedd eller träffade en herre som i sitt dagliga liv, kanske tanklöst, undertecknat hundratals dödsdomar och förvisningar, som framställde sig vara i kompani med gud, innehade kontroll över alla kanaler till det existerande rättsväsendet, befallde över polis och militär, följaktligen utövade ensam härskarmakt eller representerande sådan makt.

Jag anser mig inte i detta sammanhang ha någon befogenhet att diskutera huruvida det var rätt eller inte. Det skulle bli en alltför vidlyftig avhandling, att framställa vad man talar för och emot i ett sammanhang som detta. Våldet har alltid karaktäriserats som ultima ratio, en sista utväg.

I anarkismens politiska och sociala tankevärld har våldet ingen plats. Såväl de politiska som sociala uttrycksformerna skapar en miljö och atmosfär, som avlägsnar ifrån våldet och främjar inbördes hjälp. Dessa förändringar bygger anarkisterna inte på en sinnets förändring som grundlag, men på fakta som att möjligheterna för det sociala välståndets fördelning uppnåtts och herraväldets och förtryckets förverkligande avlägsnats.

Den fulländning som anarkismens samhällsideal företräder bygger på orsakernas upphävande, orsakerna till våldsmentaliteten.

De invändningar som göras, bygga på helt andra förutsättningar. Den ägande som fruktar för att tjuvar och rånare skola tillägna sig hans egendom, vinkar indignerat bort pratet om att våldet skulle bli överflödigt, noggrant förbiseende att människorna under kommunistiskt-anarkistiska samhällsformer inte ha någon anledning att stjäla eller med våld försvara sig mot stöld.

Militären, som tränat in sin yrkesmentalitet och den fanatiske chauvinisten komma med sina argument! Skola vi inte försvara oss mot utländska fiender?

Här är en fråga som redan nuet borde taga klar ställning till. Finns det någon mening i att försvara sig mot utländska fiender? Vad är det man kan och vill försvara? Marken, naturen, sjöarna, kan inte försvaras, kan inte erövras. Under ett krig kan man däremot förstöra dem. Ja, måste förstöra. Fransmän och belgare förstörde stora delar av sina egna områden, direkt, när tyskarna trängde fram under världskriget, förstörde för att inte tyskarna skulle få nytta av det. Franska och belgiska sprängämnen och volymkulor träffade fransk och belgisk natur - och förstörde kanske lika mycket som "fienden", tyskarna, förstörde.

Krigets mekanisering är ett kapitel som vilar tungt på vågen när det gäller att mäta våldets uppgift i nuet. Förr, när en hord människor dreva mot varandra med pikar och muskedunder, var det hela ett farligt äventyr, som begränsades av vapnens räckvidd. Nu finnes det inte längre någon sådan begränsning. Brand-, gift- och spränggaser ha förverkat varje tanke på "försvar" och mobiliserat angreppstanken som enda möjlighet i en våldskonflikt mellan staterna. De långskjutande kanonerna understryka denna utveckling. Ett krig blir blott ett fruktansvärt förgörande av allt levande.

Enda synpunkten som talar för att med krigets våld lösa de mellanfolkliga konflikterna, är den, att vapenfabrikerna och sprängämnestillverkarna behöva experimentera och måste ha stora dividender.

title: Pengarsipan Anarkis: Kritik & Kritik-Diri #1
content:
Belum selesai menghadapi permasalahan ekonomi yang bagai melempar api setitik ke padang ilalang itu, muncul permasalahan baru yang kini menghantui pengarsipan anarkis, permasalahan yang lebih halus dan bahkan tidak dipermasalahkan karena tidak tampak bermasalah di permukaan.

Kata-kata yang dicetak dan diterbitkan (atau bahkan yang tidak diterbitkan sekalipun), seperti buku, pamflet, leaflet, zine mendapat tempat yang signifikan di kalangan anarkis. Karena media tersebut terbukti mampu menyimpan berbagai pengalaman dan pemikiran banyak individu, yang bahkan dalam kasus tertentu, jika terdapat intervensi terhadap media cetak tersebut, eksistensinya akan tetap bertahan—untuk tidak menyebut abadi—lebih lama dari umur para individu yang mengalami pengalaman dan yang mencetuskan pemikiran tersebut. Dan individu-individu yang secara lengkap menyimpan kata-kata yang dicetak serta diterbitkan itu pun kemudian akan mendapatkan suatu manfaat, seperti dapat memiliki akses untuk melihat kembali “praktik untuk mencapai emansipasi” (gerakan dan perjuangan) yang terdahulu.

Itulah mengapa, menurut Baker (2023) ketika meneliti budaya tandingan—atau proses perubahan evolusioner—anarkis Spanyol, banyak perpustakaan anarkis dibangun untuk menyediakan akses terhadap koleksi lengkap kata-kata tercetak yang telah lama tidak diterbitkan kembali. Sayangnya, sejarah pertumbuhan budaya tandingan atau proses perubahan evolusioner anarkis ini tidak terjadi secara mulus atau bahkan macet di Indonesia. Karena Indonesia mengalami periode otoritarianisme—dalam artian paling kerasnya—yang berkepanjangan. Para anarkis tahun 1920-an habis dibuang ke Digul pasca pemberontakan 1926; sedangkan para individu berkecenderungan (anarkis-)sindikalis yang muncul pada tahun 1940-an disingkirkan secara paksa oleh rezim Orde Lama Karno dari pabrik-pabrik yang mereka swa-kelola dan disingkirkan secara perlahan dari arena pemikiran/intelektual oleh PKI; dan menjadi sama sekali tidak terlacak eksisensinya pasca genosida 1965 dan naiknya rezim Orde Bau Harto ke tampuk kekuasaan (Bima, 2018).

Walaupun, periode otoritarianisme berkepanjangan tersebut tidak khas dialami oleh para anarkis di Indonesia saja. Periode otoritarianisme keras yang berkepanjangan, yakni rezim Komunis Gheorghe Gheorghiu-Dej (1948-1965/17 tahun) dan Nicolae Ceaușescu, menjadikan para anarkis di Rumania dan di Indonesia memiliki—tanpa menafikan perbedaan dampak dari pasca-komunis di Rumania dan pasca-kolonial serta pasca-otoriter-militer di Indonesia yang menciptakan perbedaan yang kompleks—kesamaan dalam hal sejarah perkembangan budaya anarkis mereka. Karena ketika rezim komunis naik ke tampuk kekuasaan para anarkis disingkirkan mulai dari ditekan pergerakannya sampai dibunuh, dan sebagian yang hidup harus pergi mengasingkan diri ke luar negeri atau tetap di Rumania tetapi memilih untuk mengambil sikap tiarap total (Anarhiva, 2021). Situasi ini akhirnya, menurut Tataran (2026), membuat para anarkis yang bermunculan di Rumania pada masa-masa keruntuhan rezim komunis pada 1989 atau setelahnya, yang mayoritas bergerak di skena anarko-punk, hanya memiliki pengetahuan yang secuil atau bahkan tidak memiliki sama sekali pengetahuan tentang para anarkis yang eksis sebelum mereka, sehingga secara otomatis mereka tidak memiliki pengalaman kolektif yang dapat dijadikan rujukan ketika mereka menjalankan praktik anarkis/anti-otoritarian.

Sejalan dengan Adrian Tataran, Ucok (2026) dalam diskusi buku Unfinished Nation yang diselenggarakan di Perpustakaan Bunga di Tembok pun mengatakan hal yang nyaris sama. Menurutnya, sebelum buku Perang yang Tidak Akan Kita Menangkan karya Bima Satria Putra terbit—jauh setelah reformasi—pada tahun 2018, para anarkis yang bermunculan—dan sama seperti di Rumania, yang banyak pula bergerak di skena anarko-punk—saat masa-masa kejatuhan Harto beserta rezim Orde Baunya dan masa setelahnya tidak memiliki pengetahuan tentang gerakan anarkis terdahulu, sehingga sempat terbersit dalam pemikiran mereka kalau diri mereka adalah anarkis generasi pertama di Indonesia. Alhasil, tanpa pengalaman dan memori kolektif yang diwariskan dari para anarkis terdahulu, para anarkis yang hadir kemudian tersebut harus mulai membangun dari awal; berbanding terbalik dengan otoritarianisme yang walaupun dikatakan runtuh, mereka sudah memiliki birokrasi, struktur, militer, yang telah dibangun selama berdekade dan mapan serta siap diwariskan, sehingga bukan hal yang sulit untuk kembali ke tampuk kekuasaan …

author: Unknown
title: Карл Юджин Строд - Стремление учиться
content:
Автор

: Карл Юджин Строд

Название

: Стремление учиться

Дата

: 2021

Дополнительная информация

: «The Tendency to Learn» — Carl Eugene Stroud

Переведено для

https://t.me/black4red

Источник

: Переведено и скопировано 28.10.2026 с https://anarchistpedagogies.net/resources-en/the-tendency-to-learn


 Сегодня революционная борьба страдает от недостатка способностей на индивидуальном, организационном и социальном уровнях. Нашим крупнейшим социальным движениям, как и нашим самым страстным индивидуальным усилиям необходим милитантский импульс, способный стратегически соединять разрозненные действия. Милитантность позволяет массовым движениям испытывать обоснованную гордость и ощущать свою причастность к наиболее успешным революционным действиям. Она также даёт активному меньшинству чёткую цель и место в формировании социальной силы. Однако стойкая милитантность — это акт свободы, но сегодня большинство людей оказываются «втянуты» в неё не из сознательного выбора, а в силу обстоятельств. Мы, люди, борющиеся за социальную революцию, хотим иметь возможность самим решать, как развивать нашу милитантность. Мы требуем возможности сознательно участвовать в милитантской практике, поскольку так революционный потенциал наших движений будет обеспечен свободой людей.


 И всё же, даже при наличии свободы выбрать милитантскую деятельность остаётся вопрос:


 Куда революционерам направить свои усилия, чтобы их деятельность была связана с той реальностью, в которой в конечном счёте будет жить народ, пробуждала в людях чувство субъектности в Истории и принятие ответственности за этичность своих действий в настоящем?


 Наш ответ следует искать во взрослом образовании, которое представляет собой особенно благоприятную почву для долгосрочного участия в судьбе народных движений. Людям всегда будет необходимо учиться. Поэтому мы предлагаем создать, поддерживать и защищать революционное образовательное направление, которое станет местом встречи и обмена опытом для людей, стремящихся учиться и учить других, — в том числе членов сообщества, активистов, организаторов, диссидентов и милитантов.


 Стремление учиться, которое обычно связывают с молодёжью, новичками, студентами и теми, кому недостаёт опыта, не следует отвергать как стихийную форму организации. Нередко люди, «научившись», переходят к «действиям»: применяют полученные знания, но покидают пространство обучения, в котором они развивали свои способности, не заботясь о том, чтобы сохранить прочную связь с его методами и целями.


 Однако мы настаиваем на том, что это пространство нуждается в целенаправленной защите, если оно должно оказывать долговременное влияние на социальные преобразования. Прежде всего, защита этого пространства со временем будет способствовать коллективному становлению милитантов, которые смогут использовать общий образовательный опыт как основу для единой стратегии и политической программы. Кроме того, сохранение этого пространства будет способствовать пониманию значимости милитантов в социальной борьбе и осознанию того, насколько милитантность необходима для успеха революционных движений.


 Стремление учиться должно выполнять две функции: с одной стороны, служить пространством, где люди получают инструменты и обретают сообщество, необходимые для становления милитантами; с другой — знакомить более широкое сообщество с понятием милитантности и её теорией. Таким образом, наша цель едина, но включает два самостоятельных аспекта, которые необходимо развивать одновременно:


 Мы должны создать образовательное пространство для становления милитантов, а наше регулярное участие в его жизни должно обеспечивать надёжные пути как к милитантской деятельности, так и обратно — к образованию.


 Таким образом, стремление учиться станет пространством, где люди с большим и меньшим опытом смогут встречаться и учиться друг у друга.


 При столь ясных целях нас, несомненно, будут оценивать по нашим же критериям — приверженности делу и стойкости. Ясное определение того, что представляет собой стремление учиться, сможет воплотиться в жизнь лишь благодаря нашей приверженности ему, а его эффективность можно будет оценить лишь по тому, насколько долго оно сохраняется и насколько верно остаётся своим целям.

¿QUÉ es el patriotismo? ¿Es el amor por el lugar donde uno nació, el lugar de los recuerdos y las esperanzas de la infancia, de los sueños y las aspiraciones? ¿Es el lugar donde, con ingenuidad infantil, contemplábamos las nubes fugaces y nos preguntábamos por qué nosotros tampoco podíamos correr tan rápido? ¿El lugar donde contábamos los miles de millones de estrellas centelleantes, aterrorizados ante la idea de que cada una de ellas fuera «un ojo» que traspasara lo más profundo de nuestras pequeñas almas? ¿Es el lugar donde escuchábamos el canto de los pájaros y anhelábamos tener alas para volar, como ellos, hacia tierras lejanas? ¿O el lugar donde nos sentábamos a los pies de nuestra madre, embelesados por maravillosos relatos de grandes hazañas y conquistas? En resumen, ¿es el amor por ese lugar, donde cada pulgada representa recuerdos queridos y preciosos de una infancia feliz, alegre y juguetona?

Si eso fuera patriotismo, pocos hombres estadounidenses de hoy en día podrían considerarse patriotas, ya que el lugar de juego se ha convertido en fábrica, molino y mina, mientras que los sonidos ensordecedores de la maquinaria han sustituido a la música de los pájaros. Tampoco podemos ya escuchar las historias de grandes hazañas, pues las que cuentan hoy nuestras madres no son más que historias de dolor, lágrimas y aflicción.

¿Qué es, entonces, el patriotismo? «El patriotismo, señor, es el último recurso de los sinvergüenzas», dijo el Dr. Johnson. León Tolstói, el mayor antipatriota de nuestro tiempo, define el patriotismo como el principio que justifica la formación de asesinos en masa; un oficio que requiere mejor equipamiento para el ejercicio del asesinato que para la fabricación de artículos de primera necesidad como zapatos, ropa y viviendas; un oficio que garantiza mejores beneficios y mayor gloria que el del trabajador medio.

Gustave Hervé [1], otro gran antipatriota, califica acertadamente el patriotismo de superstición —una mucho más perjudicial, brutal e inhumana que la religión—. La superstición de la religión tuvo su origen en la incapacidad del hombre para explicar los fenómenos naturales. Es decir, cuando el hombre primitivo oía un trueno o veía un relámpago, no podía dar una explicación a ninguno de ellos y, por lo tanto, concluía que detrás de ellos debía de haber una fuerza mayor que él mismo. Del mismo modo, veía una fuerza sobrenatural en la lluvia y en los diversos cambios que se producen en la naturaleza. El patriotismo, por el contrario, es una superstición creada artificialmente y mantenida a través de una red de mentiras y falsedades; una superstición que despoja al hombre de su autoestima y dignidad, y aumenta su arrogancia y vanidad.

De hecho, la vanidad, la arrogancia y el egoísmo son los elementos esenciales del patriotismo. Permítanme ilustrarlo. El patriotismo parte de la base de que nuestro planeta está dividido en pequeños rincones, cada uno rodeado por una verja de hierro. Quienes han tenido la suerte de nacer en un rincón concreto se consideran mejores, más nobles, más grandiosos y más inteligentes que los seres vivos que habitan en cualquier otro rincón. Por lo tanto, es deber de todo aquel que vive en ese rincón elegido luchar, matar y morir en el intento de imponer su superioridad sobre todos los demás.

content:

In einem Briefe an „Les Temps Nouveaux“ (seinerzeit als „Le Revolté“ von Kropotkin und seinen Freunden gegründet) und in einem zweiten an den bürgerlichen „Temps“, der aber nicht veröffentlicht wurde, nimmt Peter Kropotkin Stellung zur antimilitaristischen Propaganda. Es handelt sich in erster Linie um die Frage, wie sich die Revolutionäre im Falle eines Krieges zu verhalten hätten, und hier nimmt Kropotkin eine gerade entgegengesetzte Stellung zu der antimilitaristischen Richtung, die in letzter Zeit in dem Professor Hèrvé einen energischen Vertreter gefunden. Während diese Letztere für die vollständige Unterdrückung des Militarismus eintritt und selbst im Falle eines „Verteidigungskrieges“ mit dem Streike der Militärpflichtigen antworten will, tritt Ersterer für eine bedingte Beibehaltung des Militärs ein, welches Frankreich, das daran ist, die Grundlagen seiner Gesellschaftsform zu ändern, gegen Angriffe von reaktionären Feinden, unter welchen er hauptsächlich die Deutschen versteht, zu schützen hätte.

Nach unserer Ansicht beruhen die Schlüsse, welche Kropotkin zieht, auf einer allzustarken Unterschätzung der Deutschen, was man ihm aber wahrlich nicht übel nehmen kann; waren es doch die „Germanen“, welche stets wie ein Bleigewicht auf den Gang der internationalen Arbeiterbewegung wirkten. Ganz so pessimistisch denken wir jedoch nicht, vielleicht eben weil wir „Deutsche“ sind, sonst hätten wir es schon längst aufgegeben, unter einer solchen elenden Schafherde Propaganda zu machen.

Nun ist zu sagen, dass, seitdem Russland aufgehört hat, eine stete Bedrohung der freiheitlichen Bewegung in Westeuropa zu sein – was man heute schon mit Bestimmtheit sagen kann – ist es auch Deutschland nicht mehr in dem Masse, weil es an „Rückgrat“ verloren hat. Es wird bald damit genug zu tun haben, die „eigenen Völker“, namentlich die Polen in der Zucht zu halten, dass es sich nicht mehr erlauben kann, ein grosses Volk, das sich zudem noch im Befreiungskampfe befindet, zu unterjochen.

An die Ausführungen von Kropotkin knüpfen sich eine Reihe von Auseinandersetzungen, und es ist auch für uns Schweizer nicht unnützlich, der Sache näher zu treten und sich darüber gründlich auszusprechen, weil es das beste Argument der Bourgeoisie und Sozialdemokraten gegen die antimilitaristische Propaganda ist, dass wir „Freiheiten“ gegen lüsterne Räuber zu verteidigen hätten.

Nachbringend bringen wir die charakteristischsten Ausführungen Kropotkins zum Abdruck, und in Fortsetzung eine Entgegnung von Charles Albert auf dieselben, ebenfalls in „Les Temps Nouveaux“ veröffentlicht.

Dies schreibt unser Peter Kropotkin in einem Briefe an „Les Temps Nouveaux“:

„Wenn Frankreich durch einige Militärmächte überfallen wird, so ist die Pflicht der Revolutionäre nicht, die Arme zu kreuzen und dem eindringenden Feinde freies Spiel zu lassen. Sie ist: die Revolution anzufangen und das Territorium der Revolution zu verteidigen, um sie fortzusetzen.

Die Formel „Streik der Conscrits“ (der militärpflichtigen jungen Leute, D. Ueb.) sagt nicht genug. Sie hat die Unannehmlichkeit, sich auszuschweigen über den eigentlichen Zweck der Propaganda, und gibt Anlass zu falschen Deutungen desselben. Sie sagt nichts von der Revolution und sagt nichts von der Notwendigkeit, in welche die Revolutionäre versetzt werden, diese, jeden Zoll französischer Erde, der sich in Revolution befindet, mit den Waffen in den Händen zu verteidigen gegen die bürgerlichen und kaiserlichen Horden deutscher, englischer oder vielleicht russischer Räuber.“

Und weiter in seinem Briefe an den „Temps“: „Aber wenn die Deutschen Frankreich überfallen, an der Spitze – wie sie es ohne Zweifel machen werden – einer mächtigen Koalition, und die Hände der kleinen Grenzstaaten (Belgien und Schweiz) binden, alsdann wird der Streik der Conscrits nicht genügen. Man müsste machen, was die „Sanscullotes“ im Jahre 1792 getan haben, welche in ihren Sektionen die revolutionäre Kommune vom 10. August konstituierten, das Königtum und die Aristokratie über den Haufen warfen, gewaltsam Steuern von den Reichen erhoben, die Legislative (die gesetzgebende Körperschaft der grossen Revolution) zwangen, das erste wirkliche Dekret zur Vernichtung der feudalen Rechte zu erlassen und deren Zurücknahme durch die Bauern des kommunalen Bodens, und die marschierten, um die französische Erde zu …

author: 张皓翔
title: The Dislocation of Vendémiaire (II): The Illusion of National Economics and the Polarization of Political Economy【葡月的错位（二）国民经济学的幻象与政治经济学的极化】【A commentary on the French riots between September and October】
content: This essay, titled The Dislocation of Vendémiaire, explores the theoretical and practical contradictions within contemporary capitalist society, using the socio-political unrest in France as a backdrop. Grounded in Marxist philosophy and dialectics, the author critically examines the illusion of national economics and the polarization of political economy. By distinguishing between "national economics" (which obscures exploitation through material comfort) and "political economy" (which reveals the deep alienation of social relations), the text argues that modern digital capitalism has stripped workers of their "wealth of real relations" (现实关系的财富). The essay articulates a fundamental shift from the "first struggle" (economic demands for wages and welfare) to the "second struggle" (reclaiming the autonomy of labor production and resisting the reduction of human beings to mere production factors). Ultimately, it posits that the recent French protests represent a historical "dislocation"—an attempt at the second struggle without the necessary political foundation of the first.

author: Unknown
title: Эррико Малатеста - Наконец-то! Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"
content:
Автор

: Эррико Малатеста

Название

: Наконец-то! Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"

Дата

: 28 сентября 1920

Источник

: Umanità Nova, год 1-й, №187


НАКОНЕЦ-ТО!

Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"


 Наконец-то появился тот, кто говорит ясно!


 До сих пор, когда мы говорили, что то, что социалисты называют

диктатурой пролетариата

, на самом деле есть не что иное, как диктатура некоторых людей, которые с поддержкой партии становятся над пролетариатом и навязывают себя ему, нас за это называли чуть ли не клеветниками.


 Вопреки всякой вероятности и всем установленным фактам утверждалось, что в России разрешена та квадратура круга, которой было бы правительство, действительно представляющее интересы и волю управляемых.


 Соответственно, Москва стала Меккой пролетариата: оттуда исходил свет, а вместе со светом – и категорические приказы относительно идей, которых должны придерживаться, и линии поведения, которой должны держаться те, кто с разрешения вышестоящих хотел называть себя коммунистами.


 Вследствие этого изумительного открытия, сделанного в России, – правительства, созданного по образу народа и для блага народа (или пролетариата, как угодно называть), – всё, что приходило из России, казалось обладающим чудотворной силой; и достаточно было назвать по-русски

советом

 любое собрание или комитет, чтобы он был возведён в верховный фактор революции.


 Но вот очарование разрушено.


 На этот раз не мы раскрываем секрет: мы, анархисты, злоязычные и непочтительные по убеждению. На этот раз это официальная газета Итальянской социалистической партии, до сих пор наиболее авторитетный орган московского слова.


 Это

Avanti!

 от 20-го числа текущего месяца, которая говорит:


 «....

В России при советском режиме Партия действительно направляет всю политику Государства, и вся общественная деятельность как отдельных лиц, так и коллективов подчинена решениям Партии, так что

 В САМОМ ДЕЛЕ ДИКТАТУРА ПРОЛЕТАРИАТА ЕСТЬ ДИКТАТУРА ПАРТИИ И, СЛЕДОВАТЕЛЬНО, САМОГО ЦЕНТРАЛЬНОГО КОМИТЕТА».


 Итак, теперь мы знаем, чего нам следует ожидать: диктатуры Руководящего органа Социалистической партии, или диктатуры нарождающейся Коммунистической партии, или даже диктатуры Д'Арагона и компании!


 Но руководители Социалистической партии, претендующие ввести Диктатуру, должны понять, что это, по крайней мере в Италии, невозможно: невозможно, потому что есть мы, анархисты и синдикалисты.


 Если бы мы находились в том же соотношении сил с социалистами, в каком, возможно, оказались наши товарищи в России, дело было бы простым: диктаторы избавились бы от нас средствами, дорогими всем диктатурам, – виселицами и тюрьмами, – и шли бы вперёд, пока не были бы свергнуты революцией или реакцией.


 Но мы уже сила, с которой необходимо считаться, и мы быстро развиваемся, чему благоприятствуют обстоятельства и то, что

Avanti!

 называет

необузданным темпераментом трудящихся масс

. И мы твёрдо решили не подчиняться.


 Не то чтобы мы верили, что массы всегда правы и что мы хотим всегда следовать за массами в их изменчивых настроениях. У нас есть программа, идеал, который мы хотим привести к победе, и поэтому мы отличаемся от массы, – мы люди определенного направления. Мы хотим воздействовать на массу, подталкивать её по пути, который считаем лучшим; но поскольку наша цель – освобождение, а не господство, мы хотим приучать массы к свободной инициативе и свободному действию.


 Мы верим, что свобода учит свободе и солидарности, и поэтому питаем отвращение к любому авторитарному устройству – как в обществе в целом, так и в любой отдельной партии или объединении.


 Социалисты хотели бы подготовить народ к свободе посредством власти.


 Но если бы, по предположению, которое мы отвергаем, было верно, что для торжества революции и устройства нового общества необходимо сосредоточить в немногих руках государственную власть, если бы было верно, что кто-то обязательно должен командовать, – тогда, пусть социалисты хорошенько поймут, – командовать хотели бы мы и не подчинились бы, разве что силой, командованию того, кто, по нашему мнению, заблуждается.


 Следствием чего было бы то, что революция, совершённая по авторитарным меркам и с диктаторскими целями, неизбежно привела бы в Италии к войне между одними революционерами и другими.


 Этого не хотели бы мы; этого не должны хотеть социалисты.


 Поэтому, оставив в стороне теории и судя о вещах реалистично, социалистам следовало бы отказаться от всяких диктаторских притязаний и принять либертарную …

SAMHAIN. Pronounced “sow-ween” or “sow-ain”, the term is the old Gaelic name for this time of year. Today it is better known as Hallowe’en, All Hallows Day, All Saints’ Day, and All Souls’ Day, and covers the time between October 31 to November 2 inclusive.

It is a lot more than going from door to door begging for candy, although this enjoyable modern ritual also has its place, binding us to our ancestors’ other children (especially those who still are children!).

But it goes much further than that.

This week, I thought I would simply open a Samhain Open Memorial Thread amongst the Anti-Capitalist Meetup community. On this day, when the ancient, pre-Christian Lore of the Celtic peoples of Western Europe teaches that the Veil between the living and our dead Ancestors is thinnest, it is appropriate to bring those Ancestors to remembrance by name that our memories of them and our debts to them may live on. Let us remember them, love them, revere them, and give them our gratitude in Solidarity for what their lives have given us.

I thank ZhenRen for his contributions to our Diary of two weeks ago, which I have taken the liberty of adapting to this week’s Diary by making a very small set of textual changes to expand the poetry to cover all of our Ancestors instead of just one.

From this Comment by ZhenRen, I open our Memorial this evening:

Come, you ancestors! Brothers, sisters, comrades, come! Come you all, for the Veil is thinnest On this very night of nights! Come ye, that we may love you again That we may bond with you again That we may share Solidarity with you again For: “Our heart is with you! Our anger is fuelled by your strength. We are all here. We are all here. It’s just your bodies which will stay where they are. You will be with us forever. You will be our light and illumination forever.”

— words after “For:” adapted from Emel’s eulogy of Ali Kitapci

I offer the text from Istanbul Indymedia in Ali Kitapci’s memory as a lesson tonight:

It’s raining. On all our memories with Ali… It’s raining. Yet yesterday the killers have washed away the blood on the street long ago. It’s raining. All those drinks we had together, all those actions we went, all those slogans we shouted, all that gas we breathed. Ali’s asthma crisis.. It’s raining. State attacks. It’s raining so badly. All the comrades, we are together just like we did 20 years ago. We are together, just like it happened in 1936! Ali had given his life to the class struggle, to the trade-union movement. He was one of those unnamed “heroes” struggling to transform the anarchist movement from a weak breath into a lively alternative of freedom. Let his memory be our comrade… We won’t forget, we won’t forgive!

To this I add: We are all together, just like it happened in 1936….. and 1886…. and 1917…. 1914….. 1940…. and many, many other times!

On this night, all of our comrades are together; we living reaching out to you who live no more as we live; but …

title: Fragenbogen-Wehrpflicht
content:

Sie ist wieder zurück, die Wehrpflicht in Deutschland. Wieder einmal haben die rot-grünen Kriegstreiber unter Beweis gestellt, dass sie die geeigneten Steigbügelhalter für Kriege und Genozide sind, dass sie im Zweifel immer bereitstehen, um einen militaristischen Mobilisierungsschub einzuleiten und nicht bloß Menschen in entfernten Landen, weit außerhalb des Blickfeldes ihrer „Wählerschaft“ zu metzeln, in Kriege zu stürzen und mit militärischer Gewalt aus ihrer Heimat zu vertreiben, zu vergewaltigen, zu morden und auszuhungern, sondern auch den Krieg im „eigenen“ Lande, sprich dem besetzten Territorium über das sie herrschen, vorzubereiten. Und dazu gehört nicht bloß das großspurige Säbelrasseln der Außenpolitik, die Investitionen in Rüstungsproduktion, dafür erforderlichen Raubbau, Infrastrukturprojekte und Neuanschaffungen von allerhand Kriegsgerät, sondern auch der propagandistische Prozess der Erzwingung von Konformität in der Bevölkerung, die Förderung der Kriegsbereitschaft durch (nationalistische) Hetze, durch das herbeiphantasieren und nötigenfalls auch die repressive/geheimdienstliche Erzeugung von „Bedrohungen“ wie Terroranschlägen und -gefahren, „hybride Kriegsbedrohungen“, Inflation usw. Und schließlich ist es unverzichtbar die Bevölkerung hinsichtlich ihrer Eignung für die Vernutzung im Kriege zu erfassen und segmentieren.

Dass dabei die Wehrpflicht, die vor gut einem Jahrdutzend ausgesetzt wurde, zunächst einmal nicht vollumfänglich zurückkehrt, sondern als verpflichtend auszufüllender Fragebogen, ebenso wie die schwachsinnigen, an jeder Realität vorbeigehenden medial inszenierten Debatten darum, mögen darüber hinwegtäuschen, dass so ein Fragebogen schlicht eine Modernisierung und Effizienzsteigerung des Musterungsverfahrens darstellt und zudem ein geeignetes Instrument ist, um die „Musterung“ von rund einem Dutzend Jahrgängen effizient nachzuholen. Zuglich bietet die Niederschwelligkeit eines solchen Fragebogens, die Möglichkeit ihn abends auf dem Sofa auszufüllen, eine Gelegenheit, auch jene, die bislang nicht von einer Wehrpflicht betroffen waren, Frauen, auf (vorerst) freiwilliger Basis ebenfalls zu „mustern“ und damit eine weitere Planungs- und Vernutzungssteigerung zu erzielen. Um das wirklich zu verstehen ist es notwendig, einen kurzen Blick darauf zu werfen, wie ein Militär funktioniert, wie es klassischerweise funktioniert hat, und wie es in der heutigen Gesellschaft funktionieren soll.

Als erstes müssen wir dazu mit einem Mythos aufräumen: Das Militär ist nicht bloß das, was an der Front kämpft. Tatsächlich ist die Front sogar der allerkleinste Teil des Militärs und oft sogar nicht einmal der mörderischste. Aber alles zu seiner Zeit. Worum genau geht es bei einem militärischen Konflikt? Klar, die wirtschaftlichen und politischen Eliten streiten sich darum, wer wen ausbeuten darf, bzw. wer wie viel Profit von der gemeinsam organisierten Ausbeutung von Menschen und Erde einstreichen darf. Das ist immer das Gleiche, egal ob es uns als Geopolitik, Besetzung von Territorien oder Konflikte um Handelsrouten präsentiert wird. Aber um das geht es ja auch in Zeiten des sogenannten Friedens, in denen ökonomische Ränkespiele, Verträge, Investitionen, usw. das gleiche regeln. Die Besonderheit des militärischen Konflikts liegt darin, dass zwei oder mehr Parteien um die physische Kontrolle eines bestimmten Territoriums ringen – und zwar mit Waffengewalt. Das beinhaltet einerseits den gewaltsamen Sieg über die Truppen des Feindes/der Feinde, andererseits aber auch die Bevölkerung dieses Territoriums entweder der neuen Herrschaftsordnung gegenüber gefügig zu machen, oder aber sie auszulöschen, bzw. zu vertreiben. Meist ist das eine Mischung: Plündernde, mordende und vergewaltigende Truppen brechen den Widerstand der Bevölkerung, verschleppen diejenigen, die Anstalten machen, sich zu wehren, oder auch nur Einspruch zu erheben, in Gefangenenlager, wo sie sie entwürdigen, versklaven und vergewaltigen, manchmal auch ermorden, schlagen sie in die Flucht und regieren dann über den verbleibenden Rest der Bevölkerung durch Abkommen mit lokalen Eliten. Wir sehen das auf der ganzen Welt, alltäglich, egal ob in Afghanistan, Syrien, Irak, Gaza, der Krim und Ukraine, Korea, Vietnam, Kongo, usw. usw. Im Grunde gibt es kein Territorium auf der Welt, in dem die herrschende Regierung nicht …

title: Özdal: Ruling elites openly robbed large sections of society
content:
The economic and political repercussions of the financial developments that erupted in Turkey in September and became known publicly as the "fund crisis" continue to be debated. Allegations have emerged that numerous individuals, including figures affiliated with the Justice and Development Party (AKP), obtained illicit profits through investment funds.


Some figures released in connection with the crisis suggest that losses may have reached as much as 2.7 trillion Turkish liras. Investigations involving the names of AKP figures and state officials have intensified public debate, while criticism of the government's handling of the crisis has also grown. President Tayyip Erdoğan's latest remarks on the fund crisis have been interpreted as an indication of growing discontent over the developments even among AKP supporters.


Journalist Hakkı Özdal spoke to ANF about the causes of the fund crisis, the relationship between political authorities and financial circles, the role of international capital and the crisis's potential impact on society.


'The bubble economists and journalists had warned about has burst'


Hakkı Özdal said that numerous warnings had previously been issued about the developments known as the fund crisis. He emphasized that the crisis had not emerged suddenly, but was the result of a financial system that had operated for years before being pushed into crisis by international intervention. Özdal added that international financial institutions had intensified their warnings to Turkish authorities and that the crisis erupted following regulations introduced by the Capital Markets Board (SPK) concerning money market funds and hedge funds.


Özdal said: "The chain of events described as the fund crisis actually emerged when a form of fraud that had been going on for years, and about which certain journalists and financial market commentators had long been issuing warnings, was triggered by international intervention and then inevitably exploded. As you know, international financial institutions began intensifying their warnings to Turkish authorities at the beginning of the summer. The Capital Markets Board subsequently introduced significant restrictions and tighter regulations on money market funds and hedge funds, which came into effect on 28 August. The fund crisis then struck like a tsunami. A bubble that international financial institutions, as well as economists and even journalists in our country, had already identified finally burst."


'Ruling elites openly robbed large sections of society'


Özdal argued that the high returns generated through money market funds primarily benefited political and economic elites. However, he noted that small savers, wage earners, industrialists and tradespeople had also turned to these funds in an effort to protect their savings. Özdal underlined that persistently high inflation over many years had driven broad sections of society toward alternative investment instruments, adding that mass participation in these funds had paved the way for large-scale financial fraud.


Özdal said: "The beneficiaries of the massive profiteering through high returns on money market funds were the elites of political and economic power. This is now plainly evident. However, in our country, which has been struggling with high inflation for nearly eight years, wage earners in particular turned to these funds to protect their modest savings from the devastating effects of inflation. It also appears that small and medium-sized industrialists and traders, as well as a very large number of small business owners, who have been unable to access credit and affordable financing amid high inflation and high interest rates, invested money in these funds even to address their short-term financing needs. These massive financial fraud schemes were made possible precisely by this widespread participation. In a sense, the ruling elites openly robbed a very large section of society. Yes, there is absolutely nothing wrong with calling it what it was: robbery."


'Those running the regime had no choice but to intervene'


Özdal said that the political leadership had been forced to intervene after the crisis erupted, warning that its consequences would not be confined to financial markets but could also affect production, trade and employment. Özdal pointed to estimates suggesting that the losses exceeded $100 billion, arguing that the crisis would have social and political consequences as well …

title: 'Voce Arcaica' Festival in memory of Nagihan Akarsel to take place in Rome on 7 November
content:
The 'Voce Arcaica' (Ancient Voice) Art and Culture Festival, organised annually in Italy by the Jineolojî Academy, is held in memory of Nagihan Akarsel, a member of the Jineolojî Research Centre, writer and journalist who was assassinated in an armed attack outside her home in Sulaymaniyah (Silêmanî) on 4 October 2022.


The festival will take place on 7 November at the Teatro Biblioteca Quarticciolo in Rome, and aims to bring women together through art, culture and collective creation.


In an

article

, the Jineolojî Academy wrote that the festival was organised to continue the work of Nagihan Akarsel, who made significant contributions to Jineolojî, women's journalism and research on women, and to keep her ideas alive through art.


The article emphasised that art is not merely a form of expression, but also a means of passing on women's collective memory, resistance and experiences of struggle.


Four stops on the festival's journey


As part of this year's third edition, events have been held throughout the year in Rome, Reggio Calabria, Turin, Bologna and the Dutch town of Haelen. At these gatherings, the book

Voce Arcaica

 (Ancient Voice), a collection of 16 articles by Nagihan Akarsel, was introduced. Participants also took part in a collective embroidery project featuring a portrait of Nagihan Akarsel.


Through workshops, readings and artistic events held in different cities, women came together to discuss Nagihan Akarsel's ideas and Jineolojî. The collective embroidery project continued throughout the festival's various stops, with women from different communities contributing to the work.


During these gatherings, participants shared ideas, emotions, dreams and memories. The portrait of Nagihan Akarsel is scheduled to be exhibited at the Rome gathering on 7 November.


Theatre, music and dance


The programme on 7 November will begin with a workshop in the Quarticciolo neighbourhood, running from 10 am to 1 pm. Led by Barbara Criscimanno from Palermo and the Trizzi Ri Donna collective, the workshop will explore the choral, dance and rhythmic traditions of southern Italy. The workshop will be free of charge and open to women and people of diverse identities.


The festival's evening programme will begin at 8.30 pm on the stage of Teatro Biblioteca Quarticciolo. Performers will include Rachele Andrioli & Coro a Coro, Deniz Deman, the European Jineolojî Choir and Controchiave Teatro. The event will feature theatre, music and dance performances, conveying women's stories of struggle and resistance through art.


The festival is being organised in collaboration with the Jineolojî Academy, alongside women's organisations and solidarity networks including Rete Jin, Rete Donneche Tessono il Futuro, Oltre and Non Una di Meno Roma. The event forms part of wider initiatives aimed at bringing women together through art and culture ahead of 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women.

title: Tekirdağ'ın Saray ilçesinde taşkın: Köprü kapatıldı, mahsur kalan 2 kişi kurtarıldı
content:
Tekirdağ'ın Saray ilçesinde Galata Deresi'nde meydana gelen taşkın nedeniyle Kiremithane Köprüsü, güvenlik amacıyla geçici olarak ulaşıma kapatıldı.

Saray Belediye Başkanı Abdül Taşyasan, Fen İşleri Müdürlüğüne bağlı ekiplerin köprüde gerekli güvenlik önlemlerini aldığını bildirdi. Köprü çevresinde polis ekiplerince de güvenlik önlemi alındı.

Mantar toplamak için Kanara Kanyonu'na giden Y.B. ve A.K, derenin debisinin yükselmesi sonucu mahsur kaldı. İhbar üzerine bölgeye AFAD, jandarma ve itfaiye ekipleri sevk edildi. Mahsur kalan 2 kişi, ekiplerin iş makinesiyle yürüttüğü çalışma sonucu kurtarıldı.

Safaalan Mahallesi'nde ise su baskını tehdidi altındaki bir ev ekipler tarafından boşaltıldı. Evde yaşayan 6 kişilik aile, Saray Belediyesi tarafından otele yerleştirildi.

Sağanağın etkili olması beklenen ilçede belediye ekipleri, yaşanabilecek olumsuzluklara karşı tedbir amacıyla hazır bekletiliyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Şüpheli şekilde yaşamını yitiren Nurcan Akpirinç’in dosyasında 5 aydır gelişme yok
content:
Diyarbakır'ın Bağlar ilçesinde 20 Haziran’da evinde şüpheli bir şekilde ölü bulunan 23 yaşındaki Nurcan Akpirinç’in ölümüne ilişkin soruşturma sürerken, aradan geçen 5 aya rağmen otopsi raporu hâlâ çıkmadı. Anne Asiye Akpirinç, kızı ve katledilen tüm kadınlar için adalet talebinde bulundu.

Olay günü mahalleye ambulans geldiğini 4 ay sonra öğrendiklerini belirten Asiye Akpirinç, birinin 112'yi arayıp yardım istediğini, ambulanstakilerin mahalleye gelip arayanı bulamayarak geri gittiğini söyledi. Kızının sağlık ekiplerini arayıp yardım istediğine inandığını ifade eden anne Akpirinç, bu durumun ve 112 çağrısının detaylı bir şekilde araştırılmasını istedi.

Kızının ölümünün üzerinden 5 ay geçmesine rağmen otopsi raporunun hâlâ çıkmadığını ve verdikleri dilekçelere her seferinde "incelemede" yanıtı aldıklarını kaydeden Asiye Akpirinç, "Kaç defa dilekçe verdik, otopsi raporunu istiyoruz. Kızımın 112’yi arayıp yardım istediğinin araştırılmasını istiyoruz. Neden hâlâ bize bir cevap verilmiyor?" diye tepki gösterdi.

Kızının alnında ve sağ kulağının arkasında darp izleri gördüğünü belirten anne Akpirinç, M.A. ve annesi C.A. tarafından sürekli şiddete uğradığını ifade etti. Olay günü kendilerine bilgi verilmediğini, kızının evde olmadığının söylenerek köyde aranmasının istendiğini, saatler sonra ise aynı evde yaşamını yitirdiğini öğrendiklerini aktaran Akpirinç, "Kızımın intihar ettiğine inanmıyorum" dedi.

Sorumluların açığa çıkarılmasını ve cezalandırılmasını talep eden Asiye Akpirinç, "Adalet istiyorum. Hükümet sesimizi duysun, savcılar, hâkimler sesimizi duysun. Sadece kızım için değil, katledilen bütün kadınlar için adalet istiyorum. Başka annelerin canı yanmasın. Bu işin peşini bırakmayacağız, sonuna kadar mücadele edeceğiz" ifadelerini kullandı.

Diyarbakır'ın Bağlar ilçesinde 20 Haziran’da dini nikahla evli olduğu aktarılan M.A. ile tartıştıktan sonra annesini arayan Nurcan Akpirinç ailesinin yanına gitmek istemişti. Kızlarından haber alamayan ailenin evine gitmesi üzerine Nurcan’ın evde olmadığı söylenmiş, yaklaşık iki saat sonra ise evin misafir odasında yaşamını yitirdiği ortaya çıkmıştı. Aile, Nurcan’ın daha önce defalarca tehdit edildiğini belirtmesine rağmen 5 aylık süreçte otopsi raporunun çıkmadığı ve yalnızca aile bireylerinin ifadesinin alındığı bildirilmişti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.
