author: Daron Letts
title: ‘Government-wide effort’ needed to fix broken foster system: premier
content:
One day after the federal auditor general’s office published its latest

report

 on the state of Nunavut’s foster care system, Premier John Main pledged his government will do better.


“This report is upsetting,” Main said during a news conference at the legislative assembly Wednesday.

“The responsibilities that lie with our government are serious and we need to live up to the duties that have been entrusted to us.”


Deputy auditor general Andrew Hayes tabled the report,

Foster Care in Nunavut,

 in Nunavut’s legislative assembly on Tuesday. The federal auditor general has the authority to review the effectiveness of Government of Nunavut programs.


The document outlines the Family Services department’s failures to maintain regular contact with children in care, to screen and monitor foster homes, and to maintain reliable information on the number of children in the system and where they had been placed — a problem that was highlighted in the auditor general’s

2023 report

.


“The Department of Family Services did not provide timely and effective foster care services to protect and support the safety and well-being of children,” Hayes said during a news conference Tuesday afternoon. “It could not consistently demonstrate that basic safeguards intended to protect children and place them in safe environments were being followed.”


The department’s failure to solve the lapse in data stems from the department staff’s lack of training on its

centralized reporting system

, known as Matrix, Hayes said.


“We saw differences between the manual lists that the department is working with and the information in Matrix. That is a problem,” Hayes said.


Family Services Minister Gwen Healey Akearok said that is changing.


“The Matrix training has been unrolling throughout the territory,” she said at the news conference. “There’s another one happening this month.”


She said 90 per cent of front-line staff and 80 per cent of other staff have been trained so far.


“We know we need that evidence. We need strong documentation. We need excellent records,” Healey Akearok said.

“Every foster file is now in one system.”


She said that

97 per cent of home studies have been completed and, as of October, 82 per cent of annual reviews had been completed.


“There’s still work to be done,” she added.


The auditor general will release another report in the spring of 2027, on the department’s “quality assurance work,” Hayes said. 


Nunavummiut will see improvements in that report thanks to “a government-wide effort,” Main said.

“Our sincere hope is that future audits will show real improvement.”


Asked if any staff will lose their jobs over the report’s findings, Main said he will not share that publicly.


“From the upper management on down, there is an expectation that you will fulfill your duties, and if not, you’ll face the consequences,” he said.

author: Katharine Trendacosta
title: Google Summaries Aren't About AI, They're About Lock-In
content:
Whether they call it AI summaries, knowledge panels, or AMP, Google takes actions that are less about functionality and more about locking you into its own ecosystem. Knowing that makes it possible for all of us to choose better services than Google's, defeating their anticompetitive goal. In this case, as it is so often, knowledge is power.

 


In the old days, when dinosaurs roamed the earth and getting online involved your computer making eldritch shrieking, Google was a website that took whatever you typed in and gave you a list of links that best matched what you were searching for. As it's grown beyond that, however, the core function of Google Search has moved from giving you the best answer to your query to a number of other things, most of them about making money for Google.

 


This is obviously not a new observation. It's at the core of what EFF Special Advisor Cory Doctorow named "

enshittification

." But it's important to remember that whatever shiny new name or technology is wrapped around these tools, it's not about the wrapping, it's about the monetization.

 


In the case of Google Search, the company has a history of rolling out new "features" that are less helpful to the searcher and more designed to keep you and your data within the Google ecosystem. One easy example of enshittification is putting sponsored links and ads at the top of search results, forcing you to scroll down past a bunch of not relevant links to get to your answers. Or, in some cases, accidentally clicking on sponsored links that might be designed to give you the opposite information of what you're looking for or for a competitor to the product you intended to buy.

 


The other clumsy version of this is Google's self-preferencing, where Google's own services—say YouTube if you're looking for a video—are weighted so that they appear at the top of a search over a competitor's. Similar to this was Google's push for websites, particularly news ones, to be made available via what it called

"Accelerated Mobile Pages" or AMP

, which in theory stripped out features that might make loading a page on mobile too slow, but also handed over control of how webpages looked on mobile to Google and turned mobile links, often by default, into Google links.

 


But the other way that Google has historically kept your—and your valuable eyeballs—on its website has been to just obviate the need to even click on a link and leave Google at all. The first version of this was what Google calls "knowledge panels." These are snippets of information shown on the results page of a search that purport to answer your question. Knowledge panels predate the AI push and haven't always been what you could call

accurate

.

 


Knowledge panels are extremely similar to the AI summaries we now see at the top of Google Search results, except that instead of pulling quotes from specific linked sources, it's the AI doing the summarizing, though also sometimes with links. They are basically the same thing, mostly changed only in branding, because AI is now the cool kid on the block. The goal is essentially the same—it's less about providing you with the best answer to your query and more about making you think it's unnecessary to click a link and leave Google's ecosystem. And, more importantly, it keeps you on Google's pages longer to read the content. More time on the page is more time exposed to ads and sponsored links and more money for Google. 

 


The biggest irony here is that

it didn’t even work

. People choosing to use “AI mode”—and possibly made accustomed to getting information as text instead of links through the knowledge panels and the AI summaries at the top—has caused

“lower monetization”

 via ads. Ads, remember, are Google’s main source of revenue. Like newspapers before them, Google is finding that counting on a monopoly on ad space maybe isn’t the most sound strategy in a shifting technological landscape. And to get out of the hole it has made for itself, it is lighting cash on fire to try to get back on top. Perhaps they should consider pivoting to video.

 


Every time you see a feature like this, no matter what it is called or what "new" technology they claim fuels it, remember that it is Google's monetary incentives that drive the decisions and not necessarily the tech itself. And you can always choose to ignore it, scroll past, disable it, or even

go to another service entirely

.

title: “Donald … Call Me Senator”: Abdul El-Sayed Wins by 7 in Triumph Over GOP Bigotry
content:
“Donald, I know you struggled with my name. So after JD swears me in … call me senator,” El-Sayed said.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Abdul El-Sayed walloped his Republican opponent, Mike Rogers, in Michigan on Tuesday, marking a massive triumph over the strategy of flat-out Islamophobic bigotry that Donald Trump, the GOP, and even many liberals embraced in the months of fierce campaigning against the progressive pro-Palestine senator-elect.

“They went all in on one of the ugliest campaigns we’ve seen in our lifetimes,” said El-Sayed in his victory speech early Wednesday morning. “They weren’t just attacking me. They were targeting and attacking you. They were targeting and attacking the very idea of America.”

With over 95 percent of votes counted, El-Sayed had 52.5 percent of the vote compared to Rogers’s 45.5 percent — matching the exact margin that El-Sayed predicted he would win back in May.

This is despite Trump and Republicans making him one of their primary targets this midterm cycle, with Trump spewing Islamophobic hate and incitement to violence against El-Sayed nearly every time he spoke at a rally or with the media. At a rally in Michigan in late October, Trump said El-Sayed is a “jihadist” and that the Senate should install a metal detector just to screen him.

He and others like Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) suggested that El-Sayed was violent with no evidence, pointing only to his faith. After winning the primary in August, Rogers’s first statement suggested that El-Sayed was a terrorist. “I spent years hunting terrorists and bringing Osama bin Laden to justice,” he said.

Liberal pundits and politicians, too, joined in on the bigoted pile-ons; El-Sayed’s AIPAC-backed primary opponent, Haley Stevens, used hateful tropes against him during the bitter primary race, and she ultimately issued a surprise endorsement of Rogers two days before the election.

El-Sayed often spoke out against the hate, hammering people like Trump and Vice President JD Vance. He also kept a laser-focus on his agenda: Medicare for All, banning corporate money in politics, and opposing further assistance to Israel.

On Wednesday night, El-Sayed said that his win was for “all the parents who struggled to explain why the president openly mocked” people like him.

“Mike, enjoy your retirement…. You chose hate, and Michigan chose hope. May we never have to see the likes of you in this state ever again,” he said.

“JD, habibi. There is this delicious irony that you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January,” El-Sayed went on, to raucous cheers from the crowd. “Donald, I know you struggled with my name. So after JD swears me in in January, you can just go on and call me senator.”

El-Sayed also spoke out against the pro-Israel lobby, with AIPAC pouring a record amount into the election to defeat him. He espoused the “love” that he has for the Palestinian people, drawing a sharp contrast to the hatred levied against him.

“To AIPAC who spent $42 million against us: Thank you for giving me the opportunity to beat you twice,” he said. “They try to call you hateful if you believe that Palestinian kids should get to grow up in the land of their forefathers, to not be murdered by our tax dollars. If you believe in equal rights to peace, dignity, and self-determination, that’s not hate, it’s love.”

The corporate media waged an all-out attack on El-Sayed, in part due to his stances on Israel. Outlets like The New York Times ran stories about him losing Jewish voters and accusing him of antisemitism, without evidence. Corporate outlets also spread a narrative that he had “struggled to win over Black voters” in the state, as Politico wrote on Sunday, or that many Democrats were peeling off from him to vote for Rogers.

But Tuesday’s result shows that these narratives were overblown. Exit polls suggested that Jewish people overwhelmingly went for El-Sayed, and data from VoteHub finds that El-Sayed won majority-Black districts by a whopping 81-point margin. The “Democrats for Mike Rogers” PAC, which poured millions into the race, was revealed by Truthout in October to be a Republican front group.

author: Sasha Abramsky
title: The Egg on Elon Musk’s Face Cost More Than $440 Million
content:
Musk’s astronomical campaign contributions were no match for outraged voters across the US.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Elon Musk, the world’s wealthiest man, went on a spending spree in the weeks leading up to the midterms. By Election Day, he had invested — and I use that word deliberately — more than $440 million into propping up the GOP to try to make its message and its candidates more palatable with voters during an election cycle in which their brand had become increasingly toxic.

Astoundingly, nearly half of that money — more than $190 million — was spent on one campaign: Ken Paxton’s effort to make the leap from an impeached state attorney general to being U.S. senator for Texas. Musk was, in broad daylight, like the gilded age oligarchs of the late-19th century, essentially trying to buy himself a senator.

Many rich candidates have in recent years self-funded their candidacies or intervened in initiative campaigns — Michael Bloomberg put in more than $1 billion into his go-nowhere presidential campaign in 2020, Tom Steyer spent upwards of $200 million in his recent futile attempt to become the California governor, and a cluster of billionaires, led by Google’s Sergei Brin, put obscene amounts of money into opposing the billionaires’ wealth tax initiative before voters in California this election. This year, the Texas race seems to be the first time a single non-candidate donor has put this much money into a particular marquee contest.

Musk — who relocated to Texas during the pandemic in a fit of pique against California’s public health mandates — has a large and growing business footprint in Texas, and a desire to take over more land both for his space launch business and his data centers; he therefore needs political figures from the state not only on his side but in his pocket, as Democrats began gleefully pointing out in the final month of the campaign.

The SpaceX titan isn’t, of course, alone in his mega-donations. The Brennan Center for Justice has reported that in the 2026 election cycle, 40 mega-donors altogether ponied up an astounding $2.5 billion, the large majority for GOP candidates. But the scale of Elon Musk’s financial outlay does put him in a league of his own. Individually, in 2026 Musk gave more than twice as much to candidates as did the entire cryptocurrency industry — which has also not been shy about buying political loyalties as its footprint has increased in size.

Most of Musk’s money was channeled through the Senate Leadership Fund, the coordinating fund the GOP ran for its Senate candidates. This move allowed Paxton, whose entire career has been a pinball exercise caroming from one corruption scandal to the next, to flood the vast Texas media market with attack advertisements in the weeks leading up to the election. The Republican candidate’s campaign promptly used this money to lean ever further into anti-trans messaging, saturating the airwaves with ads accusing Democratic candidate James Talarico of being an extremist for transgender rights.

Then, as the governor’s race in Texas tightened, with Democrat Gina Hinojosa making an unexpectedly strong run to break the GOP stranglehold on the state’s top office, Musk also began injecting millions of dollars into Greg Abbott’s re-election campaign.

But Musk’s ambitions weren’t limited to the Lone Star State. In this election cycle, the oligarch gave tens of millions of dollars to super PACs supporting vulnerable GOP candidates in House races around the country and funneled millions more to gubernatorial and attorneys general campaigns, recognizing that a Democratic victory would likely harm his corporate ventures and reduce the flow of money from government contracts.

In New Hampshire, Musk’s super PAC, America PAC, pumped $1 million into supporting Republican candidate John Sununu for a Senate seat that the GOP identified early in the campaign season as a possible pick-up. In New York, the trillionaire’s PAC put hundreds of thousands of dollars into efforts to salvage GOP Congressman Mike Lawler’s campaign in the competitive 17th congressional district. Singlehandedly, Musk seemed intent on showing, throughout election season, just how much financial sway the oligarchy can have on U.S. politics. author: David Swanson
title: Taxpayers Mobilize in Washington, D.C., to Protest $1.5 Trillion Military Budget
content:
Economic Cost, Immorality, Nonviolent Activism, North America, What to do

By CODEPINK and a large coalition of advocacy groups, November 4, 2026

Taxpayers from across the U.S. will gather in Washington, D.C., from November 10 to 12, 2026, to protest the proposed $1.5 trillion 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). Organized by CODEPINK and a large coalition of advocacy groups, the demonstration aims to put the country’s excessive and harmful military spending at the forefront of the national conversation after the midterms.

“The midterm elections were a nationwide condemnation of Trump and Hegseth’s horrible war in Iran. The Taxpayer Uprising is about creatively and beautifully making sure this current Congress doesn’t forget about it – because passing Trump’s war budget would mean green-lighting his reckless wars for the remainder of his presidency,” explained CODEPINK’s national co-director Danaka Katovich.

The three-day event will feature office visits with elected officials and visual demonstrations. Tentative schedule as follows:

Tuesday, November 10: Senate Office Visits from 10 am- 4 pm: The group will kick off the first day of action at the Dirksen Cafeteria at 10 am. They will break off into specific advocacy groups and visit senators’ offices.

Wednesday, November 11: Victims of the War Budget Processional, 10–2 pm, starting at Peace Monument.

Thursday, November 12: House of Representatives office visits, 10 am-4 pm. The group will meet at the Rayburn Cafeteria at 10 am, then break into groups to visit their representatives’ offices. There will also be an Ice Cream Social with Ben & Jerry’s own Ben Cohen at 2pm at the Intersection of First Street SE and Independence Avenue SE.

Constituents from various states, including California and Texas, will join organizations like CODEPINK, World BEYOND War, RootsAction, National Priorities Project at the Institute for Policy Studies, Doctors Against Genocide, Climate Defenders, CAIR National, Eisenhower Media Network, National Iranian American Council, Fellowship of Reconciliation, American Muslims for Palestine, Veterans For Peace, DSA International Committee, and more in demanding a reallocation of funds towards domestic needs.

“We’ve tried voting our way to represent our overwhelming public preference for less war funding and more funding of human and environmental needs. Now let’s add the powerful tool of nonviolent activism. Now let’s make it harder to defy the people of this country than it is to defy the war profiteers.” – David Swanson, Co-Founder and Executive Director, World BEYOND War.

“Americans are increasingly recognizing the connection between funding the genocide in Gaza, the ongoing ethnic cleansing in the West Bank, Israel’s escalating aggression across the region, and the illegal war on Iran, and their own struggles to make ends meet and achieve economic mobility. Our lawmakers appear more concerned with appeasing the Israel lobby and war profiteers than listening to the majority of Americans, who do not want endless, unjustified wars and instead support greater investment in social welfare, education, healthcare, and workers’ rights. The Taxpayer Uprising is our way of continuing to build the political power necessary to secure a future that prioritizes people over war and invests in the well-being of our communities.” AMP executive director, Dr. Osama Abu Irshaid

The Trump Administration’s proposal marks the largest increase in military spending in modern history, prioritizing the war budget over human needs like healthcare, education, and housing. The proposed budget allocates about $116.43 million per hour to US warfare, ranging from illegal boat bombings in the Americas to the disastrous war in Iran. Half of that will go directly to contractors in the arms and AI industries. Meanwhile, nearly 45,000 Americans die annually due to lack of health insurance. Shifting even a small share of military spending to healthcare and social programs would save countless lives in the US and worldwide.

If you select to make a recurring contribution of at least $15 per month, you may select a thank-you gift. We thank our recurring donors on our website.

author: Chris Walker
title: Jeffries Downplays Trump Accountability Push After Democrats’ Midterm Blowout
content:
The potential Speaker of the House has brushed aside plans by Democrats to investigate the Trump administration.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

House minority leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York) is downplaying the potential to hold the Trump administration accountable following Democrats’ monumental win in the 2026 midterm elections, despite a large proportion of voters signaling that they believe there are grounds for impeaching President Donald Trump.

In an interview following the midterm elections, Jeffries, who is considered Democrats’ top prospect for Speaker of the House, disregarded plans by high-ranking members of his party to pursue inquiries into the White House’s actions over the past two years.

On MS NOW’s “Morning Joe” program, conservative host Joe Scarborough asked Jeffries how he plans to keep Democrats “focused on the things that got them elected,” listing several affordability issues but rejecting the idea of “retribution” against the administration. Jeffries appeared to agree with Scarborough’s framing.

“The American people don’t want us to get even; they want us to get things done on their behalf, because life is way too expensive,” Jeffries said, adding that the party “won on affordability.”

In his Tuesday night speech celebrating the outcome of the midterms, Jeffries only briefly mentioned a commitment to fighting corruption. Instead, he delivered a reconciliatory message — “This is not a partisan moment. This is a patriotic moment,” he said. “This is not a blue moment or a red moment. It’s a red, white and blue moment because America has won tonight.”

While the economy was the top issue for voters, a sizable number of Americans stated in polls conducted prior to the midterms that accountability and opposition to corruption was a higher priority for them.

In an Economist/YouGov poll published late last month, for example, more than a quarter of likely voters, 26 percent, said that “presidential leadership,” “corruption and waste,” and “democracy and the rule of law” were their top priorities. Among Democratic voters, 41 percent of respondents said these were their top issues, while around 3 in 10 independent voters (29 percent) counted them as their top priorities.

Americans have also stated that their votes should be seen as a direct check on Trump. According to an NPR/PBS NewsHour/Marist poll published in September, 45 percent of voters said their choices in the midterms should be viewed as a “vote against” the president.

Support for impeaching Trump is high among the electorate, with a Politico survey from October finding that 54 percent of voters believe there are grounds to do so, while only 33 percent disagree.

Despite strong support from voters for the concept, Jeffries appeared to reject impeachment as a possibility in remarks to reporters on Wednesday, claiming that no one in his conference had discussed it with him yet.

“I haven’t had a single member of the House Democratic caucus talk to me about impeachment. We’ve been relentlessly focused on affordability and accountability,” Jeffries said.

Economist Paul Krugman wrote on his Substack that Democrats would be mistaken to view the results of Tuesday night’s elections as solely about affordability.

“Trumpflation created by tariffs and the Iran debacle helped” Democrats to win, Krugman said. “But an election swung by public anger over high prices looks like 2024, when Trump won the popular vote by 1.5 percentage points. Last night, Democrats appear to have won the popular vote by 13-14 percentage points.”

The outcome suggests that a broad coalition of voters is upset with how Trump is governing overall.

“What drove this amazing victory?” Krugman continued. “Hispanic voters, who swung to Trump in 2024 in the naïve belief that he would bring prices down, turned massively against a regime that is arresting, imprisoning and deporting their friends and families. [Black voters] turned out in droves against a transparently racist party that is trying to take away their voting rights. Americans of every kind were repelled by the administration’s cruelty and its rampant, brazen corruption.”

“MAGA took 2024 as proof that Americans want fascism, and acted on that premise. But tens of millions of Americans in effect said, no, that is not what we want. That is not who we are,” he added.

author: Brad Reed
title: Montana Votes Overwhelmingly to Ban Corporate Cash From Political Campaigns
content:
Supporters have billed the initiative as a way to strike a blow against the Supreme Court’s 2010 Citizens United ruling.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Voters in Montana on Tuesday delivered a major blow to big moneyed interests by overwhelmingly passing a ballot initiative barring corporate cash from political campaigns in the state.

With 87% of votes counted as of Wednesday morning, Montana Constitutional Initiative 194 has received support from more than 65% of voters, with just 35% registering opposition.

The initiative prohibits what it describes as “artificial persons” — which includes corporations, nonprofits, trusts, partnerships, and trade associations — from giving money to political campaigns.

Supporters of the initiative have billed it as a way to strike a blow against the Supreme Court’s 2010 ruling in Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission, which opened the door to unlimited campaign spending in US politics.

“A yes vote on I-194 means that only real people — not corporations, unions, trade associations, nonprofits, or groups with anonymous donors — are allowed to spend money in Montana elections,” the Yes on Initiative 194 campaign explained on its website. “It’s time to kick the oligarchs out of Big Sky country.”

The initiative’s overwhelming victory drew praise from Tom Moore, senior fellow at the Center for American Progress, who congratulated the people of Montana for taking “a historic step toward ending the scourge of corporate and dark money in politics.”

Moore noted that the initiative passed by Montana is similar to a law passed in Hawaii earlier this year that classified corporations as “artificial persons” who do not have a constitutional right to make political donations.

Both states, Moore said, are “setting a bold example for other states to follow suit, sending a powerful message that we don’t have to give corporations unlimited power.”

“The more states that follow this innovative approach,” he added, “the more we can make Citizens United irrelevant.”

Stacy Mitchell, co-executive director at the Institute for Local Self-Reliance, hailed the initiative’s passage as a win for democratic governance.

“We’ve largely forgotten that states define what corporations can do,” Mitchell wrote in a social media post. “Yesterday, Montana voters overwhelmingly stripped corporations of the power to spend money influencing elections. Hawaii did the same in May. Both face court fights. Our nascent citizen muscle is coming to life.”

Adam Bojak, a Democrat who on Tuesday won an election in New York State Assembly District 149, said he’d like to see the Empire State follow the trail blazed by Montana and Hawaii.

“Congratulations to the people of Montana!” Bojak wrote. “I can’t wait to bring this legislation to New York in next year’s session.”

author: Daniel Hunter
title: Voters repudiated Trump. Grassroots momentum will shape what comes next.
content:
This article

Voters repudiated Trump. Grassroots momentum will shape what comes next.

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


The broad strokes of the midterms are clear: a massive repudiation of MAGA’s fascist wave has ended the Trump 2.0 era of congressional complicity with his authoritarian takeover. Trump’s lame duck presidency now begins. 


This lopsided electoral rejection is historically rare: Flipping control of both the House and Senate in a midterm has only occurred

three times since World War II

 (1946, 1994 and 2006). The breakthroughs are astounding:

the first Native American governor and senator

,

five Black governors

, the first

majority of Democratic governors in 16 years

, and critical downballot wins like the first Democrat to win as

Texan oil regulator since 1990

 and the

first openly transgender state legislator in Alabama

.


Authoritarians do not do well when trapped — and with a famously norm-busting president, anything is possible. But, critically, election deniers like

Darline Graham

 and

Greg Abbott

 are conceding their races. Donald Trump is already saying he’s

“absolutely willing”

 to accept the results and

told CBS

, “Congratulations to the Democrats, and I look forward to working with you for the good of our country.”


So what do we do now?


1. It’s OK to exhale


These midterms have left me, like many, with abundant free-floating anxieties. The

“what if” scenarios

 have been abundant — and while some of the most extreme versions did not happen, the federal government was weaponized against the election system like never before.


Because the times have been so rough, it can be hard to exhale and accept a win, especially since elections are not material changes — they are promissory notes that the future may be different. Until Jan. 3, we live under the same dangerous authoritarian government, even if the atmosphere has changed.


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


Before I advocate for you to breathe, let’s affirm all the many hard reasons to not exhale. The wins were not universal, as some big losses cut deep. There’s a reality that all of this is ephemeral if Democrats cannot govern a policy of change — if we only manage an economic status quo it will disillusion and likely result in yet another whiplash election in the other direction. And it’s hard to breathe in a dizzying moment.


Further, the attacks on elections were treasonous. I won’t list the complete litany of federal assaults — but we have a Department of Justice captured by authoritarian forces using its power nakedly for partisan goals. The far right openly prepared

sham legal theories

 to refuse certification of Democratic representatives. While we did not get systematic federal law enforcement terror at polls, we saw National Guard throughout

Washington, D.C.

 We still have too many election officials committed to the Big Lie. And ongoing structural impediments to a fair election are consequential: In Mississippi, the Senate margin remains tiny while any win may be marred by

equipment trouble, poll changes,

 and

voters unexpectedly removed by data purges from the voting rolls

.  


Notably, the election maps themselves have been gerrymandered by racists to ensure power — though their greed rebounded

multiple losses

 in these redistricted seats. (Groups like Black Voters Matter deserve a huge shout-out for fighting in the South and in races Democrats had abandoned.)


Despite all that, we managed a pro-democracy win that was too big to rig. The country delivered a shellacking to MAGA politics — an encouraging sign for all of us who are hoping for a better future. Ultimately, the election proceeded with voters refusing to be intimidated.


Buddhists remind me we can take a breath anytime. But this moment seems as good a moment as any, especially when we remind ourselves exhaling isn’t signaling that things are over. Exhales are how our body gets in tune with this moment and releases the latest tension. Bracing doesn’t make us wiser, just tenser.


So really, take five breaths right now. As you breathe, read in a poem by

Jarod Anderson

: “

You can be still while the world is whirling. / You can be silent while your heart is thundering. / You can be alone while your memory is teeming. / You can live forever in the span of a moment. / You can grow kindness in the soil of hatred. / You can decide purpose. You can decide …

author: Andrea DiP
title: “Em nome do Pai”: evangélicos se afastam de Flávio porque nunca gostaram do filho de Jair
content:
“Esses filhos de Bolsonaro são uns jumentos. Só se aconselham com gente errada! Faz carta, fala bobagem, depois corrige (…) Um bando de amadores babacas”. A frase,

revelada pela coluna de Malu Gaspar para O Globo

 no último dia 28, foi enviada em um grupo de WhatsApp pelo pastor e influenciador político Silas Malafaia, um dos maiores líderes evangélicos do Brasil e aliado de primeiro escalão de Jair Bolsonaro durante seu governo. O comentário foi feito após a fuga de Flávio Bolsonaro aos Estados Unidos e da publicação da carta (ou seria das cartas?) em que o candidato derrotado se apresentava como o verdadeiro presidente do “Brazil”. 


As trapalhadas do 01 têm levado pastores das mega-igrejas protestantes a se posicionarem publicamente em uma tentativa de se distanciar de vez do nome da família Bolsonaro e de sua trilha de escândalos.

 No dia seguinte à eleição de Lula no segundo turno, o bispo Alessandro Paschoall da Igreja Universal publicou o trecho de um culto realizado por Edir Macedo em que ele criticava o lema “Deus, pátria e família” usado pelos Bolsonaro. “Na Universal, nós priorizamos essa hierarquia: primeiro Deus, depois família, e depois o resto. Não concordo com essa teoria “Deus, pátria e família”. Porque se não houver família, vai haver pátria? Impossível. Só há pátria se vier da família, que vem de Deus”, disse Macedo na manhã da votação do segundo turno. 


Curiosamente, o lema – que, vale lembrar, foi usado no Brasil na década de 1930 pela Ação Integralista Brasileira, movimento nacionalista de inspiração fascista liderado por Plínio Salgado –só incomodou o bispo agora. Macedo, que é pragmático e costuma se aliar a quem estiver no poder, foi um apoiador de Jair Bolsonaro em 2018 e em 2022, mas se manteve distante nas eleições deste ano. 


Outro bispo, Abner Ferreira, da Assembleia de Deus, que apoiou Flávio no segundo turno e chegou a participar de um mega culto promovido por seu irmão Bispo Samuel Ferreira, presidente da Convenção Nacional das Assembleias de Deus no Brasil no Maracanãzinho com direito a pedido de voto e a presença de Flávio, reconheceu rapidamente a vitória de Lula e publicou um texto em suas redes sociais na semana passada dizendo que a democracia “exige maturidade, equilíbrio e respeito às decisões populares, independentemente das convicções e preferências individuais”.


Outros bispos e pastores evangélicos também têm se manifestado na mesma direção, como o bispo JB Carvalho, da Comunidade das Nações, igreja de Brasília onde Flávio foi batizado em 2024 e o Líder da Igreja Fonte da Vida, Apóstolo César Augusto, também aliado de Flávio. Ou estão em silêncio.


Mas essa tentativa de afastamento por parte de líderes das principais igrejas evangélicas não começou após a carta golpista. É um movimento que vem se anunciando e que reflete também o desgaste desse apoio descarado entre os fieis.

Parece haver uma avaliação de que o saldo positivo desse apoio incondicional aos Bolsonaro ficou só para a família, enquanto as igrejas tiveram cada vez mais sua reputação atrelada a golpes, violência, escândalos de corrupção, etc. 


Em conversa com a coluna, a professora do Programa de Pós-graduação em Sociologia e coordenadora do LePar (laboratório de estudos em Política, Arte e Religião da Universidade Federal Fluminense) Christina Vital, que é pesquisadora do campo evangélico de longa data, faz uma reflexão sobre esse reposicionamento: 


“O afastamento de líderes evangélicos em relação ao bolsonarismo tem a marca das eleições de 2022. De lá para cá só vimos crescer esse afastamento com críticas veementes como tentativa de se limparem moralmente em relação à truculência e corrupção associadas ao bolsonarismo.

Nas eleições de 2026 isso se agravou e não vimos um investimento continuado e intenso em torno do nome de Flávio Bolsonaro por parte de muitos líderes evangélicos e, logo após a derrota, vimos as críticas públicas se avolumarem. A fuga para os EUA foi o estopim de uma relação que já não se sustentava

”, diz ela. 


Segundo ela,

Flávio Bolsonaro não era um nome desejado por ninguém. Líderes religiosos não viam nele a força e maturidade suficientes.

 Michelle Bolsonaro também não foi uma apoiadora de primeira hora, e chegou a jogar contra com o vídeo de 27 minutos, revelando que as críticas que ela faz ali não são tudo o que ela sabia.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Google UK Signs ‘Sweetheart Deal’ With Employer-Friendly Union
content:
Google UK has been accused of signing a “sweetheart deal” with an employer-friendly union to undermine workers’ ability to organise within the tech company. 


Google

signed an access agreement with Prospect union on Monday

 to make inroads among its 7,000 UK workers – excluding DeepMind staff – after

new rights for unions to access workplaces

 in Britain came into force last week.


However, critics say Prospect lacks a strong record of organising with Google employees – known as Googlers – in the UK. The two largest and most active unions in Google UK are Unite and the Communication Workers’ Union (CWU) via their United Tech and Allied Workers (UTAW) branch. 


Prospect was granted access to the Google UK workforce over Unite and the CWU, despite the latter two unions applying for access as soon as formally possible. This means Prospect can now

communicate with non-unionised workers

 and encourage them to join. 


In a joint Unite and CWU statement to members seen by Novara Media, the two unions warned that Prospect’s agreement with Google is only for “occasional meetings and an internal page, falling far short of the legal minimum requested by your unions”. 


A Google UK software engineer and UTAW rep, speaking to Novara Media on the condition of anonymity due to fear of professional reprisals, called the deal “a huge slap in the face for me and all UTAW and Unite organisers in Google”.  


The software engineer said: “We have worked diligently over the past few years to represent our fellow Googlers’ needs through collective action. We fought to keep as many jobs as possible during redundancies, we demonstrated against Google’s military contracts, and we demanded a stronger, worker-led regulation on Google and DeepMind’s AI direction. 


“For all of our fastidious work, our request for a right as basic as access has been ignored and given to Prospect, a union with laughably low membership in Google which has not participated in a single one of our aforementioned struggles.”


Unite and the CWU are asking why Prospect, which has not engaged in member-led unionising activity at Google, was granted access so quickly and alleging that the Prospect deal was pre-planned because Prospect may be considered a “tamer” or more employer-friendly union.


The Google software engineer added: “This conduct by Google is an insidious way to undermine worker organisation while veiling themselves in the guise of a benevolent, pro-union company. It is telling that this deal was conducted by Google UK’s current senior labour relations consultant, Philip Bickerstaffe, an ex-national officer at Prospect.”


Bickerstaffe worked at Prospect as a national officer from 2004 to 2011, according to his LinkedIn profile, before going on to roles with BT, Boeing, Amazon and Google. 


The Prospect-Google deal follows

a similar agreement

 between Prospect and Meta, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram and Whatsapp. Meta employs roughly 5,000 people in the UK. 


Right of access to workplaces in the UK – even where employers are hostile to trade unions organising onsite – was included in the Employment Rights Act 2025, and came into force on 30 October. 


Unite and the CWU say they put in an access request at the stroke of midnight on 30 October, and received a formal acknowledgement from Google on 3 November, which said their request would be considered and responded to “within the appropriate time frame”.


Employers then have 15 days to respond and a further 25 days to negotiate. The Prospect deal was announced on 2 November, suggesting that little, if any, time was spent negotiating the terms of the deal, which has added to the impression that the deal is favourable to the employer.


Unite, the CWU and Prospect are all members of the Trade Union Congress (TUC), which means they must

respect the principle

 that a union shouldn’t organise at a workplace where another union already has the majority of workers as members or is actively engaged in significant organising activity. 


Unite and the CWU say Prospect has violated this national cross-union agreement by signing the access deal with Google UK. 


A Prospect spokesperson said: “These allegations are false and seem designed to undermine union organising at Google. Our access agreement with Google was agreed in accordance with the TUC principles and does not include Google DeepMind where other unions are making a recognition bid.”

author: Erin Reed
title: Republicans Spent Nearly $200 Million on Ads Attacking Trans People — and Lost
content:
The election was a stunning rebuke of anti-transgender politics, and Democrats should take note moving forward.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

By now, you have likely seen the results of the 2026 midterms: a wave election for Democrats the likes of which we have not seen in years. Republicans and their allies spent nearly $200 million on anti-transgender ads alone, bankrolled in part by billionaires like Elon Musk. Virtually every Democrat in a highly contested race was the target of these kinds of ads. And what did it buy the Republican Party? An earth-shattering loss, and a stunning rebuke of anti-transgender politics.

A blue Texas in the face of the biggest anti-trans ad spend of any race this cycle … a victory in Michigan from a Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate who forcefully defended trans people at every step of the race … a western Montana smokejumper who will go to Congress after telling voters the government has “no business sticking its nose into our personal lives” when it comes to transgender health care and sports … and an Alabama trans Democrat who won her race running on bread-and-butter issues in a conservative district in the Huntsville suburbs. These are just a small handful of the dozens of races we will remember as proof that anti-trans politics simply no longer works for the Republican Party, and that Democrats need never fear such attacks again.

I started writing about anti-transgender politics back in 2022 after the extreme efforts of Texas Gov. Greg Abbott and Attorney General Ken Paxton to sweep the state for transgender kids. In that dark time, they ordered child abuse investigations into the parents of transgender youth, and many of those families fled the state. Now, not only does James Talarico win in the face of ads built around him saying “God is nonbinary,” but Gina Hinojosa, who waved a trans flag on the Texas House floor after Democrats ran out the clock on a sports ban in 2021, wins the governorship. Vikki Goodwin wins the lieutenant governorship after being endorsed by Equality Texas and after voting no on every anti-trans bill that reached the House floor. And more than that, it appears the Texas House is going to go to Democrats for the first time since 2003. The dark era of horrific anti-trans targeting of trans Texans is over, and there is hope that one day, some of the trans people who fled may get to return to the state, despite the millions Elon Musk poured into Texas trying to prevent it.

The positive results for transgender people were not limited to Texas — they were seen across the board. If you were a Democratic consultant who believed that you had to moderate on transgender issues to win an election, the results in places like Montana’s 1st Congressional District make it clear that such capitulation is not necessary in the slightest. Smokejumper Sam Forstag, a Democrat running in a stubbornly Republican House district, won his election handily. When asked whether he supports transgender participation in sports or gender-affirming care for transgender youth, his answer was that the government has no place banning any of it, and that the issue is an attempt to distract voters while Republicans “pick our pockets.” Trump campaigned in Montana for Aaron Flint, his opponent, who ran anti-trans ads. It wasn’t enough. Western Montana will have a Democratic congressman who supports transgender people, and he won one of the toughest races in the country handily.

Several Democrats who championed transgender people won in major swing races, and the most notable was probably Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed. El-Sayed was the target of millions in anti-transgender ads on one side, and drew the ire of centrist Democrats on the other for not moderating on many progressive causes, including transgender people. When asked in a hostile CBS “60 Minutes” interview about trans people and other “social cultural issues,” his response was that “a failure to show up and fight for that right is a failure to show up and fight for your own.” Then, when asked specifically about schools, he called the fight over what kids learn in school a manufactured “cultural flash point.” It cost him nothing in a state Trump won in 2024. El-Sayed won Michigan’s U.S. Senate race by about 6 points as of the early morning hours.

It was also a big night for transgender …

author: David Corn
title: A ressaca eleitoral de Trump
content:
É como se os eleitores norte-americanos, depois de uma longa noite de farra, tivessem acordado de ressaca, arrependidos das decisões da noite anterior.


Com os democratas conquistando com facilidade ampla maioria na Câmara dos Representantes (equivalente à Câmara dos Deputados no Brasil) e assumindo o controle do Senado, o eleitorado enviou uma mensagem clara: está cansado de Donald Trump. Em vários estados, os republicanos sofreram uma derrota histórica. Foi um tsunami azul, a cor do Partido Democrata.


Na Carolina do Sul, a democrata Annie Andrews obteve uma vitória surpreendente sobre Darline Graham na disputa pela cadeira no Senado, anteriormente ocupada pelo irmão de Graham. No Texas, o deputado estadual democrata James Talarico derrotou o procurador-geral republicano Ken Paxton na disputa por uma vaga no Senado, enquanto a deputada estadual Gina Hinajosa venceu o governador republicano Greg Abbott. Ela será a primeira governadora latina do estado, onde um democrata não vence o Senado desde 1988.


Na Geórgia, o senador democrata Jon Ossoff foi reeleito com facilidade, e a ex-prefeita de Atlanta Keisha Lance Bottoms foi eleita governadora por ampla margem de votos.

Ela será a primeira mulher negra a comandar um estado na história dos Estados Unidos.


Os candidatos democratas ao Senado também venceram nos estados republicanos do Meio-Oeste do país, Iowa e Kansas. Já em Ohio, a democrata Amy Acton derrotou Vivek Ramaswamy na disputa pelo governo estadual. Na Flórida, deputados democratas que eram alvos do

redesenho eleitoral

 feito pelos republicanos nos distritos do estado sobreviveram à disputa. 


Em todo o país, os democratas derrotaram com ampla margem os candidatos republicanos à Câmara em distritos nos quais Trump havia vencido por dois dígitos nas eleições de 2024.


À medida que as notícias desastrosas para Trump e o Partido Republicano se acumulavam, o presidente fez uma série de posts nas redes sociais reclamando da rede de televisão Fox News. Enquanto isso, assessores da Casa Branca tentavam freneticamente lembrar aos jornalistas que Trump não era candidato naquela eleição. Mas há alguns dias, Trump

disse

: “Peço a todos que finjam que meu nome está na cédula”.


Esses resultados sinalizam que a política repugnante de Trump — baseada em mentiras, enganos, divisão, preconceito, tribalismo, ódio e demagogia, plenamente abraçada pelo Partido Republicano — já não encontra eco na maioria dos americanos. Seus discursos estridentes, nos quais acusa os democratas de serem comunistas que odeiam os EUA, de quererem impor cirurgias de transição de gênero a crianças e de destruir o país, não conseguiram desviar a atenção da maioria dos eleitores. 


As realidades escancaradas do segundo governo Trump são preços elevados, a guerra no Irã — mal conduzida e com objetivos equivocados —, uma cruzada cruel de deportações em massa, uma política econômica errática e improdutiva, corrupção descarada e em larga escala, autoritarismo crescente e doses generosas de caos.  


As eleições de 2026 estabelecem um claro padrão.

 Os eleitores podem cair na conversa de Trump quando ele é candidato, ataca as elites que estão no poder e faz grandes promessas (como a de uma “era de ouro” para os EUA). Mas, na hora de avaliar seu desempenho na Casa Branca, a aprovação desaparece. 


Em 2016 e 2024, ele teve uma boa performance como aspirante à Presidência, desempenhando o papel de herói nacionalista e grande outsider que poderia enfrentar o sistema, confrontar as elites, provocar os liberais e garantir prosperidade.

Essa encenação — vendida com a convicção de um vigarista e a empolgação de um anunciador de circo — funcionou.


No entanto, Trump na Presidência não impressiona, e suas ações na Casa Branca provocam reações contrárias. Em 2018, os eleitores se voltaram contra ele, e os democratas conquistaram a Câmara dos Representantes. Em 2020, enquanto Trump administrava mal a pandemia de Covid-19, os eleitores o tiraram do poder e entregaram o comando a Joe Biden. Os democratas mantiveram o controle da Câmara e conquistaram a maioria no Senado.


As eleições de meio de mandato de 2026 seguem a mesma tendência. Depois de quase dois anos de crises, autocracia, brutalidade, corrupção, políticas plutocráticas e todo tipo de excentricidade, os eleitores rejeitaram pela terceira vez uma presidência de Trump.

Isso significa que o republicano nunca recebeu uma avaliação positiva de seu desempenho por parte do eleitorado.


Estas …

author: Local Journalism Initiative
title: Two years after Joshua Papigatuk died in a police shooting, Salluit awaits answers
content:
Two years after a police intervention in Salluit ended with Joshua Papigatuk dead and his twin brother Garnet Papigatuk seriously injured, Quebec prosecutors have decided whether the officers involved will face criminal charges but are waiting to speak to the family before making their decision public.


Lucas Bastien, spokesperson for the Director of Criminal and Penal Prosecutions, said an announcement is expected soon but did not specify when.


“Our decision to proceed or not can only be made public once we have met with the deceased’s family,” he said in an email Tuesday to Nunatsiaq News.


Early on Nov. 4, 2024,

two police officers responded to a report

 of impaired driving, according to a news release from Bureau des enquêtes indépendantes, Quebec’s police watchdog, at the time of the incident.


Minutes later, an altercation broke out between the officers and two people. Police used a stun gun and pepper spray to try to control them.


An officer fired a gun once in the direction of one of the individuals, who was injured. A struggle continued with the second person and more shots were fired. One was pronounced dead, and the other was medevaced.


Garnet Papigatuk, who survived the shooting and has since recovered from his injuries, faces assault and obstruction charges in connection with the incident.


His next court appearance is scheduled for this month, said Louis-Nicholas Coupal, a lawyer who advises Garnet Papigatuk and members of his family on potential civil litigation.


On Monday, Garnet Papigatuk and David Annanack Sr., whose son Mark died following a police shooting in Kangiqsualujjuaq in May 2025, renewed in a letter their demands to improve the region’s justice system.


The letter expresses disappointment over what the families describe as a lack of response to a list of demands that they sent to provincial leaders on July 22, 2025, which calls for investments in victim support services and a public inquiry into systemic policing problems.


They are also calling for police to use non-lethal weapons instead of firearms.


“The demand for real, structural change has not changed,” Coupal said in an interview.


In Salluit, “Justice for the twins” signs remain posted in some parts of town and frustration over the lack of a public decision remains, said Stephen Grasser, the community’s regional councillor.


“It’s cruel that the town and the family have been kept in the dark for so long,” he said.


Quebec’s police watchdog submitted its investigation report to prosecutors in June 2025. However, the prosecution service said the file was not considered complete until a supplementary investigation was completed in July 2026, said Bastien.


“It should be noted that the time required for a Crown prosecutor to review a file varies from case to case, depending on the specific circumstances,” he said.


“This timeframe depends on several factors, including the completeness of the file, requests for additional evidence (including the need for expert opinions) and the time required to obtain it, the complexity of the issues raised, the volume of evidence, and so on.”


Ungava MNA Sonia Caron said in an email to Nunatsiaq News that she intends to raise the matter with the provincial ministries involved and follow up on the delay in the Crown’s decision.


Kativik Regional Government chairperson Maggie Emudluk also acknowledged the impact the incident has had on the community.


“I recognize that this prolonged wait has been difficult and that many people continue to seek answers,” Emudluk said in a statement to Nunatsiaq News.


Nunatsiaq News reached out to Joshua Papigatuk’s parents for comment but did not receive a response.


Story by Dominique Gené, Local Journalism Initiative Reporter

Two years after Joshua Papigatuk died in a police shooting, Salluit awaits answers

author: CMI Argentina
title: El rechazo a Trump y el gran triunfo demócrata en ambas cámaras
content:
La oposición tendrá mayoría en el Congreso en los dos últimos años de su gobierno.


Demócratas celebran en Arizona


Por Beverly Fanon-Clay y Mirko Trudeau


El Partido Demócrata consiguió una gran victoria en las elecciones de medio mandato celebradas el martes en Estados Unidos, obteniendo mayorías en las dos cámaras, según las proyecciones, por lo que los dos últimos años del gobierno del presidente Donald Trump serán con un Congreso completamente adverso a sus intereses.


Donald Trump, el 2 de noviembre, en Washington: ¿triste, solitario, final?


La narrativa del presidente estadounidense «elegido por Dios» se ha hecho añicos ante realidades mucho más mundanas: pagar las facturas, llenar el depósito del coche y hacer la compra. La derrota histórica ha venido desde dentro, por lo que aún ha sido más dolorosa. Cinco grandes feudos republicanos y cruciales para el control del Senado le han dado la espalda al presidente estadounidense: Carolina del Norte, Carolina del Sur, Texas, Iowa y Kansas se han teñido de azul.


Los votantes estadounidenses eligieron a su primera gobernadora negra, su primer senador abiertamente gay, el primer senador musulmán y la primera gobernadora indígena en unas elecciones de medio mandato que reflejan un liderazgo cada vez más diverso. Fue una gran reprimenda contra el odio y la división», señaló Bill Shiebler, director de estrategia de la organización no gubernamental State Voices.


Tan importante como la magnitud de la debacle es la responsabilidad por la misma, en la medida en que Trump se empeñó en que los comicios fueran un referendo sobre su persona. A principios de año, nada sugería que los demócratas pudieran hacerse con la mayoría del Congreso; de hecho, todavía en mayo 59 por ciento de los adultos tenían una opinión desfavorable de dicho partido.


Los analistas señalan cuatro factores centrales del resultado electoral: la injerencia de Trump en los procesos internos de los republicanos, en los que impuso a candidatos contra el criterio de las militancias locales, la agresión criminal contra Irán, que rompió la promesa de no meter al país en más guerras interminables en el extranjero que, a su vez, desató una ola inflacionaria y la inhumana e indiscriminada cacería desatada contra los migrantes, sin importar su estatus legal, que enajenó al trumpismo el voto latino, crucial para sus victorias anteriores.


La mejor muestra de este cambio de preferencias entre los descendientes de latinoamericanos se encuentra en Texas, donde James Talarico y Gina Hinojosa aplastaron a sus contrincantes conservadores por márgenes que nadie anticipó en la carrera senatorial y por la gubernatura. En Florida, la ultraderecha estuvo muy cerca de perder su bastión ante proyectos liberales.


James Talarico ofrece un discurso en Austin tras convertirse en el primer senador demócrata elegido por Texas en 38 años


Quizás la principal lección de la derrota rotunda de los republicanos y Donald Trump, para Estados Unidos y el resto del mundo, es que la democracia vive en el país que acaba de celebrar los 250 años de su fundación. No es una lección menor, y ni siquiera era seguro que sucediese dada la aversión de Trump hacia la separación de poderes y su sistemática impugnación del legítimo proceso electoral. .


El partido azul ha recuperado el control del Senado y de la Cámara de Representantes después de imponerse en bastiones republicanos donde las encuestas ni siquiera les daban posibilidades. Uno de los triunfos de la noche es el de Texas, donde Gina Hinojosa se convierte en la primera gobernadora hispana tras derrotar al (ex) todopoderoso Greg Abbott.


En Míchigan, el demócrata Abdul El-Sayed ganó las elecciones al Senado y se ha convertido en el primer musulmán en la Cámara alta. Los republicanos han mantenido el escaño en el Senado por Florida, con el triunfo de Ashley Moody, y Byron Donalds será el primer gobernador negro de ese Estado, que se consolida como principal enclave conservador. “Estoy un poco sorprendido. Pensé que lo haríamos mejor”, ha comentado Trump. Tras admitir la derrota, ha dicho que aceptará los resultados.


El demócrata Xavier Becerra convierte en el primer gobernador de origen latino al frente del Gobierno de California en más de 150 años. «Qué gran noche para ser californiano. Qué gran noche para ser estadounidense, para ser hijo de inmigrantes de la Unión, para estar de pie en la victoria junto a todos vosotros», ha afirmado en su discurso de celebración en …

author: La Zarzamora
title: Indignación ante ataque a Mujeres Trans en Palermo en medio de oleada fascista en Argentina
content:
A una semana de la marcha del orgullo, la noche del sábado 31 de octubre, un grupo de entre 50 y 60 jóvenes y adolescentes varones se organizaron a través de un grupo de Whasapp para atacar, agredir y violentar en masa a trabajadoras sexuales Trans y Travestis que se encontraban en Los Bosques de Palermo.

Llegaron llenos de ira, violencia y rabia, arriba de sus bicicletas, denostando a las travestis por su trabajo; usando palos con clavos, piedras, tirándoles vidrios y conos de tránsito. Y no se quedaron ahí, para mayor crueldad, uno de ellos, mientras corrían detrás de las mujeres, fue grabando y registrando todo lo ocurrido para después subirlo a redes sociales. En el video mencionaban con total naturalidad e impunidad la idea de ‘’ir a cazar travas’’ alcanzando más de 700.000 vistas, con comentarios transódicos, mofándose y celebrando el hecho.

Muchas de las mujeres que fueron atacadas por este grupo de adolescentes se encuentran con heridas, golpes y el trauma de haber vivido este despreciable hecho. Para la comunidad travesti de Argentina esto no es más que un resultado o consecuencia de los naturalizados discursos de odio hacia la comunidad LGBTIQ+, ya que baja ni más ni menos que desde la presidencia de Argentina.

Como ejemplo el discurso de Milei en el 2025 World Economic Forum, en el que niega la existencia Trans, mencionando que serían ‘’hombres disfrazados de mujer’’. Además, menciona algunos casos de violencia dentro de la comunidad de personas condenadas para generalizar hechos delictivos para toda la comunidad: ‘’porque en sus versiones más extremas la ideología de género constituye lisa y llanamente abuso infantil: son pedófilos’’, estableció, generalizando y denostando a toda una comunidad con su transodio presidencial.

Mientras tanto y en paralelo el mismo presidente apoya y avala al Estado genocida de Israel, haciéndole alabanzas a pesar de que han matado a miles de niñeces, han violado mujeres, infancias y destruido a todo un territorio.

Además es amigo de Trump quien está relacionado al ‘’Caso Epstein’’ donde un grupo de hombres violaba y asesinaba a mujeres en una isla.

Milei ha instalado la naturalización del odio hacia las personas Trans, mujeres, homosexuales y fomentando el odio hacia toda la comunidad, por lo que esto no sería más que los resultados de los discursos fascistas y totalitarios clásicos frente a la realidad, imponiendo una idea de lo ‘’bueno’’ y lo ‘’malo’’, e instalando en el imaginario la idea de que unas personas son mejores que otras, o que unas pueden estar por encima de otras.

Igual que en el patriarcado más antiguo, que parece antiguo, pero es más actual que nunca, las cacerías existen, las violaciones en manada o el aumento de los femicidios a mujeres, Travestis y Mujeres Trans, tan solo en octubre en el mismo país se registraron 39 femicidios en 31 días.

Por lo mismo dentro de la comunidad LGBT+ existe un repudio total ante lo ocurrido y ante el Estado y su funcionamiento histórico que es en desmedro de las comunidades excluidas, disidencias y animales.

También llaman a la organización y a cuidarse en colectividades para enfrentar y defenderse de la violencia cotidiana.

author: infolibre
title: Πανεκπαιδευτικές πορείες – διαδηλώσεις, την Πέμπτη 5/11
content:
Την Πέμπτη 5/11, σε Αθήνα, Θεσσαλονίκη και άλλες πόλεις, θα πραγματοποιηθούν πανεκπαιδευτικές διαδηλώσεις ενάντια στην εκπαιδευτική αναδιάρθρωση και την υποβάθμιση της δημόσιας παιδείας. Μετά τις μαζικές κινητοποιήσεις της 21ης Οκτωβρίου, μαθητ(ρι)ές, φοιτητ(ρι)ές, σύλλογοι εκπαιδευτικών, οργανώσεις και συλλογικότητες κατεβαίνουν μαζικά στους δρόμους και διαδηλώνουν με βασικά αιτήματα την υπεράσπιση της δημόσιας και δωρεάν παιδείας, την μείωση του αυξημένου κόστους σπουδών και στέγασης, καθώς και την άμεση πρόσληψη μόνιμων εκπαιδευτικών με αξιοπρεπείς μισθούς και συνθήκες εργασίας.


Καλέσματα:


Αθήνα, στις  11.00 και 12.00, στα Προπύλαια


Θεσσαλονίκη, στις 12.00, στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου


Πάτρα, στις 12.00, στη πλατέια Βασ. Γεωργίου


Χανιά, στις 12.00, στη πλατεία Αγοράς


Γιάννενα, στις 12.00, στη Περιφέρεια Ηπείρου


Λάρισα, στις 12.00, στη πλατεία Ελευθερίας


Ξάνθη, στις 12.00, στη πλατέια Δημοκρατίας


Πανελλαδικά Καλέσματα:


Πρωτοβουλία Αναρχικών Φοιτητών/-τριών Αθήνας


Το μέλλον κατακτιέται στους δρόμους.


Όλοι/όλες στις Πανεκπαιδευτικές Διαδηλώσεις


Πανεκπαιδευτική διαδήλωση την Πέμπτη 5/11-


Αθήνα: 12.00, Προπύλαια


Θεσσαλονίκη: 12.00, Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου


Για να καταλάβουμε τους νέους νόμους γύρω από την εκπαίδευση που έχουν ψηφιστεί τα τελευταία χρόνια θα πρέπει να κατανοήσουμε ότι δεν μιλάμε για αποσπασματικές πολιτικές διαφόρων κυβερνήσεων ή διαφόρων υπουργών, αλλά για ένα ενιαίο κρατικό σχέδιο, την εκπαιδευτική αναδιάρθρωση, η οποία οργανώνεται και εκτελείται σε βάθος χρόνου. Η ίδια η δομική αντίληψη του νεοφιλελευθερισμού η οποία και υποδαυλίζει την κρατική επίθεση που βιώνουμε, βρίσκεται στο ότι κάθε κοινωνική σχέση και δραστηριότητα (εκπαίδευση, υγειονομική περίθαλψη, ψυχαγωγία κλπ.) πρέπει να αναδιαρθρωθεί και να μεταστραφεί με τέτοιο τρόπο ώστε αυτή να γίνεται προς όφελος του Κεφαλαίου και υπό τον έλεγχο του Κράτους.


Έτσι, βλέποντας τα μέτρα τα οποία έχουν ψηφιστεί μόνο τα τελευταία χρόνια γύρω από το κοινωνικό αγαθό της παιδείας και βάζοντας τα σε μια σειρά, μπορούμε εύκολα να κατανοήσουμε τα συμφέροντα που υπηρετούν και τον ρόλο που επιτελούν. Ξεκινώντας από την δευτεροβάθμια εκπαίδευση, μια σειρά μέτρων από την Ελάχιστη Βάση Εισαγωγής η οποία άφησε εκτός πανεπιστημίων δεκάδες χιλιάδες μαθητών, η εντατικοποίηση των μαθημάτων και τα νέα σχέδια περί εθνικού απολυτηρίου και τριπλών πανελλαδικών εξετάσεων, μια μετά από κάθε τάξη του Λυκείου, δημιουργούν μια συνθήκη ολοένα και εντονότερου ανταγωνισμού μεταξύ των μαθητών/-τριών για την εισαγωγή τους στο πανεπιστήμιο, την ίδια ώρα που στην τριτοβάθμια τμήματα πανεπιστημίων κλείνουν ή συγχωνεύονται, οι θέσεις των εισακτέων μειώνονται ενώ η φοιτητική μέριμνα -ιδιαιτερα όσων αφορά το ζήτημα της στέγασης και της σίτισης- ολοένα και υποβαθμίζεται γεγονός που συχνά καθιστά αδύνατη τη μετακίνηση των φοιτητών/-τριών σε άλλες πόλεις για να σπουδάσουν. Σαν επιστέγασμα της συνθήκης αυτής, οι διαγραφές φοιτητών, έρχονται για να πετάξουν εκτός πανεπιστημίων εκατοντάδες χιλιάδες φοιτητές/-τριές . Το αποτέλεσμα είναι πως ένα συνεχώς αυξανόμενο κομμάτι της νεολαίας ουσιαστικά μένει εκτός πανεπιστημίων -με κριτήρια άμεσα και απροκάλυπτα ταξικά. Από το σώμα αυτό των νεολαίων που πετάχτηκαν εκτός πανεπιστημίου, το πιο υποβαθμισμένο ταξικά κομμάτι θα εκτοπιστεί πλήρως από την εκπαιδευτική διαδικασία, ενώ όσοι είναι σε θέση να πληρώσουν θα έχουν την ευκαιρία να σπουδάσουν σε κάποιο από τα νεοϊδρυθέντα ιδιωτικά πανεπιστήμια.


Σημαντικό είναι να δούμε και τον ρόλο που παίρνει το δημόσιο πανεπιστήμιο εν μέσω αυτής της διαδικασίας. Πιο συγκεκριμένα, τόσο ο ανταγωνισμός με τα ιδιωτικά πανεπιστήμια, η υποχρηματοδότηση όσο και οι συνειδητές πολιτικές αποφάσεις κράτους και πρυτανικών αρχών οδηγούν τα πανεπιστήμια να μετατραπούν και τα ίδια σε επιχειρήσιες που θα λειτουργούν σύμφωνα με τους νόμους των αγορών, περιορίζοντας από τη μια τα έξοδα και τις “σπατάλες”, και ανοίγοντας τις πόρτες στο ιδιωτικό κεφάλαιο από την άλλη. Έτσι, το δημόσιο χρήμα που θεωρητικά ενισχύει την ακαδημαϊκή έρευνα χρησιμοποιείται εντέλει για τις ερευνητικές ανάγκες ιδιωτικών εταιρειών. Στη σημερινή συγκυρία, που πλέον η κυρίαρχη μπίζνα στην Ευρώπη είναι η πολεμική βιομηχανία και που το σύνολο των δυτικών κρατών επανεξοπλίζονται, προετοιμαζόμενα για τους πολέμους που έρχονται, μέσω στοχευμένων κονδυλίων και της εμπλοκής του στρατού και της πολεμικής βιομηχανίας στην έρευνα το πανεπιστήμιο μετατρέπεται σε ένα πολεμικό εργαστήρι το οποίο θα φτιάχνει “έξυπνα” ντροουν και οπλικά συστήματα. author: CMI Argentina
title: Nuevo paro en las universidades para que se cumpla la Ley de Financiamiento
content:
Docentes y trabajadores no docentes de las universidades nacionales realizaron este martes una nueva jornada de paro en todo el país. Reclaman que el Gobierno cumpla la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario, mejore los salarios y garantice los recursos necesarios para sostener el funcionamiento de la educación pública.


Escuchar/descargar el reporte de Gabriel Robledo de Radio Futura de La Plata


El conflicto continúa abierto y ya se anunciaron nuevas medidas de fuerza. La ley fue aprobada por el Congreso y el veto presidencial fue rechazado, pero el Gobierno todavía no la aplica. El reclamo atraviesa a distintas universidades de la provincia de Buenos Aires, entre ellas la Universidad Nacional de Luján.


Patricio Grande, trabajador de esa casa de estudios, cuestionó el presupuesto que pretende implementar el Gobierno y señaló que los fondos previstos no alcanzan para cubrir las necesidades básicas de las universidades.


“El Gobierno pretende imponer un presupuesto universitario de ajuste total. Esos 7 billones no alcanzan para cubrir los gastos de funcionamiento mínimo que requieren las universidades y están muy alejados de cualquier atisbo de cumplir con la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario”, afirmó.


Desde el sector advierten que los recursos contemplados por el Gobierno en el presupuesto universitario 2027 serían insuficientes para sostener el funcionamiento de las instituciones y garantizar el derecho a la educación superior.


Ver esta publicación en Instagram


Una publicación compartida por FATUN – 100% NODOCENTES (@fatun.oficial)


En ese sentido, Clara Chevallier, secretaria general de CONADU, sostuvo que el ajuste pone en discusión el modelo de universidad pública y cuestionó la falta de políticas educativas por parte del Gobierno.


“Le tenemos que recordar también que la universidad pública argentina es parte de nuestro ADN. Por más que al Gobierno le guste más o menos, es parte de nuestro ADN y no vamos a permitir que la vuelva un negocio”, expresó.


Chevallier afirmó que el ajuste es la única política que impulsa el Gobierno para el sector y advirtió que puede abrir la puerta a un modelo en el que la educación universitaria deje de ser un derecho para convertirse en un negocio. También cuestionó el incumplimiento de la ley y señaló la responsabilidad del Poder Judicial en la situación institucional.


Mientras continúa el conflicto, la Federación Argentina del Trabajador de las Universidades Nacionales (FATUN) anunció nuevos paros de 24 horas para el personal no docente. Las medidas se realizarán el jueves 12 y el lunes 16 de noviembre.

author: Mzi Velapi
title: Slow start to elections in the Western Cape
content:
Voting started slowly in the Western Cape’s most populous townships, Mitchells Plain and Khayelitsha, today. When

Elitsha

 visited voting stations in wards 96, 93 and 89 in Khayelitsha and 116 in Mitchells Plain, between 09h00 and 11h30, there were no queues and voters would arrive in groups, get processed and leave soon after.


According to the provincial electoral officer, Michael Hendrickse, all the Western Cape’s 1,623 voting stations were opened this morning but not without any hiccups. Problems with the voter management devices at some voting stations were resolved, while Hendrickse said, long queues at some voting stations were shortened by getting more personnel and material to the stations.


Hendrickse told reporters that by midday, the Independent Electoral Commission had issued just a quarter of all ballots, most of them in the City of Cape Town. 3.4 million registered voters in the Western Cape are expected to cast their votes today.


“At around 12h30 this afternoon, 824,242 voters were already issued with ballots in the province and of these, 524,162 were issued in the Cape Town Metro,” he said. He stressed that if a voter is in a queue by 21h00, they would still be able to vote.


Issues for voters


Ward 89 resident and voter, Amanda Ntsweza said that youth unemployment is a big problem in her community and she would like the new council to prioritise it. “If you were to go with me into the community, you will find young people loitering with nothing to do. In terms of service delivery, we have a problem of overflowing drains and when we speak to the ward councillor, he does not help,” she said.


Blowey resident in ward 93, Liziwe Ngindane said her house is one of 17 that burned down in November last year; they are still waiting for material to rebuild their homes. “The cause of fire was faulty electrical appliances at one of the residents. We got some food from the Department of Social Development but that is the only help we got. We are still waiting for Eskom to fix and re-install electricity in our area,” she said.


Grade R teacher, Joy Mentor from Eastridge said that crime and gang wars are ravaging the communities in Mitchells Plain. Mentor said that the next council should prioritise education and make sure that children’s issues are attended to.


Fiona Jacobs said that housing and subsidisation of the poor by government must be a priority for whoever comes into power after the elections. “I grew up in Eastridge, struggling, but I’m in Portlands now. People are really struggling out there with the high cost of living and homelessness,” she said.


There are 106 political parties contesting the elections in the Western Cape. The voting stations will close at 21h00 today.

Li gorî nûçeya Ajansa Welat piştî serdanan li ber girtîgehan daxuyanî hate dayîn û hevserokan diyar kir ku hevalên wan ên siyasetmedar bi awayekî neqanûnî di zindanan de girtî ne û bang kirin ku demildest werin berdan. 


Di 4ê Mijdara 2016an de li dijî HDPê û siyasetmedarên Kurd êrişeke hate destpêkirin. Di çarçoveya vê derbeya siyasî de 9 siyasetmedar hatibîn girtin. Piştî serdanan hevserokan li ber girtîgehan daxuyanî da. "Divê hemû girtiyên siyasî demildest werin berdan"


Tuncer Bakirhan li pêşiya Girtîgeha Kandirayê axivî û daxuyanî da. Tuncer Bakirhan bi bîr xist ku îro salvegera 4ê Mijdarê ye û ev roj di dîroka siyasî ya Tirkiyeyê de rojeke reş û birîneke kûr e û wiha axivî:

Niha divê gavên yekalî yên dîrokî bersivekê bibînin.


Di vê serdema ku em hewl didin serdema şer biqedînin. author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "The Earth Shook Last Night": Talarico Wins Senate, Hinojosa Becomes First Latina Governor in Texas
content:
Texas Democrats have shattered more than three decades of Republican dominance in the state, winning races for U.S. Senate, governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general and even railroad commissioner. They are also poised to possibly take control of the Texas House of Representatives for the first time since 2003. The Republican governor of Texas, Greg Abbott, lost his bid for a fourth term to Democratic state Representative Gina Hinojosa, who defeated him by nearly 700,000 votes. She will be Texas’s first Latina governor. And James Talarico will be the first Democrat to represent Texas in the U.S. Senate since 1993.


“We’re celebrating these wonderful candidates who won office, and we’re also starting to think about what it means to hold power,” says Mike Siegel, a city council member from Austin, Texas, who founded Ground Game Texas, a statewide voter turnout organization. “We need to start thinking very quickly about how we will protect public education, how we will stop data centers and the encroachment of AI on our society, how we will protect public schools, how we stop collaboration with

ICE

.”

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Abdul El-Sayed Becomes First Muslim Senator as Democrats Rout GOP Across the U.S. in Rebuke to Trump
content:
In a stunning repudiation of President Trump, Democrats regained control of both chambers of Congress in Tuesday’s midterm elections, flipping seven Senate seats: Iowa, Kansas, Ohio, Maine, North Carolina and South Carolina. Meanwhile, progressive Democrat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican Congressmember Mike Rogers for an open Senate seat in Michigan with over 52% of the vote. El-Sayed campaigned on a platform of Medicare for All, tackling economic inequality and getting big money out of politics — as well as ending military aid to Israel. He is the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. El-Sayed faced vitriolic, Islamaphobic attacks by top Republicans throughout the campaign.


“Last night wasn’t just about Dr. Abdulrahman being a Muslim, winning and going to the United States Senate,” says Palestinian American organizer and author Linda Sarsour, who has been campaigning for El-Sayed. “It demonstrated that progressives can win in states like Michigan” and that “we can win on standing up for the human rights of the Palestinian people.”
