author: Bruno Fonseca
title: Contas espalham conteúdo falso sobre bets nas redes enquanto STF discute proibição
content:
“A diarista que trabalha aqui em casa mostrando a conta com 46 MIL REAIS. Falei: que isso mulher, tá rica??? Ela responde: Dizendo que ganhou 40 mil jogando no tigrinho e ainda me manda o print pq eu fiquei sem acreditar kkkkkkk”. A história, apesar de absurda, parece ser contada por uma pessoa normal. Mas não é.

A

Agência Pública

 encontrou uma rede de perfis que publicam mensagens enganosas em série como essa, divulgando bets. Os perfis se seguem e amplificam entre si mensagens de ganhos irreais com as apostas.


O perfil que publicou a história acima é de uma conta com pouco mais de 8 mil seguidores no X/Twitter. A foto do perfil, chamado

gigimonteiros

, é de uma mulher jovem. Não há nenhuma outra informação pública na conta, criada em novembro de 2021.


A fala sobre a diarista foi postada pela primeira vez no dia 2 de novembro.

Hoje, dia 3, enquanto o Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) realiza uma audiência pública para discutir as ações de inconstitucionalidade dirigidas a Medida Provisória (MP) do presidente Lula que

proibiu as bets

 no Brasil no dia 25 de setembro, o perfil voltou a compartilhar a mesma postagem.

 A conta incluiu a frase: “Gente a diva falou que esse mês não vai vim trabalhar kkkkkk certíssima. Merecedora de curtir umas férias”.


Quatro dias antes, no dia 30, o mesmo perfil contava outra história, de como a diarista teria ganhado mais de R$ 20 mil no tigrinho. No dia 23 de outubro, a profissional teria ganhado mais de R$ 7 mil. Todas as postagens são acompanhadas de supostos prints de extratos bancários da diarista em bancos diferentes.


Além dos vários ganhos da diarista, o perfil já contou sobre os prêmios recebidos pela “moça que trabalha na limpeza aqui do prédio”, do porteiro, do motorista de Uber, da “mulher do ônibus”, do moto Uber, do “pai de 58 anos” e até da mãe.

Cada vez, um valor diferente teria sido pago pelas bets. Há postagens com quase meio milhão de visualizações de alcance.


O perfil fez propaganda de apostas mesmo antes da proibição das bets pelo governo Lula. A

Pública

 encontrou postagens parecidas desde junho. Em uma delas, o perfil divulga o link da bet Greenasbet. O nome da casa de apostas não estava na

lista de julho

 de casas autorizadas a operarem no Brasil, antes da proibição. O site é registrado na Califórnia, nos Estados Unidos. 


Contas divulgam histórias enganosas sobre prêmios em dinheiro e divulgam bets que seguem proibidas no Brasil

Contas divulgam histórias enganosas sobre prêmios em dinheiro e divulgam bets que seguem proibidas no Brasil

Contas divulgam histórias enganosas sobre prêmios em dinheiro e divulgam bets que seguem proibidas no Brasil


Contas atuam em rede para propagar tigrinho


O perfil de

gigimonteiros

 não atua sozinho.

Outros perfis que interagem e se seguem foram identificados pela

Pública

. Em comum, todos contam variações de histórias de pessoas que teriam ganhado valores altos com bets.


Um deles, com mais de 14 mil seguidores, repete a mesma estratégia. Numa hora, é a mãe que pede dinheiro emprestado e ganha com bets. Na outra, é a mulher que joga no ônibus. Motoristas de uber e namorados se revezam nos relatos, sempre engraçados e com linguagem que tenta simular naturalidade: “Ela fala que esse ano já ganhou 9 mil e reformou a casa dela, e guardou 2.000 pra ficar jogando de 2 em 2 reais. Eu tô em choque tô gag”, escreveu uma das contas que se seguem.


Há inclusive contas diferentes que usam a mesma imagem para contar histórias repetidas — e com indícios de ser gerada por Inteligência Artificial.

 A reportagem encontrou duas contas que fizeram postagens com um dia de diferença sobre diaristas que teriam ganhado com o tigrinho. Ambas usam o mesmo print de um suposto extrato do aplicativo da Caixa Econômica Federal que mostra um saldo de R$ 7,8 mil.


As contas amplificam as histórias, e, algumas delas, passam de centenas de milhares de visualizações.


No STF, dirigentes do futebol e lobistas defendem “drama” dos clubes


A audiência pública realizada nesta terça-feira, 3 de novembro, no STF não teve o objetivo de decidir sobre os pedidos de inconstitucionalidade relacionados à proibição das bets no Brasil, definida pela MP de Lula em setembro. Ela foi convocada pelo ministro Luiz Fux, que relata oito ações diretas de inconstitucionalidade sobre as casas de apostas, duas delas abertas após a proibição.

author: Stelinsky
title: Comment te dire adieu, Raoul?
content:
Αποχαιρετώντας τον Ραούλ Βανεγκέμ

Το να προσπαθείς να συμπυκνώσεις σ’ ένα κείμενο, σε λίγες εκατοντάδες λέξεις, μία ολόκληρη ζωή, με αφορμή το τέλος της, είναι εγχείρημα που από μόνο του εγκυμονεί δυσκολίες και κινδύνους. Τόσο οι δυσκολίες, όσο και οι κίνδυνοι, πολλαπλασιάζονται όταν αφορά ένα πρόσωπο αναγνωρίσιμο, που έχει αφήσει πίσω του μια συγγραφική πορεία άνω των 60 χρόνων και μια παρακαταθήκη που κατάφερε (και καταφέρνει ακόμα) να επηρεάσει και να διαμορφώσει συνειδήσεις επιδρώντας στον τρόπο σκέψης τόσο στην γενιά του, όσο και στις επόμενες γενιές που ήρθαν.

Δεν πρόκειται για τεχνική δυσκολία, ούτε έχει να κάνει με τον όγκο των πληροφοριών προς διαχείριση: για κάθε τέτοιο πρόσωπο, η επίσημα καταγεγραμμένη ιστορία έχει φυλαγμένο κι ένα βάθρο, σχεδόν μεταφυσικών διαστάσεων, κι ένα επίχρυσο περιτύλιγμα, περίπου ανάλογο του αποτυπώματος που άφησε στο πέρασμά του. Κάτι τέτοιο όμως θα ήταν άστοχο για τον άνθρωπο που αρνούνταν να ανέβει σε μια πλατφόρμα να μιλήσει, σε εκδηλώσεις στις οποίες ο ίδιος ήταν καλεσμένος.

Απ’ τον ίδιο και τους συντρόφους του, έχουμε μάθει πως το πρόβλημα δεν εξαντλείται στο ποιος αφηγείται το παρελθόν και πώς. Είναι εάν οι άνθρωποι μπορούν να αναγνωρίσουν τον εαυτό τους ως δημιουργούς της ιστορίας (τους) ή αν περιορίζονται στο να παρακολουθούν την ιστορία να εκτυλίσσεται μπροστά στα μάτια τους, ως ήδη καθορισμένη από κάποιους άλλους.

Συνεπώς, εδώ, δεν θα μιλήσουμε για την Ιστορία του, σαν ένα αποθετήριο νεκρών ημερομηνιών, προσώπων και των επιτευγμάτων τους. Για εμάς (εικάζουμε και για τον ίδιο), λίγη σημασία θα είχε να παραθέσουμε μία βιογραφικού τύπου καταγραφή της πορείας του συγγραφέα, ή του στοχαστή Ραούλ Βανεγκέμ.

Θα τον αποχαιρετήσουμε ως έναν άνθρωπο που δεν χωρά εύκολα σε μια τέτοια αφήγηση. Θα τον αποχαιρετήσουμε αφήνοντας χώρο για όσα εξακολουθούν να κινούνται χάρη σ’ αυτόν, προτρέποντας τις απανταχού εξεγερμένες, ευαίσθητες ψυχές να συνεχίσουν να βρίσκουν τρόπους να διαρρηγνύουν την ψευδαίσθηση ότι η υπάρχουσα πραγματικότητα είναι η μόνη υπαρκτή πραγματικότητα.

Λένε πως ο άνθρωπος πεθαίνει όταν πεθάνει κι ο τελευταίος που τον θυμάται, και σ’ αυτή την περίπτωση, έχουμε ένα μέλλον που μας μέλει να απολαύσουμε.

Κύριε καθηγητά, ευχαριστούμε για όλα.

author: Stelinsky
title: [Σκουριές Χαλκιδικής] Ενάντια στης φύσης τη λεηλασία, αγώνας για τη γη και την ελευθερία
content:
Δεν προσκυνάμε, δεν μετανιώνουμε – κι ας μη νικήσουμε ποτέ, θα πολεμάμε πάντα

Το μεταλλευτικό έργο των Σκουριών πρόκειται για ένα μεγάλης κλίμακας εξορυκτικό και μεταλλουργικό έργο στη Βορειοανατολική Χαλκιδική, με αιχμή την περιοχή των Σκουριών ως τόπο δημιουργίας μεγάλου ανοιχτού ορυχείου, με υπόγειες μεταλλευτικές εργασίες και εγκαταστάσεις επεξεργασίας μεταλλευμάτων. Το αρχικό ενιαίο «Επενδυτικό Σχέδιο Ανάπτυξης» των Μεταλλείων Κασσάνδρας, από την εταιρεία «Ελληνικός Χρυσός», θυγατρική της παγκόσμιας εμβέλειας Eldorado Gold, κατατίθεται στο Υπουργείο το 2006. Οι παραπάνω εταιρίες, εκμεταλλευόμενες χρόνια οικονομικής κρίσης, έρχονται και αυτοσυστήνονται ως φιλανθρωπικά ιδρύματα, και μαζί με το Υπουργείο Περιβάλλοντος και Κλιματικής Αλλαγής προσπαθούν να πείσουν το πανελλήνιο ότι το έργο στη Β. Χαλκιδική θα αποφέρει όχι μόνο τοπικά αλλά και εθνικά οικονομικά οφέλη, στοιχείο που ως και σήμερα δεν έχει αποδειχθεί.

Το μεγαλόπνοο αυτό σχέδιο αποτελεί μια οδυνηρή προοπτική για τον τόπο. Μια βαριά χημική βιομηχανία τεράστιας έκτασης απειλεί να προκαλέσει ανεπανόρθωτη περιβαλλοντική καταστροφή. Η ρύπανση του εδάφους, των υδάτων και του αέρα, η καταστροφή της χλωρίδας και της πανίδας, και η εξάντληση των υδάτινων πόρων θέτουν σε κίνδυνο την υγεία και την ποιότητα ζωής, ενώ ταυτόχρονα υπονομεύουν τις οικολογικές ισορροπίες (και την κληρονομία του τόπου). Παράλληλα, το έργο ακυρώνει τον πρωτογενή τομέα πλήττοντας σοβαρά τους επαγγελματίες της υπαίθρου αλλά και κάθε άλλη τοπική δραστηριότητα. Έτσι, απειλεί την οικονομική και κοινωνική συνοχή της περιοχής, το μέλλον των κατοίκων και τη δυνατότητά τους να συνεχίσουν να ζουν και να δημιουργούν στον τόπο τους.

Στη θετική εξέλιξη της αδειοδοτικής διαδικασίας και στην αδιαφορία της κεντρικής κυβέρνησης για τις αντιθέσεις της τοπικής κοινωνίας, βρήκε έδαφος και ρίζωσε η ανάγκη για πιο διευρυμένα σχήματα αντίστασης. Έτσι στα τέλη της άνοιξης του 2007 άτομα και φορείς της περιοχής συγκροτούν την Επιτροπή Αγώνα Μεγάλης Παναγίας, που ως και σήμερα συνεχίζει να υπάρχει και να λειτουργεί μέσω της ανοιχτής γενικής της συνέλευσης.

Ο αγώνας των Σκουριών συγκροτήθηκε αρχικά σε τοπικό επίπεδο μέσα από την επιθυμία των κατοίκων για αυτοδιαχείριση του τόπου τους, και από την αμφισβήτηση ενός αναπτυξιακού μοντέλου που προβάλλει την εξόρυξη ως μονόδρομο. Η Επιτροπή Αγώνα Μεγάλης Παναγίας αποτέλεσε βασικό όχημα αυτής της αντίστασης, καθώς η συλλογική συγκρότηση μετέτρεψε την αγανάκτηση σε οργανωμένη δράση. Με συνεχείς παρεμβάσεις και τη δημιουργία δικτύων αλληλεγγύης συνδέοντας κι άλλους αγώνες, η υπεράσπιση του τόπου εξελίχθηκε σε διαρκή κοινωνική σύγκρουση με εταιρείες, κράτος και κατασταλτικούς μηχανισμούς, δημιουργώντας ένα κύμα αλλεπάλληλων δράσεων που ξεπέρασε τα τοπικά όρια. Τα έτη 2012-13, το δάσος των Σκουριών μετατράπηκε σε πεδίο μάχης: Πορείες, αποκλεισμοί δρόμων, σαμποτάζ εργοταξίου, που απαντήθηκαν με υπέρμετρη αστυνομική βία, κατόρθωσαν την επιβράδυνση αλλά όχι την κατάργηση του έργου.

Από αυτό το σημείο και έπειτα, το κίνημα σταδιακά ήρθε αντιμέτωπο με πληθώρα κατασταλτικών μέσων. Οι δικαστικές διώξεις/συλλήψεις ποινικοποίησαν τον αγώνα. Οι οικονομικές και κοινωνικές πιέσεις, σε συνδυασμό με τις μακροχρόνιες επιδιώξεις, δημιούργησαν διχασμό της τοπικής κοινωνίας ως προς την υποστήριξη του έργου, και εξάντληση των αγωνιζόμενων. Το 2015, με την άνοδο του ΣΥΡΙΖΑ στην εξουσία, η προσδοκία μιας θεσμικής λύσης από ένα καλόπιστο μέρος του κινήματος, μετατόπισε το κέντρο βάρους από την αυτοοργανωμένη και ριζοσπαστική αντίσταση προς την αναμονή πολιτικών αποφάσεων οι οποίες δεν πάρθηκαν ποτέ (η «ριζοσπαστική» κυβέρνηση ουδέποτε προέβη σε κινήσεις που να ικανοποιούν τα προτάγματα του αγώνα).

Έτσι, παρά την επιβράδυνση του έργου και τη μεγάλη κοινωνική ανταπόκριση, ο αγώνας βρέθηκε αντιμέτωπος με τα όρια και τις αντιφάσεις του, το κοινωνικό κίνημα περιορίστηκε και πολλοί αγωνιζόμενοι υπέκυψαν εν τέλει στις διεφθαρμένες υποσχέσεις για εργασιακή αποκατάσταση, και έγιναν στρατιωτάκια του μεταλλωρυχείου.

Φτάνοντας στο σήμερα, 20 χρόνια μετά, και έχοντας προηγηθεί όλα όσα προαναφέραμε, είχαμε την… τιμή να παρακολουθήσουμε, από «απόσταση ασφαλείας», τα εγκαίνια του εργοταξίου στις Σκουριές. Ανταποκρινόμενοι στο κάλεσμα της Επιτροπής, βρεθήκαμε εκεί για να σταθούμε αλληλέγγυα δίπλα στους ανθρώπους που επί χρόνια έχουν αφιερώσει τη ζωή τους σε αυτόν τον αγώνα. Γιατί, όσο κι αν κάποιοι επιλέγουν να γιορτάζουν, υπάρχουν κι εκείνοι που δεν ξεχνούν όσα προηγήθηκαν, ούτε τον αγώνα που δόθηκε και …

content:
El sábado 31 de Octubre se llevó a cabo la 8.ª Marcha Transfeminista y del Orgullo en el barrio Padre Carlos Mugica de Retiro, más conocido como Villa 31.

La consigna de este año, “Operativo Tormenta de Orgullo”, es una respuesta desafiante ante el operativo “Tormenta Negra”, desplegado por el Gobierno de Jorge Macri, de discriminación y persecución contra las y los vecinos de los barrios populares de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires.


“En un contexto donde se criminaliza a los barrios populares, la respuesta es con organización, identidad y resistencia comunitaria. El orgullo también es villero”, declararon desde la Asamblea Feminista de la Villa 31 y 31 Bis, impulsora de la jornada.

“No fue una marcha más: tuvimos un recorrido y un despliegue hermoso por el barrio donde esa tormenta no solo se vió, se sintió!”, aseguró Dalma Prince, de la Asamblea Feminista V31.


“Frente al hostigamiento y las políticas de ajuste y persecución del gobierno de Jorge Macri, y de Javier Milei respondimos como sabemos hacerlo: en comunidad, organizadxs, con alegría y con muchísima furia travesti”, agregó la activista drag.


“​Vivimos una jornada histórica en la 8.ª Marcha Transfeminista y del Orgullo en la Villa 31, demostrando que nuestros barrios populares tienen memoria, resistencia y, sobre todo, un orgullo que no se apaga con ningún operativo”, afirmó, y concluyó:


“A pesar de las realidades que atravesamos día a día, nos abrazamos con tanto orgullo que eso pudo más contra tanta homofobia y discriminación en un contexto de hostigamiento constante,pero aca seguimos con la convicción intacta de que ¡el amor vence al odio!”.

author: Savanna Craig
title: Akwesasne family carries on 16th century Haudenosaunee tradition
content:
For the first time, 10-year-old Kenna back-weaves the threads of a beaded loom belt that she designed and beaded herself.


Glossy white beads cover the loom as bright and colourful designs, a turtle to represent the turtle clan; her favourite flowers, roses and forget-me-nots; and a monarch butterfly–her favourite insect- fill the belt.


Kenna sits in a large leather-cushioned chair, leaning over the loom. After she’s beaded one row, she highlights the section of her design on a printed-out drawing of the loom belt, keeping track of each row she’s completed.


As she focuses on weaving each bead through the loom, her mother, Kelly Back, stands beside her, guiding her through the process.


“Then you pull it through,” says Kelly, watching over her daughter. “There you go.”


Kelly Back

 runs

Fire Loom Creations

 with her husband, Tyson, in

Akwesasne

 Mohawk Territory. The duo designs custom loom belts, telling the stories of the individual or community they are designing the belt for.


“My Mohawk name is Tsieriwaiens, so [it means] bringing a good message, again,” says Kelly. “And I do just that by retelling people’s stories, people’s messages.”


Kelly flips through a binder filled with images of her completed designs.


“This binder holds all of our community belt designs,” says Kelly, pointing to a missing and murdered Indigenous woman and Every Child Matters Day themed belt.


Their work carries on a 16th century Haudenosaunne tradition.


“Wampum belts were a way for Haudenosaunee people, or a lot of First Nations tribes, to document history,” says Kelly. “We didn’t write with a pen and paper, so our way to express and document history–storytelling was through artwork.”


Some of Fire Loom Creation’s designs, including their booklet showcasing drawings of their community belts. Photo: Savanna Craig/APTN.


One of the most notable wampum belts is the two row wampum. This belt documents an agreement between the Haudenosaunee and Dutch settlers. The design shows two boats navigating the river of life without overlapping or interfering with one another.


These belts were once made by hand; then the loom was introduced.


“The loom is another tool that was added to make it easier and faster to do,” says Tyson.


The duo tells each individual or community’s unique story through their loom belt.


“We’ll get to know them; they tell us what they would like to see on their belt design,” says Kelly. “A lot of them ask for certain symbolism to help represent who they are as a person–what clan family they belong to, any tribal designs from whatever tribe they belong to.”


A cabin sits behind Kelly and Tyson’s home. This is where the duo hosts tours inviting both community and non-community members to learn how to bead with the loom.


“We use this little cabin for our tours,” says Kelly.


Through this experience, participants can learn how to bead their own two-row wampum bracelet.


The cabin is now under renovation, but it will soon reopen to the public.


“People from outside the community can come in and take tours and learn from us,” says Kelly. “They learn a little bit about our culture and us.”


A beaded image of Kelly and Tyson’s wedding photo. Photo: Savannah Craig/APTN.


Fire Loom Creations was born from a love story.


“[Tyson and I] decided to get married traditional and I wanted to make Tyson a beaded loom belt,” says Kelly, describing that he had never made a piece that big. “He had created a design when he was younger for a gustoweh headband, and so I took that design and I kind of tripled it and made him a belt.”


Since then, the duo has beaded 227 belts for ceremonies, weddings, graduations and more.


The duo often includes their children in their travels and milestones.


A highlight from their work is designing a Buffalo Bills themed belt, showcasing the history of the Buffalo Bills. The belt is now on display at the Buffalo Bills Stadium located in Orchard Park, New York.


Fire Loom Creations recently won the Indigenous Artist of the Year at the 28th annual American Indigenous Tourism Conference. Photo: Savanna Craig/APTN.


Last month, the duo took their three young children with them to see the belt on display.


The family recently celebrated another win for their business. Kelly holds a woven award Fire Loom Creations recently won at the 28th annual American Indigenous Tourism


“We [won] the Indigenous Artists of the Year,” says Kelly.


One day the family business may one day be …

author: Keelan Jacobs
title: AFN presses Ottawa for funded plan to close $376B infrastructure gap in upcoming federal budget
content:
The Assembly of First Nations is calling on the federal government to use Thursday’s budget to set out a fully funded plan, developed with First Nations, to close an infrastructure gap now estimated at more than $376 billion.

National Chief Cindy Woodhouse Nepinak said at a news conference Tuesday that the scale of the infrastructure gap shortfall demands immediate and sustained attention.

“The AFN estimates put the First Nations infrastructure gap at over $376 billion over the next ten years. Canada committed to closing this gap by 2030. The budget must set out a funded plan with First Nations to deliver on that commitment,” she said.

Woodhouse Nepinak pointed to joint research with the Conference Board of Canada showing the economic payoff of those investments.

“Through our research with the Conference Board of Canada, the Assembly of First Nations describes how these generational investments will create hundreds of thousands of jobs and return $1.82 for every one dollar invested in closing the gap,” she said.

She warned that continued underfunding is driving costs higher.

“Federal investment has not kept pace with First Nations infrastructure needs, and delays are making the gap more costly to close.”

The national chief noted that Prime Minister Mark Carney has already acknowledged more is required.

“The prime minister acknowledged more was needed to close these gaps. So we will watch Thursday’s budget very closely.”

The infrastructure shortfall covers housing, water and wastewater systems, schools, roads, health facilities and community buildings on reserve.

According to AFN’s Closing the Infrastructure Gap (CTIG) reports, the gap means overcrowded and mould-damaged homes, long-term drinking-water advisories, schools that fail basic space and safety standards and limited ability to support economic development or climate adaptation.

ITK asking for Inuit identity card

The Inuit Tapiriit Kanatami (ITK) is calling for a standalone “Inuit-specific section consistent with the Inuit Nunangat Policy.”

The ITK represents approximately 70,000 Inuit in Inuit Nunangat across the North.

President Natan Obed is also calling for an “income-tested $7,500 refundable tax credit for low-income individual residents of Inuit Nunangat to address extreme cost-of-living pressures” and permanent funding of “$120 million annually for a long-term replacement of the Inuit Child First Initiative”

ITK, according to its 2026 pre-budget submission, calls for the government to introduce “legislation as part of the Budget Implementation Act to establish the Inuit Nunangat University,” coupled with $10 million over three years to develop and distribute a “National Inuit Identity Card” and a new “Build Inuit Nunangat Fund of $1 billion over five years”.

APTN News reached out to the ITK for an interview but did not hear back.

Métis National Council asking for $2B for health

The Métis National Council’s 2026 pre-budget submission seeks “distinctions-based investments” that strengthen Métis governments, and calls for “$5.2 million over five years to renew the Canada-Métis Nation Housing agreement, $3.8 million over three years to enable Métis economic participation in nation-building projects; $15 million over five years to renew Métis-led urban and youth programming; $181 million over five years to expand the Métis Nation Post-Secondary Education Strategy; $4.5 million over three years for Métis participation in elementary and secondary education systems and $2.14 billion over five years for Métis health infrastructure and extended health benefits.”

Keelan is Anishinaabe from Walpole Island First Nation (Bkejwanong Territory). He graduated with an Honours B.A. In Political Science from the University of Toronto and follows the stories where power, money and public policy meet. Keelan has a strong interest in economics and finance, and is a lifelong hockey and sports fan.

author: Dennis Ward
title: Inuk actress Anna Lambe says North of North role has brought ‘so much joy into her life’
content:
Inuk actress Anna Lambe was willing to do anything to score a role, any role, on

North of North

.


Lambe had auditioned for the lead role of Siaja but was losing sleep as time passed and she hadn’t received a call back.


Lambe had previously worked with the creators, Stacey Aglok MacDonald and Alethea Arnaquq-Baril on the critically acclaimed film

The Grizzlies

and knew from the outset that

North of North

was going to be great.


“I didn’t expect that it was going to be this big because the writing was there, the team was there, the casting was there, everything was there to make this show a hit show,” says Lambe on the latest episode of

Face to Face

. “It had all of the elements to make it very, very good. So, from the moment I read the breakdown, I was like yup this is the stuff. This is what the kids call the stuff.


“While we were shooting, I had no fears. I had fears about my performance, it was my first time doing comedy, so I was terrified and I would look up at the ceiling going to bed going alright that was my last day on set, I’m going to get fired tomorrow, they’re going to have a new Saija and that’s ok.


“That didn’t happen but the actual content of the show, I was like people are going to love this, I love this, we all love this, we all love making it.”


The first season of North of North was nominated for 20 Canadian Screen Awards. The show won nine, including Best Comedy Series and Best Lead Performer, Comedy for Lambe.


The show is centered around a young Inuk mother [Lambe], who “wants to build a new future for herself after a spontaneous — and extremely public — exit from her marriage. But it won’t be easy in a place like this, where everybody knows your business,” according to a synopsis by Netflix.


“This job has been a bigger gift than I can ever imagined. I feel like I was gifted a can of worms that has exploded and brought so much light and join into my life,” says Lambe who is originally from Iqaluit, Nunavut and moved back in with her parents while the show is in production in the northern community.


Lambe says Nunavummiut are “very much aware of what’s happening in the rest of the world and its about time the rest of the world is aware about us.”


“From an outsider’s perspective, we’re always placed within a historical context and not seen as living, breathing, human beings with communities that still exist and still live in the north and a culture that’s still very much alive and a language that’s still alive and being reclaimed amongst our younger generations.”


“To be able to show Inuit as we truly are is so important and so necessary because it shows that we’re a voice in the north. I think people often talk about the Arctic and the north as if nothing is up there and we don’t exist and as if we’ve been gone for a very long time and that the arctic and the north is free game, they can do whatever they want. I know that Arctic sovereignty, the conversation is a very important one that is being had right now and it feels like a lot of these conversations are actively avoiding Inuit voices because there’s this idea that we don’t exist. So, North of North is a huge part of showing the world that we very much do and were not just a culture and a community that is surviving, we’re very much thriving.”


The 26-year-old’s career has also been thriving in the past two years.


In addition to

North of North

, she was also in

True Detective: Night Country

.


Lambe is also one of the stars in Nyla Innuksuk’s

Slash/Back

 follow up

In the Heart of the South

which debuted at the Toronto International Film Festival, in September.


She also has roles in the Brad Pitt starring

Heart of the Beast

and Aaron Sorkin’s

The Social Reckoning.


Season 2 of North of North is currently airing on APTN and debuts on Netflix on November 5.

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: Auditor General finds Nunavut foster care continues to fail vulnerable children
content:
The Auditor General of Canada tabled

a distressing report

 Tuesday in the Legislative Assembly of Nunavut on foster care in the territory, finding the system has failed to meet its own standards in providing safe and healthy homes for children in care.


“When children are removed from their homes and placed in foster care for their protection, the department takes on responsibility for their safety and well-being,” the auditor general’s team writes in the introduction to the report. “Yet, the department [of Family Services] still could not consistently demonstrate that the basic safeguards intended to protect those children were being followed.”


In 2023, the auditor general described Nunavut’s child-and-family-services system as being “in crisis,” and though a follow-up report in 2025 found the Department of Family Services (DFS) had begun to take action, the current report notes in 2025 that “substantial work remained before those efforts would translate into better services and outcomes for children.”


This year’s audit is focused on foster care and finds there have been little to no changes to serious flaws in the system that the auditor general previously identified and marked for attention.


Among the most damning statistics in the report is the figure that 90 per cent of children or their caregivers did not receive monthly contacts the DFS was required to provide, while five cases showed no evidence DFS contacted children or caregivers for over a year, and one case saw no contact from DFS over 17 months.


The report notes that 100 per cent of files on foster children in the Kitikmeot region, 92 per cent of files in the Kivalliq and South Qikiqtaaluk regions, and 80 per cent of files in the North Qikiqtaaluk region were not compliant with the required regular contact between the department and children in care. In three regions – Kivalliq and both North and South Qikiqtaaluk — 100 per cent of files (along with 75 per cent of files in Kitikmeot region) showed inadequate contact between the DFS and foster caregivers.


Safe home data missing


Another significant failure was in the screening and monitoring of foster homes.


Prior to DFS approving foster homes as safe for children to be placed in, homes are supposed to be subject to a “home study” to assess both the foster caregiver and the safety of the home environment, a clear foster-home agreement laying out roles and responsibilities, a “vulnerable-sector check” to make certain a caregiver does not have any history of crimes against children, and an annual home review to make sure the home remains a safe place for kids.


Unfortunately, for five of 21 homes recently opened, the auditor general found home studies were missing or incomplete, while in another five cases, home studies occurred only after the child or children were already placed in the foster home.


In 53 per cent of foster homes, the report found vulnerable-sector checks were missing or late for some or all adults in the home. Annual home reviews occurred in only 24 per cent of cases, while 76 per cent of files had either incomplete or inadequate home reviews. Finally, 78 per cent of foster home files were missing a signed and up-to-date foster home agreement.


The report notes home studies are important for providing safe environments for children, while “Failure to complete vulnerable sector checks for all adults living in foster homes puts children at risk of being exposed to individuals who may cause them harm.”


Lack of annual home reviews, the report notes, “leaves the department without up to date information on the safety and needs of children in care.” And a lack of signed and up-to-date foster home agreements “increases the risk that foster caregivers do not understand their entitlements or their obligations to help keep children safe.”


Meanwhile, the report finds DFS failed to maintain “complete, accurate, and up to date information on all children placed in foster homes,” in part due to the haphazard rollout of a new information management system called Matrix, which began in the end of 2023.


“We found that the department continued to rely on a manually compiled list of children in care as the most accurate source of reporting information,” the report reads, “instead of its new case management software, Matrix, because employees had not yet fully adopted Matrix or achieved proficiency in using the system.”


Rather than technical concerns, however, the report found …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Gentec Plantium: 89 despidos y planta cerrada en Villa Constitución
content:
El viernes pasado, los trabajadores de la empresa Gentec Plantium de la localidad de Villa Constitución, en Santa Fe, fueron a trabajar y encontraron las puertas cerradas con candado. Poco después les empezaron a llegar los telegramas de despido, y decidieron ocupar la planta. El dueño salió a hablar, culpó a las importaciones y la caída de ventas, y dijo que quiere reabrirla, pero con menos empleados.


Foto: El Sur Diario de Villa Constitución


Plantium es una compañía argentina que se especializa en agricultura de precisión, con desarrollos tecnológicos destinados a mejorar la eficiencia de las tareas agrícolas, como monitores de siembra, pilotos automáticos y sistemas de gestión de datos. En 2002 orientó su negocio hacia soluciones para el campo y se especializó en proyectos vinculados con robótica e inteligencia artificial. Hace apenas cuatro años, inauguró en Rosario un centro de investigación y desarrollo, con más de 50 profesionales especializados. La otra compañía del grupo Gentec es proveedora de equipos para el agro.


Fue un gran impacto para vecinos y trabajadores ver esta empresa de Villa Constitución cerrada y enterarse de los despidos masivos,

detalló la periodista Graciela Moreno en

BAE

. Hace dos años que Plantium tenía problemas y este año la situación empeoró, cobraban los sueldos en cuotas. Mientras buscaba socios o compradores, la empresa pagaba $200.000 semanales a los trabajadores.


Hasta hace dos semanas estaban en negociaciones con inversores chinos, pero la oferta se cayó. El dueño habría planteado la necesidad de ajustar la planta: pasar de 200 a 70 o 60 trabajadores. Se habló de retiros voluntarios, pero al final, llegaron los telegramas.


Una protesta sindical amenazada penalmente


Este martes los trabajadores de Plantium abandonaron la planta de Villa Constitución, que ocupaban desde el viernes, luego de una reunión realizada el lunes en la sede de Rosario del Ministerio de Trabajo de la provincia de Santa Fe. Allí la empresa ofreció un pago parcial que los despedidos aceptaron por falta de alternativas.


Con la regresiva reforma laboral de Javier Milei, aprobada en febrero pasado por el Congreso de la Nación y actualmente vigente, permanecer dentro de la planta era ilegal y exponía a los trabajadores y al gremio a denuncias penales, explicaron desde el Sindicato de Empleados de Comercio (SEC) de Villa Constitución, que representa a los trabajadores.


Su Secretario General, Fulvio Monti, aseguró

en declaraciones a

El Sur Diario

 que ante la posibilidad que el Ministerio de Trabajo dispusiera una conciliación obligatoria o realizara una denuncia para el desalojo, el sindicato resolvió retirarse.


“Hoy no podemos estar adentro de la fábrica”, dijo Monti, y explicó que, tras un fin de semana de mucha angustia, se les explicó la situación a los trabajadores: “No podemos impedir los ingresos a la planta y tenemos que seguir con la lucha afuera”. Por lo que se organizó la presencia en la puerta de la planta.


El pago ofrecido y la votación


En esa instancia, la empresa propuso lo que, según planteó la patronal, podía afrontar: 1.500.000 pesos y dos bonos de 500 mil pesos en alimentos, correspondientes a noviembre y diciembre. La propuesta fue votada el mismo lunes por los trabajadores. Ya se depositó una primera parte de $1.300.000, los bonos están habilitados y los $200.000 restantes se abonarán el 21 de diciembre.


Monti marcó que no se trató de un acuerdo deseado: “Salimos (de la planta) sin conflicto, nada más, pero no fue ningún acuerdo”, afirmó. Y agregó que la disyuntiva era “salir gratis o salir con esto”. Según explicó, el gremio había planteado que, para abandonar la planta sin conflicto, se pusieran los sueldos al día, ya que se adeudan alrededor de tres, pero la empresa dijo no estar en condiciones de afrontar ese costo.


Además, desde la patronal se aseguró que pretende seguir funcionando con 60 personas y que no se quiere ir a la quiebra. Monti aclaró que ni el gremio ni los trabajadores se oponen a que la planta continúe: “Nadie quiere que la fábrica cierre”, remarcó. Pero advirtió: “Es una utopía total pensar que la fábrica puede seguir trabajando como si nada con 60 personas y dejando 89 personas en la calle sin darle una solución”.


El dirigente reclamó un orden de prioridades: “Tiene que resolver el conflicto de la gente que echó y después bienvenido sea que trabaje”. Según indicó, hay despedidos que no tienen cómo afrontar el alquiler, la obra social ni …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Pentagon Sued Over Hegseth’s New “Future of Warfare” Committee Led by Musk
content:
The lawsuit comes as Democrats are eyeing impeachment for Hegseth if they win Congress.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth broke the law in establishing an advisory committee, co-led by Elon Musk, to guide the “future of warfare,” a new lawsuit says, citing “major conflict of interest concerns.”

The lawsuit, filed by watchdogs Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW), Public Citizen, and Project on Government Oversight (POGO), says that the Pentagon did not go through the proper requirements under the Federal Advisory Committee Act (FACA) in the creation of “Project Meridian: The Future of Warfare.” This means that the committee is not subject to public disclosures or scrutiny as it should be, the suit says, and is operating illegally, having had two meetings already.

The lawsuit also alleges that Department of Defense leaders failed to ensure there is a proper balance of expertise and viewpoints on the committee, which is being led by Musk, Anduril CEO Palmer Luckey and former GOP Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich. This has led to “enormous” conflict of interest concerns regarding the group’s makeup, CREW’s president noted.

Pentagon officials “have failed to comply with FACA’s procedural and substantive requirements for new federal advisory committees, including FACA transparency requirements that disallow Project Meridian’s closed-door operations,” the lawsuit says. “Compounding the problem, Project Meridian’s private-sector membership raises precisely the type of conflict-of-interest concerns that FACA was designed to address.”

“As a FACA committee, Project Meridian cannot lawfully provide critical military advice to DoD without public participation and balanced membership to counteract the self-interest and biases of its private-sector members,” it goes on.

The lawsuit comes as Hegseth is slated to be under the microscope if Democrats win Congress, with top House Democrats hinting that impeachment of Hegseth will be their top priority.

Hegseth directed that the Pentagon form the committee in a memo dated September 30. “Project Meridian will study the battlefields of the future, identify which weapons and technologies warfighters will need to harness to dominate in these environments, and propose actionable solutions to start developing, testing and fielding these capabilities,” it says. The memo also says that the “Joint Staff and all services” should transfer its research and plans to the group.

Anduril and Musk’s SpaceX have been awarded with tens of billions of dollars’ worth of federal contracts, including from the Department of Defense, in Trump’s second term. Musk was also under scrutiny recently for seemingly unilaterally deciding to harm Ukraine’s military efforts against Russia by throttling their internet service, which is provided by SpaceX’s Starlink.

“The Federal Advisory Committee Act sets clear requirements about transparency and avoiding conflicts of interest, and Project Meridian must either comply or stop operating,” said Donald K. Sherman, CREW’s president, in a statement.

Public Citizen co-president Robert Weissman raised concerns that Musk and Luckey would work to entrench Big Tech’s interests into military operations, pointing out that FACA was written to prevent such strong influence in government committees.

“Project Meridian would outsource design of grand military strategy to two extremist Pentagon contractors, Elon Musk and Palmer Luckey,” said Weissman. “Very predictably, they will recommend more spending, much more spending, on more AI-enabled weaponry. That would simultaneously make the world more dangerous and starve funding for domestic and human needs.”

author: Chris Walker
title: US Continues Strikes on Iran Despite Trump Claims That War Is Over
content:
The White House has not reported on the US’s strikes on Iran over the past several weeks.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

On Monday night, the United States conducted a series of strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island, the latest in a number of strikes over the past several weeks that have previously gone unreported.

Qeshm Island reportedly houses a large underground missile site and a naval base. It also has a desalination plant, which may be considered a civilian target rather than a military one.

Speaking to reporters on Monday, Trump dismissed the idea that other previously unreported strikes have been taking place.

“We had a war with Iran. We won,” the president claimed during a speech at the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, adding that the U.S. hasn’t engaged in “any fighting for months.”

However, other officials speaking to The Wall Street Journal said that the U.S. has been launching smaller-scale strikes for several weeks, with one source telling the publication that the administration has been downplaying the attacks to avoid signaling any intention of resuming major combat operations.

Trump has been inconsistent in his remarks regarding the future of the U.S.’s war on Iran. During his speech on Monday, he told reporters that a peace deal with the country “looks like [it’s] coming together very nicely.” That comment came shortly after Trump stated on Truth Social that a deal “could happen,” and that Iran wanted a resolution to the conflict “as soon as possible.”

But for several weeks, the president has been suggesting that major hostilities could resume shortly after the midterm elections, sometimes using explicitly genocidal terms. Less than a day after his speech at the Reflecting Pool in which he said a deal was close, Trump indicated in an appearance on “Fox & Friends” that he may restart major attacks on Iran.

Asked by the Fox News hosts what “the next thing” in the war would be, Trump nonchalantly suggested that he could order the resumption of major combat operations.

“I’m not looking to kill lots of people, but if we have to, we’ll have to,” Trump said.

Notably, Trump spent most of the interview peddling blatant falsehoods — including falsely claiming that “inflation is solved” and that “everything is going good” regarding the economy.

In response to The Wall Street Journal report, the National Iranian American Council (NIAC) expressed alarm at the revelation that the U.S. has been launching strikes without publicly announcing them.

“After eight months of an illegal war, there was finally some hope that a diplomatic agreement might be within reach and this war could end through negotiations rather than spiral into the violent scenarios being threatened after the midterm elections,” NIAC President Jamal Abdi said in a statement. “But these deeply alarming revelations suggest we may be heading in precisely the opposite direction.”

Every day that Congress fails to intervene is another day this administration is allowed to wage an unauthorized war, conceal its military operations, and gamble with millions of lives. Congress must immediately demand answers, oppose further military action, and use its power to cut off funding for this unauthorized war.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Federal Agencies Use Internal List to Send Pro-Trump Email Blast Before Election
content:
Experts said the emails likely violate federal law barring use of an official office for election activities.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

The Social Security Administration (SSA) and Internal Revenue Service (IRS) sent out mass emails praising President Donald Trump to online account holders just days before the midterm elections, potentially violating federal laws prohibiting the use of official government resources for a campaign.

The emails were sent on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday, with statements from the agencies’ shared director, Frank Bisignano, touting Trump’s supposed achievements during his second term.

“Under President Donald J. Trump, the Social Security Administration (SSA) is transforming into a model of excellence, one that meets and exceeds customer expectations for fast, accurate and secure service,” said one email signed by Bisignano, a Trump nominee. The wording is similar to that of a press release issued by the SSA last month.

Another email seemingly sent to the IRS account holder list touted the 2025 Republican tax cuts, which are estimated to lead to 51,000 early deaths each year while taking money from the poor and handing massive sums to the rich.

“Last year, President Donald J. Trump signed into law the Working Families Tax Cuts, landmark legislation that ushered in a new era of tax relief and prevented the largest tax increase in American history from taking effect,” the email said, per screenshots posted online and news reports. “Hardworking Americans like you are keeping more of what they earn because of President Trump’s historic tax cuts.”

Recipients of the email expressed fury over receiving the emails on social media. It’s unclear how many emails were sent.

Experts said that the emails may be the latest potential violation of the Hatch Act by the Trump administration, which has been desperate to sway elections in Republicans’ favor as pollsters and analysts predict a blue wave. The Hatch Act and other government ethics laws prohibit federal employees from using federal resources to participate in political and election-related activities, partly with the goal of ensuring that federal programs are administered in a nonpartisan fashion.

One expert likened the emails to the TV ad praising Trump that ran on networks in September and was paid for with taxpayer money.

Critics have said that this administration is a frequent violator of the Hatch Act. One recent complaint by Democracy Defenders Fund said that the Trump administration likely violated the Hatch Act in its pre-dawn raid of Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D-Minnesota) home last month, just weeks before the election in which she was running.

The Trump administration has also repeatedly seemingly misused personal information for political projects.

For now, courts have blocked the Trump administration’s plan for the IRS to transfer massive amounts of taxpayer data to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in order to facilitate mass deportation. And, earlier this year, the Department of Justice admitted that a member of Elon Musk’s “Department of Government Efficiency” team had signed an agreement to hand over Social Security data to a group that seeks to overturn election results.

author: Daron Letts
title: Auditor general points out ‘fundamental weaknesses’ in Nunavut’s foster care
content:
This story was updated on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, at 5:53 p.m. ET.


Nunavut’s Department of Family Services “did not provide timely and effective foster care services to protect and support the safety and well-being of children,” says Canada’s deputy auditor general Andrew Hayes.


Family Services Minister Gwen Healey Akearok sits in the Legislative Assembly last week. On Tuesday, Canada’s auditor general published a report that found her department “did not provide timely and effective foster care services to protect and support the safety and well-being of children.” (File photo by Lilli Akpaleeapik)


He tabled the report,

Foster Care in Nunavut

, in the legislative assembly Tuesday. Family Services Minister Gwen Healey Akearok had announced in March that the audit was underway.


“Fundamental weaknesses” in the territory’s foster care system includes “failures to maintain regular contact with children in care, weaknesses in the screening and monitoring of foster homes, and unreliable information on children and their placements,” according to a news release issued by the auditor general’s office Tuesday, ahead of Hayes’ tabling of the report.


While it’s estimated that about 400 children are in the foster care system, the department remains unaware of the exact number or where the children are located, the latest report states.


This is despite the department rolling out a

 

centralized reporting framework

 called Matrix three years ago.


The audit states that the department relied on a manually compiled list instead of using the software.


Additionally, the department failed to keep up monthly in-person contact with children and foster caregivers, “a basic safeguard intended to protect children in care,” the report states.


“In more than 90 per cent of the files we reviewed, there was no evidence that the required monthly contact with children or foster care caregivers had been maintained,” Hayes said at a press conference in the legislative assembly, where he tabled the report earlier in the afternoon.


In five cases, there was no documented contact with a child for more than one year, including one gap of more than 17 months.


The report also found cracks in the department’s screening process. Family services conducted 52 per cent of home studies, which evaluate the safety of a foster home, before it placed a child.


Long-term monitoring also fell short, with annual reviews that confirmed a foster home remained safe were missing or

incomplete in 62 per cent of examined cases.


Caregivers were not given important information about a child — such as health, family or trauma history — in 32 of 44 files.


An onboarding process for new caregivers was absent, training for caregivers was infrequent

and the foster caregiver manual had not been updated in more than 10 years, the report states.


“There’s recruitment and retention issues that the department needs to address,” Hayes said. “In some cases, housing can be a problem.”


Previous audits in

 2011

,

 2014

,

 2023

 and

 2025

 found similar problems, including one finding from 2023 that the department

 could not provide

 an accurate count for the number of children in its care.


Following the October 2023 report, former family services minister Margaret Nakashuk

apologized

 for the department’s failure to protect children in its care.


“Ultimately, we need to see more from the department and improve services to these families and children,” Hayes said.


“Hopefully there is an urgency that is being recognized by the department and that the legislative assembly members can use our report and the department’s responses to hold the department accountable for making the improvements that they’ve committed to.”


The auditor general will release another report in the spring of 2027, on the department’s “quality assurance work,” he said.


Akearok thanked the auditor general for the report and its recommendations, saying it validates many of the actions already underway in her department.


“Meaningful change requires accountability, consistent follow-through, and sustained action,” she said in a Government of Nunavut news release issued after the report was tabled.


Akearok said her department is strengthening prevention and family supports, improving oversight, equipping staff with tools and training, and supporting foster caregivers.

title: Κινητοποίηση ενάντια σε απειλή έξωσης, την Τετάρτη 4/11, στις 08.30, στη Τράπεζα της Ελλάδος, Ιωάννινα
content:
Αφίσα/Κάλεσμα από τον

Ρουβίκωνα

:


Κάλεσμα σε κινητοποίηση την Τετάρτη 4 Νοεμβρίου και ώρα 08:30 π.μ. στην Τράπεζα της Ελλάδος, για τη στήριξη οικογένειας με γονείς με αναπηρία ενάντια σε απειλή έξωσης.


Απειλή επικείμενης έξωσης οικογένειας με γονείς ΑμεΑ από την πρώτη και μοναδική κατοικία της έλαβε χώρα στις 23/10/2026 από εισπρακτική εταιρεία, η οποία προχώρησε σε χυδαία αμφισβήτηση της κατάστασης της υγείας των γονέων.


Τα αδηφάγα κοράκια επιμένουν ότι η κόρη της οικογένειας πρέπει να αναλάβει τα χρέη των γονιών της, παρ’ όλο που η ίδια αγόρασε πίσω το σπίτι της οικογένειάς της από τον πλειστηριασμό του, καθαρό από οικονομικά βάρη.


Τα κοινωνικά αγαθά της στέγασης, πρόσβασης σε νερό και ενέργεια και των βασικών ανθρώπινων αναγκών είναι και θα παραμείνουν αδιαπραγμάτευτα. Δε θα επιτρέψουμε σε κανέναν να πετάξει έξω από το σπίτι του καμία οικογένεια, πόσο μάλλον ανθρώπους ευάλωτων κοινωνικών ομάδων.


Απέναντι στην τρομοκρατία αυτή το μόνο όπλο μας είναι η αλληλεγγύη και η μόνη ασπίδα προστασίας της λαϊκής κατοικίας είναι οι οργανωμένοι και μαζικοί αγώνες της κοινωνικής βάσης.


Στηρίζουμε την κινητοποίηση στην Τράπεζα της Ελλάδος, οδό Αβέρωφ 2.

title: 17 HENS LIBERATED IN SOLIDARITY WITH RUCIO, CASO SUSARON.
content:
October, Argentina.


via: @anarcoveganismo.arg


ENGLISH (translation):


“There are nine of us hiding in the night, lying in wait. Our objective is crystal clear: we must get someone out of those cages—no matter what. On the way to the site (a farm for egg laying hens) we coordinate our roles; each person is vital and essential to achieving this act of animal liberation tonight.

We arrive in the dead of night, the lights in the sheds still on. As we finish cutting through the wire fencing, the lights go out. ‘GO! THIS IS OUR CHANCE!’ We wait a few moments, then slip inside—and there they are, terrified, surrounded by their own excrement and rats.

We begin opening the cages. The cool night air, the tall grass, and our dark clothing helped us reach them. We fill our bags and ensure the area is clear for our exit. Our companions are waiting by the fence, others in the cars; we load them up and leave, looking back at all those we couldn’t rescue today; but perhaps we will tomorrow, because this doesn’t end here.

This is a war against speciesism, a fight to liberate the slaves of an exploitative, murderous system.

Against all odds, and against all authority.

There is no veganism without animal liberation.

We dedicate this action to Nico Rucio (Susaron case); an anti-speciesist, anarcho-nihilist, straight-edge prisoner held within the territory occupied by the oppressive Chilean state.


Warm hugs, wishing for your swift and urgent release.”


SPANISH (original):


“Somos 9 personas merodeando en la noche, al acecho. Tenemos bien en claro el objetivo, sacar a alguien de las jaulas si o si, camino al lugar (una granja de gallinas ponedoras) nos ponemos de acuerdo en nuestros roles, cada unx es importante y fundamental para lograr esta noche la liberación animal.

Llegamos en plena madrugada y las luces de las naves estan prendidas, terminamos de cortar el alambre y se apagan, “VAMOS, ES NUESTRA OPORTUNIDAD” esperamos unos minutos y ya estamos adentro y ahí están ellas, temerosas y acompañadas por sus heces y las ratas.

Comenzamos a abrir las jaulas, la noche fresca, la hierva alta y nuestra ropa oscura nos ayudó a llegar hoy hasta ellas, llenamos los bolsos y nos aseguramos de que la zona sea segura para salir, nuestrxs companerxs nos esperan en el alambrado, otrxs dentro de los autos, las cargamos y nos vamos mirando atrás a todas esas que no pudimos sacar hoy, pero tal vez si mañana, porque esto no termina hoy.

Esta es una guerra contra el especismo, es liberar a lxs esclavxs de un sistema explotador y asesino.

Contra todo pronóstico y contra toda autoridad.

No hay veganismo sin liberación animal.

Queremos dedicar esta acción a Nico Rucio (Caso susaron) presx antiespecista-Anarco-nihilista straight edge en el territorio ocupado por el estado opresor chileno.

Un abrazo cómplice, pronta y urgente libertad”

author: Clara Saliba
title: O Lula venceu. E agora, haverá ajuste?
content:
O presidente Lula foi reeleito para seu quarto mandato, em meio a uma virada de votos histórica que contou com a participação popular em peso, nas ruas e nas redes. Ufa. 


As brasileiras e os brasileiros avaliaram o que tinham a perder com uma vitória de

Flávio Bolsonaro

. Para não falar da aproximação do ex-senador com as milícias ou dos escândalos de corrupção, me restrinjo a comentar a promessa de um “tesouraço” de até R$ 200 bilhões nas contas públicas que,

conforme apuração da Folha de S.Paulo

, poderia incluir congelamento de benefícios, desvinculação das aposentadorias ao salário mínimo e o fim dos pisos constitucionais de educação e saúde (o mínimo que obrigatoriamente tem que ser gastos por estas pastas). 


Por isso, no dia 25 de outubro, o povo escolheu. Na minha visão,

a vitória de Lula, amparada no que talvez tenha sido a maior mobilização popular desde a redemocratização, não deixou dúvidas sobre o projeto de governo que ganhou as eleições. Os votos foram contra os cortes nos programas sociais. 


Mas,

já no dia seguinte, os jornais bradavam pela imperativa necessidade de um ajuste fiscal. Sinalizavam que a dívida pública brasileira, hoje no patamar de 82,9% do PIB, é preocupante, e não resta escolha para o governo vindouro a não ser colocar as contas nos eixos. 


Esse movimento, de cobrar a partir “do mercado” uma política econômica diferente daquela que foi eleita, tem sido chamado entre os economistas e analistas políticos de “terceiro turno” da eleição presidencial. Escolhemos o presidente. Agora, precisamos escolher o projeto econômico. 


É nesse contexto que escrevo sobre ajuste fiscal nesta coluna. Antes de mais nada, esclareço que, as eleições só têm dois turnos.

O projeto econômico já foi escolhido, junto com o presidente – e qualquer movimentação que vá em direção ao corte em programas sociais é estelionato eleitoral. Isso não significa que nenhum corte de gastos possa ser feito

; mas voltaremos a isso mais à frente. 


Primeiro, precisamos entender o que é o tal do ajuste fiscal, e por que ele tem sido vendido como incontornável. Em palavras simples,

um ajuste fiscal é uma reordenação na política fiscal, ou seja, na forma como o governo arrecada e gasta seus recursos, com vistas a reduzir a diferença entre o gasto e a arrecadação.

 Ele pode ser de várias dimensões e incidir sobre diferentes etapas do grande guarda-chuva do “gasto público”. 


A necessidade de ajuste vem da ideia de que uma relação muito alta entre a dívida do governo e o produto da economia pode causar problemas, como desconfiança no mercado, elevação do risco-país e a inflação. 


Sem entrar no mérito da validade dessa discussão,

vale lembrar que, se nossa dívida está na casa dos 80%, a dos Estados Unidos está em 123%, a da França em 113% e a do Reino Unido chega a 92%.  


Mais importante que isso é entender o que leva nossa dívida pública para cima. Muito mais do que os gastos com Bolsa Família ou Pé de Meia,

o que coloca a relação dívida/PIB do Brasil num patamar relativamente alto é a nossa taxa de juros astronômica. 


A maior do mundo, vale lembrar. 


Em 2026, o pagamento dos juros da dívida pública respondeu por 83% da pressão sobre a dívida pública

, como explicou meu colega Lucas Marçal, em

texto para o jornal Hora do Povo

. O resultado primário, isto é,

a diferença entre o que o governo arrecada e o que ele gasta, respondeu por menos de 10%. 


Ou seja: dá para fazer ajuste sem cortar programas sociais, e de forma muito mais efetiva.

 Por exemplo, repensando o modelo de metas de inflação, que coloca nossos juros em patamares cronicamente altos e sufoca a possibilidade de estabilização da dívida.


Também dá para fazer ajuste mexendo em outros gastos governamentais, como os supersalários do judiciário ou as emendas parlamentares impositivas, em especial as “emendas pix”, que caem diretamente na conta dos entes federativos sem destinação clara. Ou, ainda, aumentando a arrecadação, elevando a carga tributária sobre os mais ricos e revendo isenções fiscais a grandes empresas.

author: Scot Nakagawa
title: The fight after the vote
content:
This article

The fight after the vote

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


The good news is that the courts closed off most of the routes by which the Trump administration could have impeded, intimidated or purged voters before Election Day. On September 14, the Supreme Court blocked the Postal Service’s restrictions on mail ballots, and in June it

upheld

 grace periods for ballots postmarked by Election Day. The Justice Department has reportedly lost nearly all of its 30 lawsuits seeking states’ voter files. And federal law already bars armed federal agents from polling places, a protection seven states reinforced this year by advancing bans of their own.


Pressure doesn’t disappear when one door closes. It moves to the next one. With the front end of the election largely protected, the softer targets are now the count, certification and the seating of the new House.


What to expect


The most likely danger is also the most familiar: a fraud story built on slow counts. Fourteen states and the District of Columbia count ballots that arrive after Election Day, so in many places the results will take days. That delay is normal, and it’s a sign the system is working. But it’s also an opening for anyone who wants to claim that votes counted later are suspect, and the ground is already prepared. One

survey

 found that fewer than half of voters expect a fair election.


The second danger may already be under way. The “

sanctuary surge

” the administration announced in late September is bringing immigration enforcement into 11 states in the days before the vote. The Homeland Security secretary says agents will appear at polling places only in response to “a threat” or with a warrant. Whatever happens at the polls, the surge’s real effect may be to frighten eligible voters in immigrant and mixed-status families into staying home.


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


After the votes are cast, the fight shifts to close races. Democrats need a net gain of about six seats to win the House, so a handful of tight contests could decide who controls it. Expect recounts and lawsuits in every one of them. Expect, too, that some county boards will refuse to certify results. Courts have forced certification every time a board has tried this since 2020, but each refusal buys time and headlines for the story that something went wrong.


Two darker scenarios are less likely but would do far more damage. The first is the seizure of ballots or voting machines by federal authorities. That would break the chain of custody that makes results trustworthy, and it isn’t hypothetical: The FBI has already raided election offices in Fulton County, Georgia, and Maricopa County, Arizona. The second would be a fight over seating the new House on January 3, in which a newly installed House clerk could leave contested Democrats off the roll. Scholars call that far-fetched, and it could only work if control of the House rests on a handful of seats. But the fact that it’s being discussed at all tells us how much of our democracy now depends on officials choosing to follow the rules.


The work after the vote


What can grassroots groups and local officials do once the polls close? The honest answer is that the most useful work will be slow and procedural. It isn’t glamorous. It comes down to three things: making sure every valid ballot is counted, making sure certification happens on time, and keeping the public calm while both are under way.


The first 72 hours matter most. The deadlines to fix rejected ballots, known as cure deadlines, run only a few days, so coalitions should be helping voters amend ballot mistakes right away, while trained observers watch the count. Their public message should be simple and repeated until it sinks in: Slow counts are normal. Local election officials have a parallel job. They can give daily public updates on the count, open counting rooms to observers from all sides, secure ballots and machines, and refuse to release any of them without a court order.


Over the following two weeks, the action moves to county canvass and certification meetings. Coalitions should attend every one, document problems and report them to election protection lawyers, and thank election workers in public, because many of them have been threatened for doing their jobs. Officials, for their part, should certify on time and say in advance that they will, with county …

title: After ICE Terror, Poll Finds 61 Percent of Latino Voters Say They’ll Vote Blue

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

In 2024, Donald Trump won the presidency with the support of 44% of Hispanic voters, suggesting that a major realignment in party preferences might be underway. But just two years later, it appears much of that support has eroded. Sixty-one percent of Hispanic voters say they will now support Democrats in the midterms, including 11% who previously had voted for President Trump.

We get a bird’s-eye view of what to expect from the Latino vote from Marisa Franco, the co-founder and director of the advocacy organization Mijente. While ICE brutality will be at the front of voters’ minds, she says, Democrats cannot continue to take Latino voters for granted. “The vast majority of Latinos are working-class. Quite simply, they voted for Trump because they were looking at issues of economy, cost, inflation,” explains Franco. “And at the end of the day, these same issues have worsened under Trump’s administration, under Republican control. So people, I think, are looking for someone who’s going to explain what’s happening and propose solutions and be dogged about finding them.”

We end today’s show looking at how Latino voters could impact today’s midterms. In 2024, President Trump won the presidency with the support of 44% of Latino voters across the country — a significant shift following decades of Democratic advantage among Latinos. Two years later, it appears much of those Republican gains have eroded, and Democratic voters are significantly more motivated to go to the polls. Polling suggests cost of living is the top concern for all voters, including Latinos, who now trust Democrats more than President Trump to manage the economy. author: David Venn
title: Ikur’raq cabin program expands with $500,000 in federal money
content:
The federal government has topped up a cabin program meant to reduce homelessness in Nunavut, Family Services Minister Gwen Healey Akearok announced Oct. 27.


Close to $514,000 will go towards the territory’s Ikur’raq Cabins Initiative, a project meant to give people a temporary place of respite from overcrowding, violence and addiction issues. The money will fund 15 cabins.


“Out-of-shelter homelessness is a major public health and safety issue,” Akearok said in her minister’s statement at the legislative assembly. “The Ikur’raq cabins offer a practical response to this urgent need.”


The GN funded the

first set of 16 cabins

 in 2022 and the program was revived in 2025 with $1 million in federal money to build 20 additional cabins.


Akearok’s Oct. 27 announcement will bring the total to 51.


Hamlets, non-profits and hunters and trappers organizations can apply for $50,000 grants with the new round of funding.


The original 16 cabins include three Pangnirtung, two each in Arviat and Pond Inlet, and one cabin in each of Coral Harbour, Iqaluit, Clyde River, Naujaat, Baker Lake, Igloolik, Kugaaruk, Taloyoak, and Kugluktuk.


As of Oct. 20, six cabins from the second round of funding were complete and 14 were under construction, according to Family Services spokesperson Irma Arkus. Sanirajak and Kugaaruk have finished two each, while Sanikiluaq and Iqaluit have finished one each.


Two cabins in Arctic Bay are under construction, while one cabin in Arviat, Baker Lake, Chesterfield Inlet, Gjoa Haven, Igloolik, Kugluktuk, Naujaat, Pangnirtung, Pond Inlet, Qikiqtarjuaq, Rankin Inlet and Taloyoak are under construction.


Akearok said her department is working to build the cabins “in the communities where the need is greatest.”

author: CMI Argentina
title: Cientificidio: en tres meses se destruyeron casi 23 empleos por día
content:
El promedio se ubicaba en 8,5 trabajos perdidos por día desde diciembre. Un informe del grupo Economía Política Ciencia (EPC) del CIICTI explicó que este descenso en velocidad del empleo científico se debe, principalmente, a la reducción de becas en el CONICET, los retiros en el INTA y el recorte de personal en la empresa pública FADEA.


Por Guillermo Lavecchia


El

cientificidio

 que lleva adelante el Gobierno nacional, cuyas consecuencias se verán en los próximos años (o décadas), tiene efectos concretos, números reales, personas e investigaciones truncas detrás.


Un

informe del grupo Economía Política Ciencia

 (epc) del Centro Iberoamericano de Investigación en Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación (CIICTI) da cuenta de cómo la destrucción de los puestos de trabajo en ciencia y tecnología creció drásticamente en el tercer trimestre del año en curso. Mientras que el promedio se ubica en 8,5 empleos perdidos por día desde diciembre de 2023, en los últimos tres meses la cifra se elevó a 22,8 por día.


El Grupo EPC explicó que este descenso en velocidad del empleo científico se debe, principalmente, a la reducción de becas en el CONICET, los retiros en el INTA y el recorte de personal en la empresa pública FADEA.


Foto: Edgardo Gómez @jedgardogomez


El CONICET, principal organismo nacional de investigación científica, perdió 722 investigadores de carrera y personal de apoyo desde diciembre de 2023. Además, disminuyó su cantidad de becas en 2418, lo que recorta drásticamente la formación de profesionales a mediano y largo plazo.


El informe del Grupo EPC detalla la situación del INTA, organismo golpeado por la desarticulación de programas y actividades de ciencia y tecnología, que redujo casi 1.000 trabajadores en el último trimestre: su deterioro alcanza una reducción de personal de 27,3% desde diciembre de 2023.


Un país sin ciencia es un país sin inteligencia colectiva


Ya en julio pasado, trabajadores y trabajadoras de Universidades, Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas (Conicet), Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Agropecuaria (INTA), Instituto Nacional de Tecnología Industrial (INTI), Servicio Meteorológico Nacional (SMN) y Comisión Nacional de Energía Atómica (CNEA) firmaron en conjunto una dura carta contra la política de destrucción del sistema científico del gobierno de Javier Milei. “Alertamos de la crisis terminal que atravesamos y el impacto destructor para la Argentina en el presente y el futuro”, advirtieron.


Definieron al “proceso de destrucción de su sistema científico, tecnológico y universitario” como “absolutamente irracional desde el punto de vista político, social y económico” y recordaron que la

inversión pública

 en la función ciencia y técnica, por debajo del 0.15% del PBI, es la más baja en la historia de nuestro país, al menos desde los últimos 54 años.


El desfinanciamiento sostenido, los retiros voluntarios, despidos y renuncias de personal altamente calificado forzados por pérdidas salariales cercanas al 40% desde diciembre de 2023, y la paralización total de programas estratégicos “son un proceso planificado por el actual gobierno que busca destruir capacidades construidas durante décadas por generaciones enteras de argentinos y argentinas”.


Científicas y científicos remarcaron que “nunca un país que hizo un esfuerzo sostenido durante más de 200 años para generar capacidades científicas y tecnológicas al servicio de la sociedad las destruyó en tan corto tiempo”.


https://t.co/BCNEqe6iNS


— Jorge Aliaga (@jorgeluisaliaga)

July 6, 2026


Las y los firmantes consideraron que el desmantelamiento del sistema científico tecnológico puesto en marcha desde diciembre de 2023 “no tiene absolutamente nada que ver con el déficit cero o restricciones presupuestarias”. Por el contrario, “es una decisión política y cultural tomada por un gobierno que ha declarado abiertamente su voluntad de destruir al Estado que conduce”.


Cuestionaron que hoy investigadores, docentes y técnicos altamente calificados se ven forzados a migrar, realizar otros trabajos ajenos a su formación o al pluriempleo. “Argentina invirtió en la formación de estos recursos humanos, una inversión que este gobierno tira a la basura impidiendo que trabajen para el desarrollo de nuestro país (…) Este ataque a las instituciones y a sus trabajadores y trabajadoras es principalmente un ataque feroz a la capacidad colectiva de la sociedad argentina para cuidarse, producir, imaginar y construir futuro” …

author: CMI Argentina
title: El Sindicato del Subte advirtió por medidas de fuerza ante descuentos arbitrarios de Emova
content:
La Asociación Gremial de Trabajadores del Subte y Premetro (AGTSyP) denunció “reiteradas malas liquidaciones de haberes y descuentos indebidos” y le advirtió a la empresa concesionaria que evalúa nuevas medidas de fuerza.


La Asociación Gremial de Trabajadores del Subterráneo y Premetro (AGTSyP – Metrodelegadxs) emitió un comunicado este lunes 2 de noviembre en el que informó que se encuentra en “estado de alerta” debido a los problemas salariales que atraviesan los trabajadores del sector debido a las prácticas arbitrarias que está desarrollando la concesionaria Emova, específicamente “las reiteradas malas liquidaciones de haberes y descuentos indebidos a trabajadoras y trabajadores desde hace meses”.


Ante esta situación, desde el Sindicato que conduce actualmente Néstor Segovia -tras el fallecimiento el año pasado del histórico dirigente “Beto” Pianelli- advirtieron a la empresa que se abstenga de repetir este accionar en la próxima liquidación de sueldos.


El comunicado fue firmado por Segovia junto a la secretaria de Organización Virginia Bouvet.


Los metrodelegados fueron categóricos al señalar las responsabilidades institucionales y laborales. “Siendo la única responsable de las medidas de autodefensa que resulten de este accionar arbitrario”, sentenciaron, sin detallar cuáles serían las medidas, que pueden incluir asambleas, retención de tareas, liberación de molinetes o paros que afectan directamente el servicio.


POSIBLES MEDIDAS DE AUTODEFENSA


Informamos que nos encontramos en estado de alerta por las reiteradas malas liquidaciones de haberes y descuentos indebidos a trabajadoras y trabajadores desde hace meses.


— Prensa AGTSyP (@prensadelsubte)

November 2, 2026


La empresa Emova Movilidad S.A. fue conformada para obtener la concesión de la red de Subte de Buenos Aires, lográndolo desde el 1 de diciembre de 2021. Es un consorcio integrado por Benito Roggio Transporte y Metrovías.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Reform Councillor Charged With Rape and Making Indecent Images of a Child
content:
The leader of Reform UK in Hampshire county council has been charged with 12 counts of rape and two counts of making indecent images of a child, among multiple other offences. 


George Madgwick, 37, represents North East Havant on the council, where he leads the Reform group. 


He was charged on Tuesday with a total of 35 offences, which also include eight counts of actual bodily harm, two counts of assault by penetration, two counts of sexual assault and two counts of controlling and coercive behaviour.


“He has also been charged with making a threat to kill, false imprisonment and stalking,” a spokesperson for the

Crown Prosecution Service said

. “Our prosecutors have worked to establish that there is sufficient evidence and that it is in the public interest to bring the case to court.”


They added: “We remind all concerned that proceedings against the defendant are now active and that he has the right to a fair trial. There should be no reporting, commentary or sharing of information which could in any way prejudice these proceedings.”


The charges come after an investigation by Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary into allegations relating to four complainants between 2008 and 2021.


The

police investigation began

 on 24 July last year after officers received a report of a sexual offence. Madgwick was arrested on 6 January 2026.


He will appear at Portsmouth Magistrates Court on 25 November. Reform UK said he had been suspended with “immediate effect”.
